We present a theoretical framework that connects the out-of-plane optical response in both regimes to the fluctuating in-plane superconducting state, and contrast the sensitivity of different types of terahertz nonlinearities to fluctuating order.

authors.name: Albert Liu, Danica Pavicevic, Alex G\'omez Salvador, Marios H. Michael, Michael Fechner, Pedro M. Lozano, Qiang Li, Genda D. Gu, Eugene Demler, Andrea Cavalleri

papers.title: On the Structure of the Nuclear-Clock Isotope $^{229}$Th Beyond Quadratic Order
papers.summary: Precision measurements of the exceptionally low-energy nuclear transition of $^{229}$Th, offer an extraordinary sensitivity to a variety of new light fields. However, interpreting such measurements requires nuclear-structure information beyond what is currently constrained by spectroscopy. We develop a systematic description of the electric multipole interactions governing the hyperfine structure of ${}^{229}$Th, including the hexadecapole contribution, and perform a symmetry-based analysis of the resulting hyperfine splittings in crystalline environments. Hyperfine spectroscopy generally constrains combinations of nuclear moments and crystal-field gradients, leading to degeneracies when higher multipole interactions are allowed. We then combine experimental nuclear observables, particle-rotor relations, and a deformed-Fermi charge-density model to investigate the electromagnetic contribution to the nuclear clock's sensitivity to variations in the fine-structure constant. We find that higher-order nuclear deformation and state-dependent differences in the radial charge distribution of the clock states can substantially alter the predicted sensitivity, introducing large uncertainties that are not constrained by existing measurements. Our results highlight the importance of combining nuclear and solid-state theory with complementary measurements, including spectroscopy of higher-spin states, to constrain the nuclear structure and improve predictions of the clock's sensitivity to new physics. Our symmetry-based analysis also provides a framework for using hyperfine spectroscopy to investigate local defect symmetries in crystalline hosts.

authors.name: Chaja Baruch, Doron Gazit, Hans-Werner Hammer, Fiona Kirk, Joachim Kopp, Gil Paz, Ekkehard Peik, Gilad Perez, Yotam Soreq, Konstantin Springmann

papers.title: Probing scalar-mediated Lorentz violation with hydrogen masers and spin-precession of molecules
papers.summary: We propose using hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession experiments, traditionally employed in precision frequency measurements and searches for the electron electric dipole moment, as complementary probes of light scalar-mediated, spin-dependent fifth forces. We investigate their sensitivity to Lorentz-violating interactions mediated by scalars with masses ranging from $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4}~\mu\mathrm{eV})$ to $\mathcal{O}(10~\mathrm{keV})$. While hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession measurements probe different combinations of Lorentz-violating couplings, we find that the strongest projected sensitivities can be achieved using spin-precession of ultracold molecules, benefiting from their extended coherence times. These experimental approaches provide access to previously unexplored regions of parameter space, probing interaction ranges extending from centimeter to sub-angstrom scales. Our proposals highlight the potential of precision atomic and molecular experiments to search for new spin-dependent scalar-mediated interactions and violations of fundamental spacetime symmetries.

authors.name: Djuna Croon, Tanmay Kumar Poddar

papers.title: Magnon-Phonon-Polariton Optomechanics in a van der Waals Magnet
papers.summary: The layered anti-ferromagnet CrSBr hosts self-hybridized exciton-polaritons that couple parametrically to coherent magnons and phonons. In this work, we explore the tripartite optomechanical interaction between these quasiparticles in suspended CrSBr membranes supporting high-$Q$ breathing-type acoustic phonon modes. Using resonant pump-probe spectroscopy on the polariton state, we resolve the coupled dynamics in the $\simeq 20$ GHz range while sweeping the magnon mode across the phonon resonance with an external magnetic field. We observe an attractive magnon-phonon interaction of strength $V/2\pi = -43$ MHz, which primarily leads to phonon amplification. At the magnon-phonon resonance, we find predominantly unidirectional energy flow from magnons to phonons while the possible back-action is limited by kinetic losses of coherent magnons. Our study enables direct interfacing of collective magnetic excitations with sound and light in layered van der Waals materials, paving the way for quantum-coherent transduction in the GHz range with optical readout.

authors.name: Jens-Christian Drawer, Vladislav Yu. Shishkov, Bo Han, Vita Solovyeva, Iva Plutnarov\'a, Zden\v{e}k Sofer, Christian Schneider, Anton V. Zasedatelev, Martin Esmann

papers.title: High-Order Regularization for Singular and Nearly Singular Laplace and Stokes Layer Potentials in Two Dimensions
papers.summary: Layer potentials represent the solutions of many elliptic boundary value problems, but their kernels have the singularity of the fundamental solution, so standard quadrature loses accuracy at targets on or near the boundary. In two dimensions, Gaussian regularization of the logarithmic kernel gives a smooth kernel involving the exponential integral $E_1$, but for the single layer its regularization error is only first order in the smoothing radius $\delta$. We construct modified kernels for two-dimensional Laplace and Stokes single- and double-layer potentials that achieve regularization error $O(\delta^p)$, $p=3,5,7$, uniformly for targets on and near the curve. The resulting method is both high-order accurate and easy to implement: the integrals are evaluated directly by the periodic trapezoidal rule on a single fixed set of boundary nodes for all targets. Choosing $\delta=c h^q$ with $q<1$, where $h$ is the node spacing, keeps the discretization error smaller than the regularization error as $h\to0$, and numerical experiments confirm the predicted $O(h^{pq})$ convergence. Finally, we combine the near-curve evaluation with a fast Poisson solver to compute the potentials on the entire Cartesian grid.

authors.name: Han Zhou

papers.title: Fundamental physics with quantum sensors in space
papers.summary: Quantum sensors such as atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and atomic magnetometers can be used as sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. Space offers microgravity, long baselines, low environmental noise, access to varying gravitational potentials, and unique opportunities involving the Sun, Moon, planets, and asteroids. These proceedings of the Aspen Center for Physics workshop on "Fundamental physics in space with quantum sensors," held February 22-27, 2026, summarize the scientific case, current capabilities, and space mission concepts for investigating dark matter, testing general relativity, and detecting gravitational waves in frequency bands inaccessible from the ground.

authors.name: Jason Arakawa, Daniel J. Blumenthal, Oliver Buchmueller, Dmitry Budker, Luigi Cacciapuoti, Emily D. Caldwell, Andrei Derevianko, Benjamin P. Dix-Matthews, Michael A. Fedderke, Naceur Gaaloul, Susan Gardner, Jonah Glick, Paul Hamilton, Elena Jordan, Hidetoshi Katori, Peter Kurczynski, David R. Leibrandt, Anna L. Marchant, Indra Periwal, Igor Pikovski, Marianna S. Safronova, Christian Sanner, Sascha W. Schediwy, Volodymyr Takhistov, Yu-Cheng Tien, Yu-Dai Tsai, Jason R. Williams

papers.title: Stokes flow in a wedge with a moving contact point: well-posedness with a fixed contact angle and Navier slip
papers.summary: We study 2D Stokes flow in a wedge-like region bounded by a solid substrate with Navier slip and by a free surface driven by surface tension. The two meet at a moving contact point with a fixed contact angle. This is the model of a moving contact line at scales below the slip length, in its simplest setting. The slip length is the only length scale, and nothing is prescribed at the contact point beyond the angle: no relaxation law for the angle, and no contact-point dissipation. Slip removes the paradox found by Huh and Scriven, the infinite dissipation at a contact line that moves without slip, but in this model a weaker singularity remains. We give, to our knowledge, the first rigorous characterisation of this singularity for solutions of the free-boundary problem near the stationary state. For small contact angles and small initial data satisfying two compatibility conditions, we prove local existence, uniqueness and Lipschitz dependence on the data. The compatibility conditions are the price of the fixed angle for solutions regular in time up to the initial time. Rather than hiding the singularity, the solution class carries it explicitly in corner expansions. The velocity is continuous up to the contact point. The pressure has a logarithmic singularity, the slip-regularised version of that of Huh and Scriven. Its coefficient is proportional to the contact-point velocity. The slope of the free boundary has a corresponding logarithmic correction, the slip-scale counterpart of the Cox-Voinov relation. The linearised problem combines terms of different scaling, which prevents a direct treatment by the Mellin transform. We solve it by a Lax-Milgram argument, and an auxiliary test function problem shows that the variational solution satisfies the equations. Explicit Mellin representations then yield the corner expansions, and the nonlinear problem is solved by a contraction argument.

authors.name: Manuel V. Gnann, Hans Kn\"upfer, King Ming Lam, Nader Masmoudi, Jonas Sauer

papers.title: QCap: a physics-corrected graph neural network for the capacitance matrix of any planar superconducting device layout
papers.summary: Electromagnetic simulations of device layouts to extract capacitance are computationally intensive, a major obstacle to accurate design of circuit devices. Machine learning models can bypass these simulations, but previous approaches have been restricted to layouts using only particular components, and require thousands of simulations of those same components as training data. We present QCap, a model that accurately predicts the Maxwell capacitance matrix of an arbitrary superconducting device layout in seconds, compared to minutes to hours of Ansys Q3D simulations. We develop a novel design-embedding algorithm that converts the layout into a universal graph format, allowing the model to work with any layout created with any tool. To achieve high accuracy, we obtain a coarse physics prior from a fast method of moments simulation of capacitance, then train the model to correct this prior. On 4,009 test designs withheld from training data the model outputs agree with Q3D simulations to a median error of 0.177%, and on never-seen component families it stays below 1% error. We demonstrate the model's scaling by obtaining the capacitance matrix of a 9-superconducting-qubit device in 12 seconds on a laptop (compared to 19.9 h and 228 GB of memory in Ansys) with sub-percent error, and capacitance of a (too large to simulate) 100-qubit, 781-conductor device in 3.4 min on a laptop. We provide the open-source models and data on SQuADDS and Hugging Face. Our results provide a powerful tool for large-scale accurate circuit design and guide the development of models to bypass other physical simulations.

authors.name: Sadman Ahmed Shanto, Saikat Das, Eli M. Levenson-Falk

papers.title: Second Harmonic Flexoelectricity
papers.summary: Flexoelectricity (polarization induced by strain gradients) is assumed to be insensitive to space inversion in all materials: flexoelectric polarization should not depend on whether a crystal is bent upwards or downwards. In this work, we show that this assumption is wrong for ferroelectrics of all thickness and at all curvatures, owing to an intrinsic quadratic contribution that persists down to strain gradients of 1 m-1 or less, which is millions of times smaller than conventional expectations for nonlinear flexoelectricity. As a consequence, ferroelectric crystals can generate second-harmonic voltage at twice the oscillation frequency of the bending.

authors.name: Zhiguo Wang, Yida Yang, Shuai Yang, Haoran Li, Chunchun Li, Zhibin Wen, Zhengqiu Xie, Wenbin Huang, Konstantin Shapovalov, Jiawang Hong, Longlong Shu, Fei Li, Gustau Catalan

papers.title: Perturbative Recovery of Stabilizer-Subspace Correlations for Quantum Computational Chemistry
papers.summary: Stabilizer-based subspace methods can substantially reduce the quantum resources required for electronic structure calculations, but the resulting projection neglects Hamiltonian couplings to configurations outside the retained subspace. In this work, we introduce Stabilizer-Subspace Perturbation Theory (SSPT) to recover the associated correlation contributions, using the Contextual Subspace Variational Quantum Eigensolver (CS-VQE) as a representative application. The central idea is to exploit the Pauli terms eliminated by stabilizer projection as perturbative operators that generate an external manifold from the optimized reference state. Their energetic contributions are evaluated using an Epstein-Nesbet-type second-order correction or a resolvent-based formulation that retains couplings within the external space. By exploiting the factorized structure of the stabilizer-constrained reference state, the required matrix elements can be evaluated through Pauli expectation values on the reduced contextual register without explicitly reconstructing the full-space wave function. Molecular benchmarks demonstrate substantial reductions in projection-induced energy errors, allowing chemical precision to be achieved with fewer contextual qubits in several cases. These results establish stabilizer-guided perturbation theory as a promising strategy for improving the accuracy of resource-efficient quantum chemistry calculations.

authors.name: Qianjun Yao, Jie Liu, He Li

papers.title: Swift Heavy Ion Tracks in Polymorphs of Titanium Dioxide: The Effects of Electron Beam and Crystal Structures
papers.summary: Swift heavy ion (SHI) irradiation generates nanoscale damage in materials, offering opportunities for controlled modification of structural properties. Understanding the fundamental processes governing damage formation in altered regions remains a longstanding challenge. This work explores how crystal structure influences swift heavy ion-induced damage formation and evolution in rutile and anatase TiO2. Combining transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate how differences in atomic arrangement govern track morphology and structural recovery. Although irradiation produces amorphous tracks in both polymorphs, their morphologies differ considerably. In rutile, tracks develop pronounced diameter variations, forming hourglass-like structures, whereas in anatase they retain a relatively uniform cylindrical shape. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that these differences arise from the distinct recrystallization behavior of the two crystal structures during rapid cooling, leading to different pathways of track evolution and recovery. Particular attention is paid to electron beam induced effects during TEM characterization, which can substantially modify the structure and apparent morphology of ion tracks. Prolonged electron beam exposure promotes the recrystallization of initially amorphous tracks and surface hillocks, accompanied by the development of Fresnel contrast. These findings highlight the importance of understanding beam-induced transformations for the reliable interpretation of TEM observations of radiation-damaged materials.

authors.name: Xiaoting Jia, Lijun Xu, Ruslan A. Rymzhanov, Wenqiang Liu, Peipei Hu, Shengxia Zhang, Jiande Liu, Jian Zeng, Jie Liu, Pengfei Zhai

papers.title: Observation of temporal routing of topological edge states
papers.summary: The switching or routing of topological edge states is crucial for disorder-immune state transfer. Previous experimental observations have primarily relied on optical waveguide arrays that treat the spatial coordinate as an equivalent temporal dimension. However, direct experimental observation of the routing dynamics of topological edge states in physical time remains challenging. Here, we report the experimental observation of temporal routing of topological edge states. By constructing a lattice composed of two coupled nonlinear Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains, the topological edge states exhibit temporal routing behavior controlled by nonlinearity. As the excitation voltage increases from the linear regime, we observe that the voltage intensity distribution transitions from periodic interchain exchange to slowed interchain exchange and ultimately to localization with strongly suppressed interchain exchange, thereby validating the phenomenon of temporal routing. These dynamics are experimentally observed within a finite time window limited by circuit dissipation. Our findings provide valuable insights into the temporal manipulation of topological edge states.

authors.name: Letian Xu, Muhammad Imran, Yongtao Jia, Ying Liu, Huibin Tao, Rujiang Li

papers.title: Orbital differentiation in a rare earth ion near half filling
papers.summary: In the electronic structure of rare earth ions, details can be crucial for understanding the origin of correlated states. Currently, state-of-the-art wavefunction-based methods (e.g. CASSCF) can capture single-ion properties of molecular magnets and some band insulating systems, but are expensive to perform, and cannot be applied to metallic systems. Here, we carry out full multiplet calculations for SmN with the cubic rock-salt structure using the crystal field software Quanty. The calculated experimental observables from our model agree precisely with magnetic susceptibility and inelastic neutron scattering experiments, and the spatially resolved spin density also agrees with DFT predictions. By tuning the crystal field parameters, our full multiplet-derived wavefunctions reveal the presence of orbital differentiation of the ground $J=\frac{5}{2}$ manifold into two groups, which are distinct subspaces with different orbital stiffness. This violation of Hund's rule, observed with a fast and inexpensive calculation tool, represents a step forward for microscopic models of rare earth materials, and may provide support for the claim of unconventional triplet superconductivity in SmN.

authors.name: D. W. Tam, {\O}. S. Fjellv{\aa}g, B. Gonano, E. X. M. Trewick, M. M{\aa}nsson

papers.title: A branchless single-precision Voigt approximation for spectral synthesis
papers.summary: The Voigt function is evaluated repeatedly in spectral synthesis, and several widely used implementations carry an absolute error floor. We construct QLG, a family of branchless, single-precision approximations, separable in the damping parameter $a$. QLG is named for its three ingredients: Lorentzian and Gaussian generators $L$ and $G$, and an envelope $q$ that multiplies every fitted correction and vanishes at both endpoints. The leading Lorentzian wing amplitude is fixed analytically. Three members reach observed maximum full-profile relative errors of $6.5\times10^{-3}$, $9.2\times10^{-4}$, and $7\times10^{-5}$ over $a\in[10^{-9},10^{9}]$ and $|v|\le10^{5}$. Extended-domain and randomized checks support these error levels. For the tested SIU, MOOG, and Humlicek w4 implementations, the relative error instead approaches 100% towards small values of the damping parameter. We compare synthesis-weighted costs on an Apple M1 and an AMD EPYC 9554 using gfortran 15, and propagate errors through solar-dwarf, red-supergiant, and M-dwarf syntheses. The least expensive member costs 0.98-1.05 times as much as the tabulated Synspec kernel on the M1 and 1.11-1.20 times as much on the EPYC, with a maximum flux error smaller by a factor of 3.6. The intermediate member costs less than every tested arithmetic kernel and holds the flux error below $10^{-3}$. The most accurate member costs 1.6-3.0 times less than w4 and gives 3.4-5.0 times smaller maximum flux errors in the tested syntheses.

authors.name: Richard Hoppe

papers.title: Burgers vectors from Voronoi topology
papers.summary: Automated dislocation analysis is standard in atomistic simulations, yet current tools are limited to a handful of crystal structures. We introduce an algorithm without adjustable parameters, based on Voronoi topology, that identifies dislocations in a broad class of crystals. Each face shared by two cells that match the ideal crystal is taken as a step in it, and summing these steps around closed circuits of such cells yields exact Burgers vectors, without geometric templates. Tested on dislocations inserted into all 9,610 Materials Project structures whose Voronoi cells are stable with a wide margin, the algorithm finds every dislocation with its correct Burgers vector. In raw molecular-dynamics snapshots, including eleven dislocation types in $\theta$-Al$_2$Cu and bcc iron up to its melting point, every Burgers vector it returns is correct, although near melting the dislocations merge into one cluster. Voronoi topology thus provides a natural language in which a crystal, its defects, and their Burgers vectors are all described.

authors.name: Emanuel A. Lazar

papers.title: Targeted material doping to enable the formation and coherent propagation of Laser Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LIPSS): the ZnO paradigm
papers.summary: This work explores how the initial free carrier density governs the formation and coherent propagation of Low Spatial Frequency Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LSF-LIPSS). As a paradigm we have analyzed the behavior of ad-hoc-doped ZnO films. ZnO is a multifunctional Transparent Conducting Oxide (TCO) with many scientific and technologic uses including applications in biomedicine, photonics, sensing or photocatalysis. Many of them would benefit from the use of large area, electrically anisotropic surfaces. By introducing small amounts of Yb3+ as donor dopant in ZnO films grown by Pulse Laser Deposition (PLD), we have substantially improved its carrier density at room temperature (RT) and its electrical conductivity while preserving the functional properties of pure ZnO. For RT carrier densities ne > 1019 cm-3, coherent propagation of LSF-LIPSS has been successfully achieved upon irradiation with 350 fs laser pulses at 1030 nm at high repetition rate (500 kHz) and for laser scanning speeds well above 1 m/s. However, the ablation mechanism (ZnO sublimation at the LIPSS valleys) and the large melting temperature of ZnO, make the thermal conductivity of the substrate, the film thickness and the irradiation pulse duration to play a crucial role in determining the morphology of the LSF-LIPPS propagated over large areas, especially in avoiding film cracking. The results achieved upon optimization fully confirm the role of free carrier density in the large-scale propagation of high quality LSF-LIPSS in doped ZnO and enable using these structures to easily generate large electrical anisotropies over macroscopic regions with conductivities along the LIPSS several times larger than transversally.

authors.name: Gonzalo Gomez-Munoz, Rocio Ariza, Juan Francisco Ramos-Justicia, Fatima Cabello Pardos, Antonio Pablo P\'erez-Mar\'in, Jose Gonzalo, Bel\'en Sotillo, Binbing Xia, Paloma Fernandez, Javier Solis

papers.title: Magnetic Flux Eruptions in Magnetically Arrested Disks: Magnetic Reconnection and Bubble Expansion
papers.summary: Using a high-resolution GRMHD simulation of a magnetically arrested disk, we investigate the physical mechanism driving magnetic-flux eruption. The horizon-threading magnetic flux declines mainly in off-equatorial regions, whereas localized hot spots associated with magnetic reconnection appear near the equatorial plane around the onset of flux decline. A non-axisymmetric, magnetically supported low-density structure, which we identify as a magnetic bubble, expands radially and azimuthally within a pre-existing low-density channel in the filamentary accretion flow. Based on these findings, we propose a physical picture linking reconnection, bubble expansion, and horizon magnetic flux decline. The reconnection occurs in the pre-existing low-density channel, and may reconfigure the field and promote bubble expansion. Magnetic-pressure gradients provide broadly distributed outward support for the expansion, while magnetic tension contributes a localized outward force near the equator. Bubble expansion may limit gas replenishment, helping to maintain the low-density region and reduce the total pressure near the equator. This pressure reduction may facilitate equatorward electromagnetic energy transport. In the simulation, the polar electromagnetic energy flux reverses from poleward to equatorward near the onset of the horizon-flux decline. The equatorward transport is concentrated in the bubble sector and carries electromagnetic energy from the off-equatorial magnetosphere to the equatorial region. This energy supply may sustain localized reconnection and plasma heating as the eruption develops.

authors.name: Guoqiang Zhang, Feng Yuan

papers.title: Altermagnetism-induced magneto-optical effects
papers.summary: Altermagnets break time-reversal symmetry despite their zero net magnetization, enabling time-reversal-odd responses while retaining the advantages of antiferromagnets. However, magneto-optical (MO) effects are not universal among altermagnets because MO effects typically arise from magnetic dipole order (ferromagnetism), which is generally absent in altermagnets. In this work, we address this limitation by establishing octupolar MO effects, which arise from magnetic octupole order through spatial dispersion. Owing to this distinct origin, octupolar MO effects do not necessarily require spin-orbit coupling even in collinear magnets and can arise without an external magnetic field in antiferromagnets where conventional MO effects are symmetry-forbidden. Such antiferromagnets include $d$-wave altermagnets such as RuO$_2$ and KV$_2$Se$_2$O, certain $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, including CrSb, as well as noncoplanar antiferromagnets such as MnTe$_2$ and pyrochlore iridates with all-in-all-out magnetic order. From an experimental perspective, octupolar MO effects can reach detectable magnitudes and offer potential for magnetic-domain imaging, as supported by numerical calculations showing $\mu$rad-scale Faraday rotation for a 100-nm-thick sample in the visible-light range and a sign reversal between opposite domains. Furthermore, octupolar MO effects are linked to an $f$-sum rule, enabling a quantitative estimate of the spin magnetic octupole moment from optical measurements. These results extend the scope of MO effects to a broad class of antiferromagnets, including altermagnets, and open a field-free optical route to exploring magnetic octupole order.

authors.name: Jun \=Oik\'{e}, Robert Peters, Koki Shinada

papers.title: Molecular energies from sparse quantum prolate diagonalization on a trapped-ion quantum processor
papers.summary: We introduce sparse quantum prolate diagonalization (sparse QPD), which combines the original formulation of QPD [Phys. Rev. Res., 8(3), 033177, (2026)] with compressed sensing to exploit Hamiltonian spectrum sparsity for molecular systems. We show that sparse sampling reduces the sample complexity of QPD from $\mathcal{O}(N_s)$ to $\mathcal{O}(\log N_s)$, where $N_s$ is the number of sampled points of the autocorrelation function (i.e.\ distinct circuits), without increasing circuit depth at chemical accuracy. With a two-orbital active-space-embedded Hamiltonian for an interacting arginine--tryptophan residue pair in water as an example, we show that on the Quantinuum Helios trapped-ion quantum computer, sparse QPD resolves the Hamiltonian energies to chemical accuracy with circuits of up to 448 two-qubit gates. For a suitably large quantum processor, we demonstrate numerically in the weakly correlated regime that the method extends to larger systems.

authors.name: Davide Castaldo, Marvin Kronenberger, Marek Miller, S\'el\`ene Forget, Gemma C. Solomon, Kresten Lindorff-Larsen, Matthias Christandl, Markus Reiher

papers.title: Axion electrodynamics and the advection-diffusion structure of TEM modes in hollow-conductor waveguides
papers.summary: We present a systematic investigation of transverse electromagnetic (TEM) modes in hollow-conductor waveguides filled with a dielectric medium described by axion electrodynamics. While such modes do not propagate in conventional single-conductor waveguides, the coupling of the axion field to an external magnetic field enables their propagation. We show that the resulting TEM modes are governed by an advection-diffusion-type equation for the transverse electrostatic potential, establishing a direct mathematical connection between axion electrodynamics and advection-diffusion phenomena. We illustrate this connection through explicit solutions and field profiles for cylindrical waveguides, considering uniform and rigid rotational drift fields, both individually and in combination, as well as different values of the parameter controlling the advection-to-diffusion ratio (P\'eclet number). These results establish a transport-based framework for understanding how spatial variations of the axion-electrodynamics background shape the transverse electromagnetic fields in hollow-conductor waveguides.

authors.name: Andr\'e H. Gomes

papers.title: Mechanically induced self-propagating reactions within the realm of mechanochemistry: Fundamentals, overview, in situ monitoring and perspectives
papers.summary: Mechanically induced self-propagating reaction (MSR) represents a promising but rather underexplored phenomenon within mechanochemistry, a solvent-free alternative to classical solution-based chemistry. In contrast to the gradual mechanochemical reactions, MSRs are sub-second combustive-like processes bringing about substantial benefits such as faster product formation, time efficiency, and lower energy consumption. Despite the fact that the mechanochemical field is in the research spotlight, MSR investigation remains on the periphery. This review aims to catalyze a renaissance in MSR fundamentals investigation by reviewing the current state-of-the-art. This is done via systematically reviewing the reaction systems that were reported to react via a MSR in the past twenty years, such as metal-metalloid ones (carbides, borides, silicides, and carbonitrides), metal chalcogenides, metal oxides, and other specific types of reactions. A couple of case studies are briefly reviewed for each system, and the comprehensive table follows afterward. The review also revisits the factors impacting the MSR course from milling conditions and reagent's properties point of view, showing either a direct or inverse relationship with MSR ignition time. The recent development in the in situ monitoring of mechanochemical reactions allowed to obtain some mechanistic insights into the MSR process, which are summarized in the last chapter.

authors.name: Imelda Octa Tampubolon, Matej Bal\'a\v{z}

papers.title: Temperature Flips the Sign of the Hydrogen Response in Nanogranular Palladium Networks
papers.summary: In nanogranular palladium networks, hydrogen uptake has two opposing effects on electrical resistance. Absorbed hydrogen scatters electrons within the particles, raising their resistance, while particle expansion narrows the gaps between them and lowers the junction resistance. Such networks are widely studied as resistive hydrogen sensors, and the sign of their net response is usually treated as a fixed property of the architecture. In networks grown by atomic layer deposition on macroporous silicon, we show that changing the operating temperature can reverse this sign at a fixed hydrogen concentration. A thermodynamic model indicates that scattering contributes less as temperature rises, allowing sub-angstroem changes in gap width to dominate. Where the two effects cancel, the network absorbs hydrogen yet gives the same reading as in hydrogen-free gas, so a leak could escape detection. Between 25 and 40 degrees Celsius, this cancellation point is predicted to rise over tenfold, crossing reported leak-alarm setpoints. At 55 degrees Celsius, the measured response stays negative but passes through a minimum, so a concentration above a setpoint can mimic one below it. Annealing at 200 degrees Celsius alters the calibration and turns the room-temperature response negative at the lowest concentration tested. Quantitative sensing therefore requires a defined thermal pretreatment and an operating temperature giving distinct signals across the intended concentration range. Response polarity becomes an operating parameter rather than a fixed property. More broadly, any nanoparticle network whose particles deform on sorption may show the same temperature-dependent competition between transport within and between particles, with implications for sensors and switches beyond palladium-hydrogen.

authors.name: Niclas Alkazaz, Robert Zierold, Patrick Huber

papers.title: Sobolev theory for the inverse problem of time-dependent density functional theory on the torus
papers.summary: We show that, given a sufficiently regular time-dependent density, there exists a unique potential such that the Schr\"odinger equation with this external potential has the prescribed one-particle density. We treat densities that are twice differentiable in time and of finite Sobolev regularity in space; the resulting potentials are continuous in time and of finite Sobolev regularity in space. Our method of proof is to rewrite the problem as a nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with a loss of derivatives, which we in turn handle with a completion-of-the-square argument. This is a refinement of our recent work [Lauritsen, Lewin, and Oldenburg, arXiv:2609.08984], which handled this loss of derivatives using the Cauchy-Kovalevskaya theorem and treated analytic-in-space densities and potentials.

authors.name: Asbj{\o}rn B{\ae}kgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, Jakob Oldenburg

papers.title: Variable-length MDI QKD under source imperfections and local randomization over horizontal links
papers.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) provides security guarantees that hold despite device imperfections and finite-size effects. We address these challenges in measurement-device-independent (MDI) QKD, combining its intrinsic untrusted detection with an imperfection model for Alice's and Bob's sources via fidelity bounds. We establish variable-length general security under the Marginal-constrained Entropy Accumulation Theorem (MEAT), estimating the relevant R\'enyi entropies through conic optimization. We evaluate our model under a horizontal channel link, reporting secret keys for blocks as small as n~3x10^4 rounds under atmosphere-free conditions, and show that compensating for unequal channel attenuation through appropriately chosen transmitted amplitudes improves performance in asymmetric configurations, enabling communication distances beyond 80 km for commercial satellite systems.

authors.name: Gabriele Staffieri, Mart\'i Sales-Moragues, Carlos Pascual-Garc\'ia

papers.title: Right shape, wrong time: phase errors of ODE solvers in the flame problem
papers.summary: The flame model $y'=y^2-y^3$, $y(0)=\delta$, is a standard illustration of stiffness: for $\delta=10^{-4}$ the stiff MATLAB solvers ode23s and ode15s need only 99 and 140 steps, against 3040 for ode45. We show that these cheap solutions have the right shape at the wrong time: they place the front 29 and 329 time units early, with maximal errors 0.95 and 1.00. Because all solutions are time translates of one master profile, the global error of every numerical solution with values in $[\delta,1)$ is exactly a phase error, $y_k=y_\delta(t_k-D_k)$. For fixed-step one-step methods of order $p$ we prove $D=h^p\int_\delta^{y}g+O(h^{p+1})$ with a remainder bounded uniformly in $\delta$, so that the delay grows at most like $h\ln(1/\delta)$ for $p=1$ and stays bounded for $p\geq2$. For any computed solution the delay is exactly the sum of its defects with respect to the exact flow, converted into time; a heuristic model, confirmed by MATLAB runs, explains why it is created in the first few steps and why tightening the tolerances is an expensive cure. Integrating for $1/y$, which runs like a clock in the slow phase, with an absolute tolerance reduces the error by several orders of magnitude, at a median cost close to that of the standard formulation. The mechanism needs only that the equation is autonomous; its general form is the subject of a companion paper.

authors.name: Imre Boros

papers.title: Spin and Orbital Angular Momentum Textures at Chiral Molecule-Metal Interfaces
papers.summary: Chiral molecular adsorption can modify the spin and orbital character of metal surface states, providing an electronic-structure basis for interpreting spin-dependent interfacial phenomena. Using first-principles calculations with spin-orbit coupling, band unfolding, and an atom-projected orbital angular momentum (OAM) analysis, we investigate spin and OAM textures at chiral heptahelicene/Au(111) interfaces and compare them with clean Au (111) and an achiral coronene/Au system. Adsorption changes the orientations of the spin and OAM vectors and reduces the sampled OAM magnitudes of Au-derived surface states near the Fermi level. The two heptahelicene enantiomers exhibit textures related by mirror and time-reversal symmetries, whereas the comparison with coronene identifies changes that also occur without molecular chirality. These results clarify how molecular adsorption modifies interfacial spin and orbital character and establish symmetry constraints relevant to chirality-dependent photoemission.

authors.name: Gyanu P. Kafle, Amos Afugu, Zhen-Fei Liu

papers.title: Frequency Multiplexing of Purcell-Enhanced Optically Coherent NV Centers
papers.summary: Integrating optically coherent quantum emitters into nanophotonic structures is key to scalable quantum networks. Realizing them with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is hindered by the degradation of optical coherence accompanying nanofabrication. Here, we overcome this challenge by integrating multiple NV centers into a monolithic diamond photonic crystal nanocavity while preserving near-lifetime-limited optical coherence. We observe linewidths as narrow as 19 MHz, enabling the frequency multiplexing of spectrally distinct NV centers within a common cavity mode, while maintaining charge-state stability over several minutes under resonant excitation. Tuning the cavity into resonance with the NV zero-phonon line enhances the optical emission, consistent with Purcell enhancement predicted by finite-element simulations. Additionally, individual cavities can be independently brought into resonance with NV zero-phonon lines on the same chip. These results combine bulk-like optical coherence with frequency multiplexing and cavity-enhanced emission, establishing a scalable nanophotonic platform for NV-based quantum network nodes.

authors.name: Alok Gokhale, Marco E. Stucki, Malo Bezard, Maarten H. van der Hoeven, Kilian Unterguggenberger, Gregor Pieplow, Tommaso Pregnolato, Julian M. Bopp, Laura Orphal-Kobin, Tim Schr\"oder

papers.title: An Efficient Method for Directly Integrating the Vlasov Equation in Collisionless and Weakly-Collisional Simulations
papers.summary: We describe and test a new numerical method to solve the Vlasov/Boltzmann equation in systems with arbitrary levels of collisionality. The method combines recent ideas to evolve the distribution function (DF) directly in 6+1 dimensional phase-space in a manner which is Lagrangian in both position+velocity. The 'particles' of traditional Monte-Carlo/Particle-In-Cell/N-body (MC/PIC/NB) methods become mesh-generating points defining a volume partition, each of which carries a set of momentum-Lagrangian basis functions representing a local anisotropic momentum DF. The DF is then integrated between cells and bases via a higher-order reconstruction and Godunov-type method, evolving a 10 or 13-moment representation of each basis to ensure manifest mass/momentum/energy conservation. The method allows one to represent arbitrary DFs, including multiple independent streams but also collisional or phase-mixed or thermal distributions (unlike traditional 'moments' or waterbag/tessellation methods), and the cost is bounded to a modest multiplier of MC/PIC/NB costs. We provide an example implementation which uses a spatially-Lagrangian volume partition, second-order reconstruction, and simple set of bases which ensure constant cell masses and couple directly to existing MC/PIC/NB machinery, made public in the code GIZMO. We validate in a series of test problems, demonstrating manifest conservation, Galilean and translation and rotation invariance, and ability to represent complex DFs without spurious dissipation or instability. We discuss applications where this method can have advantages compared to traditional algorithms for simulations of dark matter, stellar, weakly-collisional neutral gas, and particulate/dust dynamics; multiphase/polydisperse flows; cosmic ray and radiation transport/hydrodynamics; and plasma physics.

authors.name: Philip F. Hopkins

papers.title: Memory kernel and closure for systems driven by intermittent forcing with power-law waiting times
papers.summary: Many systems are controlled by intermittent control variables that take on a random value for a random time interval. In the presence of such noise at update steps, the main equation for the controlled variables has a memory kernel whose coefficients are the cumulants, also known as $G$-cumulants, of the noise, which are fully ordered in time. In the case of Poisson switching, these correspond to the Boolean cumulants of the jump distribution, and the kernel can be summed exactly. We derive an exact decomposition of these coefficients for any waiting-time distribution with independent amplitudes and durations, which separates the jump statistics from the renewal statistics. In the case of waiting times that follow a power-law distribution with a finite mean, it is highly probable that a long time interval will be covered by a single period, and we have shown that, as a result, the coefficients for long delays intersect in all orders, from Boolean cumulants to the usual moments of the jump law. The long-lag kernel thus becomes a superposition of frozen deterministic flux kernels, weighted by the expression $\xi^2p(\xi)$, and from this the corresponding main equation in closed form follows. For $2<\mu<3$, where the noise correlation time is infinite, the second-order closure retains a finite error even in the presence of slow dynamics, whereas the main equation of the frozen flows in this limit yields an exact stationary mean value. The telegraphic process is the only case of noise with renewal steps for which second-order conclusions are exact. An exactly solvable model with additive and correlated multiplicative noise confirms these predictions.

authors.name: Marco Bianucci, Riccardo Mannella

papers.title: Spontaneous axis formation through defect fusion in active nematics
papers.summary: Initially spherical embryos break symmetry to establish a body axis. Topological defects in tissue nematic order have been implicated in axis formation, but the physical mechanisms underlying defect organization in active materials remain unclear. We study an active nematic fluid on a sphere using a fully covariant hydrodynamic theory that ensures thermodynamic consistency in the passive limit. We find that, in compressible systems, active nematic traction drives a spontaneous transition from the equilibrium configuration of four separated +1/2 defects to two antipodal +1 defects through pairwise fusion. The resulting state defines an axis, with aster or vortex textures at the poles depending on the flow-nematic coupling. These results identify a physical mechanism by which active forces reorganize topological defects to establish an axis on a spherical surface.

authors.name: Mathieu Dedenon, Claire A. Dessalles, Aur\'elien Roux, Karsten Kruse

papers.title: Causality, determinism and predictability: Probing nature through classical and quantum eyes
papers.summary: In this article, mainly focussed on students and interested readers, we discuss how the understanding of causality, determinism and predictability is transformed as we move from the classical world view to the quantum description. We first explain how determinism and predictability operate in classical dynamics and outline the notion of causality. A paradigm shift occurs within the framework of quantum mechanics where we have to revisit, and even give up, the notions of determinism, predictability and maybe even strict causality. An engrossing and fascinating debate ensues, after the formulation of quantum mechanics among the giants of physics like Einstein, Bohr, Heisenberg, Pauli, and many others. While some questions have been settled in the last century in favour of quantum world view, there are still many open questions, most important of which is the role of gravity in shaping events within the quantum framework.

authors.name: Mundur V N Murthy, Usha Devi A R

papers.title: Quantum amplification with a linear quantum coupler
papers.summary: Josephson parametric amplifiers (JPAs) are essential components for quantum-limited microwave measurement, but their dynamic range is often constrained by Kerr and other pump-induced nonlinear effects. In this work, we systematically study the performance of a parametric amplifier based on the linear inductive coupler (LINC). Starting from the driven-circuit Hamiltonian, we derive the effective three-wave-mixing amplifier model, including leading flux-driven nonlinear corrections relevant to realistic operation. We analyze the resulting gain response, saturation behavior, and intermodulation distortion, comparing them with representative state-of-the-art JPA designs. Our results show that the symmetry-protected structure of the LINC suppresses static Kerr nonlinearity. Moreover, suitable circuit-parameter optimization can further reduce the dressed-squeezing and driven-Kerr effects, leading to considerable improvements in power-handling metrics. These results identify the LINC architecture as a promising platform for high-linearity Josephson parametric amplification.

authors.name: Changqing Wang, Yao Lu

papers.title: Performance analysis of a Rydberg atom THz radiometer concept
papers.summary: THz receiver technology lies between electronics and photonics; as such, its implementation is not as mature. This warrants investigation into alternative THz receivers such as Rydberg atom sensors, which are highly susceptible to electric fields. In particular, the conversion architecture has been demonstrated to coherently transduce thermal radiation. This system offers room-temperature operation and does not necessarily require a local oscillator at the frequency of the input signal. We provide an assessment of the feasibility of such sensors for THz radiometry within the context of Earth observation.

authors.name: Richard J. Murchie, Petronilo Martin-Iglesias, Julian Hofmann, Christophe Buisset

papers.title: Terahertz emission from $\alpha$-W/CoFe epitaxial spintronic emitters
papers.summary: We report efficient terahertz (THz) generation in epitaxial $\alpha$-W/Co$_{60}$Fe$_{40}$ spintronic emitters. Two types of emitters have been investigated; epitaxial $\alpha$-W$(110)$/Co$_{60}$Fe$_{40}(110)$ and $\alpha$-W$(001)$/Co$_{60}$Fe$_{40}(001)$ deposited on single crystalline Al$_{2}$O$_{3}$($11\bar{2}0$) and MgO($001$) substrates, respectively. First principle calculations of the electronic band structure at the W$(001)$ surface reveal Dirac-type surface states, similar to that reported previously for the W$(110)$ surface. The generated THz radiation is about $10\%$ larger for $\alpha$-W$(110)$/Co$_{60}$Fe$_{40}(110)$ grown on single crystalline Al$_{2}$O$_{3}$($11\bar{2}0$), which is explained by the fact that the $\alpha$-W$(110)$/Co$_{60}$Fe$_{40}(110)$ interface for this emitter is more transparent to the spin current due to the presence of \AA ngstr\" om-scale interface intermixing at the W/CoFe interface. Our results also reveal that the generation of THz radiation is larger when pumping with the laser light from the substrate side, which is explained by a larger part of the laser light due to interference effects in the film stack being absorbed in the ferromagnetic Co$_{60}$Fe$_{40}$ layer in this measurement configuration.

authors.name: Venkatesh Mottamchetty, Rimantas Brucas, Anna L. Ravensburg, Renan Maciel, Danny Thonig, Jurgen Henk, Rahul Gupta, Arne Roos, Cheuk Wai Tai, Vassilios Kapaklis, Peter Svedlindh

papers.title: Topological Control of Polaritonic Flatbands in Anisotropic van der Waals Metasurfaces
papers.summary: Anisotropic van der Waals (vdW) materials exhibit direction-dependent optical and electronic properties, making them valuable for tailoring directional light-matter interactions. Rhenium disulfide (ReS$_2$) stands out for its strong in-plane anisotropy and its thickness-independent direct-bandgap excitons, which can hybridize with light to form exciton-polaritons. In parallel, metasurfaces, engineered arrays of nanoscale subwavelength resonators, can support ultra-sharp photonic modes in the form of quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs). Topological transformations of photonic modes can give rise to flatbands, i.e., dispersionless states with quenched kinetic energy and vanishing group velocity. Intrinsic material anisotropy offers an unexplored route to robust far-field flatband formation and control. Here, we demonstrate how structuring an intrinsically anisotropic excitonic material into a resonant metasurface fundamentally transforms its photonic topological features and light-matter coupling behavior, allowing us to drive and topologically control extended far-field flatband formation. To this end, we fabricate C$_4$-symmetric metasurfaces directly from bulk ReS$_2$. The intrinsic anisotropy lifts the initial double degeneracy of the qBIC mode and yields two distinctly polarized resonances. It also reshapes the topological landscape: the integer topological charge of the qBIC mode splits into momentum-separated half-integer singularities, thereby flattening the far-field photonic dispersion. The resulting topologically-controlled photonic flatbands are then tuned in resonance with the linearly polarized excitonic transitions of ReS$_2$, resulting in two distinct, directionally hybridized exciton-polariton flatband regimes. These findings establish anisotropic vdW metasurfaces as a new platform for topologically engineered flatbands and flatband-driven light-matter coupling.

authors.name: Connor Heimig, Thomas Weber, Cristina Cruciano, Armando Genco, Thomas Possmayer, Luca Sortino, Gianluca Valentini, Cristian Manzoni, Maxim V. Gorkunov, Giulio Cerullo, Alexander A. Antonov, Andreas Tittl

papers.title: Energy calibration of bulk events in the BULLKID detector
papers.summary: BULLKID is a cryogenic, solid-state detector designed for direct searches of particle Dark Matter candidates, with mass $\lesssim 1$ GeV/c$^2$, and coherent neutrino-nucleus scattering. It is based on an array of dice carved in 5 mm thick silicon crystal, sensed by phonon-mediated Kinetic Inductance Detectors. In previous works, the array was calibrated with bursts of optical photons, which are absorbed in the first hundreds nanometers of the dice and give rise to surface events. In this work, we present the reconstruction of bulk events through the 59.5 keV $\gamma$-ray generated by an $^{241}$Am source, which emulates more closely the interaction of Dark Matter and neutrinos. The peak resolution is $5\%~(\sigma)$ and its position is shifted by less than $10\%$ with respect to the optical calibration. We observe that the resolution is further improved by a factor $2$ combining the signal from neighboring dice. These results confirm the performance of the detector in view of the physics goals of the BULLKID-DM experiment for dark matter search.

authors.name: M. Folcarelli, D. Delicato, A. Acevedo-Renter\'ia, L. E. Ardila-Perez, L. Bandiera, M. Calvo, M. Cappelli, R. Caravita, F. Carillo, U. Chowdhury, D. Crovo, A. Cruciani, A. D'Addabbo, M. De Lucia, G. Del Castello, M. del Gallo Roccagiovine, F. Ferraro, S. Fu, R. Gartmann, M. Grassi, V. Guidi, D. Helis, T. Lari, L. Malagutti, A. Mazzolari, A. Monfardini, T. Muscheid, D. Nicol\`o, F. Paolucci, D. Pasciuto, L. Pesce, C. Puglia, D. Quaranta, C. M. A. Roda, S. Roddaro, M. Romagnoni, G. Signorelli, F. Simon, A. Tartari, E. V\'azquez-J\'auregui, M. Vignati, K. Zhao

papers.title: Transient Signal Propagation in Heterogeneous Networks under Various Inputs
papers.summary: Transient signals in neural, biological and technological networks rarely follow a single route. Their strength and timing depend on where the input enters, on the intrinsic dynamics of each node visited, and on the feedforward and recurrent pathways that carry it. Previous theory has clarified important limits of signal propagation, but often for a single input type, averaged network structure, or asymptotic regimes. It has remained unclear how finite heterogeneous networks transform sustained, impulsive, finite-duration and stochastic inputs into node-resolved response timescales. Here, we develop a theory for network dynamics near stable operating states that answers this question. The framework identifies a canonical set of gains and timescales shared across deterministic and stochastic forcing and expresses them through matrix resolvents, spectra and directed walks. In positive, sufficiently damped networks, the walk representation gives a simple physical picture: response strength accumulates multiplicatively along a single path, whereas response time accumulates additively, through local intrinsic time constants. Competing pathways, feedback and inhibition further reshape propagation by amplifying, suppressing, reversing or delaying signals. We derive perturbative criteria that specify when these signatures, and the resulting node rankings, persist beyond the positive regime. Applied to a Wilson--Cowan model of the primate cortex, the theory links structural connectivity, excitatory--inhibitory balance and local biophysical timescales to hierarchical response timescales. Our results provide a mechanistic framework for input-dependent timescales in finite heterogeneous networks.

authors.name: Xiaoge Bao, Wei P. Dai, Jan Nagler, Wei Lin

papers.title: Statistical State Dynamics of Couette MHD Turbulence
papers.summary: The roll streak structure (RSS) is ubiquitous in shear flow turbulence and is fundamental to the dynamics of the self-sustaining process (SSP) maintaining the turbulent state. The formation and maintenance of the RSS in wall-bounded shear flow suggest the presence of an underlying instability that has recently been identified using statistical state dynamics (SSD). Due to the parallelism between the Navier-Stokes equation and the induction equation, it is reasonable to inquire whether the RSS in wall-bounded shear flow has a counterpart in the MHD equations formulated as an SSD. In this work we show that this is the case and that an analytic solution for the composite velocitymagnetic field RSS in the MHD SSD also arises from an instability, that this instability equilibrates to either a fixed point or to a turbulent state, that these turbulent statistical equilibria may be self sustaining, and that both the fixed point and the turbulent states may correspond to large scale coherent dynamos.

authors.name: Eojin Kim, Brian F. Farrell

papers.title: Electrokinetic effects on flow and ion transport in charge-patterned corrugated nanochannels
papers.summary: The phase offset between surface charge modulation and geometric undulations in a corrugated nanochannel provides a tunable mechanism for rectified, diode-like ion transport under purely pressure-driven conditions: reversing the applied pressure gradient selectively activates transport of opposite ionic species, generating a net ionic current whose sign and magnitude are set by the charge-geometry alignment. Fully coupled Poisson-Nernst-Planck-Stokes simulations reveal the underlying two-regime structure: at low driving force (Regime I), throughput is suppressed below the Poiseuille limit by a localized streaming potential that pins counterions within the electric double layer; above a threshold pressure (Regime II), the mechanical force overcomes electrostatic resistance, producing an abrupt, orders-of-magnitude rise in mean velocity. Electroosmotically driven flow undergoes a qualitatively similar but smoother transition. Peak charge selectivity is achieved at near-complete electric double layer overlap and driving forces just below the Regime I-Regime II transition. Random walk particle tracking confirms selective rectification and quantifies the dependence of ion dispersion on surface charge placement across both regimes.

authors.name: Thomas Petersen, Pouya Golchin, Jinwoo Im, Felipe P. J. de Barros

papers.title: Implementation of Girsanov Reweighting in CP2K
papers.summary: Dynamical reweighting of path measures is a powerful approach for accurately evaluating slow molecular processes using modified potential energy surfaces used in enhanced sampling methods. Integrating this reweighting framework into the CP2K electronic-structure and molecular-dynamics (MD) software package delivers a robust and widely applicable tool for metadynamics, uncertainty quantification, and force-field optimisation based on both \textit{ab initio} and classical MD simulations. Based on the Girsanov theorem for stochastic dynamical systems, the method is adapted to the Bussi-Donadio-Parrinello velocity-rescaling scheme. This scheme is accessible through the CSVR thermostat and can be interpreted as a Langevin OVRVO/OBABO update scheme requiring two random numbers per integration step. Comprehensive implementation details are provided, including a complete overview of the modified CP2K modules involved in the MD cycle and the computation of reweighting factors. The framework supports multiple sources of bias potentials, enabling reweighting via the PLUMED interface or CP2K-native external potentials and restraints. The feasibility of the implementation is demonstrated through rerun benchmarks, dynamical reweighting of Markov state models (MSMs) and computation of transport properties based on CP2K trajectories, showing excellent agreement with reference simulations.

authors.name: Sascha J\"ahnigen, Bettina G. Keller

papers.title: Exploration stabilizes learning dynamics and promotes cooperation in stochastic games
papers.summary: Understanding and stabilizing collective learning dynamics is a central challenge in stochastic games. Although exploration is widely used in learning algorithms, its effects on the coupled dynamics of agents and their environment remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we derive analytical equations for entropy-regularized actor-critic learning in stochastic games by separating the timescales of value estimation and policy adaptation. Without exploration, the system preserves a weighted volume in the policy phase space, ruling out asymptotically stable fully mixed equilibria. We provide a unified characterization of exploration's effects on objective curvature, preference dynamics in log-ratio coordinates, and the forgetting of past action preferences. Exploration reduces local volume expansion and can stabilize learning dynamics. In a two-state Matching Pennies game, it suppresses chaotic learning and promotes convergence to a mixed equilibrium. In a Prisoner's Dilemma with environmental feedback, intermediate exploration eliminates the defective attractor and expands the basin of attraction of the cooperative equilibrium. Our findings reveal how exploration shapes collective behavior, informing the design of cooperative and resilient multi-agent systems.

authors.name: Yuxin Geng, Xingru Chen, Wolfram Barfuss, Longzhao Liu, Xin Wang, Shaoting Tang, Feng Fu

papers.title: Measurement and Modeling of Structure-Induced Surface Scattering on Terahertz Channel
papers.summary: As terahertz (THz) frequencies emerge as promising candidates for next-generation wireless networks, accurate characterization of propagation mechanisms in indoor/outdoor environments becomes essential for system design and performance optimization. This article presents an experimental and theoretical investigation of structure-induced indoor surface scattering on THz channels, examining how material properties and structural configurations jointly govern channel power and angular distribution. Six representative indoor surfaces are characterized, revealing that intrinsic structural inhomogeneity - particularly the quasi-periodic earlywood-latewood arrangement in pine wood - induces measurable angular scattering whose dominant lobes and angular shifts are reproduced by a beam-propagation modeling (BPM) framework. Material-covered surface configurations are further investigated, demonstrating that thin dielectric covering layers can substantially modify reflection characteristics through thickness- and frequency- dependent thin-film interference effects. Wide-angle bistatic measurements in a conference room show that folded curtains broaden the measured angular distribution of detectable received power. These findings suggest that structure-induced surface scattering mechanisms may provide scattering-assisted propagation opportunities for indoor non-line-of-sight THz scenarios.

authors.name: Peian Li, Yapeng Ge, Jiacheng Liu, Wenbo Liu, Jiayuan Cui, Jiabiao Zhao, Qiang Niu, Yuping Yang, Xiangzhu Meng, Yiming Zhao, Jianjun Ma

papers.title: Improved Pion-Kaon Identification in Heavy-Ion Collisions with a Two-Dimensional Transformation
papers.summary: Accurate identification of charged pions and kaons is essential for precision measurements in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, but becomes increasingly challenging at intermediate and high transverse momentum because of the increasing overlap of the TPC and TOF particle identification responses. In this work, we quantitatively benchmark a two-dimensional shift-and-rotation PID procedure that combines the $n\sigma_{\pi}$ and mass-squared $(m^{2})$ information. The benchmark is performed using Au+Au collision events generated with the AMPT model, where the detector response is modeled using $p_{T}$-dependent PID parameters extracted from STAR data. Since the true particle identities and input yields are known in AMPT but are not used during the reconstruction, the procedure can be evaluated through a direct closure test that is not possible with experimental data alone. The two-dimensional procedure is compared with a reference one-dimensional method consisting of an $|n\sigma_{\pi}|<$ 3 preselection followed by a Gaussian fit to the $m^{2}$ distribution. While both methods perform well when pion and kaon PID responses are well separated, the two-dimensional procedure provides improved yield closure as the PID distributions increasingly overlap at high $p_{T}$. The reconstructed-to-input yield ratio remains within 2\% of unity up to $p_T =$ 3 GeV/$c$, whereas the reference one-dimensional procedure shows a larger deviation. Reaction-plane $v_{2}$ closure tests show that both the reference one-dimensional and two-dimensional PID procedures reproduce the AMPT input $v_{2}$ within the statistical uncertainties over the studied $p_{T}$ range. These results demonstrate that the two-dimensional procedure substantially improves the high-$p_{T}$ yield reconstruction without introducing a detectable bias in the extracted $v_{2}$ under the STAR-like detector response considered here.

authors.name: Shaowei Lan, Bijun Fan, Like Liu

papers.title: System Size Dependence of Collisionless Reconnection Rate
papers.summary: It is a widely accepted paradigm that collisionless magnetic reconnection proceeds at a universal fast rate of $\sim0.1$ when normalized to a properly defined reconnecting magnetic field and Alfv\'en speed, effectively independent of the macroscopic system size. This conclusion, derived primarily from kinetic simulations of classical Harris current sheets with kinetic-scale thickness, stands in contrast to results from forced reconnection and island coalescence, where the rate significantly depends on the system size. Here, we reconcile this disparity by performing a rigorous scaling study of Harris sheets using both particle-in-cell and Hall magnetohydrodynamic simulations. We demonstrate that when the global magnetic configuration is preserved by scaling the initial current sheet thickness proportionally with the system size, the ``universal'' fast rate disappears. Instead, the reconnection rate decreases as the system size increases. By establishing a consistent scaling trend across different magnetic configurations, these findings challenge the paradigm of scale-independent fast reconnection and necessitate a reevaluation of energy release rates in astrophysical plasmas.

authors.name: Yi-Min Huang, Naoki Bessho, Li-Jen Chen, Judith T. Karpen, Amitava Bhattacharjee

papers.title: Data-driven reconstruction of band dispersion and quantum geometry via Koopman dynamic mode decomposition
papers.summary: We present a data-driven framework for reconstructing band structures using Koopman operator analysis and dynamic mode decomposition (Koopman-DMD). Instead of deriving spectra from an explicit Hamiltonian, the approach reconstructs band dispersion and modal dynamics directly from spatiotemporal data, including wavefunctions and observables. This framework establishes a correspondence between Hamiltonian Floquet-Bloch decomposition and Koopman-DMD, whereby the extracted DMD modes encode frequencies, decay or growth rates, spatial profiles and projection weights. These quantities allow the reconstruction of spectral functions, local density of states, and delocalized-to-localized measures such as the inverse participation ratio. Also, these extended DMD modes enable inference of quantum-geometric and topological properties, including the quantum metric, Berry curvature and geometric phases. Applications to prototypical one- and two-dimensional tight-binding models, including disordered Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model and its Floquet and non-Hermitian variants, graphene and Haldane models, demonstrate that Koopman-DMD provides a unified route for the data-driven analysis of wave propagation, localization, and topological phases in condensed matter, photonics, and related fields.

authors.name: Yiming Pan, Jinze He, Jiapeng Yang, Zhiwei Fan

papers.title: Unexpected Marangoni Condensation in Negative Binary Mixtures
papers.summary: Marangoni condensation - where surface tension gradients induce instabilities that lead to condensate film breakup into discrete droplets - has traditionally been considered limited to positive binary mixtures, where the less volatile component has higher surface tension. Negative mixtures were expected to exhibit stable filmwise condensation. Here, we demonstrate unexpected spontaneous Marangoni-driven pseudo-dropwise condensation in negative water-ethylene glycol and water-triethylene glycol mixtures. Strong thermo-diffusion in these dilute mixtures enables preferential glycol enrichment in colder condensate film regions during condensation, generating surface tension gradients that trigger film breakup, leading to greater than 6x wettability-independent heat transfer enhancement compared to filmwise condensation at moderate subcooling. Our work challenges the conventional framework that restricts Marangoni condensation to positive mixtures; a superficial classification that oversimplifies the underlying interfacial mechanisms that can trigger robust Marangoni condensation, offering new pathways for enhancing phase change heat transfer in industrial applications without the need for expensive and degradation-prone surface coatings.

authors.name: Abenezer Abere, Patricia B. Weisensee

papers.title: Soft Mobility Theory
papers.summary: Predicting how a deformable body moves and deforms in a viscous flow underlies problems ranging from microorganism locomotion to soft microrobotics, yet existing frameworks are either problem-specific or ill-suited to inverse design. We propose a soft mobility theory. Applying the principle of virtual power to an assembly of hydrodynamically interacting spheres connected by springs and rods yields a saddle-point problem, whose explicit solution is a configuration-dependent ordinary differential equation for the generalized coordinates of the body. This soft mobility equation extends classical rigid-body mobility theory in that the elastic, body-force, and flow-coupling tensors all depend explicitly on the instantaneous deformation. It is not restricted to sphere assemblies: the same equation follows from the continuum problem of a hyperelastic body in a background Stokes flow, of which the assembly is a Galerkin restriction. We compute the mobility from the Rotne-Prager-Yamakawa approximation and validate the framework on canonical problems spanning rigid and flexible bodies in quiescent and shear flows. An open-source JAX implementation makes entire simulations end-to-end differentiable. This allows efficient gradient-based inverse design: as proofs of concept, we recover the asymptotic optimum of a three-sphere swimmer and design a soft gyrotactic "surfer" that exploits passive deformation to ascend faster than its rigid counterpart in a Taylor-Green flow.

authors.name: Christophe Eloy

papers.title: Students' Validation Criteria for AI-Generated Physics Solutions
papers.summary: A physics solution can be clear without being valid. This distinction becomes important when students read AI-generated solutions that appear coherent but still require physical and mathematical checking. We examined how pre-service physics teachers in a calculus-based introductory electromagnetism course evaluated AI-generated solutions to a charged-rod electric-field problem after attempting the problem themselves. Although the AI-generated solutions analyzed were correct, no student accepted a response as valid after a first reading. Students who had solved the problem fully or in part could examine the responses using physical and mathematical criteria, while others withheld acceptance because they could not follow the mathematical development. These results suggest that, in physics instruction, AI-generated solutions should be treated less as answers to be accepted or rejected and more as worked-out responses that students learn to reconstruct, question, and test.

authors.name: \'Alvaro Su\'arez, Richard Gonz\'alez

papers.title: Terahertz Generation through Photon Deceleration of Long-Wavelength Infrared Laser Pulses in Plasma
papers.summary: Efficient terahertz (THz) generation with high field amplitude and pulse energy is studied through the interaction of a single-color long-wavelength infrared (LWIR) laser pulse with gaseous targets. Particle-In-Cell (PIC) simulations are performed to investigate the underlying mechanism and analyze the properties of the emitted THz radiation. The results reveal that THz pulses at frequencies below 10 THz are generated via photon deceleration of the LWIR laser, driven by enhanced electron density accumulation at the pulse front in the self-modulated wakefield regime. The influence of key parameters, including target density, laser intensity, and propagation length, on nonlinear laser modulation and the resulting THz generation efficiency is analyzed. Important scalings governing the laser-to-THz energy conversion efficiency are identified from PIC simulations and validated through theoretical analysis. The study demonstrates a laser-to-THz energy conversion efficiency of approximately $4\%$, significantly exceeding previously reported values. For the laser parameters considered in this study, the energy of the emitted THz pulses is approximately 50 mJ. The findings of this study provide valuable insights for the development of next-generation high-energy THz sources.

authors.name: Srimanta Maity

papers.title: Reconstructing the Probability Measure of a Multi-group Curie-Weiss Model with Interacting Groups
papers.summary: We study the problem of reconstructing the probability measure of a multi-group version of the Curie-Weiss or mean-field model of ferromagnetism from a sample of the voting behaviour of the population. While originally used to study phase transitions in statistical mechanics, the Curie-Weiss model has been applied to study phenomena where many agents interact with each other, in particular in case of a heterogeneous population with identifiable subpopulations. The degree of social cohesion within social groups manifests in the way the members of the group influence each others' decisions as well as how they behave under outside influence from voters belonging to another group. While the maximum likelihood estimator of the coupling parameters has desirable statistical properties in theory, computational challenges make applications to larger populations impractical. Therefore, we analyse an estimator based on asymptotic approximations to the behaviour of the Curie-Weiss model valid for large populations. Due to the wide application of models such as Curie-Weiss, the estimator is potentially useful in disciplines such as political science, sociology, automated voting, and preference aggregation.

authors.name: Miguel Ballesteros, Gerardo Franco Cordova, Fedro Guillen, Gabor Toth

papers.title: One dimensional high-order moment models with realistic collisions for nonequilibrium ion transport in weakly ionized plasmas
papers.summary: Ion-neutral collisions are fundamental in the transport of partially ionized plasmas. When collisional scales are comparable to the system scales or the electric field is strong, nonequilibrium conditions for the ions arise that are beyond classical transport models due to large drifts, strong heat flux, and temperature anisotropy. In this paper, we propose the resolution of non-linear high-order moment closures for simulating nonequilibrium ion dynamics in one-dimensional weakly ionized plasmas. We compare a four-moment anisotropic Maxwellian model (mass, axial momentum, and axial and perpendicular energies), a five-moment hyperbolic quadrature-based model (first five axial moments), and a novel six-moment hyperbolic quadrature-based model (first five axial moments + perpendicular energy). We derive analytical collision source terms from the Boltzmann operator for ion-neutral scattering with arbitrary differential cross sections. This formulation generalizes the Chapman-Cowling theory for arbitrary drift velocities, temperature anisotropies, and heat flux, ensuring strictly realizable distributions. The models are validated via non-linear simulations benchmarked against kinetic solutions for argon plasmas with realistic cross sections (0.05-500 mTorr). We test a bounded plasma between floating walls and a direct-current discharge. The six-moment model robustly captures ion dynamics, particularly under strong nonequilibrium, where anisotropy and heat flux are non-local. It reconstructs the distribution function with high fidelity, without noise, and at a cost comparable to fluid models in a self-consistent manner.

authors.name: Anatole Berger, Alejandro Alvarez Laguna

papers.title: Predictive beam-lattice reduction for higher-order topological modes in a 2D SSH phononic crystal
papers.summary: We develop a mechanically faithful reduced model for a two-dimensional topological phononic crystal composed of rigid square masses connected by slender elastic ligaments. Exploiting Euler Bernoulli beam theory, we derive a Hermitian 12 degree of freedom dynamical matrix that retains in-plane translations, rotations, and ligament eccentricity. This reduction captures effects that are absent from scalar mass spring SSH models while remaining computationally much more tractable and more easily interpretable than full finite element simulations. Dimerizing the ligament widths produces a mechanical 2D SSH lattice with a full band gap and a quantized bulk polarization. The sign of the dimerization controls the transition from trivial to non trivial phases, while ligament eccentricity provides an additional purely geometric mechanism for changing the topology. Ribbon and finite cell calculations predict in gap edge and corner modes, quantified by localization measures and confirmed by finite element simulations. Measurements on 3D printed samples show an evanescent response in the trivial structure and enhanced boundary/corner response in the non trivial structure within the predicted gap. The results provide a validated route for designing topological elastic metamaterials using a continuum informed discrete model rather than either idealized mass spring networks or brute force numerical optimization.

authors.name: Eloi Perez Compte, Michele Brun, Giorgio Carta, Nicola M. Pugno, Antonio S. Gliozzi, Federico Bosia

papers.title: Modern aerodynamics models do not capture important unsteady forces and delays--the failure of the quasi-steady approximation
papers.summary: Aerodynamic unsteadiness is inherent to the operation of many engineering applications, especially those that involve large-scale rotating blades, such as modern wind turbines. Over the past few decades, wind turbine rotors have grown rapidly and are now exceeding 200 meters in diameter, causing them to operate in conditions where limited empirical data are available, and where models have not been validated. Here, we use a highly pressurized wind tunnel to probe these conditions and evaluate the quasi-steady approximation, often used to simplify the modeling of the unsteady aerodynamic response of an airfoil to slow changes in inflow conditions. We find that the quasi-steady approximation is not valid for a large range of frequencies where it is normally applied. This finding suggests that the loading on wind turbine blades will be significantly underestimated when using conventional models, especially near stalling conditions, which modern wind turbines typically encounter.

authors.name: Victoria M. Malarczyk, Marcus Hultmark

papers.title: Cryogenic Mechanical Loss of GaAs/AlGaAs Crystalline Coatings
papers.summary: Optical coatings with minimal thermal noise are essential for high-precision, laser-based metrology experiments. Substrate-transferred crystalline GaAs/Al$_{0.92}$Ga$_{0.08}$As coatings have the lowest thermal noise for high-reflectivity mirror coatings with $\lambda =900$ nm -- 12 $\mu$m. Time-frequency stabilization experiments have demonstrated that GaAs/AlGaAs mirror coatings have a lower noise floor than amorphous mirror coatings. These mirrors are now being developed at sizes $\ge 300$ mm for gravitational-wave detectors.
