In order to understand the coating's fundamental loss mechanisms, which cause thermal noise, we have performed the first measurement of the mechanical loss at cryogenic temperatures using a cryogenic, multimodal, gentle nodal suspension system, which operates from 12 K to room temperature. This initial measurement used a silicon substrate whose asymmetry produced excess friction with the nodal support. Accounting for this friction and Akhiezer loss in the substrate and coating, the mechanical loss agrees well with the thermal noise observed in experiments using cryogenic fixed-cavities with GaAs/AlGaAs mirrors.

authors.name: Nicholas A. Didio, Steven D. Penn, Satoshi Tanioka, Elenna M. Capote, Garrett D. Cole, Stefan W. Ballmer

papers.title: Mixture of Polyconvex Neural Potentials for Parametric Hyperelasticity: Towards Foundation Material Models
papers.summary: Hyperelastic constitutive models enable modeling large deformations in elastic solids. In common practice, a strain energy density function is prescribed in advance and model-specific parameters are calibrated from experiments. However, many applications require constitutive models for a family of related materials whose mechanical behavior varies with composition. A fixed constitutive model-form may not capture the full range of behavior across the family, while fitting separate forms does not provide a direct way to predict the response of new compositions. Recent work has developed data-driven constitutive models that learn flexible strain energy functions while incorporating key physical constraints. In this work, we propose using mixtures of convex neural potentials based on input convex neural networks as a modular and data efficient approach to modeling material families. Each potential is convex and monotonic with respect to polyconvex strain invariants, while a conditioning network maps material descriptors to mixture weights. We compare the approach with a monolithic partially input-convex neural network using experimental data from PolyJet 3D-printed materials and a synthetic Gent-type benchmark. Across both benchmarks, the mixture architecture generalized better to material descriptors not seen during training. In the PolyJet experimental benchmark, we showed that the mixture architecture is less sensitive to model hyperparameters, while in the Gent-type benchmark it generalized more reliably with sparse data in the material-descriptor space. These results suggest that representing a material family through a small set of shared convex neural potentials provides a useful structural prior for learning descriptor-dependent constitutive behavior from limited data.

authors.name: Steven J. Yang, Govinda Anantha Padmanabha, D. Thomas Seidl, Nikolaos Bouklas

papers.title: The role of different nonlinearities and potential vorticity conservation in two-dimensional fluid ITG models
papers.summary: The nature of turbulent energy cascade of simple two-dimensional fluid models of ion temperature gradient driven turbulence is studied in detail. Notably, it is observed that a minimal two-field model of toroidal ITG behaves qualitatively differently with or without the diamagnetic nonlinearity. In its absence, the zonal flows always dominate and the system never reaches a high-transport state. In contrast, when this term is included, zonal flows dominate only near marginality, while away from it, an inverse cascade with high levels of transport is observed, requiring large-scale dissipation (hypoviscosity) to saturate and hyperviscosity to regularize small scale instability associated with this nonlinear term. However introducing such a term, together with the existence of the curvature term, breaks potential vorticity conservation, which is one of the key symmetries of drift-wave turbulence. This can be remedied by considering a more complete model that retains higher-order terms in the pressure equation. This form of the model, with four nonlinearities, conserves potential vorticity and behaves similarly to the original model, requiring hyperviscosity to saturate since the added nonlinearity generates small scale instability also for the pressure equation. To characterize the roles of potential vorticity conservation and higher-order terms in the pressure equation, the behavior of both the standard ITG system, and the potential vorticity conserving system, is studied by analyzing their spectra, turbulent cascades, and sensitivity to viscosity. Finally, the direction of turbulent cascade due to the different nonlinearities is investigated by examining their contributions to the spectral energy transfer and by considering the triadic instability assumption for each of these nonlinearities separately.

authors.name: Giridharan Paramasivam, \"Ozg\"ur D. G\"urcan

papers.title: Optimisation of importance sampling implementation in rare-event shielding simulations using Geant4
papers.summary: Rare-event search experiments demand ever-lower backgrounds, and the resulting radio-pure materials and suppressive shielding make related background simulations computationally expensive without event biasing. We present a method for optimising the widely used importance splitting and Russian roulette technique for rare-event searches, in which a whole number of equal-width importance layers fill the shielding geometry. Balancing relative uncertainty against execution time, we optimise the layer thickness for both $\gamma$-rays and neutrons, and across different shielding materials and thicknesses. Expressed as a multiple of the primary particle's mean free path, the optimal thickness generalises across energies for a given particle type and yields a physics-based prediction applicable to any shielding design. The same trend reveals that over-biasing is possible, with relative uncertainty worsening at high layer counts for fixed execution time. The optimal configuration gives an $\mathcal{O}$(20) gain in computational efficiency over the unbiased case.

authors.name: P. Knights, L. J. Milligan, K. Nikolopoulos

papers.title: Investigating the coincidence problem with Interacting Dark Energy Models
papers.summary: Interacting dark energy (IDE) models within the framework of general relativity (GR) provide a possible extension of the standard $\Lambda$CDM model and may alleviate the coincidence problem. In this paper, we investigate three phenomenological interacting dark energy models using a combination of cosmic chronometer $H(z)$ measurements and two standard cosmic rulers: baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) and quasars (QSO). The observational constraints indicate a mild preference for energy transfer from dark energy to dark matter, a scenario that may help alleviate the cosmic coincidence problem. However, the standard $\Lambda$CDM model, corresponding to the absence of interaction, remains fully consistent with the observational data, as the no-interaction case lies within the $1\sigma$ confidence interval of the inferred interaction parameter for all three IDE models. Model comparison, using Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), further indicates that the current data do not provide statistically significant evidence favouring any IDE model over the standard $\Lambda$CDM scenario or over one another. These results suggest that, while a weak dark-sector interaction is permitted by the data, present observations do not provide compelling evidence for departures from the standard $\Lambda$CDM model.

authors.name: Kshitiz Singh, Savita Gahlaut

papers.title: Direct Numerical Simulation of Thermoacoustically Unstable Flames Via Non-Drifting Acoustic Delay Characteristic Boundary Conditions
papers.summary: In this work, Direct Numerical Simulations (DNS) of thermoacoustically unstable free flames in closed-open tubes are presented. Simulations demonstrate nonlinear saturation of the primary instability as the flame flattens, resulting in a quasiperiodic acoustic limit cycle. Acoustic forcing is used to trigger secondary parametric instability, causing an oscillatory flame fingering characteristic of the unsteady Rayleigh-Taylor effect. To reduce computational cost, we perform DNS only on the region surrounding the flame. Acoustics at in- and outflows are described using the Navier-Stokes Characteristic Boundary Condition (NSCBC) method to model their delayed reentry into the domain in a formulation referred to as the Acoustic Delay Characteristic Boundary Condition (ADCBC) method. A new Averaged Proportional and Integral Linear Relaxation (APILR) method is also introduced, which modifies the Classic Linear Relaxation (CLR) method to maintain time-averaged values of inflow velocity and outflow pressure. Many moving averages may be used consecutively to increase the damping rate of boundary reflection coefficients. An integral control term is used to remove non-zero equilibrium time-averaged inflow velocities which adversely affect control over flame position in the DNS region. Both new boundary methods demonstrate their capability in inert and counterflow flames test cases. In the case of a 100 cm long tube, these methods enable the numerical simulation of combustion instabilities at 98% reduced computational expense.

authors.name: Benjamin L. Cookman, Jack R. C. King, Rapha\"el C. Assier, Steven J. Lind

papers.title: FlowMLLab: An open-source framework for reproducible computational-fluid-dynamics and scientific-machine-learning experiments
papers.summary: FlowMLLab is an open-source Python framework for scientific machine learning in thermal-fluid and aerospace engineering, covering incompressible, compressible and rarefied flows. Its 22 weeks comprise 51 notebooks and 35 lectures. Solvers and molecular sampling underpin field prediction, uncertainty quantification and reduced-order modeling. Proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and deep operator networks (DeepONets), including POD-DeepONet, connect operating conditions to flow fields alongside Fourier neural operators. Physics-informed neural networks infer solutions and constitutive coefficients. Geometry-conditioned models, including the point-cloud DeepONet variant Geom-DeepONet, handle changing domains. Aerospace applications address airfoil shock/vortex identification, rarefied-gas modeling, nozzle flow prediction and supersonic body design. Complementary thermal-fluid examples cover unsteady wakes, hydrofoil vapor clouds and noisy particle observations. Attention mechanisms support sparse-sensor reconstruction, autoregressive prediction and transfer assessment, alongside character-level language modeling. Complete-case evaluation excludes tests from selection; execution notes identify retained research outputs. A worked extension embeds a learned monotone relation for a fixed manufactured Carreau fluid in channel momentum balance. At three unseen in-support pressure gradients, it outperforms profile-interpolation and fitted-Newtonian controls with different information or priors.

authors.name: Ehsan Roohi

papers.title: Quasi-symmetric error field correction and applications to ITER
papers.summary: Reliable correction of nonaxisymmetric error fields (EFs) is essential to the safety and performance of tokamak operation. Although resonant error field correction (EFC) is well established, supported by an improved understanding of 3D plasma response, the residual fields left after resonant EFC remain an open question: they are expected to be predominantly nonresonant, yet can still degrade both confinement and stability. Here we introduce a systematic EFC scheme that minimizes resonant and nonresonant EF effects simultaneously, based on neoclassical torque response computed from self-consistent perturbed equilibria. The scheme extends the method developed for designing quasi-symmetric magnetic perturbations to the case where actual error fields are present. Application to standard ITER target plasmas with a range of intrinsic EF scenarios demonstrates the advantages of this quasi-symmetric (QS) EFC scheme for controlling residual EFs. QS EFC consistently yields low-torque solutions while strongly suppressing resonant response, outperforming single-mode resonant overlap EFC in most cases and approaching the performance of multimodal resonant EFC. We also show that the QS EFC solution varies only tolerably between half- and full-$I_p$ ITER scenarios, despite the greater sensitivity expected from its higher-order nature.

authors.name: Gwang-Geun Seo, Jong-Kyu Park, S. J. Han, M. Dubrov

papers.title: Online reduced-order modeling from primal solver trajectories for PDE-constrained optimization
papers.summary: Repeated high-fidelity state and gradient evaluations make large-scale PDE-constrained optimization computationally expensive. Reduced-order modeling provides a natural way to reduce the cost of these repeated high-dimensional computations. However, existing reduced-order modeling approaches often rely on converged high-fidelity states for model construction or updating, while their reduced spaces may lose accuracy as the design moves beyond the region represented by the available data. To address these limitations, we present Reduced-order Trajectory-based Optimization (RETO), an online framework that constructs local reduced-order models (ROMs) directly from unconverged primal solver trajectories. Each local ROM is built from snapshots collected during a finite number of high-fidelity primal iterations, without requiring full-order convergence, and supports multiple low-cost state evaluations, adjoint-based gradient evaluations, and design updates. New solver trajectories are generated at updated design points to reconstruct the local ROM and continue the optimization. Across the Poisson inversion and logistic resource-allocation problems, RETO achieves solution quality comparable to that of full-order optimization, with speedups of 14.7 times and 8.49 times, respectively. Even for the more challenging airfoil inverse-design problems, RETO retains speedups of 2.52 to 3.13 times under subsonic and transonic conditions. These results demonstrate the value of unconverged primal solver trajectories as an online information source for reduced-order optimization, allowing the reduced basis to evolve with the design rather than requiring a basis that covers the entire design space in advance.

authors.name: Zhe Lu, Wenbo Cao, Weiwei Zhang

papers.title: A Jump-Diffusion Model of Home Price Dynamics and Neighborhood Change
papers.summary: We develop a dynamical model that links the fluctuations of individual home prices to changes in the full distribution of home prices in an urban area. We model the price of an individual home as a jump-diffusion stochastic differential equation. To capture the dynamic and hyper-local economic conditions that drive the residential real estate market, we allow all parameters to depend on both time and neighborhood. In the mean-field limit, we derive the associated Fokker-Planck partial integro-differential equation (PIDE) governing the evolution of the home price distribution in a neighborhood. We quantify spatial heterogeneity within a city by using the Wasserstein-2 distance to compare home price distributions across the city's neighborhoods. We validate our model using data from Boston, Massachusetts as a case study.

authors.name: Ashley Peake, Adam Gilbert-Diamond, Jordan T. Kemp, Anette E. Hosoi

papers.title: Deep Learning-based Multiparametric Quantitative Ultrasound for Hepatic Steatosis Assessment
papers.summary: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) has shown promise for liver fat quantification in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). Incorporating multiple parameters has demonstrated the potential to outperform single QUS parameter measures. Here, we propose a deep learning-based multiparametric QUS framework that learns effective integration of multiple features from QUS measures to estimate pixel-wise hepatic fat fraction, enabling the detecting of heterogeneous fat accumulation within the liver. We developed a U-Net based network architecture to predict local fat fraction percentages, which takes 2D QUS maps as input and is trained with magnetic resonance imaging-proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) as the ground truth. We extracted 2D QUS maps (H-scan frequency, at-tenuation, Nakagami, and RF/envelope/log-compressed data) and tested various input configura-tions consisting of different combinations of the QUS parameters. We enrolled 30 patients with healthy livers or suspected/confirmed MASLD, and acquired ultrasound RF data, and validated our approach using the patient data. Among all tested input configurations, the model combining H-scan, attenuation, and Nak-agami parameters achieved the best performance, with a Spearman correlation coefficient (Rs) of 0.92 and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.98. The predicted fat fraction maps exhibited color changes concordant with the gradual increasing in MRI-PDFF, from normal liver to 45% fat ac-cumulation. These findings demonstrate that deep learning can integrate multiparametric QUS in-formation in a fully data-driven manner, providing a localized fat fraction map rather than a single whole-liver value. We anticipate that our deep learning framework can offer potential advantages for future assessment of heterogeneous disease development in liver for more complex, progres-sive liver diseases such as steatohepatitis.

authors.name: Allison Lee, Ahmed El Kaffas, Aya Kamaya, Jeremy J. Dahl, Jihye Baek

papers.title: PyOTIS: an open-source Python package for stream solute transport with transient storage
papers.summary: OTIS and OTIS-P provide transient-storage transport and parameter estimation, whereas E-OTIS adds coupled water-quality reactions in a separate MATLAB implementation. PyOTIS brings these workflows into an open-source Python package with legacy OTIS input support. Its contribution is software integration: a scriptable interface, structured simulation outputs, Jacobian-based parameter uncertainty, sensitivity analysis, and selectable transport schemes. A browser-based graphical user interface (GUI) provides example loading, custom parameter entry, breakthrough-curve and storage-zone plots, reference overlays, and calibration of supplied cases with confidence intervals. The package retains the OTIS Crank--Nicolson formulation and the E-OTIS reaction network; these are inherited model components rather than new process formulations. Evaluation distinguishes code comparisons, analytical convergence, and fits to observations. For the six OTIS manual examples, the comparisons distinguish model outputs from field observations and include agreement to seven significant figures for the steady-state iron profile. The nine-species E-OTIS comparison reports maximum absolute differences of order $10^{-14}$\,mg\,L$^{-1}$ against MATLAB. The conservative analytical benchmark shows approximately second-order convergence. For Clackamas River calibration, residual sums of squares differ from OTIS-P by 3.65--5.12\%, although individual parameter estimates differ by up to 39.1\%. These results support implementation consistency for the tested cases without establishing unique parameter estimates or validating every reaction pathway. Source code, example inputs, and verification scripts accompany the package.

authors.name: Xuchen Ying, Binbin Wang

papers.title: Twister After Dark: Diagnosing a Damaging Nocturnal Tornado in Iloilo, Philippines (08 August 2026)
papers.summary: At ~1430 UTC (2230 LST) on 08 August 2026, a significant tornado struck the Mandurriao and Jaro districts of Iloilo City, Philippines. Its parent supercell developed within the southwest monsoon enhanced by Typhoon Dolphin, under weak synoptic forcing, as a nocturnal low-level jet of ~40 kt near 1.5-3 km advected warm, moist marine air onshore. ERA5 depicted MUCAPE of ~2000 J kg$^{-1}$, negligible inhibition, an LCL below 300 m, and nearly purely streamwise low-level vorticity, but deep-layer shear (DLS, 0-6 km bulk wind difference) below 3 m s$^{-1}$. Hodographs from the newly operational Iloilo S-band dual-polarization radar (S-ILO), ~5-7 km from the storm, revealed low-level shear (LLS, 0-1 km bulk wind difference) of ~16 m s$^{-1}$ and 0-1 km storm-relative helicity of 124-211 m$^2$ s$^{-2}$. The storm exhibited a hook echo with a weak echo hole, a $Z_{DR}$ arc and ring, an elevated 55-60 dBZ rear-flank core consistent with a descending reflectivity core, and a ~50 dBZ ring interpreted as a debris ball. A survey of 31 damage indicators documented a ~2.9 km long and up to ~340 m wide path rated IF2 on the International Fujita Scale. Processor smoothing of the radial velocity and a $\rho_{HV}$ threshold for rainfall estimation masked any tornadic vortex or debris signature, although a radial velocity simulation shows that a narrow vortex (core radius ~50-100 m) with a rotational velocity of ~35-45 m s$^{-1}$ could have been concealed. This case shows that significant tornadoes can develop at night during the Philippine monsoon season and that operational radar quality control should be revised to retain severe-storm signatures.

authors.name: Generich H. Capuli

papers.title: Controlling Mode-Locking in Liquid Light
papers.summary: Mode-locking is the process by which the phases of many cavity modes organize collectively into a stationary state. In lasers, mode-locking originates from the interplay of gain, loss, dispersion and nonlinearities, most commonly resulting in the emission of short pulses. However, pulse formation is prevented when the gain recovery is fast enough to suppress amplitude fluctuations. Mode-locking then produces an extended state of nearly constant intensity, whose dynamics is governed by the phase. Yet, a general framework for designing the phase of such extended photonic states remains lacking. Here we introduce a hydrodynamic approach to designing extended photonic states, in which the phase dynamics are understood and controlled as a flow of liquid-like light. The intensity, clamped by fast gain, plays the role of a constant density, the instantaneous frequency that of a flow velocity, and the programmable radio-frequency modulation applied to the laser acts as a potential landscape that controls the flow. We derive analytical solutions connecting the applied modulation to the instantaneous frequency and hence to the spectrum emitted by the laser. We further provide experimental evidence for the liquid light shaping framework by measuring the frequency comb spectra emitted by a fast-gain semiconductor laser around 1.6 micron under the control of a programmed modulation, and comparing them to the ones predicted by the analytical solution. The hydrodynamic picture of mode-locking provides a predictive design principle for frequency combs, pointing toward a programmable synthesizer of light, and establishes fast-gain lasers as an accessible, electrically driven platform for nonequilibrium fluids of light.

authors.name: Diego Piciocchi, Francesco Fortuna, Bahareh Marzban, Lucius Miller, Ina Heckelmann, Laurenz Kulmer, Juerg Leuthold, J\'er\^ome Faist, Alexander Dikopoltsev

papers.title: Geometric encoding of turbulence for end-to-end quantum simulation
papers.summary: Simulating multiscale turbulence in engineering remains challenging. Any quantum advantage for such simulations requires efficient initial-state preparation. Yet exact loading of an arbitrary classical snapshot requires exponential quantum resources. We introduce "turbuloscope", a physics-informed geometric method that generates statistically representative turbulent initial states in a gate-based register from a parameterized Pauli-spinor multiscale distribution. Scale invariance renders conditional rotations approximately affine in Gray-code space, enabling linear-depth, ancilla-free preparation. The generalized Madelung transform and Hopf fibration map the encoded Pauli spinor to fluid observables and vortex tubes. The qubit count scales logarithmically with the Reynolds number, yielding an exponential reduction in preparation overhead relative to full-grid classical spectral synthesis. We classically emulate a 30-qubit preparation circuit and generate a turbulent field over one billion grid points at a scale-inferred Reynolds number of 35,000, exhibiting Kolmogorov's five-thirds energy spectrum, tangled vortex tubes, and intermittency. This method provides scalable initial states for quantum simulation of turbulence and multiscale systems.

authors.name: Zhaoyuan Meng, Xiao-Ming Zhang, Xiao Yuan, Yue Yang

papers.title: Plane partitions and spin adapted quantum states
papers.summary: We describe an explicit basis for the $\operatorname{SU}(2)$-invariant space of the exterior power $\wedge_{2k} \mathbb{C}^{2m}$ via the combinatorics of plane partitions. In quantum chemistry, this is the space of spin adapted quantum states of an electronic system with $m$ spin orbitals and $k$ electron pairs. We construct our basis by identifying the invariant space with an Artinian commutative ring called the excitation ring. We compute a Gr\"obner basis and enumerate its standard monomials via an explicit bijection to Dyck paths counted by the Narayana numbers.

authors.name: Abigail Price, Ada Stelzer, Svala Sverrisd\'ottir

papers.title: Ergotropy of macroscopic classical systems
papers.summary: We address the fundamental question of what is the maximal amount of energy (a.k.a. ergotropy) that can be extracted from a macroscopic classical system by means of a cyclical variation of an external parameter. We show that if the system is prepared in a statistical state of the form $\rho = F(H)$, with $H$ the Hamiltonian and $F$ a generic limited function, then the ergotropy is vanishing in the {large $N$} limit, provided the thermodynamic entropy obeys the scaling $\mathcal S(E) \simeq N^\alpha s ({E}/{N^\beta})$ with $\alpha,\beta>0$ and $s$ some strictly increasing function with certain reasonable properties. We stress that such ubiquitous condition also ensures the equivalence of the so-called "surface" and "volume" entropies. We illustrate this by introducing the notion of ``ergotropic rearrangement'' of a phase space density which we then apply to find the exact ergotropy expression of systems with constant (positive or negative) heat capacity being evenly distributed over energy shells in phase space. We discuss cases where the above mentioned equivalence does (does not) break and the ergotropy does (does not) vanish accordingly, in the large $N$ limit. The presented results shed new light on the statistical-mechanical foundations of the second law of thermodynamics.

authors.name: Michele Campisi

papers.title: QuantumXCT: Learning Interaction-Induced State Transformation in Cell-Cell Communication via Quantum Entanglement and Generative Modeling
papers.summary: Inferring cell-cell communication (CCC) from single-cell transcriptomic data remains challenging. Most existing methods retrieve curated ligand-receptor pairs, score their coordinated average expression and apply statistical testing, a static and indirect strategy that tends to overlook intracellular signaling consequences, context dependence and higher-order interactions. Here, we introduce QuantumXCT, a hybrid quantum-classical framework that defines CCC as learnable transformations between cellular state distributions induced by cell-cell interaction. By encoding transcriptomic profiles into a high-dimensional Hilbert space, QuantumXCT trains parameterized quantum circuits to learn a unitary transformation mapping a baseline non-interacting cellular state to an interacting state, and infers CCC under explicitly stated modeling assumptions. Unlike methods restricted to curated ligand-receptor pairs, QuantumXCT can evaluate any cross-cell gene pair. On synthetic data with known ground-truth interactions, QuantumXCT ranked the programmed intercellular interactions above non-interacting gene pairs (ROC-AUC 0.93). On an ovarian cancer-fibroblast mono- and co-culture model, it identified a PDGFB-PDGFRB-STAT3 axis reproducible across bootstrap resamples, amplitude encodings and search algorithms, and consistent with published perturbation experiments. The learned circuit is interpretable: its entangling topology translates into interaction networks, and post hoc contribution analysis quantifies the influence of individual interactions on the observed state transitions. QuantumXCT provides an interpretable, hypothesis-generating framework for de novo discovery of communication programs, and delineates both the potential and the current limits of quantum machine learning in single-cell biology.

authors.name: Selim Romero, Shreyan Gupta, Robert S. Chapkin, James J. Cai

papers.title: Site-selective preparation of two-dimensional dipolar quantum gases in an optical beat-note lattice
papers.summary: High-resolution microscopy of two-dimensional dipolar quantum gases requires selecting individual atomic layers, a task complicated for strongly magnetic lanthanide atoms by the limited applicability of standard magnetic-gradient techniques. We present an all-optical method for the deterministic spatial selection of single- and bilayer samples of cold dipolar atoms using spatially selective parametric heating within a beat-note superlattice. By utilizing a high-resolution microscope objective as a common retroreflector for both optical frequency components, the lattice planes are passively stabilized. This renders their positions exceptionally robust against experimental drifts and structure-borne vibrations, even eliminating the need for active laser stabilization over millimeter-scale separations from the reflecting surface. We validate this approach by demonstrating the robust isolation of one or two atomic layers in precise coincidence with the focal plane of our objective. This enables future single-atom-resolved studies of long-range interacting systems.

authors.name: Niclas H\"ollrigl, Marian Kreyer, Rudolf Grimm, Emil Kirilov

papers.title: Efficient targeting of arbitrary excited states with quantum inverse power iteration through filtering polynomials
papers.summary: In this work, we introduce a quantum inverse power iteration (QIPI) algorithm based on the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) to target arbitrary excited states. Given an energy shift $\omega$, QIPI prepares the target excited state by iteratively applying an approximation of the shifted inverse Hamiltonian $(H-\omega I)^{-1}$ to a trial state. Prior quantum inverse power approaches typically relied on Fourier decompositions of the inverse Hamiltonian, with numerical quadrature used to reconstruct the transformation, but such methods are highly sensitive to hyperparameter choices and have been observed to be numerically unstable, effectively restricting their use to ground-state preparation. To enable robust excited-state targeting, we investigate two alternative transformation techniques: a Chebyshev decomposition of the inverse (Cheb-inv) and an eigenstate filtering (EF) approach based on QSVT. We find that EF-based QIPI is substantially more robust than Cheb-inv and other decomposition-based approaches due to the symmetry of the applied filtering polynomial, avoiding divergence with respect to the choice of $\omega$ and efficiently suppressing off-target eigenstates even in closely spaced spectra. Numerical simulations for molecular Hamiltonians of H$_2$, LiH, and BeH$_2$ show improved convergence and enhanced access to higher excited states relative to other quantum power methods. Assuming standard oracle access to the Hamiltonian, we further provide logical resource estimates in fault-tolerant settings in terms of T gate counts, and conclude that QIPI can achieve high target state amplification with modest polynomial degrees, thereby making it a promising candidate for scalable excited-state preparation in fault-tolerant quantum chemistry applications.

authors.name: Srushti Patil, Nina Glaser

papers.title: Overcoming configuration bottleneck: Modular pathways to stable semiconductor spin-qubit arrays
papers.summary: Over the past decade, semiconductor spin qubits have progressed from few-qubit demonstrations toward larger-scale devices fabricated in increasingly reproducible academic and industrial processes. This progress marks an inflection point: the central challenge is no longer to demonstrate high-fidelity operation in carefully tuned devices but to discover, verify, and maintain stable operating conditions reliably across many interdependent controls, varied device geometries, and disparate material platforms. In this Perspective, we frame spin-qubit operation as a modular automation problem. We decompose the workflow into five modules: bootstrapping from minimal prior information, configuration tuning, virtualization of physical gates into effective control axes, qubit-level tuning, and an operation layer with drift-aware maintenance. Using recent demonstrations from our work and the broader community, we argue that scalability will depend on explicit interfaces between modules, standardized intermediate data products, and workflow-level metrics such as throughput, success probability, stability time, recovery time, and robustness. We close by outlining the infrastructure needed to move beyond isolated tuning demonstrations toward sustained operation: qubit-performance-aware feedback, reusable software and benchmark tasks, and tight collaboration among experimental, theoretical, and software efforts.

authors.name: Justyna P. Zwolak, Anthony Sigillito

papers.title: The muon Moonshot: Moon subsurface tomography with upward-going muons
papers.summary: We propose a novel muon Moonshot concept for lunar subsurface tomography based on upward-going muons originating from the lunar regolith. Unlike Earth, the Moon lacks an atmosphere, leaving dense regolith below and a near-vacuum environment above. Consequently, most downward-going hadrons are absorbed before decaying, while upward-going hadrons escaping the regolith can decay in flight, producing a significant flux of lunar muons. These muons can be detected by instruments on the lunar surface or in near-lunar orbit. We perform Monte Carlo simulations to investigate their energy spectra, angular distributions, and integrated fluxes under various theoretical and detector configurations. The results indicate that the lunar muon flux is sensitive to detector altitude under idealized geometry. This dependence demonstrates its potential as a novel, non-invasive probe of shallow subsurface voids. We also present case studies on the detection of underground cavities and water resources. For shallow overburden, large cavity signals remain detectable with estimated backgrounds and systematics. Weaker water signals remain challenging. Potential implementations in future lunar missions are also discussed.

authors.name: Zimo Hu, Leyun Gao, Zhengyun You, Qite Li, Qiang Li, Yuhong Yu, Liangwen Chen, Xueheng Zhang, Zhiyu Sun

papers.title: Proof-of-principle long-distance Sagnac twin-field quantum key distribution network
papers.summary: Twin-field (TF) quantum key distribution (QKD) offers a promising approach to long-distance QKD networks due to its superior performance over large channel losses. Due to specialized hardware requirements, nearly all long-distance TFQKD demonstrations have only two users exchanging keys, rather than a network with three or more users. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate a proof-of-principle three-user-pair Sagnac TFQKD network spanning 127-km using single-photon avalanche detectors without any active phase stabilization or postcompensation. We implement efficient procedures for maintaining polarization stability and circumventing Rayleigh backscattering noise to achieve a stable Sagnac interference visibility of $93\pm1$ % over one hour. Using measured data for the signal basis and simulated data for the decoy basis, an asymptotic secure key rate of $1.398\times10^{-5}$ bits per pulse is achieved over an asymmetric communication channel with 102-km fiber and 45-dB overall loss. To our knowledge, this is the first TFQKD network without active phase stabilization or postcompensation achieved over long fibers. Our results represent a highly practical and cost-effective approach to long-distance QKD networks.

authors.name: Reem Mandil, Yen-An Shih, Abhay Verma, Li Qian, Hoi-Kwong Lo

papers.title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
papers.summary: Backgrounds arising from quark- and gluon-initiated jets misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons constitute a major experimental challenge for analyses involving tau leptons. The MUltivariate Fake-Factor INference (MUFFIN) approach, a machine-learning-based method for estimating this background directly from observed events, is presented. Boosted decision tree reweighting is used to learn multidimensional, per-object correction factors directly from observed data, thereby modelling the jet to hadronic tau lepton misidentification probability across the kinematic and topological phase space without relying on low-dimensional parametrisations. Performance studies are presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb$^{-1}$. Compared to low-dimensional parametrisation methods, improved modelling of key kinematic observables is achieved, particularly in regions of high $p_\mathrm{T}$. The improved modelling leads to a reduction of up to 70% in the systematic uncertainty associated with jets being misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons. The MUFFIN method provides a robust and scalable method for background estimation in precision measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model physics involving tau lepton final states.

authors.name: CMS Collaboration

papers.title: Suppression of Grain Boundary Nitrogen Degradation by Boron in Superalloys
papers.summary: Superalloys enable the hottest sections of jet engines to operate at high temperatures, but environmentally assisted degradation limits their lifetime. In polycrystalline alloys, nitrogen penetrates beneath the protective surface oxides, to produce embrittling grain boundary nitrides. Boron is added in trace amounts to improve grain boundary strength, yet its role, if any, in oxidation-related degradation remains unclear. Here we show that boron segregates to an internal nitride--matrix interface in a Ni/Co-base $\gamma$/$\gamma^{\prime}$ strengthened superalloy. Both B-free and B-containing alloys develop stratified chromia/alumina scales at 800~$^{\circ}$C in \SI{100}{\hour}, but the B-free variant produces larger, deeper and more elongated Ti/Nb-rich subsurface grain boundary nitrides. Correlative 4D S/TEM and atom probe tomography identify the particle as a chemically complex B1 nitride and reveal interfacial boron segregation. This shows that trace alloying as an alloy strategy can control damaging internal reaction product precipitation and growth by core-shell segregation.

authors.name: C. Crabb, G. Topore, J. O. Douglas, M. C. Hardy, M. S. Conroy, D. Dye

papers.title: LH$\mu$C Concept: Energy-Frontier Antimuon-Proton Collisions at CERN
papers.summary: The concept of the LH$\mu$C, an energy-frontier antimuon-proton collider based on the HL-LHC, is presented. After recalling why energy-frontier lepton-hadron colliders are indispensable as QCD explorers and reviewing the history of muon-proton collider proposals, two ways of realising $\mu p$ collisions at the LHC are compared: with muon-collider beams and with ultra-cold $\mu^+$ beams as proposed for $\mu$TRISTAN. For the latter, a $\mu$TRISTAN-type booster and the re-use of the LHeC energy-recovery-linac tunnel are discussed; colliding 1 TeV antimuons with 7 TeV protons gives $\sqrt{s}=5.3$ TeV and peak luminosities of $8.8\times10^{33}$ and $7.2\times10^{33}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, respectively. The detector concept and the physics potential, including searches for colour-octet muons and R-parity-violating squarks, are discussed together with the main challenges.

authors.name: Arda Goroglu, Saleh Sultansoy

papers.title: Machine learning quantum data to accelerate quantum Monte Carlo
papers.summary: Simulating strongly correlated electrons in molecules and materials remains a central goal for quantum computing. A promising strategy uses quantum processors to prepare trial wavefunctions that guide classical quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). However, the enormous computational cost of repeatedly processing quantum measurements has severely limited the practical scalability of this approach. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by compressing quantum measurement data into machine-learning models that efficiently provide the wavefunction overlaps needed by QMC. This accelerates quantum-classical QMC by orders of magnitude, enabling chemically accurate simulations on up to 40 qubits, more than doubling the scale of previous hardware demonstrations with comparable accuracy. We demonstrate our approach on hydrogen chains and strongly correlated iron-sulfur clusters using measurements from Google's Willow processor. By enabling efficient reuse of quantum-state information on the classical coprocessor, our framework addresses a fundamental bottleneck in hybrid quantum algorithms that will persist even into the fault-tolerant era.

authors.name: Tong Jiang, Andrew Zhao, Shashwat Kumar, Jigyasa Nigam, Eliott Rosenberg, Ryan Babbush, Andrew D. Baczewski, William J. Huggins, Joonho Lee

papers.title: In-plane diffusion, spurious drift and a physics-structured gap predictor for a free colloidal pair
papers.summary: When the diffusivity of a Brownian particle depends on position, its mean displacement acquires a noise-induced (spurious) drift whose magnitude is set by the stochastic convention $\alpha$. Inspired by the particle-wall experiments published by G. Volpe and co-workers, we ask how much of this physics can be extracted from a pair of 1.95 $\mu$m polystyrene spheres released from blinking holographic optical tweezers at five temperatures between 2 and 40 $^\circ$C. The single-sphere diffusivity inside the pair stays between 0.093 and 0.098 $\mu$m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, whereas the Stokes-Einstein value for water rises from 0.126 to 0.361 $\mu$m$^2$ s$^{-1}$; an isolated sphere shows the same deficit, so the missing diffusivity scale originates in the measurement and not in the pair interaction. The pair is what makes the diffusivity depend on position: from the measured gap-dependent diffusivities $D_\parallel(h)$ and $D_\perp(h)$ we build a Fokker-Planck predictor of the future gap and score it on held-out releases. It recovers the 90% width of the gap distribution up to 800 ms but cannot discriminate between $\alpha = 0$, $1/2$ and $1$, because the $\alpha$-dependent mean shift is an order of magnitude smaller than that width. The ensemble spurious drift is consistent with zero at both ends of the temperature range, and the regression for $\alpha$ never exceeds $R^2 = 0.22$. We present a planar methods baseline and identify the measurements required to resolve $\alpha$.

authors.name: Juan Pablo Staforelli Vivanco, Cristobal Augusto Vald\'es Cruces

papers.title: Isomorphisms of Class S Theories with IndexLab
papers.summary: We use IndexLab to scan untwisted and twisted class $\mathcal{S}$ constructions based on ADE Lie algebras of rank up to seven, as well as $A_8$ and $E_8$. We consider surfaces of genus at most three with up to five punctures, covering 167,244,647 constructions in total. To find candidate pairs of isomorphic theories, we compare Schur and Hall-Littlewood indices, Weyl anomalies, Coulomb branch spectra, and flavor data. We set aside pairs explained by known mechanisms, leaving a catalogue of 5,278 candidate pairs. Recurring changes in rank, puncture labels, and twists suggest families of candidate isomorphisms. We group 99.58% of the pairs into 25 families and 6 finite families. IndexLab is available at superconformal.com.

authors.name: Zhihao Duan, Zhenghao Zhong

papers.title: An infrared-safe $S$-matrix for $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills
papers.summary: Scattering amplitudes of massless gauge theories are not observables: they are infrared divergent, and the standard regulators are tied either to perturbation theory or the planar limit. We study $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory on rigid AdS$_4$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where the role of the amplitude is played by correlation functions of boundary operators. These are finite, and they are defined at any coupling and for any gauge group. Among them, the four-point function of the flavor-current supermultiplet is the counterpart of the $2\to2$ amplitude of the elementary supergluon states, and arguably the simplest non-trivial observable of the theory. In this paper, we compute it at weak coupling to one loop. The tree-level correlator follows directly from the microscopic theory, and the one-loop correlator, which we obtain from AdS unitarity, takes a remarkably simple form in Mellin space. In the flat-space limit, it reproduces the one-loop scattering amplitude, with the infrared divergences re-emerging as logarithms.

authors.name: Maria Nocchi, Leonardo Rastelli

papers.title: 'Forward-backward' flows and integration cycles for semiclassical Euclidean gravity
papers.summary: Integrating Euclidean semiclassical gravity over real Riemannian metrics is subtle due to the conformal factor problem. A perturbative prescription was given by Gibbons-Hawking-Perry (GHP) where the integration contour for the conformal perturbations is rotated to be imaginary. A potential non-perturbative remedy is that the integration cycles associated to semiclassical saddle points should be deformed into the space of complex metrics in the sense of Picard-Lefschetz theory. Here we propose a non-perturbative construction of such complex integration cycles. This employs a 'forward-backward' gradient flow of the Einstein-Hilbert action, starting at a saddle point, along which the action has monotonically increasing real part and constant imaginary part. The flow is not parabolic. In a neighbourhood of a saddle point, the real part of the conformal factor flows forward and that of the conformal class backwards, with the opposite true of their imaginary parts. Starting the flow at a saddle point, then roughly speaking, one specifies the real part of the conformal class and the imaginary part of the conformal factor at the end of the flow. Solving the flow one finds the complex metrics along a one parameter path within the integration cycle of that saddle, and varying this final data generates the integration cycle, the Lefschetz thimble of the saddle point. We find that near to a real saddle point this reproduces the GHP prescription. We characterise the neighbourhood of a saddle where such forward-backward flows may exist, finding a weaker restriction than that of Kontsevich-Segal-Witten. We numerically demonstrate flows explicitly for 4-dimensional gravity, constructing sections through the integration contours for the saddles given by Euclidean de Sitter, and for Schwarzschild in a cavity.

authors.name: Nicholas M. K. Ross, Toby Wiseman

papers.title: Cosmic Censorship in the Landscape of SUSY-Broken AdS Vacua
papers.summary: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory. In particular, we examine the Penrose Inequality, which can be proven holographically using Ryu-Takayanagi, and can be independently proven in SUSY AdS vacua for spherically symmetric initial data. We prove that any EFT of scalars coupled to gravity in AdS, including in particular those of string compactifications, satisfies both the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem if a function that we call a "weak fake superpotential" exists. We demonstrate that this condition is satisfied globally for the DGKT skew-whiffed vacua in IIA. Since there is no known nonperturbative instability in this DGKT vacuum, this provides evidence that the IIA SUSY-broken AdS vacua may be absolutely stable. We also find the weak fake superpotential exists locally in field space in some SUSY-broken AdS vacua in a KKLT construction in IIB. Thus, within the framework considered here, some false SUSY-broken KKLT AdS vacua are stable against vacuum decay. Conversely, we find that some KKLT vacua do not have a weak fake superpotential, and correspondingly violate the Penrose Inequality and fail to have a positive mass theorem; the DGKT vacua only violate the Penrose Inequality in the presence of designer gravity boundary conditions. In all cases studied, this is due to false vacuum decay. We discuss the implications of these violations for holography and black hole thermodynamics in these SUSY-broken AdS vacua.

authors.name: Netta Engelhardt, Richard Nally

papers.title: Localization identities for spectral determinants: two-dimensional QCD and Ising field theory
papers.summary: Spectral determinants encode the meson spectra of planar two-dimensional QCD and of Ising field theory in the two-particle Bethe-Salpeter approximation. We derive localization identities for these determinants which express their logarithmic derivatives with respect to the spectral parameter in terms of Baxter $Q-$functions evaluated at special points, proving previously conjectured relations. Our derivation uses finite-rank commutation relations and virial identities of the underlying integral spectral operators. We identify a sufficient rational closure condition on the symbol of these operators that extends localization to a broader class of spectral problems and determines the evaluation points. Applications include generalized two-dimensional QCD with a quartic gauge-field potential and symbols interpolating between the QCD and Ising cases. We also give a general construction of the spectral operators and establish conditions for the finite-rank reduction on which localization relies.

authors.name: Bercel Boldis, Nikolay Gromov, Gregory P. Korchemsky, Alessandro Testa

papers.title: All-Genus 2D $\mathcal{N}=1$ Superconformal Blocks
papers.summary: We develop a numerical algorithm for two dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal blocks at arbitrary genera, in arbitrary plumbing channels, and for arbitrary spin structures. The algorithm utilizes two commuting copies of Virasoro subalgebras of the direct sum of the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal algebra with an auxiliary free fermion algebra, which allows us to reduce the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal blocks to Virasoro conformal blocks.

authors.name: Sam Christian, Yuchen Wang, Xi Yin, Yutai Zhang

papers.title: Not All Holographic Entropy Inequalities Are Free of Area Law Ultraviolet Divergences
papers.summary: In the AdS/CFT correspondence, linear constraints on subsystem entropies, which are necessary conditions for the validity of the Ryu-Takayanagi proposal, define the holographic entropy cone. We disprove a prior claim that all holographic constraints of this type are free of area law divergences (superbalanced). We analyze one explicit counterexample and explain how to easily find more; we report signatures of $\mathcal{O}(10^5)$ counterexamples. Our findings invalidate multiple prior claims and conjectures.

authors.name: Xin-Xiang Ju, Bartlomiej Czech

papers.title: Supersymmetric warped AdS$_3$ solutions in eleven-dimensional supergravity
papers.summary: We construct new families of supersymmetric solutions of eleven-dimensional supergravity by deforming the half-BPS $\mathrm{AdS}_3\times \mathrm{S}^3_+\times \mathrm{S}^3_-\times\mathbb R^2$ background. We consider lightlike, spacelike and timelike warpings of the anti-de Sitter factor, accompanied by deformations of the two three-spheres, and determine the supporting four-form fluxes and the constraints imposed by the equations of motion. In particular, the deformation parameters of the two spheres are necessarily equal, although their radii need not coincide. We compute the conserved charges and determine the preserved supersymmetries and Killing superalgebras. Generic lightlike solutions preserve four real supercharges, whereas spacelike and timelike solutions preserve eight, with a Killing superalgebra containing a single exceptional $\mathfrak d(2,1;\alpha)$ factor.

authors.name: Ruggero Noris

papers.title: Gravity/Thermodynamics Correspondence for Generic Dynamical Spacetimes
papers.summary: Working within covariant phase space formalism, we establish \textit{gravity-thermodynamics correspondence} for generic dynamical spacetimes. We derive local first and second laws of thermodynamics on general null boundaries, for generic non-stationary solutions to Einstein gravity {with minimally coupled matter} for physical observers that we carefully specify. Entropy variation, which receives contribution only from the gravitational sector, is the surface charge variation associated with a vector field generating the null boundary, and temperature is its non-affinity parameter (divided by $2\pi$). The statement of the second law in our setting is that the entropy variation evaluated along the null vector field is strictly non-negative for the admissible positive-non-affinity clock and matter satisfying the null energy condition. Our dynamical entropy variation, which is non-integrable for generic non-stationary solutions, becomes integrable in near-stationary configurations, reproducing the Hollands--Wald--Zhang dynamical entropy formula. Strikingly, this local second law holds even when the boundary area is decreasing, disentangling thermodynamic irreversibility and the second law from standard area theorems. Our first-principles construction demonstrates that gravitational thermodynamics requires neither a stationary background, teleological event horizons, nor an exact entropy state function on individual codimension-1 spacelike slices of the null boundary (codimension two in spacetime).

authors.name: Vahid Reza Shajiee, Mohammad Mehdi Sheikh-Jabbari, Vahid Taghiloo

papers.title: Modular Hamiltonian and modular flow of a massive scalar in an interval
papers.summary: We obtain the vacuum modular Hamiltonian of a free massive scalar in an interval, for any $mL$. Its eigenvectors are superpositions of massive plane waves emitted from the two end points, with amplitudes given by a linear integral equation whose Neumann series is an expansion in reflections, and a normalization fixed by a Painlev\'e V transcendent. We follow the modular flow of initially localized wave packets inside the causal diamond. The flow is not geometric: the commutator profiles spread and can develop peaks ahead of the conformal trajectory.

authors.name: Ra\'ul E. Arias, Daniel Fondevila

papers.title: Center anomalies without twists: torsion, exact degeneracies, and condensates
papers.summary: Mixed center anomalies are usually exposed by 't Hooft's twisted boundary conditions in a Hamiltonian formalism. On $\mathbb {RP}^3$, torsion makes the twist unnecessary: a center operator on the untwisted $SU(2)$ Hilbert space anticommutes with time reversal in Yang-Mills theory at $\theta=\pi$ and with the chiral symmetry of super Yang-Mills theory, so every level is at least doubly degenerate. The relevant semiclassical object is the BPST instanton, which descends to a charge-$\tfrac12$ saddle on the orbifold $\mathbb R^4/\mathbb Z_2$. We complete it in two ways: applying a conformal transformation maps the orbifold to $\mathbb R\times\mathbb {RP}^3$, with the saddle describing the tunneling event between the two center sectors; by resolving the orbifold singularity, we obtain the Eguchi-Hanson space, which gives the gaugino condensate at its weak-coupling value.

authors.name: Mohamed M. Anber

papers.title: Modular conjugations for thermal states and second worlds
papers.summary: The modular conjugation $J$ maps an algebra of observables onto its commutant. For the vacuum on a Rindler wedge it is a spacetime reflection, but for thermal states in two-dimensional CFTs the known expressions involve chiral fields at the complex points $x\pm i\beta/2$, interpreted as belonging to a ``second world''. Here we compute $J$ for the geometric thermal state in explicit cyclic purifications, using either the vacuum vector, through the conformal map to a Rindler wedge, or a vector in the natural cone of a local algebra. The modular images are then fields at real points, and complex coordinates arise only when operators of the commutant outside the image of the thermal representation are written as fields on the original spacetime. For the chiral $U(1)$ current we also purify by doubling the Fock space, obtain explicit formulas for $J$, show that this purification coincides with Sorce's canonical purification, and treat all primary thermal states.

authors.name: Alan Garbarz, Gabriel Palau, Guillem P\'erez-Nadal

papers.title: Giant gravitons without giant gravitons
papers.summary: We demonstrate that the partition function of a free bosonic $U(N)$ multi-matrix model admits a giant graviton expansion. For $d$ matrices, there are $d$ distinct giant gravitons, and the expansion can be characterized by a $d$-node quiver with bifundamentals connecting the nodes. This suggests the intriguing possibility of a more generalized holography where models without any obvious gravitational dual can nevertheless be given a dual brane interpretation. The giant graviton expansion of this multi-matrix model is somewhat unconventional though, as the giant graviton partition functions will necessarily have intrinsic $N$-dependence.

authors.name: Blake J. Bottesi, James T. Liu

papers.title: FLZ integrability in the 't Hooft model
papers.summary: We study the 't Hooft equation describing mesons in large-$N_c$ two-dimensional QCD with arbitrary unequal quark masses. Using its Fredholm formulation and the associated Baxter finite-difference equation, we investigate the relations between spectral determinants and canonical Baxter $Q$-functions. We derive special-point identities for the Baxter solutions by exploiting finite-rank commutator relations of the underlying integral operators. We also determine the spectral residues of the inhomogeneous solutions and obtain exact expressions for eigenfunction normalization factors in terms of values at distinguished complex points. These results establish the unit-residue property of the Baxter expressions entering the Fateev-Lukyanov-Zamolodchikov (FLZ) spectral-determinant identities. As a further application, we prove the nondegeneracy of the meson spectrum for arbitrary unequal quark masses. We further identify a broader class of integral operators exhibiting the same mechanism, which we refer to as FLZ integrability, and illustrate its applicability to the meson spectral problem in Ising field theory. Our approach reveals a connection between the analytic structure of Baxter equations and the theory of completely integrable Fredholm operators.

authors.name: Alexey Litvinov, Egor Shestopalov, Nikita Slavnov

papers.title: Simple Models of Thermal Order in $2+1$ Dimensions
papers.summary: Heating need not destroy order. We show that it persists to arbitrarily high temperatures in simple quantum field theories in $2+1$ spacetime dimensions. In a $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ model of two real scalar fields, a sufficiently negative mixed quartic coupling drives one field to condense, spontaneously breaking its $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry. When coupled to massless Dirac fermions through a Yukawa interaction, this condensate generates a fermion mass, thereby spontaneously breaking parity and time-reversal symmetries. We extend this construction to a $\mathbb Z_2\times O(n)$ scalar model, in which the Mermin-Wagner theorem precludes spontaneous breaking of the continuous $O(n)$ symmetry at finite temperatures. Nevertheless, for $n=2$, a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless superfluid phase persists to arbitrarily high temperatures. In this phase, spatial correlations decay algebraically, with an exponent that approaches zero as the temperature increases. For $n\geq 3$, we uncover a further unexpected feature of these models: the characteristic size of ordered domains grows asymptotically with temperature, revealing an unusual enhancement of spatial correlations upon heating. We establish our results using a controlled high-temperature expansion, with selected findings corroborated by numerical functional renormalization group analysis. The simplicity of the field content in these models provides a promising starting point for exploring experimental realizations of persistent thermal order in thin-film materials.

authors.name: Michael Smolkin, Lev Yung

papers.title: Structure Constants of Planar N=4 SYM at Any Coupling
papers.summary: We recast a recent conjecture for structure constants in planar N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory in a separation-of-variables-inspired form suitable for non-perturbative analysis. All state-dependent information enters through the quantum spectral curve. As a showcase, we compute at finite coupling the three-point functions of two half-BPS operators and the spin-two member of the Konishi multiplet. Our results span weak to strong coupling, reproduce the known perturbative and string-theory limits, and are consistent with conformal-bootstrap bounds. We also obtain new six- and seven-loop perturbative coefficients and extract new strong-coupling data from high-precision numerical fits.

authors.name: Simon Ekhammar, Alessandro Georgoudis, Nikolay Gromov

papers.title: Regular/Singular Black Hole Thermodynamics from Renormalised Volume/Area
papers.summary: We study the finite mismatch between the holographically and topologically renormalised Euclidean actions of the four-dimensional AdS C-metric. Starting from the relation between Renormalised Volume and the Einstein sector of Conformal Gravity, we separate the regular curvature contribution from the contributions supported on the two conical axes. After introducing the usual Euler normalisation for smooth manifolds, the residual difference between the regular action evaluations is determined by the tension-weighted Euler terms of the renormalised worldsheet area. We identify this difference with the Gauss--Bonnet entropy contribution at the polar conical points of the horizon. The ordinary Euler characteristic remains fixed, while the deficits determine how its curvature representation is divided between regular and singular contributions. At fixed total string tension, the difference of the renormalised worldsheet areas per unit Euclidean time determines the relative tension work, giving a geometric interpretation of the relative thermodynamic length.

authors.name: Gabriel Arenas-Henriquez, Rodrigo Olea, David Rivera-Betancour

papers.title: Non-integrability of open strings via Pohlmeyer reduction
papers.summary: We study integrable and non-integrable boundary conditions for classical strings from the point of view of Pohlmeyer reduction. We first consider the integrable case of strings ending on Y=0 non-maximal giant gravitons. Pohlmeyer reduction of such strings leads to a sine-Gordon model, for which a criterion for boundary integrability was provided by Ghoshal and Zamolodchikov. We confirm that the Pohlmeyer field satisfies this condition. We then turn to the main focus of our work, which is open strings on AdS3. By evaluating the Ghoshal-Zamolodchikov criterion for the corresponding Pohlmeyer-reduced models, we are able to distinguish between integrable and non-integrable cases, in line with expectations from recent analytic and numerical studies. We conclude that Pohlmeyer reduction can provide a useful perspective on open-string non-integrability.

authors.name: Divania Carelse, Laila Tribelhorn, Konstantinos Zoubos

papers.title: Higher Spin Lagrangians for Black Holes in Arbitrary Dimension
papers.summary: In this paper, we investigate the classical gravitational multipolar structure of rotating objects studying higher-spin Lagrangians coupled to gravity in arbitrary dimensions $D=d+1$. We first consider fields described by totally symmetric tensors with $s$ indices. At finite spin, the minimal coupling depends on both the spin and spacetime dimension. We show that, in the high-spin limit $s\gg 1$, the minimal multipolar expansion becomes dimension independent and it corresponds to the one which reproduces the Kerr solution in four dimensions. Furthermore, we identify a dimension independent relation among the non-minimal coupling coefficients that allows us to reproduce the Myers-Perry multipolar structure in arbitrary dimensions. We then extend our analysis to Lagrangians involving fields with different Young representations, which are allowed in higher dimensions.

authors.name: Francesco Campanella

papers.title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
papers.summary: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincar\'e algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.

authors.name: Zi-Hao Liu, Mei Huang

papers.title: Spectral recurrences and maximal analyticity: cosmological correlators at one and two loops
papers.summary: We develop a method for computing de Sitter boundary correlators based on the maximal analyticity of the two-point function and differential--difference equations satisfied by Schwinger--Keldysh diagrams. The vertex integrations are analytically continued through the relevant de Sitter tuboids onto purely imaginary Lobachevskij cycles. Taking the Mehler--Fock transform of the invariant bubble kernels on these Riemannian cycles converts their differential--difference equations into algebraic recurrences in the spectral parameter. The mixed-branch kernel obeys a homogeneous recurrence, whereas the chronological and antichronological kernels satisfy sourced recurrences whose local terms are determined by dimensionally continued tadpoles. We solve these recurrences, constructing explicit particular solutions in terms of generalised hypergeometric functions and identifying the analytic conditions selecting their physical completion. Attachment to the external boundary points then yields an intrinsic spectral representation and a complete solution of the boundary in--in diagrams considered here. Our method is fully coordinate-independent. Specialising to a Poincar\'e chart readily gives expressions that can be compared directly with those obtained by the standard coordinate-dependent approach. Composing two or more bubbles yields a multi-loop chain whose spectral multiplier is determined by the one-loop building blocks and the sum over intermediate Schwinger--Keldysh branches.

authors.name: Bruce A. Bassett, Sergio L. Cacciatori, Ugo Moschella

papers.title: Fluid/Gravity Correspondence in 3d Flat Gravity with Non-Compact Boundaries
papers.summary: We study 3d flat gravity on a restricted phase space with a non-compact spatial boundary. The charge algebra splits into two commuting chiral current algebras, which a fluid/gravity dictionary maps to the stress tensor of a two-dimensional conformal fluid, with energy bounded below by the momentum. On the line, finiteness of the charges selects integrable, square-integrable currents, and the global data are carried by the scattering variables of a Schr\"odinger operator rather than by a monodromy. We analyze Heisenberg-like and Dirichlet-like boundary conditions; the latter give independently propagating chiral kinks associated with the reflectionless P\"oschl-Teller operator. Both admit first-law relations. We outline the quantization as a Weyl $C^*$-algebra with quasi-free states. Retaining the radial dependence, the quasi-local stress tensor obeys an exact, non-perturbative flow of square-root $T\bar T$ type, which integrates to a finite boost in the radial position.

authors.name: H. Adami, R. Esp\'indola, K. Lara, A. Latifi

papers.title: Toric Calabi-Yau orientifolds: constructions, fixed loci and O-plane charges
papers.summary: We review the systematic construction of toric orientifold Calabi-Yau threefolds through divisor exchanges and coordinate reflections. We relate the homogeneous-coordinate and lattice descriptions and explain the computation of fixed loci and the geometric data entering Hodge splittings and tadpole conditions. Our triangulation-wise analysis identifies multiple compatible involutions on a single triangulation and tracks their realisations across different triangulations, revealing the orientifold structure within and across toric phases. We complement this review with new calculations and explicit examples that refine the fixed-locus geometry and the associated orientifold charge data. The examples also identify coordinate representatives of the identity and invariant hypersurface families with unavoidable singularities. These results support an ongoing update of the orientifold catalogue and provide geometric input for D-brane configurations, flux compactifications and moduli stabilisation.

authors.name: Xu Cao, Xin Gao

papers.title: Quantum phase transition and superselection sectors in two-color one-flavor matrix QCD at weak coupling
papers.summary: We numerically investigate the weak-coupling (small $g$) regime of the matrix model of $SU(2)$ gauge theory coupled to one flavor of massless fundamental quarks. The theory possesses a global Pauli-G\"ursey $SU(2)_B$ symmetry, which organizes physical states of spin $J$ into sectors labelled by its representation $B$. We find localization-delocalization quantum phase transitions (QPTs) in multiple $(B,J)$ sectors at sector-dependent critical couplings $g_\ast^{BJ}$. Direct evaluation of the localization probability reveals that the ground states are predominantly localized near $A_i=0$ for $gg_*^{BJ}$. The QPTs in different sectors exhibit distinct features, and we establish that quark-glue interactions are essential for these transitions. The transitions are singular: the ground state expectation value of $\text{Tr}(A_iA_i)$ remains finite for $g< g_\ast^{BJ}$, whereas it diverges as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above. We show that the two limiting ground states on either side of $g_\ast^{BJ}$ belong to distinct superselection sectors. Furthermore, as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above, the ground state localizes on a submanifold (of codimension 2) of the gauge configuration space, with the spin and color of its glue components becoming locked.

authors.name: Nirmalendu Acharyya, Arkajyoti Bandyopadhyay, Parthsarathi Kondapure, Sachindeo Vaidya

papers.title: 5d $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ S-folds, quotient curves, and isogenies
papers.summary: We construct Seiberg--Witten curves for the $\mathbb{Z}_3$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$, and $\mathbb{Z}_6$ S-folds of 5d rank-1 superconformal theories. Compared with the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ case arXiv:2611.09804, $\mathbb{Z}_{3,4,6}$ S-folds require stronger constraints on the mass parameters. We provide a systematic procedure of realizing the S-foldings at the mirror curve level. We obtain the same elliptic curve families by specializing the complexified mass parameters of the rank-1 $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$ theories, with holonomies motivated by the 7-brane insertions required by the S-fold prescription. The two constructions agree in Weierstrass form. The families with continuous mass deformations organize into characters of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{g}_2$, consistently with their singular fibers. Finally, we discuss that the Seiberg--Witten curves for $\mathbb{Z}_n$ S-folds can be obtained through cyclic $n$-isogenies, which may provide a uniform quotient curve description of rank-1 S-folds.

authors.name: Sung-Soo Kim, Song Liu, Mudassar Sabir, Futoshi Yagi

papers.title: Strange-Metal Magnetotransport without a Strange-Metal Ground State
papers.summary: Strange metals display a linear-in-temperature resistivity, $\rho_{xx}\sim T$, and a quadratic inverse Hall angle, $\cot\Theta_H\sim T^2$. These seemingly universal laws are often attributed to quantum criticality, yet no controlled theory realizes both at an asymptotic zero-temperature fixed point, and experimentally they persist only over finite temperature windows. Here, we show that these properties can arise from an intermediate critical regime that does not govern the ground state. Using a minimal class of holographic models, we construct a fully backreacted realization of both scalings, which appear within a finite temperature window controlled by an emergent intermediate scaling geometry. The window is bounded by relevant deformations of the corresponding fixed point: momentum relaxation sets the upper edge, while the magnetic field $B$ closes it from below at $T_{\min}\sim B^{2/3}$, up to logarithmic corrections. At $T_{\min}$, strange-metal transport, the scaling geometry, and critical thermodynamics break down together. Our results point to intermediate criticality as a distinct route to strange-metal transport, and suggest that it can be identified by the simultaneous breakdown of transport and thermodynamic scaling under a magnetic field.

authors.name: Yongjun Ahn, Matteo Baggioli, Hyun-Sik Jeong, Keun-Young Kim

papers.title: An Effective Theory for Hot Lines
papers.summary: We develop a high-temperature effective theory for spatial conformal line defects in theories with thermal screening. The defect partition function admits a local geometric expansion, whose leading terms describe the effective tension and bending response of the line. Using a convergent bulk OPE for heavy-state defect matrix elements, we derive asymptotic relations for averaged products of defect one-point coefficients and bulk OPE coefficients in the regime $1 \ll \Delta_\chi \ll \Delta^{1/d}$. We compute the leading EFT coefficients for a twisted free scalar and for the magnetic line at the $\mathrm{O}(N)$ Wilson-Fisher fixed point, large-$N$ Gross--Neveu model and $\mathcal N = 2$ Chern-Simons-matter theory. For the three-dimensional Ising model, Monte Carlo simulations yield a perimeter coefficient in good agreement with a Pad\'e interpolation of our $\varepsilon$-expansion result.

authors.name: Julien Barrat, Alessio Miscioscia, Fedor K. Popov

papers.title: The Pfaffian sector of $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ BPS cohomology: brane excitations, triality and fortuity
papers.summary: We study the classical $\frac{1}{16}$-BPS cohomology of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory with gauge group $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ in the BMN sector, including the operators built with one $\epsilon$-tensor. These operators are odd under the reflection in $\mathrm{O}(2N)$, carry the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ charge of a D3-brane wrapped on $\mathbb{RP}^3\subset\mathbb{RP}^5$, and form the Pfaffian sector. For $\mathrm{SO}(8)$ we determine this sector through level $j=18$, where the level is twice the total charge of an operator. All but one of its $106$ $\mathrm{SU}(3)_R$ multiplets are products of trace gravitons and excited Pfaffians. The exception is a singlet, represented by the singlet projection of the rank-four member of a four-term family of $\epsilon$-tensor operators. We construct a covering space for the Pfaffian sector in which this family is closed at every rank, and the family defines a non-graviton class for every $N\ge 4$. Triality pairs the singlet with a reflection-even class that is fortuitous with respect to the trace covering. The two classes restrict, along the spinor and the vector embedding of $\mathfrak{so}(7)$ respectively, to the known non-graviton singlet of $\mathrm{SO}(7)$, which is lifted at first order. We show that the two $\mathrm{SO}(8)$ classes, and the family for every $N\ge 4$, are protected to all orders of perturbation theory. Their protection is compatible with the lifting in $\mathrm{SO}(7)$ because restriction to a subalgebra does not commute with the quantum corrections to the supercharge.

authors.name: Zheng Miao, Yuezhang Tang

papers.title: CFTs with Large Virasoro Primary Gaps
papers.summary: We construct the first explicit examples of compact unitary bosonic full conformal field theories (CFTs) in two dimensions with a unique vacuum and an all-spin Virasoro-primary gap greater than two. Our constructions use asymmetric orbifolds of lattice CFTs built from even unimodular lattices of sufficiently large minimum norm, ensuring that no charged state lies below the desired gap. The gauged symmetries combine a common orthogonal action on the left- and right-moving currents with independent sign reversals; the latter project out the dimension-two scalar primary $\sum_i J_L^iJ_R^i$ that survives when the symmetry acts identically on both chiral halves. We prove that the gauging is anomaly-free and determine the exact gaps by analyzing the invariant untwisted spectrum and all twisted sectors. From lattices constructed using ternary quadratic-residue codes, we obtain an infinite family with gap three at $(c_L,c_R)=(p+1,p+1)$ for primes $p\ge71$ with $p\equiv23\pmod{24}$. From Barnes-Wall lattices, we obtain an infinite family with gap four at $(c_L,c_R)=(2^m,2^m)$ for odd $m\ge7$. We also obtain two additional examples, with gap three at $(c_L,c_R)=(48,48)$ and gap four at $(c_L,c_R)=(512,512)$.

authors.name: Ziming Ji, Jiahua Tian

papers.title: Holographic Approaches to Hadron Structure
papers.summary: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. After an introduction to the string-theoretic foundations of holographic QCD, we review the predictions of top-down and bottom-up models for the phenomenology of mesons, baryons, and glueballs. We focus on the top-down model following from probe flavor branes in the Witten model of low-energy Yang-Mills theory and, in the more phenomenological approach of bottom-up models, mostly on minimal models based on five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, which also implement global symmetries and their anomalies consistently, but allow the high-energy behavior to better match real QCD.

authors.name: Luigi Cappiello, Anton Rebhan, Shigeki Sugimoto

papers.title: Astrophysical Constraints for Bosonic Dark Matter in and Around Quark Stars
papers.summary: We investigate the structure, stability, and mass-radius relations of compact stars composed of quark matter within the non-ideal MIT Bag Model mixed with self-interacting bosonic dark matter with a $\phi^n$ self-interaction potential. By solving the coupled two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations for boson masses between 200 MeV and 1 GeV and self-interaction strengths with $n=4$ and $n=40$, we show that strong self-interactions and higher boson masses enhance the stability of compact star configurations at high central pressures, though they reduce maximum overall masses. Ultra-compact solutions with $C \ge 1/3$ capable of mimicking black holes are significantly restricted compared to hadronic models, emerging only for strong self-interactions and dark matter fractions exceeding 90\%.
