We construct differential equations for the Feynman integrals which are polynomial in the dimensional regulator, and are suitable for numerical integration. We demonstrate stable numerical evaluations throughout the physical region relevant for low-energy experiments, despite the presence of large hierarchies of scales. Our results provide essential building blocks for NNLO predictions for radiative return processes.

authors.name: Mattia Pozzoli, William J. Torres Bobadilla

papers.title: Left-right symmetry breaking in $E_6^L\times E_6^R$ occurs only in spacetime -- with possible implications for strong $CP$
papers.summary: Two-sided octonionic $E_6^L\times E_6^R$ unification trinifies each factor and so carries two colour groups: the visible $SU(3)_c$ and a second $SU(3)_{c'}$ which, gauged like the first, would colour the charged lepton and must be suppressed by hand. We argue no such device is needed: the left-right symmetry acts in spacetime, not internally -- in the gravi-weak reading $SU(2)_R$ is the gravitational frame group and the exchange is ordinary parity on the Dirac field; a spacetime operation cannot double the internal colour. Colour is single and vector-like, $SU(3)_{c'}=SU(3)_c$, and the electron is a colour singlet. The right sector contributes one colour-blind datum, $\sqrt m$ (values: the exceptional-Jordan trace split, an input; $N_R$ fixes only the colour representation). An anomaly no-go shows that no gauged $U(1)$ on the visible fermions can carry the $\sqrt m$ pattern: the dark-electromagnetic $U(1)_{\rm dem}$ carries the parity mirror of electric charge on the dark sector, the visible fermions are dem-neutral, and no visible fifth force is predicted. Hypercharge is recovered as the consistency relation $Y=Q-T^3_L$, $Q=N/3$. As an application, parity restricts the QCD angle to $\{0,\pi\}$; $\theta_{\rm QCD}=0$ is selected, not derived, by matching to the sign content of the quark mass determinant, whose phase vanishes because the flavour rotors have real determinant. Hence $\bar\theta=0$ at tree level, conditional on the gravi-weak identification, with a nonzero CKM phase. Loop stability is open: the two-loop $\bar\theta$ of the minimal universal-seesaw parity model arises from scalar exchange, so the absence of a gauged $W_R$ here does not remove its mechanism, which the Higgs-bridge sector shares. We tag throughout what is derived, what is input, and what is open.

authors.name: Tejinder P. Singh

papers.title: Nonlinear particle detectors across the Rindler firewall
papers.summary: We investigate Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to composite observables of a quantum scalar field, including quadratic coupling to the field momentum and coupling to the local energy density. We develop a distributional framework for evaluating the corresponding detector response functions and apply it to detectors crossing the Rindler firewall. While we recover the finite response of the derivative-coupling model, we show that quadratic momentum coupling leads to products of distributions that do not admit a canonical, regulator-independent definition in the sharp-firewall idealization. The vacuum correspondence between the local energy-density and quadratic momentum responses motivates the conjecture that analogous difficulties may arise for energy-density coupling in the sharp firewall model. Within the sharp, pointlike composite-coupling model considered here, our analysis further suggests that these pathologies originate from the discontinuous severing of correlations across the Rindler horizon.

authors.name: Matheus H. Zambianco, Eduardo Mart\'in-Mart\'inez

papers.title: Inflation in unimodular loop quantum cosmology
papers.summary: We study inflation in the setting of unimodular loop quantum cosmology, where time evolution is defined in unimodular time rather than with respect to a free, massless scalar field as is standard in loop quantum cosmology. The unimodular setting leads to a natural Schr\"odinger time evolution in a time coordinate with clear geometric meaning, defined independently of any particular matter content; an inflaton can be included but is not needed as a clock. We review the unimodular version of loop quantum cosmology and comment on possible connections to full (unimodular) loop quantum gravity. Then, focusing on semiclassical effective equations, we derive analytical solutions in simple cases such as a constant potential, emphasising the use of a unimodular time coordinate. We also discuss numerical solutions for phenomenologically interesting cases such as a quadratic potential and Starobinsky inflation, comparing different possible choices of initial conditions. In particular, we show that choosing an $\alpha$-attractor potential allows for models of a bounce either dominated by kinetic or potential energy, which are compatible with observations while potentially including observable imprints of the quantum-gravity regime.

authors.name: Steffen Gielen, Rita B. Neves

papers.title: GOOFy-compatible 3HDMs and beyond
papers.summary: Beyond conventional Higgs-family and general CP transformations, one may also consider a broader class of non-standard "GOOFy" transformations, in which the scalar fields and their conjugates are assigned related but inequivalent transformations. Although these transformations are not symmetries of a full Lagrangian in the conventional sense, some nevertheless stabilise the scalar potential. Their impact on the quadratic sector has not yet been systematically classified. We develop a sign-orbit technique to determine the bilinear structures compatible with these transformations. Applied to three-Higgs-doublet models, and formulated so as to extend to larger multi-Higgs sectors, the method shows that a non-vanishing GOOFy-compatible quadratic sector exists only when two independent conditions are met: the underlying group admits a non-trivial sign character, and that character is realised within the tensor product of the scalar representation and its conjugate. As a key consequence, we demonstrate that the renormalisation-group stability of the $r_0 \to -r_0$ manifold in isolation is not a generic feature of multi-Higgs potentials, but rather a direct consequence of special algebraic properties of $SU(2)$. These results provide a classification of the admissible GOOFy quadratic structures and their invariant bilinear subspaces, highlighting the algebraic obstructions to their renormalisation-group stability.

authors.name: I. de Medeiros Varzielas, A. Kun\v{c}inas

papers.title: Quadratic effective energy--momentum tensor on uniform-density hypersurfaces during slow-roll inflation
papers.summary: We investigate the quadratic-order effective energy-momentum tensor (2EMT) of scalar cosmological perturbations on uniform-density hypersurfaces during slow-roll inflation. The 2EMT is a gauge-fixed effective source rather than a gauge-invariant observable. We impose the complete scalar gauge conditions $\delta\rho=0$ and $E=0$, express all perturbations in terms of the Bardeen potential $\Psi$, and distinguish the strict infrared and ultraviolet limits from the intermediate regimes. The uniform-density time shift differs from the comoving one by an explicitly gradient-suppressed term, $Q_{\mathrm{UD}}-Q_{\mathrm{C}}=-\Delta\Psi/[3{\mathcal H}({\mathcal H}'-{\mathcal H}^2)]$. The two sources vanish at zero gradient, while their first nonzero infrared coefficients differ and give $w_{\rm raw}\simeq-1/3$ at leading slow-roll order. In the intermediate infrared, all four gauges have this leading ratio, with gauge-dependent amplitudes. In the ultraviolet, the longitudinal, spatially-flat, and comoving gauges give $w_{\rm raw}\simeq1/3$, whereas the uniform-density gauge gives $w_{\rm raw}\simeq1$. The common $1/\epsilon$ enhancement of the matter-clock gauges reflects the slow evolution of their clocks; the additional uniform-density $1/\sigma_2^2$ enhancement originates from the Laplacian contribution to the density constraint. Neither enhancement is interpreted as a gauge-independent physical instability, and the gauge reconstruction must remain perturbatively small.

authors.name: Inyong Cho

papers.title: Gravitational waves flooding the Universe after wall domination
papers.summary: We discuss a possible early Universe scenario, where radiation era is interrupted by the epoch of domination of domain walls eventually annihilating into particles. During this period the Universe undergoes accelerated expansion, while the comoving correlation length of the domain wall network remains constant. The network serves as a source of tensor modes, which get frozen upon exiting the horizon similarly to the case of inflationary fluctuations. The modes re-enter the horizon during the subsequent stage of radiation domination and since then contribute to the gravitational wave background. The period of wall domination is manifested in the spectral shape of gravitational waves via a distinctive plateau replacing a peak, which is characteristic for the scenario with sub-dominant walls. The gravitational waves are strong enough to be observed with present-day and future facilities in a broad range of frequencies. In particular, their energy density is sufficient to produce a significant impact on the effective number of neutrino species, unless the duration of wall domination is suitably constrained.

authors.name: Sabir Ramazanov, Zhen-Min Zeng

papers.title: An Orbital Curvature for ISCOs
papers.summary: Building on the fact that circular orbits are the fixed points of the phase portraits arising from the geodesic equations on a black hole spacetime, we develop a general orbital geometry, which captures the stability structure of orbits. The construction uses the orbital energy, angular momentum and angular velocity as state space variables, with response functions encoding how the circular orbits react to changes in the black hole background and in their angular motion. The associated scalar curvature provides a geometric diagnostic of certain distinguished points of the circular orbit family, such as the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), where it becomes singular. Across the ISCO, the relevant orbital response functions change sign as the system passes from the stable to the unstable circular orbit branch, and are found to vanish at marginal stability. We illustrate the framework for Schwarzschild black holes in asymptotically flat four dimensions, and five dimensional Schwarzschild AdS spacetimes. In the four dimensional case, the ISCO is associated with a degeneration of the energy response sector, while in the five dimensional AdS case it is detected through the angular response. The AdS example also exhibits a separate curvature singularity at a point which coincides with the minimum temperature of the black hole background. These results show that the orbital geometry provides a promising unified framework for characterizing the stability of circular orbits and criticality of ISCOs.

authors.name: Poulami Mukherjee, Chandrasekhar Bhamidipati, Sudipta Mukherji

papers.title: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$
papers.summary: The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion. Both local and non-local integrals of motion act simultaneously on a shared Fock space consisting of $l+1$ free fields. We provide a direct, computational proof demonstrating that these local and non-local integrals of motion mutually commute.

authors.name: Michio Jimbo, Takeo Kojima

papers.title: 21 cm Cosmology of Boosted Dark Matter
papers.summary: The formation history of low-mass halos is sensitive to the properties of dark matter. At low redshift, nonlinear evolution and baryonic processes can obscure this information. The 21 cm signal provides access to a high-redshift stage of structure formation, when the abundance and clustering of low-mass halos retain direct sensitivity to the mass and interactions of dark matter. Boosted dark matter (BDM) realizes this possibility through a two-component scenario in which the annihilation of the heavier component converts part of the mass difference into kinetic energy of the lighter component. Self-interactions redistribute this energy and generate pressure support, suppressing small-scale density perturbations even for dark matter masses in the MeV range. We calculate the global 21 cm brightness temperature and its power spectrum in BDM cosmology. The reduced abundance of low-mass halos delays the global absorption feature and shifts the characteristic redshift evolution of the power spectrum. We assess the projected sensitivity of SKA1-Low to these signatures. The sensitivity is strongest at intermediate light-component fractions, where both components remain sufficiently abundant for self-heating to affect structure formation. For $\sigma_{\rm self1}/m_1\simeq0.1\,{\rm cm^2\,g^{-1}}$, models with $0.2\lesssim r_1\lesssim0.7$ can be distinguished from the fiducial $\Lambda$CDM prediction at the $95\%$ confidence level under the optimistic forecast. We compare our results with existing direct-detection bounds from SENSEI and prospects for BDM searches at large-volume neutrino experiments, including Super-/Hyper-Kamiokande, JUNO, and DUNE. This comparison highlights the unique and complementary role of high-redshift surveys in testing BDM models.

authors.name: Min Sub Lee, Jeong Han Kim, Kyoungchul Kong, Jong-Chul Park

papers.title: Feebly-Interacting Particle Searches
papers.summary: In the last several years, feebly-interacting particles (FIPs) have moved from "exotica" to the mainstream of particle physics. This development is fueled by three motivations: FIPs are one of two broad possibilities for new particles, FIPs are as well motivated by dark matter as WIMPs, and FIPs are connected to important problems in particle physics. I review these motivations and then briefly highlight recent progress in a few areas, including axion-like particles, dark photons and other gauge bosons, the X17 anomaly, quirks, and the Forward Physics Facility.

authors.name: Jonathan L. Feng

papers.title: Plugging the Pion Chimney
papers.summary: Heavy QCD axions and other gluon-coupled axion-like particles (ALPs) with masses from MeV to GeV are well motivated and have been searched for extensively. However, a window around the neutral pion mass, the so-called pion chimney, has escaped every search. There the ALP mixes strongly with the $\pi^0$ and therefore shares its experimental signatures. We show that the chimney can be closed with existing LHC data. The key point is that mixing changes the lifetimes of the two mass eigenstates but does not make them equal, and at LHC energies the states are boosted enough for the lifetime to decide whether they escape the detector or decay inside it. The ATLAS monojet search constrains the first case and the ATLAS inclusive photon measurement the second, and together they exclude the chimney up to the cutoff of the ALP effective theory. Above the cutoff, LHC searches for the colored states of the simplest ultraviolet completions exclude the rest. We also show that the bound from the $K^+$ width does not reach the chimney, because an ALP passes the same selection as a $\pi^0$, and we derive an independent, purely kinematic constraint from the measured $\pi^\pm$-$\pi^0$ mass splitting.

authors.name: Nikita Blinov, Andrew M. Evans, Shirley Weishi Li

papers.title: Supernova Bounds on Neutrino Dipole Moments from a Modern Perspective
papers.summary: Neutrinos may have nonstandard magnetic dipole moments $\mu_\nu$. In the dense cores of supernovae (SNe), these would convert part of the neutrinos into sterile, right-handed states through the electromagnetic fluctuations of the charged plasma. The streaming sterile neutrinos with 100-MeV energies can convert back to standard neutrinos in the Galactic magnetic field, leading to a high-energy neutrino flux unobserved from the historical SN 1987A. We reassess the production rates, including scattering on both protons and electrons, and, building upon advances in SN simulations and in the description of the Milky Way magnetic field, we revisit the bounds on magnetic dipole moments. We find for Dirac electron neutrinos $\mu_{\nu_e} \lesssim 4.8 \times 10^{-13} \mu_B$, superseding all existing terrestrial and astrophysical constraints.

authors.name: Damiano F. G. Fiorillo, Martina La Rosa, Federico Testagrossa, Edoardo Vitagliano

papers.title: Active Galactic Nuclei as Beyond the Standard Model Laboratories: a White Paper
papers.summary: Multi-messenger and multi-wavelength observations of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) can provide otherwise inaccessible knowledge about physics Beyond the Standard Model (BSM), and may even lead to its discovery. Realizing this potential hinges on two parallel efforts: advancing our understanding of AGN and of the dark matter around them, and identifying the BSM signatures that are at once promising and robust against the gaps in that understanding. These fields have attracted growing interest in recent years, also motivated by the IceCube association of neutrinos to individual AGN, yet we have only begun to explore their cross-fertilization. This white paper offers a new perspective on this interdisciplinary endeavor. It concisely reviews the state of the art in each field and at their interface, and identifies the key open questions that must be addressed to strengthen our prospects for learning about BSM physics with AGN.

authors.name: Gonzalo Herrera, Filippo Sala, Piero Ullio, Misty C. Bentz, Carlos Blanco, Roberto Caiozzo, Marina Cerme\~no, Matteo Cerruti, James M. Cline, Andrea Giovanni De Marchi, Pierfrancesco Di Cintio, Alessandro Granelli, R. Andrew Gustafson, Bradley J. Kavanagh, Cristina Lagunas Gualda, Kohta Murase, Takuya Okawa, Xavier Rodrigues, Lorenzo Ubaldi, Gabrijela Zaharijas

papers.title: Thermal Composite Dark Matter at LZ
papers.summary: We show that stable fermionic resonances of Composite Higgs models provide a thermal inelastic Dark Matter interpretation of the high-energy nuclear-recoil event LZ230616. Their stability follows from an exact accidental parity of the strong sector. Annihilation channels from composite interactions link the thermal relic mass to the strong coupling, allowing masses well beyond the pure electroweak prediction. We identify three scenarios in which the neutral states form a split pseudo-Dirac pair, distinguished by the origin of the inelastic coupling to the $Z$ boson. In the pure electroweak regime, the pair consists of the neutral components of a complex Higgsino-like doublet. Its unsuppressed inelastic $Z$ coupling requires Dark Matter masses above 20 TeV. In the pure strong regime, the suppressed $Z$ coupling of neutral states with vanishing hypercharge arises from strong interactions alone, allowing for smaller splittings and TeV-scale masses. In the third regime, which interpolates between the previous two, the neutral components of multiplets with different hypercharge are mixed. This enhances their inelastic coupling, accommodating the LZ event for masses of a few TeV and splittings around 300 keV, with mixing angles of order $10^\circ$. All three cases provide a thermal Dark Matter candidate able to explain the LZ event, consistently with the solar-capture bounds, the LZ high-energy sideband, and gamma-ray indirect searches.

authors.name: Dario Buttazzo, Andrea Di Lecce, Roberto Franceschini, Giulio Marino, Paolo Panci

papers.title: Smuggling baryon asymmetry through strong washout
papers.summary: We propose a scheme in which a primordial net baryon number generated at or around the unification scale may survive subsequent strong washout phases associated with active sphalerons and interactions of right-handed neutrinos inherent to thermal leptogenesis. A simple realization of this, namely, a long-lived scalar population injecting the net $B-L$ it carries into the Standard Model matter sector late enough to be safe from a strong washout, is constructed and studied in the context of a simple Pati-Salam scalar sector with a heavy $SU(4)_C$ sextet scalar.

authors.name: K{\aa}re Fridell, Michal Malinsk\'y, Javier Perez-Soler

papers.title: Perturbative QCD Analysis for the Electric Dipole Moment of $\Xi$ and $\Sigma$ Hyperons from CP-Violating Dipole Interactions
papers.summary: Hyperon electric dipole moments (EDMs) probe CP-violating interactions beyond the Standard Model. Motivated by the recent BESIII measurement [Ablikim et al., Science 393, 1027] and the perturbative QCD analysis of the $\Lambda$ EDM form factor $d_\Lambda$ [Chen et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 051902], we extend the perturbative QCD calculation of the EDM form factor to the $\Xi$ and $\Sigma$ hyperons. We derive factorization formulas from quark EDM and chromoelectric dipole moment contributions in terms of leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs). Using lattice-QCD results for the LCDAs and the strange-quark dipole moment ranges inferred from the BESIII $d_\Lambda$ bound and neutron EDM constraints, we obtain the conditional estimates $-4.8 \times 10^{-18} < d_{\Xi^-} < 1.8\times10^{-18}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $-6.1\times10^{-19} < d_{\Sigma^+} < 2.4\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ at the scale of ${J/\psi}$ mass. Dedicated searches at BESIII and the future Super Tau-Charm Factory could further constrain these quark-level sources of CP violation.

authors.name: Xi-Yu Mu, Kai-Bao Chen, Jian-Ping Ma, Xuan-Bo Tong

papers.title: Analytic next-to-leading order electroweak corrections to Higgs boson pair production in the forward limit
papers.summary: We calculate next-to-leading order electroweak corrections for Higgs boson pair production in the gluon fusion channel, in the forward limit. We perform an analytic calculation and obtain a final result for the partonic cross section that depends explicitly on all kinematic parameters and particle masses. We describe our method, which can be readily applied to similar processes. We observe rapid convergence within the validity range of the forward expansion. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the entire phase space can be covered when this approach is combined with the high-energy expansion.

authors.name: Joshua Davies, Dominik Grau, Kay Sch\"onwald, Matthias Steinhauser, Daniel Stremmer

papers.title: $B\to K a$ decays in QCD factorization and revised bounds on ALP couplings
papers.summary: Rare flavor-changing processes such as $B\to K a$ offer sensitive probes of axion-like particles (ALPs) for masses below a few GeV. We study this process in the framework of QCD factorization and ALP effective theory, in which the ALP couples to the Standard Model (SM) fermions through shift-invariant derivative interactions. In contrast to previous studies, where flavor violation arises solely from flavor-changing ALP couplings, we also include the contributions proportional to flavor-conserving ALP couplings, in which the flavor change is mediated by the weak interactions of the SM. Based on this analysis, we derive upper bounds on both flavor-changing and flavor-conserving ALP couplings at low energies. Then we consider the UV scenario of a "minimally flavor-violating ALP", which features flavor-universal ALP-fermion couplings at very high energies, and evaluate the resulting constraints on the UV couplings.

authors.name: Upalaparna Banerjee, Cristhian Calderon, Matthias Neubert

papers.title: Probing $\tau$ lepton dipole moments at multi-TeV muon colliders
papers.summary: We investigate the sensitivity of future multi-TeV muon colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $\tau$ lepton within the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We consider $\tau^+\tau^-$ production through $\mu^+\mu^-$ annihilation and vector-boson scattering, electroweak-boson-associated $\tau$ production, and the radiative Higgs decay $H\to\tau^+\tau^-\gamma$. At high energies, the dipole-induced contributions quadratic in the Wilson coefficients become particularly important, with associated Higgs production, $\mu^+\mu^-\to\tau^+\tau^-H$, providing the strongest sensitivity through energy-enhanced contact interactions. The remaining channels offer complementary probes of the underlying dipole operators. For a $10$~TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, we obtain combined sensitivities at the nominal $95\%$ confidence level of $|\Delta a_\tau|<1.2\times10^{-5}$, $|d_\tau|<6.6\times10^{-20}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$, $|\Delta a_\tau^Z|<1.8\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_\tau^Z|<1.0\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$. Compared with FCC-ee projections, the muon collider offers substantially stronger sensitivity to the electric dipole moments, while both facilities offer complementary probes of magnetic dipole moments. These results motivate further studies incorporating realistic detector effects and systematic uncertainties.

authors.name: Dario Buttazzo, Gabriele Levati, Yang Ma, Fabio Maltoni, Paride Paradisi, ZeQiang Wang

papers.title: Double parton scattering singularities in two-loop gluon-fusion amplitudes
papers.summary: Gluon fusion to two massive colour singlets can develop a double parton scattering (DPS) singularity as $p_T\to0$: each gluon splits, and its daughters fuse pairwise. We determine two-loop logarithms using a common kernel and derive finite matching functions analytically for gluon and quark splittings. Normalised to one loop, the cubic coefficient changes sign between channels. Complete $gg\to HH$, $gg\to AA$ and $gg\to ZZ$ amplitudes confirm the predicted colour, helicity and parity dependence and phase. The kernel gives leading DPS logarithms for other pairs with this DPS configuration.

authors.name: Arunima Bhattacharya

papers.title: Flavor Entanglement as a CPT Violation Witness in Neutrino Oscillations

authors.name: Bipin Singh Koranga, Biswmkwr Boro, Vivek Kumar Nautiyal

papers.title: Top-Quark Physics after Evidence for Toponium
papers.summary: The top quark decays before it hadronizes, and toponium, the t\bar t bound state, was long thought unobservable as a resonance. CMS and ATLAS each report an excess of top-quark pairs at threshold, above five standard deviations over fixed-order quantum chromodynamics (QCD), and CMS confirms it in a second decay channel. Its angular distributions match the color-singlet pseudoscalar quasi-bound state \eta_t of nonrelativistic QCD, although an additional pseudoscalar boson is not excluded and higher-order fixed-order QCD accounts for part of the enhancement. We review the theory, ATLAS's nominal Green's-function signal model, and the measurements, whose cross sections range from about 3 to 13 pb. Part of the spread comes from the signal model and part persists between analyses using the same model. We discuss consequences for entanglement, the top mass, and heavy-pseudoscalar searches. We then review the top-quark program, from mass definitions to electroweak precision, flavor, the charge-conjugation and parity (CP) structure of the top Yukawa coupling, supersymmetry, multi-top production, and effective field theory. We close with prospects at the High-Luminosity LHC and future colliders, where an e^+e^- threshold scan can determine the top-quark mass in a short-distance scheme to a few tens of MeV.

authors.name: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger

papers.title: Triangle singularity with different dynamical couplings
papers.summary: We carry out a systematic study of the impact of dynamical couplings of the vertices on the manifestations of the triangle singularity (TS) in the loop amplitude. Twelve combinations of external and internal spin-parity quantum numbers, covering the $PPS$, $VPP$, $VVP$, $VPA$, $VVV$, $VVA$, and $VVS$ effective vertices, are enumerated. Each loop amplitude is reduced via the Passarino--Veltman decomposition into scalar integrals $A_{0}$, $B_{0}$, and $C_{0}$, whose Lorentz-scalar coefficients encode the dynamical content of the vertices. Using the masses and kinematics of the $\eta(1405)\to\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$ transition via the $K^{*}\bar{K}K$ loop with the intermediate $f_{0}(980)$ resonance in the $\pi^+\pi^-$ invariant spectrum as a common numerical benchmark for the twelve spin-parity assignments, we find that the same loop topology produces three distinct phenomena which manifest through the lineshapes, i.e. a narrow peak dominated by the $C_{0}$ contribution; a suppressed peak in which the $B_{0}$ and $C_{0}$ function contributions are comparable; and a cusp-like profile in which the coefficient of the leading Landau logarithm vanishes at the physical TS point. These results indicate that the visibility of a TS enhancement is not fixed by the Landau condition alone but reshaped by the detailed dynamics involved in the loop transitions.

authors.name: Jun Wang, Xiao-Hai Liu, Qiang Zhao

papers.title: An exact separability criterion for the $J/\psi\Lambda$ spin state in $\Lambda_b^0\to J/\psi\,\Lambda$ decays at the LHC
papers.summary: We derive an exact separability criterion for the spin state of the $J/\psi\Lambda$ pair produced in $\Lambda_b^0\to J/\psi(\to\mu^+\mu^-)\,\Lambda(\to p\pi^-)$ decays, taking into account the $\Lambda_b^0$ polarization at the LHC. Within the four-amplitude family $\{a_\pm,b_\pm\}$, the system is separable if and only if $(1+P_b\cos\theta)a_+b_+=(1-P_b\cos\theta)a_-b_-=P_b\sin\theta b_+b_-=0$, where $\theta$ is the $\Lambda$ production angle defined in the LHC environment. We propose a profiled likelihood ratio test to probe entanglement in the full five-dimensional angular analysis. Idealized pseudoexperiments compare this test with a negativity test and a test based on the angular moments $M_7$ and $M_9$ for rejecting the $a_+=b_-=0$ hypothesis. At both $3\sigma$ and $5\sigma$ significance, the proposed test achieves a $90\%$ rejection power with about half as many signal events as the other two methods. These results support the prospects for entanglement evidence with samples on the existing scale and for observation with larger samples.

authors.name: Yujie Li, Xiaofan Hu, Liming Zhang

papers.title: Millicharged Fermions as Dark Matter: Theoretical Modeling and Experimental Detection
papers.summary: Fermions with a small effective charge, $\qeff\ll1$, arise from kinetic mixing between an unbroken (or nearly unbroken) dark $U(1)'$ and electromagnetism, or from a genuinely fractional charge. Millicharged particles (mCPs) inherit the Pauli-exclusion constraints on fermionic dark matter (DM) in galaxies, while adding a long-range plasma phenomenology absent for neutral candidates. This review connects three strands: (i) the symmetry structure, cosmology and astrophysical bounds of millicharged fermions, comparing kinetic-mixing and fractional-charge realizations; (ii) the role of mCPs in galactic halo formation and dynamics, and when they fit the Ruffini--Arg\"uelles--Rueda (RAR) self-gravitating core--halo model; and (iii) experimental techniques for detecting mCPs trapped on Earth, arriving from the galactic halo, or emitted by the Sun. We show that a collisionless halo of keV--MeV millicharged fermions requires $\alpha'\lesssim7\times10^{-13}$--$2\times10^{-10}$, depending on mass and velocity, orders of magnitude below the coupling needed for thermal freeze-out via $\chi\bar\chi\to A'A'$ in the Milky Way and dwarf galaxies. A RAR halo made of the mCP itself thus needs non-thermal production, a charge-symmetric plasma and very small dark coupling, whereas a sub-dominant mCP component can be added without changing the halo. We close with open theoretical and experimental challenges and a summary of the allowed mCP parameter space.

authors.name: Momchil Naydenov

papers.title: Universal Mass Equation for Equal-Quantum Excited-States Sets~III
papers.summary: Using our simple logarithmic Universal Mass Equation, we considered heavy non-$q\bar{q}$ meson states. PDG2026 reported a series of mesons with quantum numbers not allowed for standard $q\bar{q}$ states. Using LQCD predictions, we evaluated a scalar $0^{++}$ and tensor $2^{++}$ glueball series for which predictions are available. This approach allows us to predict heavy states that require future experimental studies. Additionally, we consider the possible misidentification of some meson states.

authors.name: L. David Roper (VTech), Igor Strakovsky (GWU)

papers.title: Loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ at NLO+PS for LHC simulations: exact, fast scale and PDF event weights, theory uncertainties, and the limits of rescaled LO+PS
papers.summary: We study loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ production with charged-lepton and neutrino $Z$ decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD matched to parton showers, using public software at $\sqrt{s}=13$ and 13.6 TeV. An exact loop-amplitude cache reduces event-generation time by a factor of 26 with 450 scale and PDF weights, while Born suppression improves boosted-event statistics without changing the weighted prediction. We present inclusive results for both channels and charged-lepton differential and STXS Stage 1.3 predictions with theory uncertainties. At 13.6 TeV, fixed-order top-quark mass-scheme variations transferred to NLO+PS dominate the statistically precise central-Higgs STXS bins for $p_\mathrm{T}^V\ge150$ GeV, reaching 32-50%. An inclusive $K$ factor does not reproduce the boosted and jet-dependent NLO+PS spectra of the tested LO+PS samples, and the differences depend strongly on the shower prescription. For specified CMS- and ATLAS-style vetoed sources at 13.6 TeV, we construct separate charged-lepton and neutrino corrections using ensembles of gradient-boosted classifiers, with calibration, target-theory variations and transfer uncertainties. Independent tests show substantial improvement over inclusive rescaling in most tested distributions, but not uniform closure. In charged-lepton calibration comparisons, the median STXS uncertainty from transported NLO scales and transfer terms is 17% for both the CMS- and ATLAS-style corrections, compared with LO scale uncertainties of 28% and 26% at fixed $K$. These comparisons do not include the complete target-theory budget. The corrections do not restore the depleted hard-recoil population; the highest ATLAS-style $p_\mathrm{T}^H$ bin stays below NLO+PS even at the upper edge of its band. The setup, reference results, and source- and channel-specific models support new NLO+PS generation and reuse of existing samples within stated limits.

authors.name: Licheng Zhang, Christopher Palmer

papers.title: Imprints of Non-local Top-Higgs Interaction on Loop Induced Higgs Processes
papers.summary: A composite Higgs arising from an underlying strong sector generally has non-local interactions with the elementary sector, formulated in terms of momentum-dependent form factors. We construct the minimal Ball-Chiu-type vertices consistent with gauge-invariant non-local $\bar{t}th$ couplings containing Wilson lines, where recursive Ward-Takahashi identities connect the Yukawa interaction to higher-order contact interactions. For a symmetric monopole form factor motivated by lowest-resonance dominance, we compute the top-loop contributions to $gg \to h$ and $h \to \gamma\gamma$ amplitudes in closed form, and demonstrate a logarithmically enhanced deviation from the Standard Model. Current measurements at the LHC exclude the characteristic new physics scale below 3.6 TeV at $2\sigma$, while future colliders could extend the sensitivity to approximately 8 TeV.

authors.name: Avik Banerjee, Rohan Pramanick, Tirtha Sankar Ray

papers.title: Analytic Two-Loop Classical Bremsstrahlung Amplitude in Electrodynamics
papers.summary: We compute the leading long-wavelength term of the two-loop five-point amplitude for photon emission in the scattering of two massive spinless charges. Classical consistency suggests that two Coulomb exchanges dress the radiative tree amplitude. We show that this iteration accounts for the entire leading term and evaluate the resulting convolution. At fixed external transfer, the exchanges shift the momentum in the tree numerator, thereby changing the relative weights of its two polarization structures. We determine both coefficients at nonzero photon frequency and general relative velocity, with exact dependence on the spacetime dimension.

authors.name: Xinguang Chen, Zhengwen Liu, Rourou Ma, Yu Wu, Yang Zhang

papers.title: Electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks in a coupled-channel unitary approach
papers.summary: We study the electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks $P_c(4312)$, $P_c(4440)$ and $P_c(4457)$ and of their four heavy-quark spin partners, treated as $\bar D^{(*)}\Sigma_c^{(*)}$ hadronic molecules. The states are poles of a coupled-channel unitary amplitude with a vector-meson exchange kernel that respects heavy-quark spin symmetry. The form factors are the residues at the double pole of the photon-coupled amplitude. The current consists of one-body currents and a photon--four-hadron vertex, which we construct for this channel space. Its gauged-kernel part ensures the charge normalization through the compositeness sum rule, while its contact parts contain couplings that the model does not determine. For $J^P=\tfrac12^-$, $\tfrac12^-$, $\tfrac32^-$ and pointlike constituents, the mean squared distances between the constituents of the three observed states are $0.85-0.47i$, $0.35-0.18i$ and $1.76-0.57i\,\mathrm{fm}^2$. Within $2\%$, they equal the zero-range value $1/(4\mu_{\rm red} B_c)$, with reduced mass $\mu_{\rm red}$ and complex binding energy $B_c$, times the effective-range factor of the amplitude. The real parts of the magnetic moments are $1.7$, $-0.9$ and $1.3\,\mu_N$, within $11\%$ of the additive moments of the constituents. Variations of the constituent moments and of the magnetic contact couplings within bounds from dimensional analysis give the ranges $0.8$ to $2.0$, $-1.3$ to $-0.2$ and $0.2$ to $1.8\,\mu_N$. The charge radii depend also on the constituent structure and on electric contact currents. The photon loops of open channels have a triangle singularity at spacelike momentum transfer. We specify the analytic continuation of the residue in $Q^2$ and give the difference between its two adjacent branches in closed form.

authors.name: Nongnapat Ponkhuha, Ratirat Suntharawirat, Daris Samart

papers.title: Bayesian Multimessenger Constraints on Self-Bound Quark Stars in Revised Perturbative QCD
papers.summary: We perform a Bayesian multimessenger analysis of self-bound two-flavor $ud$ quark matter described by a thermodynamically consistent revised perturbative-QCD equation of state (EOS), incorporating the GW170817 tidal information, mass--radius measurements, and pulsar mass constraints. The resulting posterior medians and $68\%$ credible intervals are $B_0^{1/4}=137.66^{+1.72}_{-1.86}\,\mathrm{MeV}$, $M_{\max}=2.166^{+0.035}_{-0.036}\,M_\odot$, $R_{1.4}=11.778^{+0.203}_{-0.196}\,\mathrm{km}$, and $\Lambda_{1.4}=768^{+90}_{-81}$. The posterior-predictive support probability for interpreting the $2.59\,M_\odot$ GW190814 secondary as a self-bound $ud$ quark star is of order $10^{-5}$, strongly disfavoring this interpretation within the adopted EOS framework. The reconstructed EOS exhibits characteristic self-bound behavior, with finite energy and baryon number densities at the zero-pressure surface and a median surface energy density of $\epsilon_{\rm surf}\simeq187\,\mathrm{MeV\,fm^{-3}}$. Its pressure is suppressed relative to both the noninteracting $ud+e$ gas and the representative MIT bag-model prediction. Although the running strong coupling decreases with increasing quark chemical potential, its central value in maximum-mass configurations correlates positively with $M_{\max}$, indicating stronger coupling and reduced perturbative reliability toward the high-mass end. Notably, the squared speed of sound remains nearly constant, varying from $c_s^2\simeq0.321$ to $0.324$ between canonical and maximum-mass configurations, whereas the conformal measure $\Delta=1/3-P/\epsilon$ decreases substantially from approximately $0.208$ to $0.076$. This demonstrates that an approximately constant sound speed does not necessarily imply approximate conformality. The relativistic adiabatic index also increases sharply near the zero-pressure surface, reflecting the self-bound nature of the EOS.

authors.name: Shu-Peng Wang, Ju-Xiang Li, Zhen-Yan Lu, Zhi-Jun Ma, Zhen Zhang, Qi Lu

papers.title: Mapping the multimessenger horizon for $\gamma$-ray counterparts of cosmic neutrinos
papers.summary: The joint detection of high-energy neutrinos and $\gamma$-rays offers a powerful probe of the most energetic astrophysical accelerators, linking hadronic interactions to observable signatures across cosmic distances. Understanding the conditions under which these two messengers can be simultaneously observed is essential for identifying and characterizing the sources of cosmic neutrinos. In this work, we examine the detectability of $\gamma$-ray cascades associated with neutrino production in source environments that are gamma-ray transparent, focusing on how electromagnetic cascades evolve as $\gamma$-rays propagate through intergalactic space. By modeling photon interactions with the extragalactic background light and deflections in intergalactic magnetic fields, we determine the minimum neutrino fluence for transient emission and neutrino flux for steady emission required to produce a $\gamma$-ray counterpart detectable by $\gamma$-ray observatories, such as Fermi-LAT, HAWC, or LHAASO. This defines a ``multimessenger horizon" -- the region in flux-distance parameter space where neutrinos and $\gamma$-rays are jointly observable. We consider both energy-binned injection tied to IceCube's sensitivity and a continuous power-law spectrum extending from TeV to PeV energies. Our results reveal that detectability depends strongly on redshift, magnetic field strength, and photon energy, with higher-energy cascades suffering greater attenuation inside filamentary structures. The framework provides new constraints on source opacity, baryon loading, and neutrino production mechanisms, offering a predictive tool for interpreting current events and guiding future multimessenger campaigns.

authors.name: Tianyi Ding, Jose Alonso Carpio, Ali Kheirandish, Kohta Murase

papers.title: A Forecast for Testing the Decreasing $H_0$ Trend in Time-Delay Cosmography
papers.summary: In 2019 the H0LiCOW/TDCOSMO collaboration reported a decreasing Hubble constant $H_0$ trend with lens redshift in the flat $\Lambda$CDM model at low statistical significance ($< 2 \sigma$). The signal is expected if physics is missing from the $\Lambda$CDM model in the late universe. In the wake of recent TDCOSMO 2026 results, we revisit the feature. Although the statistical significance of the trend has increased in a like-for-like comparison with earlier studies, propagating mass-sheet transformation (MST) uncertainties reduces the significance to $\sim 1 \sigma$. As a result, Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) currently favours a constant $H_0$ over a decreasing $H_0$ in the ratio 2.4:1. Nevertheless, we highlight good agreement on a negative slope with independent observables and forecast that approximately 40 and 90 lenses will be required to substantiate the trend at $\sim 2 \sigma$ and $\sim 3 \sigma$ significance, respectively, if the feature is physical and current uncertainties are representative. Even now, it is evident that the TDCOSMO 2026 $H_0$ constraint $H_0 \approx 71$ km/s/Mpc reflects an average over the lens redshift distribution and is naturally anchored at intermediate lens redshifts.

authors.name: Shane Brady, Eoin \'O Colg\'ain, M. M. Sheikh-Jabbari

papers.title: Gravitational waves from cosmological first-order phase transitions with fluctuation-induced friction
papers.summary: We study gravitational-wave production in a cosmological first-order phase transition with fluctuation-induced friction using three-dimensional lattice simulations of two coupled scalar fields. Kinetic and gradient energy in the additional field $s$ accumulates near the expanding bubble walls of $\phi$ and affects their motion. The contribution from $s$ exceeds that from $\phi$ at the spectral peak and has a slope similar to that of the bulk flow model over a finite interval above the peak. In the high-wave-number (UV) direction, $\phi$ dominates and the total spectrum develops a broad feature. For the larger coupling, slowly contracting false vacuum remnants persist long after bubble merger.

authors.name: Jun-Ye Chen, Dongdong Wei, Zong-Kuan Guo

papers.title: Effects of QCD Equation of State on Cosmological Parameters and Stochastic Gravitational-Waves Spectrum
papers.summary: We investigate the thermodynamic evolution of the early Universe across the QCD crossover and up to the electroweak (EW) scale, emphasizing the systematic impact of the QCD equation of state (EoS) and electroweak degrees of freedom on thermodynamic variables, cosmological parameters, and gravitational-wave observables. Using the HotQCD EoS as a baseline, we employ Gaussian Process (GP) regression to generate ensembles of 1000 thermodynamically consistent EoS samples, each extrapolated to high temperatures with and without EW contributions. For each ensemble, we solve the Friedmann equations to obtain the expansion history and compute gravitational-wave (GW) observables, including the instantaneous spectral tilt $n_{gw}(f)$ and the normalized GW energy density $\Omega_{gw}(f)/\Omega_{gw}^{\rm rad}$. We find that including the EW sector is the dominant effect across all observables, outweighing differences among QCD baseline models that share the same lattice calibration. In particular, EW contributions drive the EoS toward the radiation-dominated limit earlier, reduce excursions of the speed of sound toward the causality bound, suppress transient fluctuations in the Hubble and kinematic parameters near $t \sim 10^{-5}$ s, and qualitatively change the GW spectrum from a strongly frequency-dependent signal to a flat, suppressed plateau. These results demonstrate that accurate modeling of the electroweak sector is essential for an unbiased extraction of QCD-era physics from the stochastic gravitational-wave background.

authors.name: Andr\'e V. Giannini, Victor P. Gon\c{c}alves, Samuel M. Sanches Jr

papers.title: How can every physicist become a Bohmian
papers.summary: The Bohmian interpretation of quantum mechanics is controversial because it attributes deterministic trajectories to microscopic particles. We propose a reformulation that sidesteps this controversy: rather than applying Bohmian mechanics at the microscopic level, we recast it as an effective deterministic description of the macroscopic pointer of a measuring apparatus, with no claims about the fundamental nature of the microscopic world. In this form, the Bohmian trajectory becomes a practical tool for visualizing the emergence of a definite measurement outcome, broadly acceptable to physicists who would otherwise reject the Bohmian program.

authors.name: Hrvoje Nikoli\'c

papers.title: Flavor-dependent quark-mass scaling and the fate of the strange-matter window in self-bound quark stars
papers.summary: In the flavor-dependent QMDD model, self-bound $ud$ quark matter can be the ground state at vanishing pressure and convert into $uds$ matter through a first-order transition. So far the mass functional has used parameters $(a,C)$ common to all flavors; here we let the strange sector have its own coupling, $C_s=\alpha\,C_{u,d}$, and map the response of the zero-pressure parameter space. The $e^0_{ud}=930\,$MeV boundary is independent of $\alpha$ by construction, whereas increasing $\alpha$ enlarges the self-bound $ud$ domain and pushes the $e^0_{ud}=e^0_{uds}$ line towards larger $a$. The causality boundary $c^0_s=c$ is almost frozen near $a\simeq5.5$. The competition closes the strange-matter window at \RA{$\alpha_{\rm crit}\simeq1.136$}: above it every causal self-bound parametrization is $ud$ at zero pressure, so a first-order $ud\!\to\!uds$ transition must occur at higher pressure, though not necessarily inside a star, since the maximum mass may be reached below the transition density. The transition pressure and the energy-density jump grow monotonically with $\alpha$, both scale \RB{approximately} with the available-volume fraction $q=1-\kappa$, and the Seidov onset-instability diagnostic stays below unity.

authors.name: G. Teruya, G. Lugones, A. G. Grunfeld

papers.title: Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization. II. Updated constraints and forecasts for the Simons Observatory and LiteBIRD
papers.summary: We update the constraints on Lorentz-violating electrodynamics from the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Within the minimal Standard Model Extension, we consider the renormalizable CPT-odd and CPT-even operators of the photon sector, which source cosmic birefringence and circular polarization, respectively. Combining Planck, Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and South Pole Telescope (SPT) temperature and $E$-mode data with $B$-mode measurements from BICEP/Keck, SPT-3G D1 and SPTpol, we constrain the CPT-odd coefficients to $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|<7.75\times10^{-45}$ GeV and $|\mathbf{k_{AF}}|<3.82\times10^{-45}$ GeV at 95% credible level. These are the strongest bounds to date from any probe, and are driven by the SPT-3G D1 $B$-mode data. For the first time in this type of analysis, we also include the Planck PR4 $EB$ spectrum, which yields a mild preference for a non-zero $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|$. For the CPT-even coefficient, we find $k_{F,E+B}<5.99\times10^{-32}$. Including the latest circular polarization measurements from the Cosmology Large Angular Scale Surveyor (CLASS) tightens this bound by about 7%. This is the first time that CMB circular polarization data contribute to constraining this coefficient. Finally, we forecast the sensitivity of the Simons Observatory (SO) and LiteBIRD. With linear polarization only, the two experiments are complementary, with SO tightening the CPT-even bound by about 30% and LiteBIRD the CPT-odd ones by 40 to 45%. Exploiting the sensitivity to circular polarization provided by the non-idealities of its half-wave plate, LiteBIRD could also improve the CPT-even bound by more than an order of magnitude.

authors.name: Margherita Lembo, Luca Caloni, Martina Gerbino, Serena Giardiello, Giulia Gubitosi, Massimiliano Lattanzi, Luca Pagano, Nicol\`o Raffuzzi

papers.title: Global Fit of Modified Quark Couplings to EW Gauge Bosons and Vector-Like Quarks in Light of the Cabibbo Angle Anomaly
papers.summary: There are two tensions related to the Cabibbo angle of the CKM matrix. First, the determinations of $V_{us}$ from $K_{\mu 2}$, $K_{\ell3}$, and $\tau$ decays disagree at the $3\sigma$ level. Second, using the average of these results in combination with $\beta$ decays (including super-allowed $\beta$ decays and neutron decay), a deficit in first-row CKM unitarity with a significance of again about $3\sigma$ is found. These discrepancies, known as the Cabibbo Angle anomaly, can in principle be solved by modifications of $W$ boson couplings to quarks. However, due to $SU(2)_L$ invariance, $Z$ couplings to quarks are also modified and flavour changing neutral currents can occur. In order to consistently assess the agreement of a new physics hypothesis with data, we perform a combined analysis for all dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory operators that generate modified $W$ couplings to first and second generation quarks. We then study models with vector-like quarks, which are prime candidates for a corresponding UV completion as they can affect $W$-quark couplings at tree level, and we perform a global fit including flavour observables (in particular loop effects in $\Delta F=2$ processes). We find that the best fit can be obtained for the $SU(2)_L$ doublet vector-like quark $Q$ as it can generate right-handed $W$-$u$-$d$ and $W$-$u$-$s$ couplings as preferred by data.

authors.name: Andreas Crivellin, Matthew Kirk, Teppei Kitahara, Federico Mescia

papers.title: Transverse Energy--Energy Correlators at Small $x$ for Photon--Hadron Production
papers.summary: We study the transverse energy--energy correlator (TEEC) observable in photon--hadron and photon--jet production in p+p and p+A collisions at small $x$. We derive the relevant expressions in the high-energy limit of the scattering where the dipole picture is applicable and show how the dependence on the fragmentation function of the hadron cancels due to the momentum-sum rule. The nonperturbative scattering with the target nucleus is expressed in terms of the dipole amplitude, which also describes nonlinear gluon saturation effects. The TEEC observable is computed in the RHIC and LHC kinematics, and we show that it can be sensitive to the dipole amplitude, making it a potentially good observable for studying saturation effects.

authors.name: Zhong-Bo Kang, Robert Kao, Meijian Li, Jani Penttala

papers.title: Machine Learning in the Hunt for Charged Higgs Bosons at Gamma-Gamma Colliders in the Type III Two Higgs Doublet Model
papers.summary: We study charged Higgs boson pair production, $\gamma\gamma\to H^{+}H^{-}$, in the Type-III Two-Higgs-Doublet Model (2HDM-III) for $100\leq M_{H^{\pm}}\leq190~\text{GeV}$ at a $\gamma\gamma$ collider with $\sqrt{s}=3~\text{TeV}$ and $\mathcal{L}_{int}=3000~\text{fb}^{-1}$. Two benchmark points, BP1 ($\tan\beta=10$, $\cos(\beta-\alpha)=-0.2$) and BP2 ($\tan\beta=20$, $\cos(\beta-\alpha)=-0.1$), are chosen in agreement with theoretical constraints, flavor-physics data and the signal strengths of the $125~\text{GeV}$ Higgs boson. The total width of $H^{\pm}$ is $10^{-4}$--$10^{-1}~\text{GeV}$, i.e. a narrow resonance, and $\mathrm{BR}(H^{+}\to\tau\nu_{\tau})$ falls from $4.6\times10^{-3}$ (BP1) and $2.9\times10^{-4}$ (BP2) at $100~\text{GeV}$ to $1.8\times10^{-4}$ and $1.2\times10^{-5}$ at $190~\text{GeV}$. The $\tau\nu_{\tau}$ and $tb$ final states are analyzed with four TMVA classifiers (BDT, MLP, Likelihood and LikelihoodD) using $1.0\times10^{5}$ generated events per process. For $171$ signal and $604$ background events, the MLP and BDT reach AUC values of $0.934$ and $0.933$ and maximum significances $S/\sqrt{S+B}$ of $9.86$ and $9.82$, compared with $0.870$ and $8.54$ for LikelihoodD and $0.815$ and $7.55$ for Likelihood. The preselection cuts raise the significance by only $0.09$--$0.91\%$, depending on the classifier. The quoted significances are statistical; systematic uncertainties are not included.

authors.name: Abdul Quddus, Ijaz Ahmed, Jamil Muhammad, M. A. Arroyo-Ure

papers.title: Photo- and Hadrodisintegration constraints on massive relics decaying into neutrinos
papers.summary: We perform a detailed study of the cosmological constraints on the decay of a relic particle $\phi$ into neutrinos, $\phi \rightarrow \nu \bar{\nu}$, in particular those arising from the observed light-element abundances in the early Universe. We focus on the late-time disintegration of the light elements previously synthesised during BBN. Several processes are relevant, including final-state radiation associated with the decay, as well as subsequent interactions of the injected neutrinos with the thermal background neutrinos or between themselves. All processes generically contribute to the production of electromagnetic and often also hadronic material and may therefore induce late-time photodisintegration and hadrodisintegration reactions, i.e.~the destruction of light elements that have previously been formed during BBN. Here, we examine this scenario with a Monte-Carlo inspired probabilistic approach rather than Boltzmann techniques, taking into account all of these different reactions as well as their interplay. We find the resulting constraints to be very significant, covering a broad range of previously unexplored masses and lifetimes of the relic source particle.

authors.name: Sara Bianco, Paul Frederik Depta, Jonas Frerick, Thomas Hambye, Marco Hufnagel, Kai Schmidt-Hoberg

papers.title: Keeping It Renormalizable: Minimal Baryogenesis induced Asymmetric Dark Matter
papers.summary: Many asymmetric dark matter scenarios have been proposed to date. Among them, perhaps the most motivated ones are those in which the dark matter asymmetry is induced from the baryon/lepton asymmetries via chemical equilibration without any new sources of CP violation. However, most of the models put forward along these lines have been excluded by now and/or are based on complicated setups. In this letter, we present a new, simple, and viable scenario. It assumes only two new fields: a scalar singlet and an inert scalar doublet, and is based only on renormalizable interactions, that slowly generate the dark matter asymmetry from the Standard Model Higgs asymmetry. The successful asymmetry transfer requires small (but technically natural) couplings which in turn make the model CP conserving in practice. The model allows for the direct detection of dark matter in the upcoming generation of experiments, and the inert doublet is predicted to be light enough to be potentially produced and observed at the LHC and future colliders, $46\,{\rm GeV}<m_{H'}<580\,{\rm GeV}$. Quite remarkably, the mass and lifetime of the inert doublet may be inferred from direct detection experiments, indicating long-lived compressed electroweak states that can be searched for at the HL-LHC.

authors.name: Miguel Escudero, Thomas Hambye, Chandan Hati

papers.title: Study of $CP$ violation in $\Lambda_b^0\rightarrow N^*M$ decays with the final-state rescattering mechanism
papers.summary: In this work, we investigate the charmless nonleptonic two-body $\Lambda_b$ decays within the framework of final-state rescattering mechanism. Using this framework, we evaluate the relevant hadronic triangle diagrams by performing the loop integrations, retaining both their absorptive and dispersive parts. Based on the established formalism, we analyze the $\Lambda_b \to N^*(1535,1520)M$ decay processes with $M =K_S, K^*_0(700)$, $f_0(500,980), \rho(770), \bar{K}^{*0}$, $\phi$, and predict various physical observables, such as their branching ratios, direct and partial-wave $CP$ asymmetries, as well as decay asymmetry parameters. These two-body decay processes are expected to contribute primarily to the subsequent four-body decay channels, such as $\Lambda_b^0 \to p\,\pi^-\,\pi^+\,\pi^-$, whose $CP$ asymmetry measurements will be accessible at the LHCb experiment.

authors.name: Hui-Qiang Shang, Tian-Liang Feng, Jing Gao, Qin Qin, Fu-Sheng Yu

papers.title: MadSpace -- Event Generation for the Era of GPUs and ML
papers.summary: MadSpace is a new modular phase-space and event-generation library written in C++ with native GPU support via CUDA and HIP. It provides a unified compute-graph-based framework for phase-space construction, adaptive and neural importance sampling, and event unweighting. It includes a wide range of mappings, from the standard MadGraph multi-channel phase space to optimized normalizing flows with analytic inverse transformations. All components operate on batches of events and support end-to-end on-device workflows. A high-level Python interface enables seamless integration with machine-learning libraries such as PyTorch.

authors.name: Theo Heimel, Olivier Mattelaer, Ramon Winterhalder

papers.title: Dispersive analysis of the $\boldsymbol{\phi \to \gamma \pi^0 \pi^0}$ process
papers.summary: We present an analysis of the radiative decay $\phi \to \gamma \pi^0 \pi^0$ in a dispersive framework, where the two-pion subsystem undergoes strong final-state interactions that cover the $f_0(500)$ and $f_0(980)$ regions. We employ a coupled-channel Muskhelishvili-Omn\`es framework that allows for a consistent treatment of two scalar resonances and crossed-channel singularities induced by the Born and vector-meson exchanges. We explicitly verify the equivalence between the modified and standard Muskhelishvili-Omn\`es representations for vector-meson pole contributions when the isoscalar Omn\`es matrix is chosen asymptotically bounded, and we adopt the standard representation in decay kinematics. This yields, for the first time, a parameter-free dispersive prediction for the kaon Born rescattering, which provides a dominant contribution. To obtain a good fit to the KLOE and SND data, we employ a once-subtracted coupled-channel dispersion relation with heavier left-hand cut contributions and two unknown subtraction constants. The results demonstrate the consistency among the data for $\pi\pi$ scattering, $\gamma\gamma$ fusion, and $\phi $ radiative decay, thereby validating the underlying dispersive formalism and the input used for the hadronic Omn\`es matrix and left-hand cuts.

authors.name: Bai-Long Hoid, Igor Danilkin, Marc Vanderhaeghen

papers.title: One-point energy correlator for deep inelastic scattering at small $x$
papers.summary: We derive the expressions for the one-point energy correlator (OPEC) in deep inelastic scattering in the high-energy (small-$x$) limit within the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework. The OPEC is computed as a function of the angle between the energy flow and the target proton or nucleus, enabling a systematic exploration of different momentum scales in the scattering process. Owing to the momentum sum rule, the dependence on fragmentation functions cancels, leaving the dipole amplitude as the only nonperturbative input. As a result, the OPEC provides a sensitive and promising probe of gluon saturation dynamics at small $x$. We present numerical results for representative kinematic configurations relevant to the future Electron--Ion Collider, demonstrating sizable nuclear suppression effects within the CGC framework and highlighting the consistency of this observable with predictions from gluon saturation.

authors.name: Zhong-Bo Kang, Robert Kao, Meijian Li, Jani Penttala

papers.title: Gravitational-lensing-modulated leptonic CP violation
papers.summary: The discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos has recently prompted interest in the role of gravity in neutrino flavor conversion. In this work, we investigate the gravity-modulated CP violation (CPV) in neutrino oscillations in the Reissner--Nordstr\"om and Hayward spacetimes. Employing analytical and numerical methods, we reveal the interplay among the CPV, the properties of neutrinos, and the space-time. The shapes of the flavor-oscillation curves show that CPV signals encode both space-time geometry and mass ordering, and that the imprints of $m_l$ are intrinsically correlated with the singular versus nonsingular structure of the background metric. In particular, our finding demonstrate that the CPV observables exceed the limitation that, in asymptotically flat space-time, gravity neither damps nor amplifies neutrino-oscillation amplitudes.

authors.name: Ze-Wen Li, Shu-Jun Rong, Ya-Ru Wang

papers.title: Particle seismology: mechanical and gravitational properties from parton-hadron duality
papers.summary: The internal structure of hadrons is characterized by form factors which correspond to matrix elements of currents. Among those, the stress-energy-momentum tensor is a universally conserved quantity providing the gravitational form factors, from which mechanical properties may be derived via the response to the space-time fluctuations. They have received much attention because of their role as moments of the Generalized Parton Distributions, where the stress-energy-momentum tensor couples to two photons, and more recently, due to the explicit lattice QCD determination for the pion and nucleon. In these lectures we attempt a pedagogical review of the topic from a purely hadronic point of view, based on the notion of dispersion relations, meson dominance, and parton-hadron duality. We show that despite the overwhelming simplicity of the approach, a rather successful description of the lattice QCD data is achieved.

authors.name: Enrique Ruiz Arriola, Wojciech Broniowski

papers.title: Optimizing Yukawa couplings to suppress Dimension-five Proton Decay in $SU(5)$ GUT
papers.summary: The minimal supersymmetric $SU(5)$ grand unified theory (GUT) provides a highly compelling framework for physics beyond the Standard Model (SM). However, it suffers from a severe phenomenological challenge: rapid proton decay mediated by colored-Higgsino exchange via dimension-five operators. Resolving this issue often requires adjustments to the Yukawa couplings and the potential sectors, generating a vast and complex parameter space where traditional brute-force numerical scans are rendered computationally intractable due to the curse of dimensionality. In this paper, we overcome this limitation by applying machine learning optimization techniques. We investigate a supersymmetric $SU(5)$ model extended with $\mathbf{45}$ and $\overline{\mathbf{45}}$ Higgs representations, defining a loss function based on the partial decay width of $p \to K^+ \bar{\nu}$. Utilizing the Adam optimizer, we systematically explore the 33-dimensional parameter space to identify regions that suppress proton decay. Furthermore, we vary $\tan \beta$ to thoroughly investigate whether the optimized proton lifetime can consistently exceed the stringent experimental lower bound of $5.9 \times 10^{33}$ years established by the Super-Kamiokande collaboration.

authors.name: Naoyuki Haba, Junpei Ikemoto, Yasuhiro Shimizu, Toshifumi Yamada

papers.title: Residual Nonextensivity from WIMP Freeze-Out: A Phenomenological Memory Channel
papers.summary: In this work we formulate the thermal decoupling, or freeze-out, of weakly interacting massive particle dark matter within a dynamical Tsallis framework. The parameter $q_\chi$ is promoted to a function of $x=m_\chi/T$, describing a relaxation toward extensivity that need not be completed before chemical decoupling. We adopt a sectorial approximation during freeze-out, with an extensive Standard Model bath, and specify the statistical weights and effective kinetic closure used for the dark matter abundance. The total derivatives of the equilibrium density contain the variation of $q_\chi$, which changes the rate at which the abundance must evolve to follow its instantaneous reference state. The residual value $q_\chi^{\rm fo}$ then provides the input for a phenomenological memory channel into the electron-positron and neutrino sectors, while photons remain extensive. We derive the corresponding chain rule terms in the radiation energy and entropy balances and formulate the photon-reheating problem without assuming that comoving electromagnetic entropy is automatically conserved when $q$ varies. The resulting construction connects the freeze-out history with the neutrino-to-photon temperature ratio and $N_{\rm eff}$. We discuss the physical motivation, closure assumptions, and conditions under which this description can be used, without presenting numerical results or observational fits.

authors.name: Matias P. Gonzalez

papers.title: Reinterpreting the ATLAS HHH$\to 6b$ Search with CheckMATE and Rivet: Validation, TRSM Benchmarks, and HL-LHC Prospects
papers.summary: We present an implementation in CheckMATE and Rivet of the ATLAS collaboration search for triple Higgs boson production in a six $b$-jets final state. The search relies on event selection using a deep neural network and a statistical model based on the HS3 format. Owing to a rich validation material provided by ATLAS, we perform a thorough validation of neural network input features and exclusion limits in the Standard Model and its extension with two additional singlet scalar fields (TRSM). Finally, we discuss expected performance of the search at the High Luminosity LHC in several scenarios of systematic uncertainty. We present projected exclusion limits for a set of TRSM benchmark models beyond those considered by ATLAS.

authors.name: Tomasz Procter, Krzysztof Rolbiecki, Andrzej Si\'odmok

papers.title: Open quantum system approach to the transverse momentum broadening of a colour dipole
papers.summary: Using the open quantum systems formalism, we study the propagation of a quark-antiquark pair propagating through a dense QCD plasma of size $L$ and transverse momentum broadening transport coefficient $\hat q$, and we derive the Lindblad evolution equation for the density matrix of the system. We focus on the boosted regime where the opening angle $\theta_{q\bar q}$ of this effective colour dipole satisfies $\theta_{q\bar q}\ll 1$. In the correlation limit where the quark-antiquark relative transverse momentum $p_\perp$ is much larger than the imbalance $q_\perp$ as well as the medium typical transverse momentum scale $Q_s=\sqrt{\hat q L}$, we demonstrate that the resulting Wigner distribution displays quasi factorisation between a hard factor describing the hard splitting producing the $q\bar q$ pair and the transverse momentum imbalance $q_\perp$-distribution encoding the broadening induced by the medium. The factorisation is violated by a "colour decoherence" factor that controls the $\theta_{q\bar q}$ dependence of the $q_\perp$-distribution through the ratio $\theta_{q\bar q}/\theta_c$, with $\theta_c \sim (\hat q L^3)^{-1/2}$. The open quantum systems approach enables us to clarify the role of this critical angle $\theta_c$ and its associated critical time $t_c$ in the genuine quantum decoherence of the density matrix in colour and kinematic space: in particular, $t_c$ controls both the suppression of the off-diagonal elements of the density matrix in colour space and the transition between singlet and octet states. We find, however, that colour decoherence sets in earlier than the full decoherence of the density matrix, thereby marking the onset of classical behaviour in the system. Finally, we investigate the corrections beyond the quasi-factorised picture due to the quantum diffusion term in $p_\perp$ of the Lindblad equation and we find that these corrections are mild.

authors.name: Fran\c{c}ois Arleo, Pietro Benzoni, Paul Caucal, Pol Bernard Gossiaux

papers.title: Dispersive analysis of the $\boldsymbol{J/\psi \to \gamma \pi^0 \pi^0}$ process
papers.summary: We present a dispersive amplitude analysis of the low-energy $\pi^0\pi^0$ system in the radiative decay $J/\psi\to\gamma\pi^0\pi^0$, using the mass-independent BESIII $0^{++}$ and $2^{++}$ intensities, the total spectrum, and the measured $0^{++}-2^{++}$ $E1$ phase difference. The isoscalar $S$-wave is described by a coupled-channel $\pi\pi/K\bar K$ Muskhelishvili-Omn\`es representation, which implements the strong final-state interactions associated with the $f_0(500)$ and $f_0(980)$. The $D$-wave is treated with a single-channel $\pi\pi$ Muskhelishvili-Omn\`es representation, where we identify all kinematic constraints of helicity amplitudes before transforming them to the experimental $E1$, $M2$, and $E3$ multipoles. Smooth short-distance production of a pseudoscalar-meson pair is encoded in subtraction polynomials, while left-hand-cut effects are estimated and found to be numerically subleading. We identify the negative solution of the BESIII $0^{++}-2^{++}$ $E1$ phase ambiguity, after using the modulo-$\pi$ freedom of production amplitudes, as the phase solution compatible with unitarity constraints, showing that the measured phase information can be accommodated with the Omn\`es phase motion without requiring large additional phases. By normalizing the BESIII intensities with the extracted branching fraction, we fix the absolute scale of the fitted amplitudes, making them suitable as input for future dispersive studies of two-pion contributions to gravitational form factors.

authors.name: Bai-Long Hoid, Igor Danilkin, Anna Testa, Marc Vanderhaeghen

papers.title: Dark Matter Attenuation inside the Earth: A Boltzmann Equation Approach
papers.summary: For strongly interacting or boosted dark matter, propagation through the Earth can involve sizable scattering and energy loss, reshaping the underground flux in energy, direction, and normalization. Scattered particles may still fall within the detector acceptance, so the detector-side signal depends on phase-space transport from the Earth's surface to the underground detector. In this work, we formulate this transport problem with the Boltzmann equation. Its integral solution organizes successive scattering effects as a deterministic expansion in scattering orders. We analyze the transport equation in flat-Earth and spherical-Earth geometries, and apply the method to Dirac dark matter with an isoscalar vector interaction. The iterative solution agrees well with the Monte Carlo spectra.

authors.name: Chuan-Yang Xing, Chen Xia

papers.title: Phenomenology of Long-Lived Dark Photons and Axion-Like Particles in a Mixed Portal Framework
papers.summary: We investigate the phenomenology of a dark photon \(A'\) and an axion-like particle (ALP) ,\(a\), connected through a mixed portal framework which simultaneously allows the conventional visible decay $(A'\rightarrow f\bar f)$ and the exotic cascade process $(A'\rightarrow a\gamma\rightarrow3\gamma)$. We derive the relevant decay widths, branching ratios, and Lorentz-boosted decay lengths, and introduce a dominance parameter \(D=\Gamma(A'\to a\gamma)/\Gamma_{\rm SM}\) to distinguish Standard Model-dominated and cascade-dominated regions, with the transition occurring at $(D=1)$. A detailed analysis of both light $(0.1\leq m_{A'}\leq10~{\rm GeV})$ and heavy $(10\leq m_{A'}\leq100~{\rm GeV})$ dark-photon scenarios shows that the exotic channel can substantially modify the expected dark-photon signatures, transforming otherwise long-lived or detector-stable states into experimentally accessible displaced multi-photon events. In addition, the ALP sector itself may exhibit long-lived particle behavior, leading to distinct displaced diphoton signatures. Our results show that mixed dark-photon-ALP portals offer a rich LLP phenomenology that can be explored at future high-luminosity lepton colliders such as the FCC-ee.

authors.name: Caglar Zorbilmez, Beyhan Tatar, Azmi Ali Altintas, Cihan Bayindir, Fatih Ozaydin

papers.title: Polarized observables in $\tau \to VV \nu_{\tau}$ decays
papers.summary:
We study polarization observables in $	au^- 	o V_1^- V_2^0 
u_	au$ decays for $(V_1^-, V_2^0)=(ho^-, ho^0), (ho^-, \omega), (K^{*-}, ho^0), (K^{*-}, \omega), (ho^-,  ar{K}^{*0})$ using the helicity formalism. While the obtained branching fraction for $	au^-	o ho^-ho^0
u_	au$ is consistent with that of angular momentum algebra method, the results for the other four channels are comparable with (smaller than) those from the effective chiral model (the aforementioned method). Our results for the longitudinal polarization fractions $f_L$ indicate that nonnegligible corrections to the endpoint limit ($f_L = 1/3$), a consequence of Lorentz symmetry, are present at the scale of tau mass. Future measurements of $f_L$ at Belle II for $	au^- 	o V_1^- V_2^0 
u_	au$ decays will provide crucial information on polarization patterns observed in nonleptonic charm decays.

authors.name: Vindhyawasini Prasad, Hiroyuki Umeeda

papers.title: Thermal Alignment as a Pathway to Axion Dark Matter
papers.summary: We study the relic energy of an axion whose homogeneous displacement is damped by a thermal gauge plasma. Dissipation is accompanied by thermal fluctuations. To calculate the energy at decoupling, we retain the covariance between the axion field and its velocity. For linear Langevin dynamics, positivity of the noise covariance provides a finite-interval lower bound on the energy generated by the bath, independently of the initial state. We consider a renormalizable $SU(2)_h\times SU(3)_\ell$ theory in which a scalar transition separates the early topological susceptibility and Chern--Simons diffusion from the confining potential acting at late times. With the specified scalar history and a local plasma response, fluctuations generated during the final cooling interval carry energy comparable to the coherent-only dark matter benchmark. The relic-density integral extends over finite momenta and cannot be inferred from the homogeneous topological diffusion rate. We also include the chiral-condensate term in the scalar free energy. For the chirally broken benchmark, this term removes the stationary high-temperature solution of the polynomial potential. Thus, a consistent microscopic realization requires both an assessment of thermal axion production and scalar phases that remain stationary in the full free energy.

authors.name: Imtiaz Khan, G. Mustafa, Chengxun Yuan, Farkhod Botirov, Ahmadjon Abdujabbarov, Farruh Atamurotov

papers.title: Amplified Isospin Breaking from Coupled-Channel Dynamics Near Threshold
papers.summary: We identify the dynamical origin of amplified isospin breaking in near-threshold states. Using a pole-residue-based measure defined directly from the pole couplings, rather than from decay observables that are also affected by different final-state kinematics, we show that threshold proximity of the pole alone is insufficient: large isospin breaking requires a sizable interaction in the companion isospin channel. In particular, the isospin-violating pole-coupling ratio vanishes when the companion-channel interaction is switched off, even at finite threshold splitting. Applied to the $X(3872)$, the observed large isospin breaking points to a nearby partner pole, $W_{c1}$, as predicted in previous studies. As a concrete realization of the previously discussed leading/shadow-pole interchange, we find that the $W_{c1}$ pole, which predominantly affects the line shapes near the charged threshold in the physical case, does not evolve into the pure $I=1$ eigenstate in the isospin limit; instead, that eigenstate is continuously connected to a more distant shadow pole.

authors.name: Xiang-Kun Dong, Feng-Kun Guo, Christoph Hanhart, Teng Ji, Ulf-G. Mei{\ss}ner

papers.title: Radiative pion-pair production in disperon QED
papers.summary: Based on the previously developed disperon QED method for incorporating data input into loop processes in Monte Carlo codes, we calculate $ee\to\pi\pi\gamma$ at NLO and include the pion vector form factor within the form-factor scalar QED approximation wherever it is physically justified. In particular, this includes insertions of the two-pion two-photon Compton tensor into loop diagrams. We also consider a subset of contributions beyond, involving the pion Compton tensor with three photons. For these terms the form-factor scalar QED approach is less well justified, but we gain insight into the associated theory uncertainty for selected experimental scenarios. All calculations are implemented and made available within the Monte Carlo framework McMule.

authors.name: Yizhou Fang, Sophie Kollatzsch, Adrian Signer, Max Zoller

papers.title: Prospects for testing Lorentz symmetry with highly charged ions
