The former has a large separation $\Delta\nu$ = (2.7$\pm$0.1) \cd, and points to a model with M = (1.84$\pm$0.07) M$_{\odot}$, a radius of R = (2.67$\pm$0.07) R$_{\odot}$, and an effective temperature of \teff = (7308$\pm$71) K. The latter, with $\Delta\nu$ = (3.25$\pm$0.1) \cd, points to a more compact model with M = (1.72$\pm$0.07)M$_{\odot}$, R = (2.28$\pm$0.05)R$_{\odot}$, and \teff = (7298$\pm$59) K. The equatorial rotation velocities are (28$\pm$1) \kms\ and (47$\pm$13) \kms, respectively. TIC~274211446 has an age of (1070$\pm$127) \myr, and TIC~16053262 is (1145$\pm$165) \myr\ old.

authors.name: David Pamos Ortega

papers.title: D/H and 12C/13C ratios of benzonitrile and indene in TMC-1 support bottom-up formation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon-like molecules
papers.summary: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) have recently been detected in cold dark clouds through their rotational spectra, but it is currently a matter of debate whether they form through a bottom-up process from small hydrocarbons or through a top-down scenario involving the fragmentation of large PAHs inherited from a previous evolutionary stage of diffuse cloud. Isotopic ratios can shed light on the origin of PAHs in cold dark clouds. Large aromatic molecules observed in the infrared are enriched in deuterium and may also be enriched in 13C because they likely formed in the ejecta of evolved stars. We synthesized indene deuterated at the aliphatic position in the laboratory and measured its rotational spectrum, together with those of the nine 13C singly substituted isotopomers of indene. We used the measured spectra of the D and 13C isotopic species of indene, together with previously measured spectra of D and 13C isotopic benzonitrile, to search for these species in the cold dark cloud TMC-1 using QUIJOTE data obtained with the Yebes 40m telescope. We used a line stack method to tentatively detect deuterated benzonitrile and detect 13C-substituted benzonitrile, but find no evidence of either the D or 13C isotopic species of indene. We derive an aromatic D/H ratio of 0.53 % from benzonitrile, an aliphatic D/H ratio 55 for benzonitrile and indene, respectively. These values are consistent with isotopic ratios derived for other molecules in TMC-1 and show no enrichment in either D or 13C that could be ascribed to inheritance from large PAHs in a top-down scenario; a bottom-up scenario is therefore the most likely.

authors.name: D. Heras, R. Mora-Lopez, J. Janeiro, M. N. Alparslan, C. Cabezas, M. Agundez, D. Perez, I. Pe\~na, M. Pereira-Santaella, M. A. Crutchfield, J. R. Moran, A. L. Steber, A. Lesarri, C. Perez, I. Garcia-Bernete, N. Marcelino, B. Tercero, J. R. Goicoechea, J. Cernicharo

papers.title: Super-Eddington Accretion onto Compact Objects: Theory Meets Observation
papers.summary: We review candidate super-Eddington populations together with semi-analytic models and radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations, with the following conclusions: $\bullet$ Likely super-Eddington sources over a range of black hole mass show similar properties, including outflow on a range of scales, hard X-ray weakness, decreased emission from jets, and suppressed optical/UV variability. $\bullet$ Theoretical treatment of super-Eddington accretion predicts similar behavior across a range of methods and initial conditions, although interesting differences remain, particularly in the importance of magnetic fields. Numerical simulations produce a puffed-up inner disk with a funnel that grows narrower at higher mass accretion rate. Radiative efficiency declines with accretion rate in thermal-pressure--supported disks. $\bullet$ Ubiquitous outflow is likely an important ingredient in galaxy feedback at high Eddington ratios, as wind mechanical power increases with accretion rate and can rival jet power. Wind kinetic power depends far less on uncertain black hole spin and magnetic fields. $\bullet$ Observational classes of objects can be sorted in a two-dimensional parameter space of Eddington ratio and orientation. Observations down the funnel observe rapid X-ray variability, while observations through the wind will see suppressed X-ray emission. At the highest Eddington ratios, we envision a regime where the photosphere extends to $r > 10^6 \, r_g$, and the observer sees only thermalized emission covering most of the sky, speculatively corresponding to super-soft sources and Little Red Dots.

authors.name: Yan-Fei Jiang, Jenny E. Greene

papers.title: Three Dimensional Structure of Jovian Polar Cyclones Revealed by Juno Microwave Radiometer
papers.summary: Jupiter's circumpolar cyclones (CPCs) represent one of the most extreme dynamical regimes of the Solar System, where rotation, stratification, and convection interact to organize a stable polygonal cyclone lattice at each pole. Yet the depth and vertical structure of these cyclones remain unresolved. Here, using Juno Microwave Radiometer observations acquired between May 2023 and May 2024, we retrieve the 3-D thermal/compositional structure of Jupiter's northern CPCs at depths beyond those detectable by Earth-based telescopes and spacecraft that have ever visited. The eight CPCs, appearing with enhanced microwave brightness, show as modest ammonia depletion near the water lifting-condensation level ($\sim$5 bar) and/or, equivalently, warm-core structures analogous to terrestrial tropical cyclones. Five of them show substantially stronger and deeper anomalies than the remaining three, with approximately twice the inferred ammonia depletion and localized heating. In contrast, the central polar cyclone exhibits little microwave brightness contrast relative to its surroundings, despite its substantially cloudier and visually distinct appearance in visible and infrared observations. Previous dynamical models have treated the CPCs and the central polar cyclone as dynamically similar structures arising from the self-organization of turbulent flows. The new observations, however, suggest that the CPCs and the central polar cyclone may have distinct origins and operate under different dynamical regimes.

authors.name: Jiheng Hu, Yuan Lian, Cheng Li, Sushil K. Atreya, Leigh N. Fletcher, Yohai Kaspi, Liming Li, Glenn S. Orton, Fabiano A. Oyafuso, John H. Rogers, Fachreddin Tabataba-Vakili, J. Hunter Waite, Michael H. Wong, Zhimeng Zhang, Steven M. Levin, Scott J. Bolton

papers.title: Improved accuracy of the reference photon calibration standards in the network of gravitational-wave observatories during the O4 observing run
papers.summary: The global network of gravitational wave observatories uses systems known as Photon Calibrators to provide absolute calibration via laser radiation pressure. Successive detector improvements are increasing sensitivity, enabling not only increase the detection rate but also detections with high signal to noise ratios. To optimally extract information from these detected signals, continual effort is directed at pushing the state of the art of the interferometer calibration accuracy. To improve the accuracy of the locally-maintained laser power standards for photon calibration, a new global calibration scheme was implemented by using transfer standards calibrated at both the National Institute of Standards and Tech- nology (NIST) in the US and the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) in Germany during the recently completed fourth observing run. We report the results of a long-duration NIST-PTB bilateral comparison conducted over almost three years and the results of propagation of transfer standard calibrations to the reference power sensors maintained at each observatory.

authors.name: Dripta Bhattacharjee, Cervane Grimaud, Matthew Spidell, Stefan K\"uck, Dan Chen, Joseph Betzwieser, Shingo Hido, Paul Lagabbe, Holger Lecher, John Lehman, Francisco Llamas, Marco L\'opez, Lo\"ic Rolland, Anthony Sanchez, Richard Savage

papers.title: A search for optical bursts from the repeating fast radio burst in the M81 globular cluster, FRB 20200120E
papers.summary: We present a search for optical bursts from the repeating fast radio burst FRB 20200120E, which is located in a globular cluster of M81 and is the closest known extragalactic FRB. We observed FRB 20200120E simultaneously with the high-speed, quintuple-beam optical camera HiPERCAM on the 10.4-m Gran Telescopio Canarias and the Effelsberg 100-m Radio Telescope. We detected one radio burst of fluence $\mathcal{F}_{\rm R} = 0.14\pm0.01$ Jy ms during our observations, but found no evidence for corresponding optical bursts in the 11.98 ms frames. We find 5$\sigma$ upper limits on the optical burst fluence of $\mathcal{F}_{\rm O} < 1.8\times10^{-3}$ Jy ms (combined $u_s g_s r_s i_s z_s$-bands) and the optical burst energy of $E_{\rm O} < 5.4\times10^{36}$ erg ($r_s$-band), corrected for interstellar extinction. We compare our upper limit on the optical-to-radio fluence ratio $\mathcal{F}_{\rm O}/\mathcal{F}_{\rm R} < 0.013$ to various emission models involving inverse-Compton scattering in the magnetosphere or nebula of a highly-magnetised neutron~star.

authors.name: V. S. Dhillon, L. G. Spitler, K. Lackeos, A. N. Mbole, W. J. Page, A. J. Brown, N. Castro Segura, M. J. Dyer, J. A. Garbutt, M. J. Green, D. Jarvis, M. R. Kennedy, P. Kerry, S. P. Littlefair, J. McCormac, J. Munday, S. G. Parsons, I. Pelisoli, E. Pike, D. I. Sahman, A. Yates

papers.title: Rapid Protoplanetary Disk Evolution and Debris Disk Formation in Taurus-Auriga
papers.summary: We present a Submillimeter Array (SMA) 1.3mm (225GHz) continuum emission survey of Young Stellar Objects (YSOs) in the Taurus-Auriga star-forming region, comprising 69 class III and 5 class I/II YSOs with spectral types B9-M3, as part of a total sample of 149 class II and 82 class III YSOs. This represents a complete sample (100%) of class II and III YSOs with spectral types earlier than K3, and a near-complete sample (85%) for spectral types earlier than M2. The survey has a median $3\sigma$ sensitivity of 1.4mJy. We did not find any emission from circumstellar dust around class III YSOs, but present three detections that can be attributed to variable stellar activity, and one from an unresolved companion. We compile and model spectral energy distributions (SEDs) for the sample, and report 27 class III YSOs with excess thermal emission. We demonstrate that the class III YSOs in Taurus are typically older than their class II counterparts. We produce millimeter luminosity and dust disk mass distributions, and present evidence for a bifurcation between the class II and III populations, implying that ${\gtrsim}99.5\%$ of the dust mass is dispersed or transformed as YSOs transition from the class II to III stage. The combined infrared and millimeter properties demonstrate that warm (inner) and cold (outer) dust reservoirs evolve on comparable timescales: there is a rapid evolution across the radial extent of disks. We demonstrate that the survey properties are broadly consistent with a belt population that formed planetesimals from class II disks with an efficiency of a few tenths to a few tens of percent.

authors.name: Joshua B. Lovell, Sean M. Andrews, Grant M. Kennedy, David J. Wilner, Richard Alexander, Adam L. Kraus, Daniel M. Krolikowski, Luca Matr\`a, Mark C. Wyatt, Jonathan P. Williams

papers.title: Euclid DR1 Legacy Science on Ultracool Dwarfs: Halpha activity, kinematic age and rotation of M7--L1 dwarfs from DESI DR1, SPHEREx and Euclid
papers.summary: The fraction of late-M dwarfs with detectable Halpha rises toward the stellar-substellar boundary while their emission weakens relative to the bolometric luminosity, a contrast attributed to the fading continuum. We measure how much of this rise the continuum explains and whether younger populations or longer activity lifetimes contribute. We select 8939 dwarfs of type M7 or later, all but 22 of them M7-L1, from DESI DR1. We compare active fractions at common thresholds in equivalent width and in log(L_Ha/L_bol), the Halpha-to-bolometric luminosity ratio, in spectra sensitive to each threshold. We jointly model continuum fading, emission weakening and an extra active component. Kinematics use Gaia astrometry and DESI radial velocities for dwarfs with G = 5) test the optical type scale, and VIS images resolve three close binaries (0.22-0.53 arcsec) with common proper motion. We confirm that the rise in equivalent-width incidence comes mostly from the fading continuum acting on weakening emission. Conditional on an age-velocity relation and uniform ages, a step model gives thin-disk activity lifetimes at log(L_Ha/L_bol) = -4.7 of 5.9 (5.3-6.6) and 6.4 (5.2-8.0) Gyr at M7 and M8. Both bins contain mostly stars, so these lifetimes describe the lowest-mass stars.

authors.name: Ramarao Tata, Eduardo L. Mart\'in, Herv\'e Bouy, Adam J. Burgasser, Nicolas Lodieu, Basmah Riaz, Ngoc Phan-Bao, Nikola Vitas, Nafise Sedighi

papers.title: A Catalog of Young Stellar Objects in the Lagoon Nebula
papers.summary: M8, the Lagoon Nebula, has been known for more than 100 years as a region forming stars. It is (in projection) very close to if not in the Galactic Bulge. As a result, the source surface density is very high and source confusion is a substantial challenge. Because of the location, there have been many surveys that serendipitously observed M8, in addition to studies specifically targeting it. But to this point, there has been no effort to resolve source confusion across all the existing catalogs, spanning many different wavelengths, sensitivities, and spatial resolutions. We have done all of this source reconciliation, and present the merged catalog here. The net result is 3019 YSOs with largely photometric data and/or YSO selection from ~50 different origins, primarily ranging from $g$-band through 25 um, but with a significant number of X-ray sources, and some data of limited sensitivity out through 70-450 um. The catalog includes several flags that enable users to select, e.g., the YSOs that have been identified as young by the most studies, or the YSOs with the most multi-wavelength counterparts, or the ones with the clearest IR excesses. We use this catalog in a companion paper; it will also be of use in, e.g., future SPHEREx and Roman work.

authors.name: L. M. Rebull, L. Venuti, A. M. Cody

papers.title: Unveiling the infrared excess of SIPS J2045-6332 II: SPHEREx spectral decomposition supports a young unresolved binary interpretation
papers.summary: SIPS J2045-6332 is an unusual low-mass object previously identified by its infrared excess and possible signatures of youth and unresolved multiplicity. Earlier work suggested that it is relatively young and may host a mid-L companion. Here we reassess the system using low-resolution 0.75-5 micron spectroscopy from SPHEREx. We perform single- and binary-template spectral decomposition with field-gravity and intermediate-gravity (beta) templates spanning M8-L4. Binary-template models consistently outperform single-template models, most strongly for the beta templates. The preferred solution, an L0beta + L1beta combination (reduced chi^2 = 10.72), best matches the combined-light spectrum, although M9beta + L1beta and M9beta + L2beta give comparably good fits. Combining bolometric luminosities from gravity-dependent bolometric corrections (log L/Lsun = -3.42 +/- 0.08 and -3.85 +/- 0.09) with the Sonora evolutionary models, we estimate component masses of ~0.015 and ~0.011 Msun at 25 Myr and >~0.043-0.046 and ~0.038-0.043 Msun at 200-250 Myr for the primary and secondary (primary values are lower limits), implying a mass ratio q <~ 0.7-0.9, i.e. a companion of comparable but not necessarily equal mass. These results independently reinforce previous interpretations that SIPS J2045-6332 is a relatively young unresolved binary, and demonstrate the capability of SPHEREx spectroscopy to characterise young low-mass binaries through spectral decomposition.

authors.name: Michiharu Hyogo, Thomas P. Bickle, Joseph R. Biggs, Adam J. Burgasser, Dan Caselden, Sarah Casewell, Sergio B. Dieterich, Hugo A. Durantini Luca, Jacqueline Faherty, Daniella Bardalez Gagliuffi, Jonathan Gagn\'e, J. Davy Kirkpatrick, Marc J. Kuchner, Carey M. Lisse, Federico Marocco, Aaron M. Meisner, Austin Rothermich, Adam C. Schneider, Steven M. Silverberg

papers.title: VLA Observations of the Ionized Jet IRAS 16562-3959
papers.summary: We present new high-resolution, high-sensitivity Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) A-configuration observations of the high-mass protostellar jet system IRAS 16562-3959 at 3.1 and 6.1 GHz. Our images resolve the five previously known jet components (OE, IE, C, IW, OW) into 21 distinct knots and sub-components, and reveal a new off-axis source, MW. Based on the dynamical timescales from previous works ($\tau_{jet} \approx 620$ yr), the spacing and structure of the knots suggest episodic accretion with a mean interval between ejections of $\sim$32 yr. We find that source MW has a substantial increase in peak brightness relative to its marginal detections in previous observations. MW exhibits a spectral index of $\alpha \approx -0.7$, characteristic of synchrotron emission from shock-accelerated relativistic electrons. Equipartition analysis yields a minimum-energy magnetic field strength $B_{me} \approx 0.4$ mG, and a minimum total energy $E_{me} \approx 4.4 \times 10^{42}$ erg. Archival 2MASS Ks data imply a total outflow dynamical age of $\sim$1400 yr, and together with a HST [FeII] 1.64 $\mu$m map, the NIR data indicate that the fast jet is embedded in a wide-angle wind with a $\sim 36^\circ$ opening angle.

authors.name: Ananay Sethi, Peter Hofner, Emmanuel Momjian, Esteban D. Araya, Tatiana M. Rodr\'iguez, Stanley E. Kurtz

papers.title: The interplay between ionized and warm molecular gas in the turbulent intragroup medium of Stephan's Quintet
papers.summary: Using JWST MIRI spectroscopy, we explore the multi-phase intergalactic gas in the hot halo of the Stephan's Quintet compact group. Unlike the coolest H2 emission, which commonly shows double- peaked profiles corresponding to the velocity of the intruder and the intragroup gas, the ionized Neon emission-lines are often systematically shifted redwards in radial velocity away from the lowest H2 peak, and into the region corresponding to gas decelerated by the collision of the intruder galaxy with intragroup gas. The majority of the brightest clumps of ionized gas are spatially correlated with the brightest H2 clumps, suggesting they are coherent structures caught up in the opposing gas flows. Gas that is progressively heated, is shifted in velocity further from the velocity of the coldest H2 peaks. Larger and larger shifts in velocity are seen as one progresses from cool to warm molecular hydrogen, to lower-excitation (Neon lines) ionized and strongly shocked heated ionized gas (gas-phase Iron). The majority of the ionized Neon in the intergalactic medium is consistent with excitation in low-velocity shocks. We suggest that this behavior is the result of gas of progressively lower densities being shocked and accelerated by the interaction of pre-existing clouds with a hot flow created by the blast-wave from the collision between the intruder and the intragroup gas. One exception is the extragalactic star forming region, SQ-A, which shows higher-excitation ionized emission lines consistent with heating from a young starburst, consistent with previous photometry of young star clusters in the region.

authors.name: Philip Appleton, Pierre Guillard, Ute Lisenfeld, C. Kevin Xu, Francois Boulanger, Jonathan Braine, Aditya Togi, Sarah Gallagher, Pathayappura Aromal, Bjorn Emonts, Loreto Barcos Munoz, Pierre-Alain Duc, Benjamin Godard, George Helou, Patrick Ogle, Ewan O'Sullivan, William Reach, Tanio Diaz Santos

papers.title: Theoretical Instability Models of Quasi-Periodic Eruptions
papers.summary: The nature of the Quasi-Periodic Eruptions (QPE) is still not firmly established while the phenomenon probes the innermost part of the accretion flow undergoing dramatic changes. In this chapter we review the possibility that the observed rapid variability is caused by the accretion disk instability. We summarise the defining observational properties of QPE sources: time scales of recurrence, the amplitudes of soft X-ray flares, high coherence over many cycles, and comparatively modest time-averaged luminosities. We then translate these into constraints on the characteristic radius, accretion rate, and energy reservoir of the inner disk. We review the main classes of disk instabilities relevant to supermassive black holes: radiation pressure induced thermal/viscous limit cycles, magnetically mediated inner disk transitions, and coupling to disk winds that can produce the oscillatory behavior. For each scenario we discuss the required parameter space (black hole mass, Eddington ratio, viscosity prescription, and truncation radius), the predicted spectral and timing signatures, and the degree of fine tuning needed to reproduce the observed duty cycles and flare morphologies. We highlight key tensions, including the extremely soft spectra, short recurrence times compared with standard viscous times at tens of gravitational radii, and the weak or absent contemporaneous optical/UV variability in several systems. Finally, we outline observational tests that may help distinguish between instability driven and geometrical or orbital models: phase resolved spectroscopy to track the temperature evolution, searches for hysteresis in hardness-intensity diagrams, reverberation and absorption variability tied to winds, and long baseline monitoring to measure drift in period and energy output.

authors.name: Agnieszka Janiuk, Bo\.zena Czerny, Marzena \'Sniegowska, Pulkit Ojha, Shuang-Liang Li, Shivangi Pandey

papers.title: Depolarization of Synchrotron Polarization in Magnetized Interstellar Media
papers.summary: We numerically study three key depolarization mechanisms of synchrotron polarization, including wavelength independent depolarization, differential Faraday rotation depolarization, and beam depolarization, across subAlfv\'enic and superAlfv\'enic turbulent regimes. Using 3D MHD simulations and synthetic observations, we analyze their effects on polarization degree and power spectra. We find that (1) SubAlfv\'enic turbulence shows high but strongly suppressed polarization under Faraday rotation, while superAlfv\'enic turbulence remains low and stable; (2) Differential Faraday depolarization dominates in ordered subAlfv\'enic media. For disordered superAlfv\'enic regimes, beam depolarization dominates at high frequencies, while at low frequencies it saturates and differential Faraday depolarization takes over as the dominant mechanism; and (3) Depolarization significantly distorts spectra in superAlfv\'enic turbulence but weakly affects subAlfv\'enic cases. Our results provide a quantitative basis for correcting depolarization biases in magnetic turbulence measurements with radio polarization data.

authors.name: Zhengkang Yang, Jianfu Zhang, Ziqi Liu, Qingzhong Liu

papers.title: Current Accretion State versus Black Hole Mass: Imprints on Multiphase Gas in IllustrisTNG
papers.summary: The coupling between AGN feedback and the multiphase circumgalactic medium (CGM) is central to understanding galaxy evolution. In a previous paper, we showed that the black hole mass ($M_{\rm BH}$) correlates negatively with cold gas mass in IllustrisTNG100. We now extend this to the Eddington ratio ($\lambda_{\rm Edd}$), which traces the current accretion state, using the same sample of 5089 central galaxies at $z=0$ under the same group-specific partial correlation framework, controlling for stellar and dark matter halo mass. We find that $\lambda_{\rm Edd}$ correlates positively with warm gas in star-forming galaxies ($\rho \approx 0.6$-$0.7$), persisting after jointly controlling for $M_{\rm BH}$, the mass in the other non-star-forming gas phases, and specific star formation rate. The $\lambda_{\rm Edd}$-cold gas correlation instead reverses sign, from negative in star-forming galaxies ($\rho \approx -0.32$) to positive in quenched galaxies ($\rho \approx 0.40$). Controlling for $M_{\rm BH}$ leaves this correlation essentially unchanged in all three galaxy types. Further controlling for the total gas mass in the other phases strengthens the star-forming correlation and weakens the quenched correlation to $\rho \approx 0.21$, which remains significant. These results establish the Eddington ratio as a phase- and type-dependent tracer of the gas-black hole connection: the cold gas reservoir records the integrated black hole growth, the warm gas in star-forming galaxies carries the signature of the current accretion state, and the sign reversal of the cold-gas correlation marks the transition between the star-forming and quenched regimes.

authors.name: Xiaoxia Zhang, Taotao Fang, Shulan Yan, Si-Yue Yu, Feng Yuan

papers.title: On Modelling the Far-Side Unsigned Magnetic Flux Evolution of Long-Lived NOAA Active Regions
papers.summary: The evolution of magnetic flux in solar active regions is central to space-weather forecasting and solar-cycle studies. Direct measurements of the far-side magnetic field, however, remain unavailable with current solar instrumentation. We develop a method to estimate the far-side evolution of active-region magnetic flux using 304 {\AA} (He II) emission as a quantitative proxy. Using SDO/AIA and SDO/HMI observations of all four near-side passages of a long-lived active region (NOAA AR 12192), we fit a single relation that gives mean per-pixel unsigned magnetic flux from mean per-pixel 304 {\AA} intensity. The fit uses only disk-centre, flare-free intervals, and flux is the dependent variable, so the relation can be applied directly to intensity measurements. The magnetogram flux is deprojected to the radial direction before fitting, and we report the line-of-sight version for comparison. We first test the relation by fitting it on the first two passages and predicting the two later passages, which were not used in that fit; the relation adopted for the reconstruction is then fitted to all four passages. We then apply the same relation to STEREO-A/EUVI 304 {\AA} observations, scaling the EUVI intensities to AIA-equivalent boundary intensities inferred from the adjacent near-side flux measurements, and so reconstruct the unsigned flux history while the region was out of view from Earth. The test on the later passages gives a median log-space residual of +0.052 dex, a root-mean-square error of 0.083 dex, and a median absolute fractional error of 14% over 272 samples that were not used in the fit. Because a single cross-instrument scale factor cannot match both ends of a far-side interval, the absolute level of each reconstructed segment carries an uncertainty of several tens of per cent; it is the shape of the far-side curve, rather than its level, that the EUVI observations constrain.

authors.name: Ahaan S. Nalavadi, Manju Sudhakar

papers.title: Non-monotonic Age-metallicity Relations Across the Galactic Disk Revealed by APOGEE Red Clump Stars
papers.summary: Using APOGEE red clump stars and open clusters with precise ages, we investigate the age--metallicity relation (AMR) across the Galactic disk as a function of Galactocentric radius $R$ and vertical height $|Z|$. For stars older than $\sim$6--8 Gyr, the AMR shows little dependence on either $R$ or $|Z|$ within the uncertainties, suggesting rapid and well-mixed chemical evolution in the early disk. In contrast, younger populations exhibit a clear negative radial metallicity gradient, with the inner disk being more metal-rich than the outer disk, consistent with inside-out disk growth since $\sim$6--8 Gyr ago. Most importantly, at fixed location, the AMR for ages $\lesssim6$--8 Gyr is non-monotonic: [Fe/H] decreases toward younger ages, reaches a minimum at intermediate ages, and then rises again. Beyond $R\sim11$\,kpc, the relation becomes even more complex, exhibiting an additional reversal and a distinct metallicity peak at an age of $\sim2$\,Gyr. Such complex behavior cannot be explained by continuous local enrichment alone, but instead points to the combined effects of a multi-phase gas-accretion history and radial migration. Episodes of metal-poor gas inflow can dilute the interstellar medium and reset its chemical evolution, while subsequent enrichment raises the metallicity again; radial migration further reshapes the observed AMR by mixing stellar populations formed at different radii and metallicities. A toy model incorporating inside-out growth, two gas-inflow episodes, and radial migration qualitatively reproduces the observed trends, highlighting the combined roles of episodic gas accretion and radial migration in shaping the chemical evolution of the Galactic disk.

authors.name: Chun Wang, Yang Huang, Haibo Yuan

papers.title: Exomoons and Exorings with the Habitable Worlds Observatory. III. Icy Moons and Rings Often Outshine Their Planets
papers.summary: If we could observe the Solar System's giant planets with the upcoming Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), the dominant sources of reflected near-infrared light would not always be the planets themselves. In fact, the brightest sources are split roughly evenly between the giants and their icy companions: at the locations of the giant planets, the dominant point sources would be Jupiter, Saturn's rings, Uranus, and Triton (Neptune's icy moon). Motivated by these Solar System cases in which rings or moons outshine their host planets, we investigate the detectability of analogous exomoons and exorings with HWO. We compute the expected signal-to-noise ratios (S/N) for moons and rings with the same albedos as their Solar System counterparts over a range of sizes, system distances, and star to planet+moon or star to planet+ring separations. We find that reflected light from Triton-analog exomoons and Saturn-analog exorings is detectable with HWO over a broad parameter space. In the nearest systems, icy Titan-sized moons are detectable at star-moon separations of ~2 AU and icy Earth-sized moons out to ~6 AU. Moreover, Saturn-like exorings are likely to be the brightest point sources in many extrasolar systems, capable of greatly outshining any planets, while remaining potentially detectable at system distances out to 100 pc. These results highlight the need for further work to develop methods for identifying and disentangling exoring and exomoon signatures from exoplanet signals in HWO observations, where these sources will be blended and spatially unresolved.

authors.name: Sam Hopper, Mary Anne Limbach, Rachel Bowens-Rubin

papers.title: 3D and 2D Radiation Non-ideal MHD modeling of the decay of FUor outbursts
papers.summary: FU Orionis (FUor) outbursts are high-accretion events in protoplanetary disks thought to be driven by the magnetorotational instability (MRI). Although these outbursts span a wide range of observed durations and can thermally process and potentially transport disk material, the physical processes governing their decay remain poorly understood. We present a three-dimensional radiative non-ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulation of the decay of an MRI-driven FUor outburst, complemented by a suite of two-dimensional models that explore its dependence on disk properties. During the decay, rings and gaps form naturally within the inner disk. Magnetic flux preferentially concentrates in the gaps, while the rings remain comparatively weakly magnetized. We show that MRI-active rings act as ``magnetic dams,'' confining magnetic flux within adjacent gaps. As the rings cool below the MRI activation temperature, non-ideal MHD effects decouple the gas from the magnetic field, allowing the trapped flux to diffuse outward. This outward diffusion can sometimes transiently reactivate MRI in neighboring rings, producing localized reheating events that we term ``Reactivation.'' By comparing otherwise identical two- and three-dimensional simulations, we find that MRI heating is systematically less efficient in two dimensions, leading to outburst durations shorter by a factor of $\sim3$--4. Our model suite further shows that the decay timescale depends primarily on the disk surface density and distance from the central star, with only a weak dependence on the magnetic field strength. We further derive an empirical relation linking the outburst duration to these quantities.

authors.name: Yisheng Tu, Lee Hartmann, Zhaohuan Zhu, Conel M. O'D. Alexander, Fred J. Ciesla, Eric Rapp III

papers.title: The Lives and Deaths of Red Supergiants
papers.summary: Red supergiants (RSGs) represent a brief yet pivotal phase in the evolution of massive stars, encompassing the final stages of nuclear burning for many core-collapse supernova progenitors. Having expanded to 100 times larger than their main-sequence sizes, they occupy the cool, luminous extreme of the Hertzsprung--Russell diagram. Characterised by extended convective envelopes, complex and dynamic atmospheres, and, sometimes, substantial mass loss, RSGs play a critical role in shaping both their own evolutionary outcomes and the circumstellar environments into which they ultimately explode. Despite decades of study, fundamental aspects of RSG physics remain poorly constrained, including the mechanisms driving mass loss and the connection between observed RSG populations and the properties of Type II supernovae. Recent observational advances have transformed the field, revealing episodic mass-loss events, asymmetric circumstellar structures, and signs of rapid evolutionary change in individual objects. Alongside these advances, studies of Type II supernovae and their progenitors have raised important new questions about the final stages of massive star evolution, including the possibility of rapid changes in the years immediately preceding core collapse. Motivated by these developments, this review aims to describe our current understanding of how RSGs live and die, from their observed properties through to their role as supernova progenitors, and where that understanding remains incomplete.

authors.name: Emma R. Beasor

papers.title: The Role of Galactic Shear in Regulating Local Star Formation Efficiency: A Combined MaNGA DynPop and ALMaQUEST Study
papers.summary: We study the local regulation of star formation efficiency (SFE) in star-forming regions of nearby galaxies using spatially resolved data from the Mapping Nearby Galaxies at Apache Point Observatory (MaNGA) and the ALMA-MaNGA QUEnching and STar formation (ALMaQUEST) surveys. We define the local SFE as $\Sigma_{\rm SFE} \equiv \Sigma_{\rm SFR}/\Sigma_{\rm H_2}$, where $\Sigma_{\rm SFR}$ is the star formation rate surface density derived from dust-corrected $\rm H\alpha$ emission, and $\Sigma_{\rm H_2}$ is the molecular hydrogen surface density derived from CO measurements. Combining these data with dynamical properties from the MaNGA DynPop project, we use random forest regression to identify the dominant factors of $\Sigma_{\rm SFE}$. Galactic shear, quantified by the Oort parameter $A_{\rm Oort}$, emerges as the dynamical property most strongly associated with lower SFE on average, exceeding the predictive power of mass surface density (either total or stellar), Toomre stability, and mid-plane pressure. However, these quantities provide only modest predictive power and primarily trace the radial variation of SFE. After removing the shear-related radial trends, only weak correlations remain between SFE and other local galactic properties, implying that the remaining azimuthal variations are likely governed by cloud-scale processes below our resolution limit. Furthermore, the relationship between SFE and shear varies among galaxies and weakens in gas-rich regions, suggesting that gas density may modulate the impact of shear. This behavior is consistent with competition between shear-induced cloud stabilization and shear-driven cloud-cloud collisions. Overall, galactic shear appears to regulate the large-scale radial distribution of SFE, while cloud-scale interstellar medium physics may drive the remaining variation.

authors.name: Kai Zhu, Shude Mao, Michele Cappellari, Sara L. Ellison, Tao Jing, Lihwai Lin, Shengdong Lu, Mallory D. Thorp, Yong Shi, Ran Li, Hsi-An Pan

papers.title: Lord/Egg of the LRDs: One geometry for its many faces
papers.summary: Little red dots (LRDs) combine V-shaped ultraviolet-optical continua, broad Balmer emission, and weak X-rays. The nearby analog SDSS J102530.29+140207.3, known as Lord/Egg, offers detailed spectroscopy and polarimetry. We test one active galactic nucleus (AGN) geometry by fitting its ultraviolet-to-infrared continuum with an inclination-dependent accretion-disk spectral energy distribution (SED), young stars, and a clumpy dusty screen. The same SED is used in Cloudy calculations of a radially stratified, virialized broad-line region (BLR). The fit favors log10(M_BH/M_sun) about 7.4, highly super-Eddington accretion, inclination above 70 degrees, and line-of-sight cloud extinction of about 3 mag. It also predicts a 2 keV luminosity below the Chandra limit. A BLR whose density rises from 10^9 to 10^11 cm^-3 near the sublimation radius reproduces the broad H-alpha profile without a separate intermediate-width Gaussian. For cloud columns near 10^23 cm^-2, it also matches the different Balmer-line widths, exponential-like wings, and Balmer decrement without electron scattering. The redshifted H-beta-H-delta absorber lacks an H-alpha counterpart, requiring velocity-coherent H-alpha re-emission into the absorption trough. Cool outer clumps explain K I and saturated Na I absorption, while the geometry recovers the continuum and H-alpha polarization and their position-angle offset. Ca II triplet absorption requires localized, non-radiatively heated, warm dust-poor zones near the sublimation front. He I absorption traces a fast, about 500 km s^-1, low-column ionized BLR skin. All projected absorber velocities remain below the local escape speeds, consistent with a bound failed BLR wind. Thus, a dusty, high-inclination accretion system can explain Lord/Egg within one connected geometry.

authors.name: Piero Madau, Roberto Maiolino, Xihan Ji, Xiaojing Lin, Xiaohui Fan

papers.title: Resolving Individual Massive Stars in an M31 Star Cluster Exhibiting Wolf-Rayet Features
papers.summary: The observed ratio of Wolf-Rayet (WR) star subtypes (e.g., WC/WN) in M31 is significantly higher than the predictions of standard stellar evolution models, yet this key diagnostic discrepancy remains unresolved. This is partly due to incomplete census and the challenge of resolving individual stars in compact clusters with ground-based telescopes. In this work, we report a young cluster with WR features with the (R.A., Dec) = (00:43:39.36, +41:10:08.7), discovered with LAMOST spectra. We use the high spatial resolution of the HST imaging data to resolve the cluster members, leading to the identification of four WR star candidates, four OB stars, and one yellow supergiant. Based on the current known WR sample in M31 observed in the HST F275W filter, about one-third of WRs are contaminated by other sources within a 1. "1 $\times$ 1. "1 aperture, while this fraction can reach up to two-thirds for the LAMOST fiber size of 3. "3. Applying the approach demonstrated in this work to a larger sample of crowded regions in M31 will yield a more complete census and allow for the measurement of a definitive WC/WN ratio, corrected for contamination. Whether this refined ratio increases or decreases the current tension with models remains to be seen, but it will provide the essential observational constraint needed to advance our understanding.

authors.name: Yunning Zhao, Yulong Gao, Wei Zhang, Fuzhen Cheng, Ming Yang, Shiming Wen, Shichao Han, Hong Wu

papers.title: Spectropolarimetric diagnostics of the lower solar atmosphere: a review of inversion techniques
papers.summary: The Sun, our host star, plays a fundamental role in astrophysics due to its vicinity. To understand the processes taking place in the outermost layers of the Sun, but also, indirectly, in its interior, we conduct high spectral and spatial resolution, high cadence observations of diagnostically important spectral lines. The intensity and the polarization of the electromagnetic radiation in the observed spectral lines are a result of the joint action of absorption, emission, and scattering processes, further altered by the Zeeman and Hanle effects. Spectropolarimetric inversions are the techniques devised for the inference of the physical parameters in the solar atmosphere through the interpretation of spectral line shapes and line polarization. This review aims to provide a pedagogical overview of the necessary radiative transfer formalism and cutting-edge techniques, and to help interested readers enter the field and use some of the concepts in their own research. The secondary aim is a critical assessment of the emerging directions for the development of spectropolarimetric inversions, namely, to discuss the friction between physical realism, numerical efficiency, and modeling of the instrumental effects.

authors.name: Ivan Milic

papers.title: Bent-tailed radio galaxies as tracers of the intrafilament medium
papers.summary: Bent-tailed radio galaxies have traditionally been associated with, and used as tracers of, the dense intracluster medium. In recent years, however, such sources have also been identified outside of clusters, with only a few discovered in low-density environments of cosmic filaments. Their occurrence in low-density environments remains rare and is still poorly understood. We announce the discovery of bent-tailed radio galaxies in galaxy cluster filaments. We have identified two bent-tailed radio galaxies, J0020-25 and J0019-26, within a filament at the redshift of $z \sim 0.1273$, and another bent-tailed radio galaxy, J0019-25, in a separate filament at $z \sim 0.1126$. We used MeerKAT observations of these bent-tailed radio galaxies to place constraints on their intrafilament medium (IFM). The effects of the filaments could be seen in the radio morphologies of these galaxies. Using faint regions in each galaxy, we estimate the intrafilament pressure, density, magnetic field strength, and total energy density. We found an IFM density of $\rho_\text{IFM} \approx 3.8\times 10^{-29}$ g cm$^{-3}$ for the surrounding medium of J0020-25 and J0019-26, and $\rho_\text{IFM} \approx (0.2 - 1.1) \times 10^{-26}$ g cm$^{-3}$ around J0019-25. We found that our estimates for the intrafilament environment around J0020-25 and J0019-26 lie within the $\rho_\text{IFM}$ literature estimates, while the density estimate found using J0019-25 is higher than the literature density estimates for the IFM and in agreement with the density of group environments. J0019-25 likely resides in a galaxy group embedded within a filament. These discoveries show the capabilities of using bent-tailed radio galaxies as probes to locate the otherwise invisible large-scale filaments.

authors.name: Katlego Morakile, Kshitij Thorat, Etienne Bonnassieux, Tiziana Venturi, Konstantinos Kolokythas

papers.title: Low-frequency Radio Observation of the Dark PeVatron LHAASO J2108+5157 Using uGMRT. II
papers.summary: We present deep radio observations of the PeVatron candidate LHAASO J2108+5157 using the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT). Our observations reveal a persistent double-lobed radio source (\gmrtext) within the vicinity of the $\geq$100 TeV $\gamma$-ray emission region, with consistent morphology across 400 MHz, 650 MHz, and 1.2 GHz. No alternative particle accelerators, such as supernova remnants or pulsar wind nebulae, are identified in the region, making \gmrtext\ the most plausible counterpart candidate. We measure the flux and spatially resolved spectra of the source using multi-band radio data. The morphology remains stable across all bands, while a comparison of non-contemporaneous observations suggests possible flux variability. From the measured spectra of the lobes the inclination angle of the jet is estimated to be $86.57^{\circ} \pm 1.15^{\circ}$. The multi-wavelength spectral energy distribution is modeled reasonably well with a lepto-hadronic scenario.

authors.name: Gunindra Krishna Mahanta, Subhashis Roy, Sagar Godambe, Bitan Ghosal, Nilay Bhatt, Subir Bhattacharyya

papers.title: Probing Velocity-Dependent WIMP Dark Matter Annihilation in Large-Scale Structure
papers.summary: The unresolved gamma-ray background (UGRB) provides a promising avenue for probing the cosmological annihilation of weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter through its cross-correlation with large-scale structure (LSS). While most previous studies have assumed a velocity-independent (s-wave) annihilation cross section, many well-motivated particle physics models predict annihilation rates that depend on the relative velocity of dark matter particles. In this work, we develop a generalized halo-model framework to investigate the cosmological signatures of velocity-dependent WIMP annihilation. Parameterizing the velocity-weighted annihilation cross section as $\sigma v_{\rm rel}\propto v_{\rm rel}^{n}$, we consider four representative cases corresponding to Sommerfeld-like (n=-1), s-wave (n=0), p-wave (n=2), and d-wave (n=4) annihilation. We show that velocity dependence modifies not only the overall annihilation emission but also the halo population dominating the signal, leading to distinct effective halo biases, redshift distributions, and angular clustering properties. As a result, different annihilation mechanisms leave characteristic signatures in the UGRB-LSS cross-correlation that cannot be captured by the overall gamma-ray intensity alone. As an illustration of the formalism, we perform a statistical forecast for the cross-correlation between the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) UGRB and the Two Micron All Sky Survey Redshift Survey (2MRS) galaxy catalog and derive the projected sensitivities to the velocity-independent annihilation coefficient for these four annihilation scenarios. Our results demonstrate that cosmological cross-correlations provide a powerful and complementary probe of velocity-dependent dark matter annihilation, offering a new avenue for constraining the particle physics of dark matter through its imprints on large-scale structure.

authors.name: Wen-Qing Guo

papers.title: Relativistic tidal excitation of g- and i-modes in neutron star binaries
papers.summary: When the gravitational wave frequency of an inspiraling binary matches a normal-mode frequency of a neutron star (NS), the mode can be resonantly excited. The excitation transfers orbital energy to the star and shifts the phase of the emitted gravitational-wave (GW) signal, thereby providing a potential probe of the NS interior. However, estimates of this phase shift in the literature vary by orders of magnitude due to different approximations and formulations used in calculating the tidal coupling strength. We revisit this problem using a fully relativistic scattering formalism, which serves as our benchmark calculation and provides a gauge-invariant mode response together with an effective tidal-mode coupling strength. We calculate the phase shifts induced by the excitation of stratification g-modes, crustal interface i-modes, and hadron-quark interface i-modes, and estimate their detectability with Fisher-matrix forecasts for current and next-generation detectors. In our models, direct g-mode excitation remains below the detection thresholds, even for the strongest stratification considered. Crust-core i-modes at large shear speeds provide the most favorable prospects and crust melting can produce a substantially larger phase shift. Hadron-quark i-modes remain below the next-generation detection thresholds.

authors.name: Binyu Zhong, Zhiqiang Miao, Zhen Pan, Huan Yang

papers.title: QPO constraints on the rotating Fan-Wang spacetime
papers.summary: In this work, we investigate a rotating regular black hole described by the Fan-Wang solution, which arises from nonlinear electrodynamics coupled to gravity. We examine the motion of neutral test particles along circular equatorial orbits and derive the corresponding orbital parameters, including the angular velocity, specific angular momentum, and specific energy. By perturbing these orbits in the radial and vertical directions, we calculate the associated fundamental epicyclic frequencies. We then employ the relativistic precession model to interpret the observed quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs) in terms of these frequencies. We numerically determine the radii of the innermost stable circular orbits and perform Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations to constrain the spacetime parameters. Using observational and theoretical estimates of the black hole mass and spin parameter from the literature, together with theoretically motivated priors on the Fan-Wang parameter, we obtain the best-fit parameter values. The inferred black hole mass, spin parameter, and QPO emission radii are consistent with the corresponding estimates reported in the literature. Furthermore, the dimensionless Fan-Wang parameter satisfies $l/M < 8/27 \approx 0.296$, in agreement with its theoretical upper bound.

authors.name: Manas Khassanov, Gulnara Suliyeva, Marco Muccino, Kuantay Boshkayev, Daniya Utepova, Ruslan Spassyuk

papers.title: Unveiling the mutual inclination distribution in astrometric surveys
papers.summary: Mutual inclination in three (or more) body systems (triple stars, circumbinary planets, multi-planetary systems, etc.) is a tracer of their formation and evolution. Gaia Data Release 4 will provide for the first time a catalog of orbital solutions for three-body systems. Because astrometry is only sensitive to the motion in the plane of the sky, there is a degeneracy in the orbital solutions leading to two possible solutions for the mutual inclination in three-body systems. We propose a hierarchical Bayesian framework to circumvent this degeneracy and unveil the mutual inclination distribution in the population. We tested our methods on simulated datasets, and showed that it reliably recovered the injected mutual inclination distributions in various cases. The method is thus promising for the statistical analysis of Gaia DR4 three-body systems.

authors.name: Jean-Baptiste Delisle

papers.title: Properties of Chromium and Manganese in Tycho's SNR with XRISM/Resolve
papers.summary: The X-ray emission of young supernova remnants gives access to the composition and spatial distribution of elements ejected in supernovae. The emission from the ejecta provides crucial insights into the explosion mechanism, especially for Fe-group elements formed in the innermost layers of the star. The objective of this paper is to provide constraints on the supernova progenitor and explosion mechanism of Tycho's type Ia supernova remnant by studying the properties of Cr and Mn. The unprecedented spectral resolution of XRISM/Resolve allows us to detect significant emission lines of Cr and Mn in different regions of Tycho's supernova remnant, even at small scale, providing a much more precise spatial distribution of Cr and Mn with respect to previous measurements. Significant Cr and Mn emission lines are observed in the Fe bright northeastern-to-southeastern emitting rim, some in the center region, but none in the southern region. The observed mass ratios of Mn/Fe, Cr/Fe and Mn/Cr, are consistent with 1D delayed detonation models of near-Chandrasekhar-mass Type Ia supernovae and 1D pure-detonation models of 1 Msol sub-Chandrasekhar-mass progenitors. In both cases, the observations imply supersolar zero-age main-sequence progenitor metallicities. Overall the best agreement is found for models with a too high metallicity to be realistic for Tycho's location. This points to additional sources of neutronisation such as carbon simmering for Chandrasekhar mass progenitor. For sub-Chandrasekhar mass, double detonation models with a WD mass lower than 1Msol are suggested.

authors.name: R. Giuffrida, A. Decourchelle, L. Godinaud, T. Tanaka, G. Ferrand, J. Ballet, T. Holland-Ashford, C. Badenes, A. Bamba, B. J. Williams, T. Mizuno, F. Acero

papers.title: Instantaneous Spectral Bandwidth of Solar Type III Radio Bursts in the Interplanetary Medium
papers.summary: Magnetic reconnection during solar flares accelerates electron beams that generate type III radio bursts through the plasma emission process. Their instantaneous spectral bandwidth is commonly interpreted as a measure of the spatial extent of the emitting population, yet contributions from viewing angle and radio-wave propagation remain poorly constrained. We investigate bandwidths of 20 type III bursts observed by Parker Solar Probe between 0.15-6.5 MHz. The bandwidth increases with frequency and is consistent with previous measurements up to 100 MHz. For the first time, simultaneous observations from multiple spacecraft show similar bandwidths despite large differences in viewing geometry. We further examine bandwidth contributions from intrinsic emission and propagation effects using numerical and analytical simulations, showing that the beam spatial extent is larger than required to explain observed bandwidths, while the spatial extent of Langmuir wave generation produces electromagnetic emission bandwidths near the observed lower limit. Temporal broadening due to radio-wave scattering can increase the bandwidth by causing emission from different frequencies to overlap in time. This effect depends strongly on turbulence level and becomes increasingly important for faster electron beams and narrower intrinsic emission profiles. The results demonstrate that observed type III bandwidths cannot be interpreted solely in terms of physically emitting regions: the intrinsic emission bandwidth follows the spatial extent of Langmuir wave generation, while propagation-induced temporal broadening provides an additional contribution that can reconcile intrinsic and observed bandwidths. Accounting for radio-wave propagation effects is essential when using type III burst bandwidths to infer the spatial properties of their emitting electron populations.

authors.name: Daniel L. Clarkson, Eduard P. Kontar

papers.title: Dual and Binary AGN at Cosmic Dawn: The need for a JWST Program to resolve the merger channel of Early Black Hole Growth
papers.summary: The discovery with JWST of accreting black holes (BHs) at z=4-9 in numbers far exceeding pre-JWST expectations, many of them overmassive relative to their hosts and linked to the enigmatic Little Red Dots (LRDs), raises the question of how early BHs form and grow. Hierarchical assembly predicts that galaxy mergers drive gas to galactic nuclei and bring BHs together, leaving a direct observational signature: dual AGN at tens of kpc separations and sub-kpc to few-kpc "duets" in post-merger galaxies, which are the progenitors of the low-frequency GW sources targeted by pulsar timing arrays and LISA. JWST has opened the window to study these systems at z>3. However, these early discoveries are very limited number and come from heterogeneous, largely serendipitous samples, so these systems can hardly be used for robust statistical studies. Within the Genesis initiative We propose a uniformly selected census of dual AGN and their hosts from cosmic noon to cosmic dawn, as a science case for the Genesis initiative. Our tiered strategy uses the survey imaging and spectroscopy for candidate selection at no extra cost, followed by NIRSpec IFU confirmation, multi-band NIRCam (and MIRI/ALMA) host characterisation, and multi-epoch revisits. Confirming and characterising about 100 pairs requires of order 1000 hr, well beyond the ceiling of standard TAC programs, and demands multi-cycle continuity. The census will deliver pair fractions as functions of redshift, separation and luminosity, BH masses and mass ratios, host properties and environments, and the empirical anchor needed to turn merger models into realistic LISA rate forecasts.

authors.name: Filippo Mannucci, Matteo Ceci, Norman A. Grogin, Anton M. Koekemoer, Muhammad A. Latif, Alessandro Marconi, Enik\H{o} Reg\H{o}s, Raffaella Schneider, Martina Scialpi, Giulia Tozzi, Alessandro Trinca, Giacomo Venturi, Maria Vittoria Zanchettin, Huanian Zhang

papers.title: Using the 0i Einstein equation to break dark-sector degeneracies
papers.summary: Over the past decade, cosmological observations have started to challenge the $\Lambda$CDM model. If these tensions persist, they immediately raise one fundamental question: what new physics could be responsible for them? More specifically, do these deviations arise from a modification of gravity, from an evolving or clustering dark energy component, or from dark matter properties beyond the cold dark matter paradigm? In this paper we show that, with current methods, any observed deviation can always be attributed to more than one sector, preventing us from determining if the tension is due to gravity, dark energy or dark matter. The main reason is that current tests rely on unobservable quantities. These quantities are then either related to observables by assuming the validity of specific equations, or compared with theoretical predictions computed within a given class of theories. Both approaches inevitably break the model independence of the tests, leading to degeneracies between gravity, dark energy, and dark matter. To overcome this limitation, we construct a set of three tests that rely only on observable quantities and that, when combined, can distinguish between the three sectors. We show that the $0i$ Einstein equation -- which is never tested in standard analyses -- adds crucial information to that provided by the gravitational slip equation and the Euler equation.

authors.name: Camille Bonvin

papers.title: Planet Formation in a Warped Disc: Gravitational Instability and Misaligned Infall
papers.summary: We perform three-dimensional smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations to investigate the impact of misaligned infall on a gravitationally unstable protoplanetary disc. The interaction between the disc and the infalling gas does not occur uniformly across all radii. As infall impacts the outer disc first, the outer disc experiences stronger torques than the inner disc, resulting in a warped disc where the angular momentum vector of the disc varies with radius. The surrounding infalling gas reprocesses stellar irradiation and re-emits it back towards the disc, resulting in a warmer disc. The higher temperatures cause the disc to become more gravitationally stable resulting in weaker spiral arms. However, over time, infall also continuously increases the disc mass, gradually altering the local conditions and strengthening gravitational instabilities despite the azimuthally averaged Toomre $Q$ indicating that the disc is stable against gravitational instability. Eventually, one of the spiral arms fragments, forming a giant planet by gravitational instability in a disc warped by misaligned infall. Hence, the impact of infall on gravitational instability in general will vary depending on the infall and disc properties due to the balance between the stabilising and destabilising effects. We also find that infall alters the expected signatures of gravitationally unstable discs by introducing asymmetries in scattered-light, continuum, and molecular line emission.

authors.name: Sahl Rowther, Josh Calcino, Richard Alexander

papers.title: FILOS: a solar Filament Oscillation Simulator
papers.summary: We introduce FILOS, a solar Filament Oscillation Simulator designed to validate methods for inferring filament dynamics from H-alpha observations. FILOS constructs synthetic filaments from measured spines populated with three-dimensional dipped threads containing hydrostatic plasma. It computes H-alpha optical depth, projects the structure onto the image plane, applies the Global Oscillation Network Group (GONG) instrumental response, and embeds the result in observed GONG background sequences. Independently prescribed damped longitudinal and transverse motions can be imposed; longitudinal periods can also be calculated from thread curvature and prominence height using the pendulum model. In a representative longitudinal experiment, thread periods range from 44.2 to 87.6 min (median 60.8 min). Normalized Lomb-Scargle power maps recover the dominant periodicity and a period-halving signature near equilibrium. Time-distance fitting recovers an onset of 19.53 +/- 0.23 min for a prescribed 20 min and a collective period of 57.71 +/- 0.35 min. Differences from input thread-level values reflect projection, image formation, and progressive dephasing. FILOS also supplies segmentation masks and opacity-weighted plane-of-sky velocity fields, enabling controlled tests of oscillation analysis, observational biases, segmentation, and motion estimation.

authors.name: G. Castell\'o, M. Luna, J. Terradas

papers.title: A comprehensive Sun-as-a-star catalog of interplanetary type-III bursts: Statistics and a framework for stellar exospace weather applications
papers.summary: Decameter-hectometric (DH) type-III bursts, produced by energetic electron beams escaping into interplanetary (IP) space, are often associated with strong soft X-ray (SXR) flares, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and solar energetic particle events (SEPEs). With future DH missions being planned, these intense bursts could provide reliable exospace weather event diagnostics, given the lack of direct stellar IP particle and CME probes. We present a catalog of DH type-III bursts associated with 538 out of 734 $\geq$C5-class flares observed by Wind and STEREO spacecraft during 2006-2025. Independent of the SXR flare strength, the occurrence and Sun-as-a-star emission properties of DH type-III bursts distinguish confined flares, CMEs with and without strong IP shocks, and SEPEs. We find that logistic-regression models combining SXR and type-III properties provide more accurate and well-calibrated CME/SEPE occurrence probabilities than a model based only on SXR parameters. Further, a space weather event probability-estimation model based on physically meaningful, scale-free parameters derived from SXR and type-III properties outperforms an SXR parameter-only model. This result presents a way to define solar-calibrated exospace weather prediction models extendable to stellar flares with a range of energy scales but similar underlying physics. We also present a catalog of 26 shock-associated type-III (S-type-III) bursts that appear to start from cotemporal DH type-II bursts and are generally associated with fast halo CMEs and major SEPEs. Our catalogs and the scale-free model form a benchmark for exospace weather studies.

authors.name: Atul Mohan, Sachiko Akiyama, Pertti Makela, Natchimuthuk Gopalswamy, Joshua Budram

papers.title: Prescription for the rotational and orbital evolution of main-sequence binaries undergoing resonance locking
papers.summary: In intermediate-mass binary stars, dynamical tides may play an important role in the orbital and rotational evolution of the system. One possible channel for long-term angular-momentum exchange is resonance locking, in which the evolution of the orbital and rotational parameters remains coupled to the evolution of the frequency of a resonantly excited oscillation mode. We aim to develop a simple prescription for describing the orbital and rotational evolution of binary systems undergoing resonance locking, and to assess the range of validity of this prescription. Using the asymptotic formalism for high-order gravity modes, we relate the temporal evolution of mode frequencies to the evolution of the orbital and rotational properties of the binary system. We then compare the resulting prescription with full integrations of the dynamical-tide evolution, including the contribution of multiple forcing frequencies. Depending on the type of resonance locking considered, we identify the regions of parameter space in which locking is expected to be possible in terms of orbital separation and rotation rate. We find that resonance locking is favoured in systems with significant spin-orbit asynchronism. When a locking is maintained, the proposed prescription reproduces the main features of the orbital and rotational evolution obtained from full dynamical-tide integrations, without requiring the explicit computation of the complete forcing-frequency spectrum. If resonance locking occurs, the evolution of the binary system can be described by a relatively simple prescription. Comparison with the observed population of binaries containing gamma-Doradus stars suggests that a significant fraction of the sample lies in regions compatible with the expected location of locked systems. Improved characterisation of these systems is required to distinguish resonance locking from alternative explanations.

authors.name: L. Fellay, M. -A. Dupret

papers.title: Temporal polarization properties of accretion flows into supermassive black holes: INSANE as an alternative
papers.summary: Temporal variability and polarization provide unique diagnostics of the magnetic field structure and plasma dynamics in accretion flows around supermassive black holes. We investigate the temporal polarization properties of horizon-scale emission using general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations coupled with polarized general relativistic radiative transfer (GRRT) for three accretion states: Standard and Normal Evolution (SANE), Magnetically Arrested Disk (MAD), and an intermediate regime (INSANE). Fourier polarization-mode decomposition, through the ratio $|\beta_m|/|\beta_2|$, shows that MAD produces the most rotationally symmetric EVPA patterns, SANE the most asymmetric, and INSANE lies in between. The multi-scale temporal behaviour of the intensity is investigated using the Continuous Wavelet Transform and Hilbert-Huang Transform. Both methods identify localized oscillatory features associated with magnetic-flux eruption events in the MAD simulations. In the shorter interval examined, INSANE distributes its variability more evenly among several time-scales, while the SANE behaviour depends more strongly on the electron-temperature prescription. To quantify the spectral distribution, we define a fast power fraction $F_{\mathrm{fast},I}$ for periods of 80-200 $M$ within a broad band of 80-1500 $M$. Both methods give the smallest fractions for MAD; the ordering of state medians, INSANE > SANE > MAD, persists when the upper fast-band boundary is varied from 200 to 500 $M$. Our analysis demonstrates that combining polarization morphology with multi-scale temporal analysis provides a useful means of distinguishing magnetization states, supporting INSANE as a distinct observational alternative to conventional MAD/SANE for interpreting horizon-scale observations of M87$^{*}$ and related systems.

authors.name: Jane SiNan Long, Akhil Uniyal, Yosuke Mizuno, Koushik Chatterjee, Kinwah Wu

papers.title: Cataclysmic Variables from XMM-Newton and eROSITA
papers.summary: Cataclysmic variables (CVs) are interacting binaries where a white dwarf accretes material from a late-type donor. The most evolved systems, referred to as period-bouncers, host degenerate donors. We present XMM-Newton and eROSITA, which provide complementary views of the CV population. We summarize the capabilities of XMM-Newton for timing and spectroscopic studies, and its ability to characterize accretion geometries, magnetic field strengths, and short-term variability across magnetic/non-magnetic CVs. These data allow studies of individual systems, including magnetic period-bouncers with soft X-ray spectra and faint luminosities that offer insights into the late stages of CV evolution. We then present an overview of eROSITA as the first X-ray all-sky survey in the soft band since ROSAT, and its impact on population studies. The eRASS:4 catalog expands the known X-ray sky and will enable volume-limited samples of CVs, complete up to 500pc for standard CVs and up to 250 pc for period-bouncers. Cross-matching eROSITA detections with optical catalogs produced the largest sample of X-ray-selected CV candidates to date, that will refine X-ray diagnostic diagrams, reassess the demographics of magnetic/non-magnetic systems, and identify new highly evolved CVs. Finally, we describe ongoing searches for unknown systems, including CVs selected through probabilistic cross-matching with Gaia, and period-bouncers identified through a multi-wavelength scorecard. These efforts led to the discovery of new period-bouncers and a promising detached period-bouncer candidate, that could validate alternative models for the evolution of CVs. Together, XMM-Newton and eROSITA provide an unprecedented view into the structure, evolution, and demographics of CVs, with eROSITA laying the groundwork for future studies of compact binary evolution, the Galactic Ridge X-ray emission, and related phenomena.

authors.name: Daniela Mu\~noz-Giraldo, Beate Stelzer, Axel Schwope

papers.title: Solar atmospheric gravity wave phase differences: insights from MANCHA simulations and observations
papers.summary: Phase-difference and coherence diagnostics are widely used to identify gravity waves in the solar atmosphere, but their sensitivity to opacity and radiative-transfer effects remains poorly understood. We investigate the robustness of gravity-wave signatures in velocity and temperature diagnostics and their appearance in spectroscopic observables. We perform k-/omega phase-difference and coherence analyses using three-dimensional radiative hydrodynamic simulations with the MANCHA code. Diagnostics are evaluated at constant geometrical heights and optical depths. Synthetic Fe I 6173 {\AA} profiles provide bisector velocities, continuum intensities, and line-core intensities. We also analyse high-resolution quiet-Sun observations from the 1-m Swedish Solar Telescope (SST). Velocity diagnostics show similar phase differences and coherence at both sampling levels, including those derived from synthetic and observed bisector velocities, indicating their relative insensitivity to the sampling method. In contrast, temperature diagnostics show stronger and more extended gravity-wave signatures at fixed geometrical height. Synthetic continuum and line-core intensities retain these signatures but exhibit phase differences more closely resembling temperature diagnostics at constant optical depth. SST observations show similar qualitative behaviour, despite quantitative differences. Our results demonstrate that Doppler velocity provides a relatively robust diagnostic of gravity-wave phase propagation, whereas temperature and intensity diagnostics are more sensitive to opacity and radiative-transfer effects. Consequently, the latter may introduce biases in estimates of wave propagation speeds and energy fluxes.

papers.title: Improved compensation for missing high-order aberrations with multi-frame blind deconvolution and phase diversity techniques
papers.summary: Context. Image restoration with phase diversity (PD) and multi-frame blind deconvolution (MFBD) techniques lead to remarkable improvement in image quality, but is limited by the number of aberration parameters that can be determined. Compensation for the missing high-order modes is needed to further improve image quality, and to compensate for residual straylight. Aims. We aim to improve on methods for compensating missing high-order aberrations previously proposed by Scharmer et al. (2010) and Lofdahl & Hillberg (2022). Methods. The wavefront is divided into a set of low-order aberrations, which are treated individually, and high-order aberrations that are treated collectively. The high-order part of the transfer function is averaged, assuming Gaussian seeing statistics with Kolmogorov turbulence for the individual aberrations. Assuming that their accumulated effect is roughly uniform over the pupil, we obtain a high-order modulation transfer function that is represented with a single free parameter. Results. The high quality of the of the proposed high-order modulation transfer function is verified by calculating the Strehl from random samples of point-spread functions for D/r0 ranging from 4 to 20, where D is the telescope diameter and r0 the Fried seeing parameter. The proposed approximation offers significant advantages over the earlier proposals. Conclusions. The proposed method of compensating for missing high-order aberrations in PD or MFBD image reconstruction can dramatically improve the fidelity of solar images. Variations of the seeing (r0) within a data-set can be compensated for self consistently during PD or MFBD processing, but the average value of r0 must be provided from an external source. The computational cost of implementing this method is marginal.

authors.name: G. B. Scharmer

papers.title: Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing Analysis (BADMET)
papers.summary: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) variability is widely recognized as a promising avenue for constraining black hole mass, yet its practical application remains limited. Although the correlation between black hole mass and variability timescale has been extensively investigated, finite observational baselines often lead to systematic underestimation of the timescale, thereby hindering reliable mass estimation for individual sources. To address this limitation, we develop the Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing analysis (BADMET), an extendable framework that provides black hole mass estimates by assimilating multiple mass-related parameters that include variability properties. We show that incorporating the variability timescale improves mass recovery in the simulated sample and enhances agreement with the reference masses in the observed sample, achieving uncertainties of $\lesssim 0.5$ dex even with a single X-ray observation.

papers.title: Low-state X-ray spectra of magnetized neutron stars: Probing accretion regimes in SFXTs
papers.summary: Supergiant fast X-ray transients (SFXTs) are a subclass of high-mass X-ray binaries characterized by prolonged quiescent states, making them ideal sources for studying accretion onto highly magnetized neutron stars (NSs) at low rates. In this work, we present a broadband spectral analysis of three SFXTs: IGR J16418$-$4532, IGR J17544$-$2619, and IGR J11215$-$5952, using archival $XMM-Newton$, NICER, and $ NuSTAR$ observations. Joint spectral fitting of the NICER and $NuSTAR$ data for IGR J16418$-$4532 confirms the presence of a cyclotron resonant scattering feature (CRSF) at $\sim 50$ keV, implying a NS magnetic field strength of $\sim 6\times10^{12}$ G. We detect a cyclotron line at $\sim27$ keV in IGR J17544$-$2619, significantly higher than the previously reported energy of $\sim17$ keV, a difference that may reflect luminosity-dependent changes in the accretion flow. Using a double-Comptonization model, we identify the characteristic two-hump spectral shape in IGR J16418$-$4532 and IGR J17544$-$2619 at luminosities $\lesssim10^{35}$ $\rm erg\,s^{-1}$, indicating that this spectral transition is a universal feature of accreting magnetized NSs independent of the source type. Furthermore, the ratio between the cyclotron line energy and the intersection energy of the two humps in both sources is consistent with the empirical relation established in Be/X-ray binaries, suggesting that the overheated polar cap atmosphere model used to explain X-ray pulsars in low-luminosity states is also applicable to SFXTs. In contrast, IGR J11215$-$5952 shows a smooth single-component spectrum at all flux levels, which indicates a relatively weak magnetic field of the NS.

papers.title: New Historical Guest-Star Candidates from Reassessed Chinese Records: Lunar Occultation of Planets
papers.summary: Ancient Chinese records of lunar occultations of planets have been used to test planetary theories and investigate long-term changes in Earth's rotation. However, certain records contain identification errors whose origins remain poorly understood; we propose that some of these errors may arise from misidentifying guest stars, such as novae or supernovae, as planets. We analyzed 67 errata on lunar occultations of planets from Liu Ci-Yuan's (2015) monograph using modern ephemerides and the open-source Python package \texttt{occultsky}, publicly available on GitHub. Using recorded dates and dynastic capital coordinates, we constructed observing windows anchored at solar noon and extending by $\pm 1$ day. Each window covered the preceding and recorded nights because the date may be off by one day. For each of the 67 records, we cataloged the apparent right ascension and declination $(\alpha, \delta)$ at the midpoint of the Moon's visibility window on each candidate night. The band swept by the lunar disk confines a possible transient to a narrow region a few degrees across; these midpoint coordinates serve as proxies for the implied guest-star positions. The catalog supplies candidate positions rather than identifications, enabling remnant and compact-object searches to test the guest-star hypothesis directly. If associations are established, these records could become dated guest-star candidates, and their dates could anchor remnant ages.

papers.title: Search for UHE photon sources using direction-time clustering algorithms with a BDT particle discriminant
papers.summary: Direction-time clustering methods for neutral particle searches are motivated by the possibility that ultra-high-energy (UHE) neutral particles are produced during flaring periods of various astrophysical sources. In this scenario, clusters of events correlated in both arrival direction and time would be generated, which, when observed, would indicate a neutral-particle flare, and a non-observation would provide upper limits on fluxes for point-like sources. Focusing on UHE photon searches, an improvement of the sensitivity of direction-time clustering methods by the application of different photon tags, such as the depth of the extensive air shower maximum (X_max), the lateral distribution of the total signal across an array of detectors (S_b), or a cumulative signal trace-based discriminant variable (C_t), is investigated. A Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) is used to combine multiple observables, by which photon tagging is optimized and photon/hadron separation is improved. The number of events required to identify a photon flare is thereby further reduced compared to using individual photon tags, across a range of flare durations. The possibility of extending the known and assumed PeVatron photon sources into the UHE regime by applying these clustering methods to existing and future observatory data is also discussed. The discovery of UHE neutral particles would mark the next milestone in multimessenger astrophysics, by which a new window onto the non-thermal universe would be opened.
