papers.title: Euclid: Quick Data Release (Q1) -- The evolution of the radio-loud AGN fraction-stellar mass relation to $z\sim3$ in the Euclid Deep Field North
papers.summary: The incidence of radio-loud active galactic nuclei (RLAGN) and their energetic output via AGN feedback are crucial in understanding the evolution of galaxies and the large-scale structure of the Universe. In the local Universe, the incidence of RLAGN has been shown to correlate strongly with host galaxy properties, particularly stellar mass. Using the large-area survey capabilities provided by Euclid and the LOw Frequency ARray (LOFAR), we present the first study of the RLAGN incidence--stellar mass relation to $z=3.0$. We perform a stringent analysis accounting for cross-matching reliability and stellar-mass incompleteness. In addition, we test the robustness of our results against AGN and host galaxy classification. This yields a sample of $3\,154$ RLAGN in the Euclid Deep Field North, comprising $2\,803$ low-excitation radio galaxies (LERGs). We find that the LERG incidence as a function of stellar mass and radio luminosity follows a tight correlation over more than two orders of magnitude in stellar mass to $z=3.0$. The slope of the power-law relation decreases from $\gamma\approx2.5$ in the local Universe to $\gamma\approx1.0$ at $z=3.0$, indicating a relative increase in low-mass LERGs at earlier epochs. Separating the LERG population into actively star-forming and quiescent galaxies reveals that quiescent LERGs show a much steeper relation between incidence and stellar mass, with $\gamma\approx2.5$ compared to star-forming LERGs that show $\gamma\approx1.5$. However, the relation seems to be independent of whether galaxies are star-forming or quiescent at $z\geq2$, where both populations show relatively flat relations with $\gamma\approx1.0$. Our results suggest an evolutionary picture in which the LERG population transitions from cold-mode, merger-dominated accretion at earlier epochs to a scenario in which systems require a massive hot halo to fuel the AGN in the local Universe.

papers.title: A novel method for dust evolution in protoplanetary disks and a new criterion for gap opening
papers.summary: We present the Grain Residence-Time Method (GRTM), a computationally efficient particle-tracking approach for studying dust evolution and trapping in protoplanetary disks. By reconstructing steady-state dust distributions from particle residence times, this method provides a way to obtain radial dust surface density profiles without directly evolving the dust as a fluid. We compare the GRTM with dust profiles computed via standard methods using the $\texttt{FARGO3D}$ code, which models the dust as a pressureless fluid, and find very good agreement over a wide range of parameter space. Finally, we investigate how dust gap formation depends on the planet-to-star mass ratio ($q$) and Stokes number ($\mathrm{St}$), through a parameter study, establishing an empirical criterion for dust gap opening. In doing so, we have discovered a new regime of gap opening for small grains with $St \lesssim 10^{-2}$ and for planet mass well below Jupiter's, which is likely very relevant for gaps seen in ALMA images.

authors.name: SM Gopika, Paul C. Duffell

papers.title: FastSpecFit: Spectrophotometric Modeling of 38 Million Extragalactic Targets from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Second Data Release
papers.summary: Optical spectrophotometry provides a direct window into the physical conditions, kinematics, and formation histories of galaxies and quasars. FastSpecFit is an open-source Python software package that forward-models each Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectrum jointly with its broadband photometry, convolving stellar-population synthesis and emission-line templates with each fiber's native spectral resolution. This forward-modeling approach preserves DESI's uncorrelated pixel statistics, fits a typical spectrum in ~0.1 s of single-core time, and scales to tens of millions of objects, with uncertainties estimated via Monte Carlo resampling. FastSpecFit measures stellar velocity dispersions, non-parametric star-formation histories, stellar masses, star-formation rates, dust attenuation, K-corrections, rest-frame magnitudes, and fluxes and equivalent widths for 46 emission lines, including separate narrow and broad components for the Balmer lines. We describe these algorithms in detail, validate the measurements against independent codes, and present the resulting value-added catalog for DESI Data Release 2, which provides spectrophotometric and physical properties for 38 million extragalactic targets at 0<z<4. We also release a companion photometry-only catalog and document the catalogs previously released for the DESI Early Data Release and Data Release 1.

papers.title: Probing the Macroscopic Imprints of Singularity Resolution: Polarization Diagnostics of Rotating ABG Black Holes
papers.summary: Recent observations by the Event Horizon Telescope have revealed important electromagnetic information around the supermassive black holes $\text{M87}^*$ and $\text{Sgr A}^*$, providing experimental supports for investigating physics near the event horizon. In the absence of a complete quantum gravity theory, exploring the observational appearances and polarized images of accretion flows in regularized geometries, and seeking specific observational differences from Kerr black holes, is of value for understanding the singularity problem. Based on backward ray tracing method, this work investigates both the optical and polarimetric observational features of rotating Ay\'{o}n-Beato-Garc\'{i}a spacetime with regularization parameter $Q$. It is found that, compared with the Kerr case, the parameter $Q$ leads to a significant contraction of the size of the inner shadow in the observed optical images. This contraction remains visible even after an illustrative Gaussian filter for images observed at a low inclination angle (e.g. $17^\circ$). In the polarized images, we focus on two observables, the electric vector position angles (EVPAs) and the depolarization regions, on the observer's screen. It is found that depolarization regions do not necessarily reside in the vicinity of the bright photon ring in images at high inclination angles (e.g. $83^\circ$), and a multi-branch structure can be observed. Furthermore, the distribution of EVPAs is insensitive to the regularization parameter $Q$ while the morphology of the depolarization regions can be impacted remarkably by $Q$. The results provide possible optical observable characteristics for the rotating regular spacetime.

authors.name: Zi-Yang Li, Jia-Hui Huang

papers.title: Observational diagnostics of external photoevaporation at millimetre wavelengths
papers.summary: External photoevaporation is increasingly recognised as an important influence on protoplanetary disk evolution. However, there are no established molecular line diagnostics that can reliably distinguish external irradiation from variations in intrinsic stellar and disk properties. We use a large grid of thermochemical models to predict the fluxes of 48 transitions from eight species observable with ALMA, spanning a wide range of system properties and external FUV fields of 100 to 100,000 G0. At fixed stellar and disk properties, all transitions generally brighten with increasing FUV field strength. HCO+ and CO fluxes increase monotonically in virtually all disks, whereas lower-excitation lines, particularly those of C2H and N2H+, respond weakly and non-monotonically. However, variations in stellar mass and disk size introduce substantial degeneracies, limiting the usefulness of individual line fluxes as tracers of external irradiation. We therefore assess all pairwise line flux ratios, which can significantly reduce these degeneracies, evaluating their correlation with the external field, the magnitude of their change across the FUV range, and predicted ALMA detectability. We identify 135 promising ratios, including several combining strong FUV sensitivity and high detectability with efficient single-tuning ALMA observations. The strongest diagnostics either contrast high- and low-excitation lines of the same or co-spatial species (e.g. CO J=8-7/J=1-0), probing different regions of the photoevaporative wind, or pair an FUV-sensitive wind tracer with comparatively insensitive emission arising closer to the disk (e.g. HCO+ J=3-2/C2H N=3-2). Our results provide a framework for identifying externally photoevaporating systems from spatially unresolved emission and constraining their incident FUV field strengths.

authors.name: Luke Keyte, Thomas J. Haworth, Tyger Peake, Alvaro Ribas

papers.title: The low-luminosity state of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205
papers.summary: Context. At low accretion rates, X-ray pulsars can develop a two-hump spectrum through the thermalization and Comptonization of cyclotron photons in an accretion-heated, strongly magnetized atmosphere. Sources with independently measured cyclotron-line energies, $E_{\rm cyc}$, are particularly important because they provide a direct estimate of magnetic field strength and allow the continuum shape to be tested against spectral formation models. Aims. We investigate the luminosity-dependent spectral evolution of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205 and constrain the accretion regime in its newly observed low-luminosity state. Methods. We analyzed three NuSTAR observations obtained during the 2023 and 2025 outbursts, corresponding to the high-, intermediate-, and low-luminosity states at $L_{3-79}\simeq5\times10^{36}$, $4\times10^{35}$, and $6\times10^{34}$ erg s$^{-1}$, respectively. We supplemented these data with Swift/XRT observations and performed broadband spectral analysis of all three states. Results. The high-luminosity spectrum follows a classical cutoff power law, whereas the intermediate- and low-luminosity spectra require two thermal Comptonization components to reproduce their two-hump shape. In the intermediate state, the cyclotron line, first reported at $\sim50$ keV in the high-luminosity state, lies on top of the high-energy hump. We interpret the low-luminosity state as representing stable accretion from a cold disk. IGR J06074+2205 thus joins the very limited sample of X-ray pulsars with cyclotron-line energies that have been observed with a double-humped spectral shape.

authors.name: Alexander Salganik, Sergey S. Tsygankov, Roman Krivonos, Alexander A. Mushtukov, Juri Poutanen

papers.title: The long-period central star of planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455
papers.summary: A significant fraction of planetary nebulae have been shown to host short-period binary central stars, but longer period central stars are scarcer. We aim to characterise the central star of the planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455 which has previously been claimed to be an intermediate-period binary with a period of approximately 12 days. We study archival and catalogue photometry to probe the previously reported photometric variability and binary spectral energy distribution. We use long-term high-resolution spectroscopic monitoring to measure the radial velocity curves of the two components of the central binary, as well as derive their atmospheric parameters. We also undertook kinematical and chemical abundance analyses of the nebula itself. We find that the central binary of MPAJ1508-6455 has an orbital period of more than five years with a large eccentricity. The binary comprises a relatively low temperature sdO-type central star and a spun-up K-type giant companion. The Kiel mass of the central star is approximately half the dynamical mass derived from the radial velocities. While the nebular systemic velocity and inclination are consistent with the radial velocities of the binary, the nebular abundance pattern adds support for a lower mass progenitor which did not experience hot bottom burning (and is thus more consistent with the Kiel mass than the mass derived from the radial velocities). To the best of our knowledge, the central star of MPAJ1508-6455 is only the fourth planetary nebula central star to have a spectroscopically confirmed orbital period longer than one year.

authors.name: Adam Mousley, David Jones, Matti Dorsch, Rajeev Manick, Roger Wesson, Nicole Reindl, Ana Escorza, Paulina Sowicka, Henri Boffin, Nicholas Chornay, Alexander Csukai, Jorge Garcia-Rojas

papers.title: A transformer analysis lowers the energy threshold and improves the sensitivity of a compact imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope
papers.summary: Context. A companion study simulated an idealised stand-alone imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope with a 5 m diameter mirror. A video vision transformer that processes the raw camera waveforms lowered its energy threshold by a factor of three, compared with the standard analysis based on image parameters. Aims. We use realistic photodetectors, compute the differential flux sensitivity, and study how hardware parameters affect the transformer analysis. Methods. With the simulation tools of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory, we compare three photodetector efficiencies (100 %, 50 % and that of the LST-1 photomultipliers) with the transformer and with a standard analysis optimised for each. We then vary the dish diameter, field of view, pulse width and sampling rate. Results. With the LST-1 photomultipliers, the energy threshold is 0.18 TeV with the transformer and 0.73 TeV with the standard analysis. The standard analysis needs a photodetector efficiency of 100 % to match that threshold. The main reason is that the transformer works with events of about 35 photoelectrons in the camera, whereas the standard analysis needs about 200 before image cleaning. A 4 m dish with the transformer is more sensitive at all energies than a 5 m dish with the standard analysis. Dishes of 4, 5 and 6 m diameter give thresholds of 0.38, 0.18 and 0.13 TeV. Sampling the pixel signals at 2 GS/s instead of 5 GS/s raises the threshold to 0.26 TeV, whereas the single-photoelectron pulse width (1-3 ns) matters little. Conclusions. The analysis matters as much as the mirror area and the photodetector efficiency. With the transformer analysis, the idealised 5 m diameter telescope comes within a factor of about four of the sensitivity of LST-1 and MAGIC above 0.25 TeV, although its mirror area is 21 times smaller than that of the 23 m LST-1. This performance should improve substantially in the coming years.

authors.name: Elli Jobst, David Paneque, Lukas Heinrich

papers.title: RevolIACT: a longitudinally distributed array of compact AI-driven Cherenkov telescopes for the time-domain sub-TeV sky
papers.summary: Context. The coming decade will be the golden era of time-domain astronomy. In ten years, however, sensitive very-high-energy observations below ~1 TeV may be possible only at the two sites of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). Each can observe a source for only a few hours per night. Aims. We quantify the loss caused by this limited coverage and assess whether RevolIACT, an array of compact stand-alone AI-driven stations, can close the gap. Methods. We estimate the sensitivity that a stand-alone station needs to detect important transients seen by current imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs). We also compute the temporal coverage of layouts of ten to fourteen stations distributed in longitude, and how many of the 4401 Fermi-GBM gamma-ray bursts each layout could have observed when they occurred. Results. For each station, a sensitivity of ~15 % of the Crab flux in one hour above 0.2-0.3 TeV, about three times worse than that of current IACT systems, would suffice for an array to detect most of these transients. With the standard analysis, a telescope with a 5 m diameter mirror misses this target by a factor of 17. With a video vision transformer, it comes within a factor of two in an idealised simulation, and a 6 m telescope within 1.5. Ten to fourteen stations would provide three to four times the temporal coverage of CTAO, averaged over the sky and for the GBM bursts. Fourteen stations can observe most sources around the clock for about two months per year. Conclusions. Temporal coverage, not only flux sensitivity, will limit sub-TeV transient astronomy in the next decade. RevolIACT would complement CTAO. The concept relies on the transformer analysis, which is still young and will improve. The decisive next step is to confirm this performance on real data, with a prototype station.

authors.name: David Paneque, Elli Jobst, Lukas Heinrich, Alexander Hahn

papers.title: Testing general relativity with galaxy cluster clustering from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys
papers.summary: Deviations from general relativity on cosmological scales have been proposed as possible explanations for dark energy and dark matter. Galaxy cluster clustering offers an independent probe of gravitational growth, benefiting from theoretically motivated halo-bias constraints and complementing cluster-abundance measurements. We analyse a subsample of the largest publicly available spectroscopic galaxy cluster catalogue to date, constructed from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Following our selection cuts, the sample comprises 85 818 clusters at $0.1\leq z \leq0.4$ with $M_{\rm 500c}\gtrsim 6\times10^{13}\,M_\odot$. To enable a robust clustering analysis of this sample, we develop and validate methods for constructing random catalogues and calibrating the effective halo bias. We model the redshift-space two-point correlation function monopole and quadrupole over separations of $10$--$150\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ to jointly constrain gravitational growth and Alcock--Paczynski (AP) distortions, fixing the matter power-spectrum shape to that of a fiducial cosmology. We infer the product $f\sigma_8$ of the linear growth rate $f$ and the matter power spectrum normalisation $\sigma_8$, obtaining $f\sigma_8=0.45\pm0.08$ at an effective redshift of $z_{\rm eff}=0.28$, changing to $0.52\pm0.03$ when excluding baryon acoustic oscillation scales with tight AP priors. Both results are consistent with general relativity within the adopted fiducial cosmology.

authors.name: Eleni Tsaprazi, Federico Marulli, Pier-Stefano Corasaniti, Amandine M. C. Le Brun, Yann Rasera

papers.title: Combining Pulsar Timing data with $\texttt{MetaPulsar}$. The linearized timing model
papers.summary: Combining the data of multiple pulsar timing array (PTA) collaborations increases the sensitivity to nanohertz gravitational waves (GWs) and other signals correlated between pulsars. The International PTA (IPTA) has combined such data, but historically these projects have taken many years. We introduce $\texttt{MetaPulsar}$, a software package that ingests the $\texttt{.par}$ and $\texttt{.tim}$ files of individual data releases, and turns them into single consistent deterministic models for the combined datasets, compatible with both timing packages $\texttt{PINT}$ and $\texttt{Tempo2}$. We validate the method in four ways. First, we show for two pulsars that the linearized timing solution of a combined dataset does not depend on the parameter values in the $\texttt{.par}$. A mild exception is formed by the Shapiro-delay parameters. No combination considered requires a manual refit. Second, for PSR J0613$-$0200 we show that the residuals are explained by the timing model if we take intrinsic red-noise and dispersion-measure processes into account, and that the single-PTA timing posteriors agree with one another and with the combination, except for the parallax. Third, we quantify the consistency of the timing parameters measured by different PTAs with a two-sample tension statistic, for every pulsar that is observed by multiple PTAs. Finally, we carry out a gravitational-wave background search on the direct combination of the NANOGrav 9-yr, EPTA DR1 (v2.2), and PPTA DR2 data releases, the constituents of IPTA Data Release 2 (DR2). The combined dataset is assembled in under two hours, and the recovered amplitude and spectral index of the common process are consistent with the published IPTA DR2 result. With $\texttt{MetaPulsar}$, a joint PTA analysis can be prototyped as soon as the individual collaborations publish their data, instead of after a years-long reprocessing effort.

authors.name: Wang-Wei Yu, Rutger van Haasteren

papers.title: oMEGACat-JWST I.: Project description and photometric data release
papers.summary: Omega Centauri (NGC 5139, $\omega$ Cen) is the most massive globular cluster in the Milky Way and the likely stripped nucleus of an accreted dwarf galaxy. Extensive HST observations have uncovered many of its peculiar features, including complex subpopulations and kinematic evidence for an intermediate-mass black hole via central fast-moving stars. High-precision astrometric follow-up is essential to constrain the orbits of these stars. We present oMEGACat-JWST, a deep photometric and astrometric catalog of $\omega$ Cen's core and surroundings that extends our previous oMEGACat efforts to near-infrared wavelengths. The superior sensitivity and angular resolution of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) provide significant astrometric and photometric improvements, particularly for faint stars. Our catalog is based on a custom reduction of NIRCam and NIRISS imaging across three JWST programs extending out to two half-light radii (10'). In total, our catalog contains approximately 677 000 sources. In the region overlapping with oMEGACat, we achieve high relative completeness (> 90% of HST sources recovered) while detecting over 86 000 new sources below HST's detection limit. Astrometric tests demonstrate a single-image precision as good as 0.5% of a NIRCam pixel (0.15 mas) at mF115W=18; at mF115W=23 the precision is still 1 mas. Color-magnitude diagrams based on our data show the well-known split between the primordial Helium and the Helium enriched populations and are particularly sensitive to light-element (CNO) variations of faint stars. oMEGACat-JWST provides the most complete photometric catalog of $\omega$ Cen's core to date. Combined with HST data, it enables multi-wavelength subpopulation analyses. Together with future monitoring observations, its high astrometric precision will improve our understanding of the kinematics of the central fast-moving stars in $\omega$ Cen.

authors.name: Maximilian H\"aberle, Callie Clontz, Massimo Griggio, Mattia Libralato, Isabella Carlton, Stefano Souza, Nadine Neumayer, Anil Seth, Peter J. Smith, Jay Anderson, Mayte Alfaro-Cuello, Holger Baumgardt, Luigi R. Bedin, Andrea Bellini, Steven Chen, James E. Davies, Anna de Graaff, Jeremy Hare, Oleg Kargaltsev, Kameron Goold, Michele Scalco, Zixian Wang, Matthew Whitaker

papers.title: A Universal Ratio Linking Cosmic Expansion and the Growth of Structure
papers.summary: We identify a universal relation between the onset of cosmic acceleration ($z_t$) and the turnover ($z_{\rm pk}$) of the linear growth observable $f\sigma_{8}$. In a spatially flat $\Lambda$CDM Universe, these two redshifts obey $R \equiv (1+z_t)/(1+z_{\rm pk}) = 1.1596$, independent of the present matter fraction and the overall expansion and growth normalisations. This provides a new consistency test for $\Lambda$CDM, linking both background and growth dynamics. We further establish the conditions under which this extends to broader classes of dark energy and modified gravity theories.

authors.name: Anjan A Sen, Purba Mukherjee

papers.title: Near Resonance, Less Ordered: Radius and Mass Ordering in Compact Multi-planet Systems
papers.summary: Compact multi-planet systems exhibit a tendency for planetary radii to follow ordered sequences with orbital position, suggesting that these non-random patterns preserve a fossil record of their formation. Here, we investigate whether ordering of planet radii and masses with orbital period is related to proximity to mean-motion resonances. We compare near-resonant and non-resonant systems using complementary rank- and inversion-based measures of ordering, while accounting for differences in planet multiplicity and uncertainties in the measured planetary properties. We find that radii and masses are less monotonically ordered in near-resonant systems than in non-resonant systems, with the primary radius analysis providing stronger evidence than the mass analysis. This result is opposite to the naive expectation that dynamical instabilities should erase the primordial ordering of initially resonant systems and leave non-resonant systems in a more disordered state.

authors.name: Agustin Heron, Songhu Wang, Cristobal Petrovich

papers.title: \texttt{StochAXtic}: a JAX-Accelerated, End-to-End Differentiable Framework for Gravitational-Wave Backgrounds from Compact Binary Populations
papers.summary: We present \texttt{StochAXtic}, a package for computing the dimensionless energy density spectrum $\Omega_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ of the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by compact binary coalescences. Rather than sampling binary populations via Monte Carlo, \texttt{StochAXtic} exploits the \emph{scale invariance} of the waveforms: at fixed mass ratio, spins and tidal deformabilities, the waveform depends on the total mass only through the dimensionless combination $Mf$. This allows all computationally expensive waveform evaluations using \texttt{LALSuite} to be performed once and stored in a population-independent lookup table. The subsequent integrals over mass and redshift can then be recast as convolutions and evaluated efficiently using fast Fourier transforms. We further employ truncated singular value decomposition to compress the lookup table, reducing both computational cost and memory requirements. Once the table has been computed and cached, \texttt{StochAXtic} evaluates $\Omega_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ in a few milliseconds, achieving a relative numerical error below $10^{-3}$ at frequencies up to $1$ kHz. Its results agree with those of \texttt{popstock} within the latter's statistical uncertainties. Implemented entirely in \texttt{JAX}, \texttt{StochAXtic} also provides gradients of $\Omega_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ with respect to population hyperparameters, enabling its direct integration with gradient-based inference methods including Hamiltonian Monte Carlo.

authors.name: Haowen Zhong, Ethan Vislosky, Emanuele Berti

papers.title: Exploring the growth-index ($\gamma$) tension with $\Lambda_{\rm s}$CDM
papers.summary: Recent analyses have revealed a significant tension in the growth index $\gamma$. When $\gamma$ is treated as a free parameter within $\Lambda$CDM, PL18+$f\sigma_8$ yields $\gamma \approx 0.64$, in $\sim4\sigma$ tension with the expected value $\gamma \approx 0.55$ (assuming general relativity). We investigate whether $\Lambda_{\rm s}$CDM -- featuring a rapid sign-switching cosmological constant (mirror AdS-to-dS transition) at redshift $z_\dagger \sim 2$ -- can alleviate the $\gamma$ tension together with the $H_0$ and $S_8$ tensions. We find that $\gamma\Lambda_{\rm s}$CDM can reduce the $\gamma$ and $H_0$ tensions relative to $\gamma\Lambda$CDM while maintaining low $S_8$ values. For PL18+$f\sigma_8$, it yields $z_\dagger>1.58$ (95% CL) and reduces the $\gamma$ and $H_0$ discrepancies from $3.7\sigma$ and $4.2\sigma$ in $\gamma\Lambda$CDM to $2.1\sigma$ and $1.1\sigma$, with $\chi^2_{\rm min}$ essentially unchanged. The largest improvement among the free-$z_\dagger$ analyses is for PL18+$f\sigma_8$+PP&SH0ES, with $z_\dagger=1.82^{+0.32}_{-0.28}$ (95% CL), $\gamma$ and $H_0$ tensions of $1.8\sigma$ and $0.6\sigma$, and an improved fit. The efficacy is, however, dataset dependent: the 3D BAO measurements from SDSS-IV/eBOSS and the first year of DESI observations tend to push the transition to $z_\dagger\gtrsim2.3$--$2.4$ and weaken the simultaneous alleviation, particularly of the $H_0$ tension. The fixed-$z_\dagger=1.7$ benchmark yields low residual tensions for PL18 and PL18+$f\sigma_8$, albeit with somewhat worse fits than $\gamma\Lambda$CDM, but is excluded at more than $2\sigma$ by the free-$z_\dagger$ analyses once the uncalibrated PantheonPlus SN Ia sample or the 3D BAO data are included. Our results indicate that $\Lambda_{\rm s}$CDM can contribute to the joint alleviation of multiple cosmological tensions, although its impact is dataset dependent.

authors.name: Luis A. Escamilla, \"Ozg\"ur Akarsu, Eleonora Di Valentino, Emre \"Oz\"ulker, J. Alberto Vazquez

papers.title: Background dynamics and cosmological tests of interacting, viscous $H^2+H^{-2}$ dark energy
papers.summary: We study dark-sector energy exchange and bulk viscosity in the HHDE model, whose density combines terms proportional to the square and inverse square of the Hubble parameter. Five viscosity cases and seven interactions give 35 fluid realizations governed by a common autonomous system. When the intrinsic dark-energy pressure is reconstructed from the continuity equation, dark-energy viscosity leaves the expansion history unchanged. Interaction and dark-matter viscosity enter through their net contribution, producing further exact background degeneracies. Each realization admits stable de Sitter attractors in physical parameter domains, either dominated by dark energy or containing residual dark matter sustained by exchange and viscous stress. Representative posterior trajectories connect the inferred present states to these endpoints. Using supernovae, cosmic chronometers, DESI baryon acoustic oscillations and a compressed Planck distance prior, the density-product interaction yields a Hubble constant of $71.15^{+1.53}_{-1.64}$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$. Conditional on the applicability of that prior, the preferred transfer from dark energy to dark matter lowers the minimum chi-squared by 75.16 relative to noninteracting HHDE and reduces the discrepancy with the local distance-ladder measurement to approximately one standard deviation when both uncertainties are combined.

authors.name: Guo Chen, Wei Fang, Chao-Jun Feng

papers.title: Optimal robust detection statistics for pulsar timing arrays
papers.summary: Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) seek to detect a nano-Hz stochastic gravitational-wave background (GWB) by searching for the characteristic Hellings and Downs angular pattern of timing residual correlations. So far, the evidence remains below the conventional $5\sigma$ threshold, as assessed using the literature-standard "optimal cross-correlation detection statistic". While this quadratic combination of cross-correlated data maximizes the deflection (signal-to-noise ratio), it does not maximize the detection probability at fixed false-alarm probability (FAP), and therefore is not Neyman-Pearson (NP) optimal for the assumed noise and signal models. The NP-optimal detection statistic is a different quadratic form, but is not used because it also incorporates autocorrelations, making it more susceptible to uncertainties in the modeling of pulsar timing noise. Here, we derive the best compromise: a quadratic detection statistic which is as close as possible to the NP-optimal detection statistic (minimizing the variance of its difference with the NP statistic) subject to the constraint that it only uses cross-correlations, so that it is less affected by pulsar noise modeling errors. We study the performance of this new NPMV statistic for a simulated PTA whose noise and (putative) signal match those of the NANOGrav 15-year data release: GWB amplitude $A_{\rm gw} = 2.1 \times 10^{-15}$ and spectral index $\gamma = 13/3$. Compared to the literature-standard "optimal" cross-correlation detection statistic, the NPMV statistic increases the detection probability by 47% when operating at a $5\sigma$ false-alarm probability of $\alpha = 2.9 \times 10^{-7}$.

authors.name: Rutger van Haasteren, Bruce Allen, Joseph D. Romano

papers.title: AGN x-ray reflection spectroscopy with ML_MYTORUS: Neural posterior estimation with training on observation-driven parameter grids
papers.summary: X-ray spectroscopy of active galactic nuclei (AGN) probes circumnuclear matter geometry. Many AGN show a narrow Fe K $\alpha$ line at 6.4 keV and associated Compton-scattered continua in their x-ray spectra, due to primary continuum scattering in cold, neutral material far from the central supermassive black hole. We present a novel approach via Simulation-Based Inference with Neural Posterior Estimation (SBI-NPE) and train a machine learning neural network (ML NN) model based on $NuSTAR$ spectral fitting results from the literature, employing the physically motivated MYTORUS-decoupled model, which distinguishes line-of-sight from global equivalent neutral hydrogen column density ($N_{\rm H,Z}$ vs. $N_{\rm H,S}$). To overcome the limitations of traditional frequentist fitting (e.g., lack of automation, reproducibility, computational cost), we implement normalizing flows and autoregressive networks to learn flexible posterior distributions from simulated spectra. From 34 $NuSTAR$ spectral fitting literature results, we simulate 34,000 spectra for both a uniform and a Gaussian parameter distribution. We train our neural network to determine four key MYTORUS parameters, $N_{H,Z}, N_{H,S}$, power-law spectral index $\Gamma$, and relative normalization $A_{\rm S}$. The observation-based grid significantly outperforms uniform sampling, achieving predictive accuracy for individual parameters >90% ($N_{H,S}$ and $A_{\rm S}$), 89% ($N_{\rm H,Z}$), and 82% ($\Gamma$) within $\pm1\sigma$. For all four parameters simultaneously, predictive accuracy remains high ($\sim$70%). The trained NN ML, ML_MYTORUS, is publicly available with a web interface for fast and reproducible parameter inference from $NuSTAR$ spectra. We illustrate its use via application to NGC 4388. This work shows that SBI offers great potential for future distant x-ray reflection studies in AGN or Galactic x-ray binary spectra.

authors.name: Ingrid Vanessa Daza-Perilla (CSST/UMBC, NASA/GSFC, CRESST/NASA-GSFC), Panayiotis Tzanavaris (CSST/UMBC, NASA/GSFC, CRESST/NASA-GSFC, APS), V. Madurga-Favieres (CSST/UMBC, NASA/GSFC, CRESST/NASA-GSFC, U. Rome Tor Vergata), M. Yukita (NASA/GSFC, JHU), A. Ptak (NASA/GSFC, JHU), T. Yaqoob (CSST/UMBC, NASA/GSFC, CRESST/NASA-GSFC)

papers.title: Improved Heavy Dark Matter Annihilation Search from Dwarf Galaxies with HAWC
papers.summary: Understanding dark matter's elusive nature is crucial for the framework of particle physics and expanding the Standard Model. This analysis utilizes the High Altitude Water Cherenkov (HAWC) gamma ray Observatory to indirectly search for dark matter (DM) by studying gamma ray emission from dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSphs). Selected for their high ratio of dark matter to baryonic matter, dSphs are useful for this type of search owing to the low background emission. In comparison to previous HAWC studies, we significantly improve our sensitivity to DM from dSphs due to improvements to our event reconstruction and reduced hadronic contamination. We expanded the number of dSphs studied, DM annihilation channels into the Standard Model (SM), and the amount of data collected on each previously studied dSph. We searched for DM signals in each dSph using the latest version of the algorithms used to reconstruct data from the primary detector of the HAWC instrument. We report that we do not detect evidence of DM from dSphs, so we place upper limits for the velocity-weighted DM annihilation cross-section ($\langle\sigma v \rangle$) on the order of $10^{-23}~\text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$ for a DM mass range of $1-10^4$ TeV.

papers.title: The deci-Hz gravitational wave signal from the collapse of rotating very massive stars
papers.summary: We calculate the gravitational wave signal from the collapse of a rotating 300 $M_\odot$ star just above the upper end of the pair-instability supernova regime. The large-scale asymmetries that develop during the collapse produce a strong signal in the deci-Hz range that has a characteristic shape that is likely amenable to a template-based search. Although tempered by the low incidence of nearby astrophysical candidates, the most ambitious designs for deci-Hz detectors could detect such signals out to distances of ~250 Mpc, possibly at a rate of 0.3 per year. Additional numerical modeling is required to refine these rate estimates, however. We also demonstrate that proposed deci-Hz GW observation missions, even without confident single-source detections, could be used to provide information about the population of astrophysical candidates and, in particular, constrain the initial mass function of very massive stars.

authors.name: Bailey Sykes, Jade Powell, Bernhard M\"uller, Alexander Heger

papers.title: Beyond the Diffusion Coefficient: Propagators and Memory in Cosmic Ray Transport
papers.summary: Cosmic ray (CR) transport is usually modeled with a single diffusion coefficient, but this description captures only the growth of the variance. Distinct transport mechanisms can share the same effective diffusion coefficient while producing different particle distributions and approaches to the diffusive limit. The distinction matters in multiphase, structured and time-dependent media, and is reflected in the observed variation of CR transport near pulsar wind nebulae, supernova remnants and molecular clouds, and in particle-tracing studies that show both superdiffusion and subdiffusion. We therefore develop a propagator-based framework centered on the probability distribution of particle positions, or equivalently its Fourier-Laplace transform. This object is compact and complete for the observable spatial transport. It naturally reveals if large scale transport has memory: when the CR flux depends on earlier rather than just the instantaneous pressure gradient. Such memory arises when dynamically relevant transport states, such as trapping or phase changes, are not retained in the macroscopic description. Using the Montroll-Weiss formalism, we measure the propagator directly from trajectories, recover the associated memory kernel, and represent broad kernels with a Prony expansion. Applied to a multiphase medium, the framework shows that slow regions can regulate escape without dominating the total residence time budget. We also introduce an accelerated Monte Carlo method for coarse-grained transport, showing that if trapping structures evolve while particles are still sampling them, the static long-time limit need not be reached. This provides a foundation for observational applications, particle-tracing measurements and CR-MHD closures.

authors.name: Naixin Liang, S. Peng Oh

papers.title: Constraining Quintessential Inflation with ACT: A Gauss-Bonnet Gateway
papers.summary:
Recent results from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT), which, when combined with Planck, CMB lensing, DESI DR2 with BAO data, indicate a higher and more tightly constrained scalar spectral index, $
s = 0.9743 \pm 0.0034$ P-ACT-LB), place several inflationary models under tension, with quintessential inflation pushed close to or beyond the $2\sigma$ boundary in the $r$--$
s$ plane for this dataset combination. In this work, we revisit quintessential inflation within the framework of Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet (EGB) gravity, where a scalar field non-minimally coupled to the Gauss--Bonnet invariant modifies the inflationary dynamics. We consider three representative coupling functions -- exponential, hyperbolic secant, and hyperbolic tangent -- and show that the exponential and sech-type couplings can shift the predicted values of $r$ and $
s$ into the $1\sigma$ region allowed by the P-ACT-LB-BK18 combination, thereby restoring consistency with these observations. In contrast, the tanh-type coupling remains disfavoured, underscoring the sensitivity of inflationary observables to the coupling structure. We further investigate the reheating phase using a model-independent parameterisation and demonstrate that viable thermal histories can be realised even in the absence of a potential minimum, with reheating temperatures consistent with Big Bang nucleosynthesis bounds. We emphasise that the quantitative conclusions are conditional on the choice of dataset combination: the preference for a higher $
s$ is driven by the ACT data and, indirectly, by DESI BAO, whereas combinations based on Planck alone or including the latest SPT-3G data yield lower central values of $
s$ and correspondingly milder tension for standard quintessential inflation.

authors.name: Yogesh, Imtiyaz Ahmad Bhat, Mayukh R. Gangopadhyay, M. Sami

papers.title: JWST and Keck observations of the off-nuclear tidal disruption event TDE 2025abcr: An evolving reprocessing layer
papers.summary: Off-nuclear tidal disruption events (TDEs) provide a rare probe of massive black holes (MBHs) outside galactic nuclei. Only a handful are known, including five X-ray-selected candidates and three optically selected events. We present observations of TDE 2025abcr, the second optically selected off-nuclear TDE, discovered at a projected offset of $9.08 \pm 0.02$ kpc from the nucleus of its host galaxy. We analyze X-ray, UV, optical, and infrared (IR) data from Swift, Keck, ZTF, and JWST. Broad H and He emission lines in the optical and IR confirm a TDE-H-He classification. From luminosity scaling relations and MOSFiT modeling, we infer a BH mass of $10^{6}$-$10^{7}\,M_{\odot}$, substantially smaller than the $10^{8.38 \pm 0.42}\,M_{\odot}$ BH inferred for the host-galaxy nucleus. We observe velocity evolution in the N III + He II emission complex, shifting from $-100$ km s$^{-1}$ at day $-7$ to $+1000$ km s$^{-1}$ by day $+29$, which we interpret as radiative transfer effects in an evolving reprocessing layer. The IR SED deviates from a thermal blackbody, with $\nu L_{\nu} \propto \lambda^{-2.13 \pm 0.04}$, significantly shallower than the Rayleigh-Jeans slope of $\lambda^{-3}$. We rule out dust as the source of this IR excess. Two possibilities remain: free-free emission from reprocessing gas, or an unresolved stellar cluster at the TDE location. Reprocessed emission provides a natural explanation for the IR excess but an underlying stellar cluster of mass $\log(M_{*}/M_{\odot}) = 7.57 \pm 0.02$ and age $<$2 Gyr is also consistent with the data. If interpreted as a stellar cluster, the inferred mass suggests a stripped remnant of a satellite galaxy. The wandering MBH most likely originated in a minor merger with a smaller galaxy, although dynamical ejection from the host nucleus cannot yet be ruled out.

authors.name: Kishore C. Patra, Emily R. Liepold, Nicholas Earl, Ryan J. Foley, Chung-Pei Ma, Sebastian Gomez, Kyle W. Davis, Enrico Ramirez-Ruiz, K. Decker French, Jonelle L. Walsh, Ravjit Kaur, Kirsty Taggart, Joshua Candanoza, V. Ashley Villar, Prasiddha Arunachalam, Phillip Macias, Samaporn Tinyanont

papers.title: The NIKA2 Cosmological Legacy Survey in COSMOS: Final 1.2mm and 2mm source catalogs and redshift distribution of dusty star-forming galaxies
papers.summary: We present the final 1.2mm and 2mm source catalogs and the redshift distribution of the mm-selected population from the NIKA2 Cosmological Legacy Survey (N2CLS) in the COSMOS field. Our aim is to provide a comprehensive dataset for studying the physical properties and evolution of high-redshift DSFGs. N2CLS covers ~1070 arcmin2 with median noise levels of 315$\mu$Jy and 91$\mu$Jy at 1.2 and 2mm, respectively. Sources are extracted with a S/N threshold of 3.9, ensuring >80% purity. Multi-wavelength counterparts are identified using high-resolution interferometric (sub-)mm data (NOEMA, ALMA) and radio observations (VLA, MeerKAT). Redshifts are compiled from spectroscopic and photometric catalogs (e.g., COSMOSWeb). The N2CLS master catalog includes 323 sources detected at >80% purity, with 104 sources detected in both bands, 197 only at 1.2mm, and 22 only at 2mm. Multi-wavelength identifications are secured for ~89% of the sample. The redshift distribution of 1.2mm sources peaks at 2.8$\pm$0.1, consistent with the epoch of peak cosmic star formation. In the total sample, we lack redshift for ~2% of the identified galaxies, plus 34 sources for which no accurate positional proxy is available, preventing the identification of a multi-wavelength counterpart. We identify 66 galaxies at z>4. The observed redshift distribution agrees well with the SIDES simulations, while four other galaxy evolution models are statistically inconsistent with the data. N2CLS is the largest contiguous deep survey to date with this depth and homogeneous coverage. This homogeneous coverage is important, as 25% of N2CLS sources lack a SCUBA2 850 micron counterpart, likely because the strongly non-uniform noise distribution of the SCUBA2 map results in lower sensitivity in parts of the field. The released data products provide a legacy dataset for studying dust-obscured galaxy evolution.

papers.title: Exploring the Dark Sector: Interacting Radiation in Light of Modern Cosmological Probes
papers.summary: [abridged] We constrain a phenomenological dark radiation (DR) framework consisting of free-streaming and fluid-like components, providing a model-independent extension of the standard radiation sector. Using Planck CMB data, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and Pantheon+ and DES Y5 (Dovekie) supernova samples, we derive constraints on additional relativistic degrees of freedom and assess their impact on cosmological tensions. We obtain $N_{\rm fld}<0.66$ (95% C.L.) from CMB data alone, while the combination with BAO yields $N_{\rm fs}=2.93\pm0.23$ and $N_{\rm fld}=0.36^{+0.16}_{-0.21}$ (68% C.L.), consistent with Standard Model expectations for free-streaming radiation. The DR framework significantly alleviates the Hubble tension through an enhanced early-time expansion rate, which reduces the sound horizon scale. The tension with SH0ES is reduced from highly significant in $\Lambda$CDM to statistically non-significant for CMB+BAO data according to the $\mathcal{T}$-statistic. Bayesian model comparison shows no decisive preference for DR over $\Lambda$CDM when SH0ES is excluded, with results in the regime of weakly disfavoured. However, including SH0ES data leads to decisive Bayesian evidence in favour of the DR scenario. Overall, DR provides a compelling framework for resolving the Hubble tension. When CMB, BAO, Pantheon$+$ and SH0ES data are considered, we find an increased effective radiation content, $N_{\rm tot}=3.63^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$, with a fraction of free-streaming radiation, $f_{\rm fs}=0.392\pm 0.026$, a reduced sound horizon scale, $r_d = 141.8^{+1.3}_{-1.2}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, and a higher primordial helium fraction, $Y_{\rm He}=0.2530 \pm 0.0017$, which lies at the level of approximately $\sim 2$-$2.5\sigma$ above direct determinations from metal-poor H II regions, while remaining broadly consistent with other abundance measurements within current uncertainties.

authors.name: Matteo Mescia, H\'ector Gil-Mar\'in

papers.title: Testing the prevalence of hydrogen-silicate miscibility in young sub-Neptunes
papers.summary: Hydrogen-silicate miscibility can significantly alter the interior structure and thermal evolution of sub-Neptunes. We consider the interplay between this miscibility and stellar-driven atmospheric escape. We find that, for the first $\sim 100$ Myrs, sub-Neptunes store most of their hydrogen content within their miscible interiors, protecting it from escape. As hydrogen is removed from the top of the atmosphere, more hydrogen is exsolved from the miscible interior, resupplying the envelope mass and delaying the planet's contraction when compared with models that do not account for miscibility. We construct a population-level Bayesian hierarchical inference model which tests for the prevalence of fully miscible sub-Neptunes. With conservative measurement uncertainty and no completeness corrections, we predict that $\sim 100-200$ observed young sub-Neptunes with measured radii, masses and ages $\lesssim 1$ Gyr are required to differentiate between fully miscible and immiscible models. This survey size requirement decreases with improved measurement uncertainty. Furthermore, one can reliably infer the underlying distributions of planetary initial conditions if completeness corrections are included in the analysis.

authors.name: James G. Rogers, Hilke E. Schlichting

papers.title: On the Separation Between the Brightest Cluster Galaxy and the Intracluster Light
papers.summary: We present a model-based framework to define an aperture separation between the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) and the intracluster light (ICL). Using the intrinsic BCG and ICL components predicted by the semi-analytic model \texttt{FEGA25}, we determine, for each halo, the aperture radius that minimizes the bias in the recovered ICL mass. The optimal radius is obtained by balancing the BCG stellar mass lying outside the aperture with the ICL mass enclosed within it. At $z=0$, the optimal aperture in physical units increases with halo mass approximately as $r_{\rm cut}\propto M_{\rm halo}^{0.28}$, close to the expected virial scaling. When expressed in units of the virial radius, the aperture becomes nearly independent of halo mass, with $r_{\rm cut}/R_{\rm vir}\simeq 0.045$ at $10^{14}M_\odot$. Applying the resulting aperture prescriptions, we recover the intrinsic BCG mass to better than 8\% (lowest percentile), while the ICL mass is recovered with median values very close to unity, and an average scatter of $\pm 3\%$. Extending the analysis to $z=1$ and $z=2$, we find that the mass trends remain similar, with the slope and intercept of $r_{\rm cut}/R_{\rm vir}$ that stay stable. Robustness tests show that the inferred aperture is most sensitive to the ICL concentration and BCG size, but the main trends are preserved. Our results provide a physically motivated aperture definition for connecting observational BCG--ICL measurements to intrinsic model components.

authors.name: Emanuele Contini, Sukyoung K. Yi

papers.title: The silent dark sector: a field-theory approach to unified dark fluids with vanishing speed of sound
papers.summary: We introduce a novel class of field-theory models that provide a unified description of the dark sector as a single perfect fluid with vanishing sound speed. These models also admit the interpretation of cold dark matter interacting with vacuum energy while avoiding any phantom behavior and including standard $\Lambda$CDM as a particular case. Built upon a single scalar field invariant under transverse diffeomorphisms, the framework naturally implements the constraints imposed in the so called mimetic models. We analyze a particular simple example exhibiting an effectively evolving dark energy and find that it can reproduce the DESI best-fit CPL evolution with the same number of free parameters.

authors.name: Javier de Cruz P\'erez, Dar\'io Jaramillo-Garrido, Antonio L. Maroto, Prado Mart\'in-Moruno

papers.title: Hermes - Towards an Optimal High-Performance Algorithm for Cosmic Statistics of Large Data Sets
papers.summary: We present Hermes, an in situ multiresolution framework for efficient and flexible measurements of cosmic large-scale-structure statistics from discrete catalogues. Hermes replaces conventional ex situ counting of particle tuples with algebraic operations among window-filtered continuous fields. A discrete point distribution is first reconstructed as a continuous density field in a compact scaling-function representation, in which two- and higher-point statistics are formulated as spatial products of locally filtered fields. This formulation expresses conventional binning for counts-in-cells and two- and higher-point correlation functions through window functions. Changing the window kernels defines generalised statistics without redesigning the estimator. We further introduce PyHermes, an open-source Python implementation of this framework, combining multiresolution field reconstruction with FFT-based window convolution, MPI/thread parallelism, and GPU acceleration for high-order field contractions. The framework supports a broad range of measurements, including isotropic and anisotropic two-point statistics, marked correlations, standard and multipole three-point functions, filtered statistics, and Fourier-space differential operators for constructing derived physical fields. Using halo catalogues from cosmological N-body simulations, we demonstrate PyHermes through a range of clustering statistics and use benchmarks to quantify its computational efficiency and scalability for large-scale data sets. By separating field representation from statistical windows, Hermes provides a unified computational framework in which a single reconstructed field can be reused for a wide range of standard and customised cosmic statistics. This field-window architecture enables scalable analysis of the large data sets expected from current and future galaxy surveys.

authors.name: Long-long Feng, Tengpeng Xu, Tian-Cheng Luan, Jiawei Li, Xin Sun, Wenjie Ju, Zhuoyang Li, Shiyu Yue, Weishan Zhu, Yan-Chuan Cai

papers.title: Gravitational Wave Modeling of White-Dwarf--Compact-Object Binaries and Observational Outlook
papers.summary: Binaries consisting of a white dwarf and a compact object (neutron stars, black holes, or sub-solar-mass compact objects) display unique orbital evolution and gravitational wave signals. We investigate the end stages of these systems by developing a novel integrator implementing mass transfer and 2.5-order Post-Newtonian kinematics. White-dwarf--compact-object binaries are subject to two phases: a slow inspiral during which binary evolution is dominated by weak-gravity radiation reaction and a quicker "outspiral" dominated by mass transfer. These systems have unique gravitational waveforms with several characteristic features including an accumulation of signal near the maximum cutoff frequency set by the transition between in- and outspiral. We investigate trends in gravitational wave parameters based on component masses. In particular, maximum cutoff frequency depends strongly on white dwarf mass and compactness. It is unlikely that extragalactic binaries will be measured by LISA or current or future terrestrial detectors. However, white-dwarf--compact-object binary end stages will be an important source for future decihertz detectors such as DECIGO and LGWA: The final inspiral of tens of white-dwarf--neutron-star binaries will be detected annually by LGWA, and millions of inspirals along with thousands of outspirals will be detected by DECIGO. The ultimate fates of these binaries are diverse and dependent upon the intricacies of angular momentum loss. In particular, we show that white dwarfs with partners of sufficiently low/high mass can end their lives in mergers, while white dwarfs do not enter contact with partners of intermediate mass. The highest frequencies produced by white-dwarf--compact-object binaries in our tests are 10--20 Hz--incapable of mimicking sub-solar-mass compact object signals in terrestrial detectors or explaining S251112cm-like signals.

authors.name: Tristan S. Weaver, David Radice, Donghui Jeong, Victor Liu

papers.title: Stellar mergers and chemical element mixing: implications for metamorphic stellar evolution in AGN disks
papers.summary: Chemical mixing during stellar mergers can significantly influence the subsequent evolution of the merger remnant. We perform a suite of three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations of stellar mergers, each evolved for $\sim100$ stellar dynamical times until the remnant reaches a quasi-hydrostatic equilibrium. The simulations incorporate subgrid-scale diffusion models to capture the turbulent mixing of chemical elements. Starting with an idealized polytropic equation of state (EOS), we first identify the dominant mixing mechanisms and investigate how the merger outcome depends on the mass ratio, relative velocity, impact parameter, and stellar structure. We then extend our simulations to the context of stars embedded in active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks, using a realistic, composition-dependent EOS and AGN stellar models generated with the stellar evolution code MESA. We find that mergers with both younger metamorphic stars and H-rich accreting AGN stars can substantially rejuvenate old metamorphic stars through efficient core mixing after thermal relaxation. The merger remnants are nitrogen-enriched, with ${\rm N/O}\sim1$--3 and ${\rm N/C}\gtrsim5$, comparable to the abundances observed in the nebula surrounding SN~1987A. During subsequent stellar evolution, the remnants may converge onto the main sequence of isolated metamorphic AGN stars once they reach accretion--wind equilibrium. They may also deposit a significant amount of chemically enriched material into the AGN disk. This work provides a physical framework for connecting hydrodynamical stellar mergers with the long-term evolution of AGN stars and their observational and chemical signatures.

authors.name: Yanlong Shi, Xiaoshan Huang, Douglas N. C. Lin, Norman Murray

papers.title: Electron transport in a radiation-dominated plasma Application to solar corona brightenings
papers.summary: Bremsstrahlung scattering of fast electrons on ions can be enhanced by the microwave radiation present in the solar corona. It can account for the electron diffusive transport along magnetic loops and high precipitation rates. This process can also dominate the transport of thermal electrons confined in such loops. The influence of stimulated Bremsstrahlung scattering on the electron transport is studied, with focus on the return current induced by the fast electron population trapped in magnetic loops. Overall, transport coefficients are reevaluated in the radiation-dominated plasma, characterized by the stimulated action of radiation on the Bremsstrahlung electron-ion collision, down to thermal velocities. We develop a theoretical framework for electron transport driven by a large bandwidth, bright low-frequency part of the photon spectrum and compute a set of radiation-enhanced transport coefficients. UV, XEUV and hard X-ray signals from flares, evidencing anomalous resistivity, thermal conduction inhibition and high precipitation rates of fast electrons, are reinterpreted. The anomalous resistivity due to stimulated Bremsstrahlung scattering is found to dominate the classical resistivity in flares. The runaway effect due to Coulomb collisions is suppressed. Thermal conduction is inhibited compared to the Spitzer conduction, in agreement with coronal seismology of slow-mode waves. Stimulated Bremsstrahlung scattering is found to be a key collisional process in flaring events. It can explain the above loop-top hard X-ray signal due to the fast electrons, and the measured electrical conductivity due to the thermal electrons. As a perspective, the corresponding transport coefficients can be used in radiation MHD codes. The radiation model could also be applied to stimulate large-angle electron scattering in the kinetic or hybrid models used to study the solar corona.

authors.name: Roland Duclous, Vladimir Tikhonchuk, Marina Leboulanger, Xavier Blanc, Allan-Sacha Brun, Antoine Strugarek

papers.title: Multi-dimensional NLTE radiative transfer for a double detonation Type Ia explosion model in the photospheric phase
papers.summary: Previous radiative transfer calculations have shown that both multi-dimensionality and NLTE (non local thermodynamic equilibrium) effects impact the synthetic observables predicted for Type Ia supernova explosion models. Here we carry out a 2D NLTE radiative transfer simulation in the photospheric phase for a double detonation model with a 1 M$_{\odot}$ carbon-oxygen core and 0.02 M$_{\odot}$ helium shell. The predicted observables demonstrate that departures from both spherical symmetry and local thermodynamic equilibrium are significant on scales relevant to comparisons with observations. The NLTE treatment leads to a bluer spectral energy distribution, more slowly declining optical-band light curves, changes to the near-infrared light curve shapes, and differences in the evolution of key spectral features. Although substantial viewing-angle variation is predicted for the model, the scale of the variation is not significantly impacted by NLTE effects up to peak. However, after peak, our 2D NLTE simulation retains a strong viewing-angle dependence in its spectra whereas our simulation of the same ejecta model using an approximate NLTE treatment predicts significantly reduced spectroscopic viewing-angle variation. The NLTE treatment leads to improved agreement with normal Type Ia supernovae, primarily due to the increased ionisation state of the simulation, although the absence of a secondary near-infrared maximum suggests that the ejecta remain over-ionised relative to observations after peak. Despite the improved agreement, many viewing angles still show excessive line blanketing, suggesting that the 0.02 M$_{\odot}$ helium-shell mass of the current model is too large to reproduce normal Type Ia supernovae over the majority of lines of sight.

authors.name: F. P. Callan, L. J. Shingles, S. A. Sim, C. E. Collins, J. M. Pollin, R. Pakmor, S. Gronow, F. K. Roepke, A. Holas, I. R. Seitenzahl

papers.title: JWST detects a dusty AGB-like source before the Type Ia-CSM supernova 2026sqf
papers.summary: Supernova (SN) 2026sqf recently appeared in the nearby face-on spiral galaxy NGC~3310 and has shown signs of strong interaction with a circumstellar medium (CSM). Such intense interaction, rare among nearby SNe, offers a valuable opportunity to reveal details on the origin and nature of its progenitor system. We analyzed the early-phase spectra and light curves (LCs) of SN 2026sqf. We identified a point source near the SN position in pre-explosion JWST and HST imaging, tested its association with the SN through astrometric alignment of pre- and post-explosion images and a chance-projection analysis, and constructed and modeled its spectral energy distribution (SED). The general characteristics of the spectra, the strengths of the emission lines, and the LC evolution all suggest that SN 2026sqf belongs to the rare SN Ia-CSM subclass, which would make it the closest known member (D~19 Mpc). The point source is a credible counterpart of the progenitor system, the first such identification for this SN subclass. Under our modeling assumptions, carbonaceous dust around a luminous evolved star provides a reasonable description of its combined SED; compared with local analogues, the candidate most closely resembles an extreme asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star. We report the first candidate pre-explosion counterpart of a thermonuclear SN identified in JWST imaging. Our results support the scenario in which SNe Ia-CSM emerge from a system consisting of a white dwarf and an evolved giant (probably AGB) star. Strong binary interaction, possibly involving common-envelope evolution or a merger, is a natural explanation for the observed properties of the SN and its candidate counterpart, though the channel and timescale remain uncertain. Late-time follow-up, especially with JWST, will test the identification and the conclusions of our early-phase analysis.

authors.name: Tam\'as Szalai, Dan Milisavljevic, Noah Zimmer, Braden Garretson, Thomas Moore, Schuyler D. Van Dyk, Anan Lu, Selcuk Topal, Ori D. Fox, Tuomas Kangas, Seppo Mattila, Andrea Reguitti, Uliana Pylypenko, Chuck Cynamon, Ting-Wan Chen, Amar Aryan, Dylan Caudill, Danielle Dickinson, Martin Bureau, Woorak Choi, Timothy A. Davis, Daryl Haggard, Thomas M. Reynolds, Maximilian Stritzinger, Patrick Wiggins

papers.title: The high entropy of the UHECR arrival direction distribution favors a light composition
papers.summary: We analyze the constraints on the composition of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), and on the density and distribution of their sources, that may be inferred from their arrival-direction distribution, using a novel semi-analytical description of the propagation energy loss of atomic nuclei ($A>4$) with energy $>2\times10^{19}~\text{eV}$, that allows generating UHECR arrival maps faster than by using detailed propagation simulations and yields insights to the impact of propagation energy loss. We show that the anisotropy of the UHECR arrival direction distribution due to the large-scale structure (LSS) of matter distribution is larger for heavy nuclei composition compared to protons, despite their larger deflections by magnetic fields, due to their shorter propagation distance and weaker dependence of rigidity on observed energy. Identifying the LSS anisotropy signal is hampered for heavy nuclei due to their large deflections by the uncertain Galactic magnetic field (GMF). We introduce a new measure of anisotropy, an "entropy" of the arrival-direction distribution, that is largely independent of the GMF configuration and has strong discriminating power between heavy- and light-composition models. Analyzing the public $>3.2\times10^{19}$~eV Auger data, we show that the correlation with the LSS on large angular scales is weak and requires a low source density, $s_0\le10^{-4}{\rm Mpc}^{-3}$, to allow masking the LSS signature by "cosmic-variance" ($s_0=10^{-2}{\rm Mpc}^{-3}$ is ruled out at $>99\%$ confidence level (CL)). The high entropy of the distribution is consistent with proton models and inconsistent with heavy nuclei models at $>96\%$ CL for $s_0\ge10^{-5}{\rm Mpc}^{-3}$. Reducing the absolute energy calibration uncertainty may allow detection of the LSS correlation for proton models (increased exposure alone will not suffice due to the dominance of cosmic variance).

authors.name: Nimrod Strasman, Eli Waxman

papers.title: PowerFull: fast and accurate computation of the relativistic angular galaxy power spectrum including local primordial non-Gaussianity
papers.summary: Current and forthcoming wide-field galaxy surveys, such as SPHEREx and Euclid, provide a unique opportunity to probe the ultra-large scales of structure formation, where primordial non-Gaussianity, often parameterized by $f_\text{NL}$, is expected to leave its most detectable imprint. At the same time, these surveys inevitably enter regimes where relativistic and wide-angle effects become significant, requiring careful modeling to extract unbiased cosmological information. We address these challenges by applying the total-angular-momentum (TAM) formalism to describe redshift-space clustering beyond the flat-sky approximation. The standard Fourier-mode description, which characterizes distortions by the angle between a mode and a line of sight, becomes ill-defined over wide fields, whereas the TAM basis naturally separates radial and angular contributions and incorporates the relevant relativistic effects. Within this framework, we provide a new parameterization of wide-angle predictions that can be compared directly with survey data. We then introduce PowerFull, a modification of the Julia-based 2-FAST package, which enables efficient computation of the full relativistic angular power spectrum. Finally, using Fisher information matrix-based analyses, we show that a survey like SPHEREx reaches $\sigma(f_\text{NL}) \sim 1$, but that neglecting the relativistic and wide-angle contributions shifts the recovered $f_\text{NL}$ by an amount of order its own uncertainty: at this precision the inferred value is biased unless the clustering is modeled consistently.

authors.name: Gregory Lukens, Donghui Jeong

papers.title: Wideband overlapped polyphase channelizer for kinetic inductance detector readout: split-path architecture and experimental characterization
papers.summary: Frequency-multiplexed readout of kinetic inductance detector arrays measures the complex transmission of thousands of superconducting resonators. The channelizer that separates them introduces systematic effects: a gain that depends on where each tone falls in the channel grid, leakage between channels and added noise. This article presents a 4096-channel polyphase channelizer with 2/1 overlap for a 4.096 GS/s input, implemented on a first-generation radio-frequency system-on-chip, and a procedure to characterize it on the board with two receive chains, one digitizing the excitation as a reference. A split-path architecture computes the two overlap states in parallel filter branches at 256 MHz and reorders them frame by frame, under three control rules; it keeps only the transform stage at 512 MHz and affords a prototype of 16 taps per polyphase path (65536 coefficients) at the multiplication rate of a published 8-tap bank. Each selected channel is exported as a complex series at 1 MS/s. The measured channel response follows the coefficient-table model within 0.15 dB down to -28 dB, with both overlapping channels at full gain across their common band. Leakage into every measured channel 1.875 MHz or more from the tone is -94 dBc or lower, apart from images attributed to converter interleaving. The signal-to-noise ratio per sample lies within 1.7 dB of the limit set by the data-sheet noise density of the converter, and an emulated detector pulse is recovered with a decay time of 14.65 $\mu$s (standard uncertainty 0.04 $\mu$s), within 0.7% of the expected value.

authors.name: Alberto Hernandez Fernandez, David Diaz Martin, Jose Javier Diaz Garcia, Roger John Hoyland, Luis Fernando Rodriguez Ramos, Diego Portero Rodriguez, Silvestre Rodriguez Perez

papers.title: COSMOS-Web: From early star-formation enhancement to late suppression in galaxy groups
papers.summary: Galaxy groups trace dense environments where interactions, gas removal, and reduced accretion may drive quenching. Common diagnostics trace star formation only over short timescales ($\lesssim100$ Myr), so time-resolved star formation histories (SFHs) are needed to separate recent changes from longer-term evolution at fixed mass and redshift. Using COSMOS-Web data, we test how group environment correlates with star-formation activity, and how this evolves with cosmic time and group-centric distance. We combine COSMOS2025/COSMOS-Web stellar masses and non-parametric SFHs with group detections and probabilistic memberships from AMICO. We compare stacked SFHs of group and field galaxies matched in mass and redshift, using the 30 richest groups in each redshift bin to measure how the SFH offset evolves with group-centric distance. Massive galaxies ($\log(M_\star/M_\odot)>10.5$) show the largest offsets but are already quenched in both environments. For lower masses ($8.11$ SFHs show weaker suppression or occasional enhancement. The radial signal evolves similarly: quenching is broad across radius at low $z$, the inner--outer contrast appears at $z>0.5$, and any ordering at $z\gtrsim2$ remains tentative given growing uncertainties in the AMICO centroids. Groups are thus more mixed at early epochs, with both suppressed and occasionally elevated SFHs, while suppression dominates at $z<1$, most clearly for low-to-intermediate-mass galaxies. This fits a picture where inner-region galaxies spend more time in the group potential, undergo more passages through dense intra-group gas, and accrete less pristine cold gas, making quenching progressively clearer with cosmic time.

Nu\~nez-Casti\~neyra, J. Rhee, R. M. Samir, M. Trebitsch, L. Tresse

papers.title: A Unified Tracer Analysis of DESI DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillations
papers.summary: We improve upon previous efforts to optimally combine overlapping galaxy samples in the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) analysis. By weighting each galaxy by its linear bias, overlapping galaxies are combined into a single, unified catalog, naturally avoiding double counting of cosmic volume and including all auto- and cross- information at the catalog level. Improvements over the previous effort include the addition of quasars out to $z=1.6$ to account for all overlapping DR2 tracers and redshift-dependent bias treatment to improve reconstruction. We report distance measurements using this unified tracer, and find them to be highly consistent with the baseline DR2 BAO analysis. We also test for tracer-dependent systematics within the DESI data, and find no evidence of tracer-dependent systematics within $0.8<z<1.6$. Finally, we take advantage of the unified tracer to rebin the analysis in redshift in order to more finely resolve the redshift-to-distance relation. Dynamical dark energy results on this finer redshift binning indicate that there is no missed feature in the expansion history in the redshifts $0.8<z<1.6$, and reproduces DESI's preference for an evolving dark energy equation of state.
