papers.title: Little Red Dots as Shock-Powered High-Energy Neutrino Sources
papers.summary: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are compact, high-redshift sources whose physical nature remains uncertain. Their optical spectra motivate a scenario in which their emission may be powered by shocks interacting with dense surrounding material. We investigate whether such interactions can power LRDs and contribute to the diffuse high-energy neutrino intensity measured by IceCube. In our simplified model, a fast central-engine outflow drives a shock through stationary or slow outflowing material, followed by a prescribed quasi-stationary interaction near the LRD photosphere. We consider the time-averaged neutrino emission from shock-active LRDs without requiring a single shock to persist throughout the LRD lifetime. We explore parameter ranges motivated by the observed and inferred properties of LRDs, finding solutions with shock luminosities 2.0e43 < L_s < 3.5e44 erg/s. Using an analytical framework for cosmic-ray acceleration and hadronic interactions in dense shock environments, we calculate the resulting high-energy neutrino emission and integrate it over the cosmological LRD population. For our fiducial cosmic-ray parameters, the average predicted contribution below 2e5 GeV increases from 0.2% for the lowest-luminosity quintile to 2% for the highest-luminosity quintile, while an illustrative higher-efficiency case reaches 13% of the IceCube diffuse neutrino intensity. These estimates assume all observed LRDs are shock-active. A smaller active fraction or a reduced covering factor would decrease the predicted intensity, whereas survey incompleteness could increase it. Improved models and population synthesis are needed to constrain the total LRD contribution.

authors.name: Tyco Mera, Chris Ashall, Shunsaku Horiuchi, Rohan Naidu, Kyle Medler, Peter Hoeflich

papers.title: A Diagnostic Method for Proto-Neutron Star Magnetic Fields by Supernova Fallback Neutrinos
papers.summary: Young isolated neutron stars exhibit a wide range of magnetic field strengths. To understand the origin of this diversity, it is important to observationally constrain magnetic fields during the proto-neutron star (PNS) phase. We propose a novel diagnostic of PNS magnetic fields using neutrinos associated with supernova fallback. By performing one-dimensional general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations of the supernova fallback onto a magnetized PNS, we investigate how the energy spectra of the fallback neutrinos depend on the PNS magnetic field strength and the fallback accretion rate. We find that stronger magnetic fields and lower accretion rates produce softer spectra because the fallback neutrinos are emitted mainly near the magnetospheric radius, which becomes larger under these conditions. To quantify this spectral softening, we define a hardness ratio based on event rates above and below 30 MeV and introduce a hardness-event-rate diagram. Using this diagram, we identify the parameter region in which our diagnostic is applicable. Its applicability depends on the PNS magnetic field strength, fallback accretion rate, onset time of the fallback phase, and neutrino mass ordering. We also investigate the dependence on the PNS radius and find that a larger radius produces softer spectra, indicating a degeneracy between the magnetic field and PNS compactness. An independent constraint on the PNS compactness would therefore enable us to better constrain the magnetic field. These results suggest that future multimessenger observations of galactic supernovae can provide a new window into the NS diversity.

authors.name: Akihiro Inoue, Yudai Suwa, Ryuichiro Akaho, Shinsuke Takasao, Kazumi Kashiyama, Hiroyuki R. Takahashi

papers.title: Revisiting damping of Alfv\'en waves in partially ionized plasmas
papers.summary: We investigate the damping rate of Alfv\'en waves by means of the linear analysis of the two-fluid ten-moments system. To treat effects of viscosity in a wide frequency range, we take account of the time evolution of the traceless part of the pressure tensor. In addition, to treat effects of viscosity in a wide range of the ionization degree, we consider interactions between hydrogen atoms and between protons and hydrogen atoms in the equation of the traceless part of the pressure tensor. We find approximate analytical solutions to the dispersion relation for some limits. Our analysis in the low-frequency limit shows that the viscous damping dominates over the frictional damping in the high-beta plasma, which is independent of the ionization degree. Therefore, the viscosity of hydrogen gas significantly affects cosmic-ray propagation in a partially ionized high-beta plasma.

authors.name: Yutaka Ohira

papers.title: Polarised X-ray emission from the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4-3658 during an X-ray outburst and a type-I X-ray burst
papers.summary: Modelling the X-ray pulse profiles of accreting millisecond pulsars (AMSPs) is a key technique for constraining the masses and radii of neutron stars. To this end, measuring the properties of polarised X-rays provides crucial information on the system geometry. We present the significant detection by IXPE of linearly polarised 2-8 keV X-rays during the decay of the 2025 outburst of the 2.5 ms AMSP SAX J1808.4-3658, with an average polarisation degree of $2.9\%\pm0.5\%$ and a polarisation angle of $46{\deg}\pm5{\deg}$ (measured East of celestial North), offset by $\sim 16{\deg}$-$24{\deg}$ from the average direction observed in the optical band over various epochs during the main part of the outburst. The observed degree of X-ray polarisation is similar to that found in the only other source of this class that has been targeted so far. By using a pulse-phase timing solution obtained with IXPE and NuSTAR, which confirms the long-term evolution of the pulsar spin and orbit, we did not find any significant pulse phase-resolved variability in the normalised Stokes parameters. Interpreting the polarised X-rays as originating from hot spots on the NS surface indicates they are almost aligned with the spin axis. We also report an indication for linearly polarised emission with a degree of $16\%\pm6\%$ (2-6 keV) during the peak of a type-I thermonuclear X-ray burst, with an angle almost orthogonal to that of the persistent emission. If confirmed, this level would exceed expectations for X-rays reflected by a thin accretion disc.

authors.name: A. Papitto, A. Di Marco, M. C. Baglio, D. Baldi Tomei, C. Ballocco, G. Illiano, R. La Placa, C. Malacaria, A. Bobrikova, J. Poutanen, T. Salmi, A. Sanna, A. Veledina, F. Ambrosino, L. Burderi, S. Campana, F. Coti Zelati, D. de Martino, T. Di Salvo, G. L. Israel, F. La Monaca, A. Marino, A. Miraval Zanon, M. Pilia, L. Stella

papers.title: Identifying deformed exoplanets with JWST and Ariel: A target selection metric for phase curve observations
papers.summary: The shape of an exoplanet encodes fundamental information about its internal structure. For close-in giant planets, strong stellar tidal forces induce measurable deformations that can be probed through high-precision photometry. These deformations are quantified by the fluid Love numbers, which characterise a planet's response to external perturbations and are directly linked to its internal density distribution. In this work, we assess the potential of JWST and the future Ariel mission to constrain the Love numbers of hot Jupiters through full-orbit phase curve observations. To identify the most promising targets for this science case, we introduce a new detection metric, the deformation metric (D), which combines the expected deformation amplitude with the anticipated photometric signal-to-noise ratio. We apply this metric to the Ariel target list and identify WASP-33 b, WASP-76 b, and HAT-P-32 b as the three most favourable targets that currently lack Love number measurements. Using WASP-76 b as a benchmark case, we perform end-to-end retrieval simulations and show that a single continuous JWST phase curve observation can constrain the Love number $h_{2f}$ to a precision of $\sigma_{h_2f} \approx 0.09$, while a single Ariel visit could achieve $\sigma_{h_{2f}} \approx 0.18$. Such precision is likely sufficient for Love number measurements to provide meaningful constraints on planetary interior models and to distinguish between competing interior-structure scenarios, opening a new observational avenue for probing the deep interiors of exoplanets.

authors.name: Vanesa Ram\'irez, Yamila Miguel, Billy Edwards, Babatunde Akinsanmi, Deivy Mercado

papers.title: The accretion flow and jet of M87: broadband modelling across spatial scales
papers.summary: The nearby radio galaxy M87 is an ideal laboratory for studying accretion flows and relativistic jet emission. The EHT collaboration conducted the most comprehensive multi-wavelength observational campaign of M87, in which radio instruments with resolutions ranging from tens of microarcseconds to about an arcsecond sampled different portions of the outflow. We model these data using a radiatively inefficient accretion flow (RIAF) with winds and a new multi-zone jet model, initially magnetically dominated, in which we solve the transport equation for the non-thermal electrons as they are injected, advected, and cooled along the jet. We then compare each radio flux with the jet emission within an effective aperture set by the angular scale of the corresponding observation and obtain the best fit for the jet parameters. The comparison across spatial scales favours a scenario in which the RIAF, rather than the jet, produces the compact $230~{\rm GHz}$ emission, while the jet dominates the lower-frequency radio, optical/UV and X-ray emission. The Jet+RIAF model connects the Bondi-scale gas supply to an accretion rate at the horizon of ${\approx}10^{-5}$ of the Eddington rate, consistent with EHT polarimetry, and the two jets carry in total ${\approx}13$ per cent of the accretion power, $10^{43}~{\rm erg~s}^{-1}$. The framework presented in this work provides a simple way to disentangle the accretion-flow and jet contributions to the emission from nearby radio galaxies.

authors.name: Eduardo M. Guti\'errez, Santiago del Palacio, Tom\'as Tob\'ias Mazzei

papers.title: Rotation in the Lagoon Nebula with K2
papers.summary: A low-mass star's rotation rate drives its magnetic field, and in the case of young stars, also affects accretion and planetary formation. Observations of the rotation rates of young stars help constrain models of star and planet formation. We present rotation rates from K2 observations of stars in the ~1-2 Myr Lagoon Nebula, one of the youngest clusters with space-based rotation rates available. From 414 light curves we obtain reliable rotation periods for 325 stars; 124 of them are disk-bearing and 201 are disk-free. This constitutes a significant increase in the collection of K2 rotation rates available for ~1-5 Myr stars. The overall distribution is broadly consistent with expectations, in that the slowest rotators are mid-K and both lower and higher masses are on average faster rotating. There is weak evidence that disked stars rotate more slowly. There are a few complex periodic variables, but they appear to be surprisingly high mass compared to prior known examples of this kind of object.

authors.name: L. M. Rebull, A. M. Cody, L. Venuti, S. Thanvantri, A. Thanvantri

papers.title: The Milky Way's Early Disk Was Built in Bursts. II. The Multicomponent Age-Metallicity Structure of the High-$\alpha$ Disk
papers.summary: Whether the high-$\alpha$ disk experienced a continuous or episodic star-formation history remains an open question. Here we investigate the age--metallicity distribution of the high-$\alpha$ disk using approximately 145,000 Gaia DR3 subgiants with $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]>-1$, 6.5~kpc $\lesssim R\lesssim9.5$~kpc, and $|Z|\lesssim1.5$~kpc. We adopt a forward-modelling framework that accounts for individual age and metallicity uncertainties and corrects for sample selection effects. The reconstructed distribution reveals two components: a broad, dominant population peaking at $\sim10.6$ Gyr and $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]\simeq-0.38$, and an older, more metal-poor population peaking at $\sim12.4$ Gyr and $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]\simeq-0.79$. These features suggest an episodic history of star formation and chemical enrichment in the high-$\alpha$ disk, qualitatively consistent with cosmological simulations in which recurrent gas accretion drives variations in the star formation rate. The age of the older component is close to the $\sim12.3$~Gyr epoch inferred for the proposed Low-energy--Kraken--Heracles accretion event, suggesting a possible connection between this early interaction and enhanced disk star formation. There is tentative evidence that the dominant population is possibly composed of two sub-components with age distributions peaking at $\sim11.1$ Gyr and $\sim10.0$ Gyr, respectively. Together, these results favour a picture in which the high-$\alpha$ disk was built through recurrent episodes of enhanced star formation rather than a single temporally smooth phase, even for the regime of ${\rm [Fe/H]}>-1$.

authors.name: Tiancheng Sun, Maosheng Xiang, Jifeng Liu, Meng Zhang, Yaqian Wu

papers.title: SpecLess: A Multi Survey Python Package for Machine Learning Classification of Galaxy Morphology and Activity from Photometry
papers.summary: Galaxy morphology and spectroscopic activity are fundamental observational diagnostics of galaxy formation and evolution. However, the extent to which these properties can be recovered from broadband photometry and preserved across different sky surveys remains an important question. In this study, we use photometric data from KiDS+VIKING, the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys and SDSS+AllWISE to systematically investigate the complementary information provided by optical, near-infrared and mid-infrared wavelengths for galaxy classification. Our machine learning models achieve macro F1 scores of 0.9237 and 0.7398 for morphological and activity classification, respectively. We show that the contribution of near-infrared photometry varies across galaxy populations, yielding an improvement of 9.25 percentage points in the classification accuracy of red spiral galaxies. Controlled experiments on 5,235 galaxies common to KiDS+VIKING and DESI demonstrate that mid-infrared photometry provides greater complementary information for discriminating spectroscopic activity classes than additional optical measurements. Furthermore, cross-survey transfer experiments conducted on identical galaxies with fixed reference labels reveal direction-dependent performance losses in the generalizability of photometric classifiers. These findings demonstrate that the limitations of photometric galaxy classification are governed not only by the choice of algorithm but also by the physical properties of galaxy populations, wavelength coverage and catalogue-specific observational differences. As an outcome of this study, we present SpecLess, an open-source Python package providing survey-specific classifiers that require no spectroscopic information at inference.

authors.name: Uzay Aydin, Mehmet Tanriver

papers.title: Gravitational Waves from Magnetically Confined Mountains on Accreting White Dwarfs
papers.summary: We propose fast-spinning, magnetic white dwarfs in binary systems as promising sources of continuous gravitational waves for future space-based detectors. The aim of this work is to determine the maximum ellipticities and gravitational wave amplitudes achievable by magnetically confined mountains accreted on the star's magnetic poles, and to assess their detectability against predicted sensitivity curves. Self-consistent magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium simulations are used to characterize the structure of the accreted mountain. A parametric search is then performed on these simulations to determine the maximum mass values that can be confined by the star's magnetic field. The stellar ellipticity $\varepsilon$ grows nearly linearly with accreted mass $M_{\rm a}$ up to a maximum, and was found to scale as $\varepsilon_{\rm max} \simeq 1.6\times10^{-2}T_5^{-2} B_{*,8}^{2}$, while the maximum gravitational wave amplitude as $h_{\rm 0, max} \simeq 1.2\times10^{-22}T_5^{-2} B_{*,8}^{2}$, where $T_5$ represents the temperature of the mountain in units of $10^5 \mathrm{K}$ and $B_{*,8}$ represents the star's polar magnetic field intensity in units of $10^8 \mathrm{G}$. Across a representative range of source inclinations, distances and spin periods, magnetically confined mountains on white dwarfs can generate continuous gravitational waves detectable by future space-based interferometers. BBO and DECIGO can probe diverse configurations, whereas LISA, TianQin, and Taiji require highly magnetized systems. Applications to known fast-spinning white dwarfs indicate that cooler accreted mountains favor detectability.

authors.name: Pedro Henrique Barboza Rossetto, Manoel Felipe Sousa, Diego Antonio Falceta Gon\c{c}alves

papers.title: DUETS: Red giant asteroseismic binaries. Binary confirmation and prospects for double-seismic model inference
papers.summary: Red giants displaying solar-like oscillations allow precise stellar properties to be derived. Asteroseismic binaries (ABs), which are gravitationally bound systems where both stars show detectable oscillations, can provide constraints on the interior of two coeval stars, allowing us to model them jointly and potentially obtain constraints unavailable from either star individually. This makes ABs potential laboratories for calibrating stellar evolution theory. In this context, AB candidates (ABCs) are systems showing two oscillators, which are as of yet not confirmed as gravitationally bound. We aimed to confirm ABCs and other red giant binary candidates, as well as demonstrate the advantages of AB modeling inference. We obtained spectroscopic indicators of binarity for 60 oscillating red giants that have photometric (33 stars) and/or asteroseismic (38) indications of binarity. We confirm 12 of our 60 targets as spectroscopic binaries, 8 of which are ABs as well. Cross-matching with Gaia DR3 and APOGEE DR17, we identify a further 9 likely binaries, at least 6 of which are also ABCs. We then investigated the impact of simultaneously modeling the oscillation modes of both oscillators of an AB. We inferred stellar properties for; one binary of extra-Galactic origin containing one detectable red-giant-branch (RGB) oscillator; one AB with RGB oscillators; and two ABCs with RGB oscillators. We find that the mode frequencies of the two ABCs and the confirmed AB are well-described with a coeval modeling of the stellar components. We demonstrate that the simultaneous modeling of ABs with two RGB stars can be used to infer the stellar helium content down to $3\%$ precision, compared to $5\%$ when using only the brightest star. Finally, the metal-poor binary KIC2971380 hints for a need to correct the $\nu_{max}$ scaling relation, supporting recent studies of extremely metal-poor oscillators.

authors.name: J. S. Thomsen, W. E. van Rossem, A. Miglio, A. Mazzi, V. D'Orazi, J. Y. Choi, W. H. Ball, M. Tailo, M. Matteuzzi, E. Corsaro, K. Brogaard, M. Marcussen, M. N. Lund, F. Grundahl, E. Knudstrup, D. Slumstrup

papers.title: Are habitable-zone TESS Objects of Interest really there? Period resolution from the full archive
papers.summary: TESS Objects of Interest (TOIs) seen as single or duo transits carry a catalogue period that is undefined or equal to the separation of the two events, and their insolation and any habitable-zone label inherit it. We reanalyse all 187 TOIs catalogued with P = 0 or P >= 200 d using all public TESS data through Sector 107, with a flux-based method that weights each alias by per-epoch transit likelihoods, the transit duration and a geometric prior, and tests for coherence, data edges, contamination by other planets and instrumental artefacts. It recovers 12 published periods blindly and, in injection-recovery tests, 71 per cent of periods constrained by a new transit, with no wrong period. It resolves 28 periods and fixes 8 more by exclusion. Are habitable-zone TOIs really there? Mostly not: of the 28 duo-transits that a catalogue-period criterion places in the conservative habitable zone, about two are expected to lie there, both giant planets, and none of the 12 small (Rp 1 yr. We release alias-marginalised habitable-zone probabilities for the whole sample.

authors.name: Juan F. Pag\'es Navarrete

papers.title: Multilayer magnetic structure toward NGC 1333 revealed by a square-degree optical polarimetric survey
papers.summary: Magnetic-field studies of star-forming regions are complicated by overlapping structures along the line of sight. We investigate the large-scale magnetic field toward NGC~1333 in Perseus, accounting for foreground polarization through stellar distances and optical polarimetry. Our wide-field $R$-band survey covers nearly one square degree and provides polarization measurements for approximately 840 stars, with distances from Gaia DR3 and StarHorse. We used polarization-distance trends and Stokes parameters to identify line-of-sight components and estimate foreground polarization. After subtracting it in Stokes space, we characterized the field using circular statistics and the angular dispersion function (ADF), comparing it with molecular-line and complementary polarimetric observations. The data reveal a polarized foreground at 160-300 pc and a cloud component beyond 300 pc. After correction, the plane-of-sky field rotates smoothly from $126.3\deg\pm0.8\deg$ in the northwest to $162.2\deg\pm0.6\deg$ in the southeast, remaining well ordered in both regions. The ADF gives turbulent-to-ordered field ratios of $0.054^{+0.025}_{-0.022}$ and $0.095^{+0.021}_{-0.047}$, corresponding to plane-of-sky strengths of $59^{+44}_{-23}$ and $46^{+50}_{-13}~\mu\mathrm{G}$. Residual foreground fluctuations may affect these estimates. CO data show multiple velocity components with spatially varying contributions. Corrected optical polarization agrees with the large-scale orientation traced by Planck, while near-infrared and JCMT/POL-2 data reveal localized deviations in denser structures. Our results indicate a coherent cloud-scale magnetic field with a smoothly changing orientation, alongside localized variations in dense structures. They demonstrate the value of combining stellar distances and wide-field optical polarimetry to disentangle foreground contributions.

authors.name: G. A. P. Franco, J. M. Girart, F. O. Alves

papers.title: Angular momentum transport in a newborn protostar--disc system: magnetic braking, spiral arms and the magneto-rotational instability
papers.summary: Angular momentum transport in young protostar--disc systems involves magnetic braking, magneto-rotational turbulence and gravitational instability, mechanisms that are usually studied separately and on different scales. We present a three-dimensional non-ideal magnetohydrodynamic simulation, including Ohmic and ambipolar diffusion, that follows the collapse of a $1~M_\odot$ dense core continuously from the cloud scale to the formation of the protostar, and then the resulting protostar--disc system for $\sim 64~\mathrm{yr}$ at a resolution of $\sim 10^{-4}~\mathrm{AU}$ at the protostellar surface. We decompose the azimuthally averaged angular momentum budget into Reynolds, Maxwell and gravitational torques, each split into a radial and a meridional component, over a quasi-steady phase of the evolution. The collapse produces a thick disc an order of magnitude more massive than the protostar, whose specific angular momentum decreases as it accretes. Accretion through the disc is vertically layered, with accreting and decreting layers at the same radius, a pattern set layer by layer by the torques. The transport separates into three regimes delimited by the coupling of the magnetic field to the gas. Magnetic braking operates in the envelope. Maxwell stresses dominate inside $\sim 0.1~\mathrm{AU}$, where the field recouples and the magneto-rotational instability develops. In the ambipolar dead zone that makes up the bulk of the disc, the Reynolds stress dominates, carried by $m=2$ spiral arms in a marginally unstable disc, with the gravitational stress as a secondary contributor. Meridional transport is as important as radial transport, so that a one-dimensional viscous model fitted to the net mass flux would require a negative $\alpha$ over part of the disc.

authors.name: Antonin Borderies, Beno\^it Commer\c{c}on, Adnan Ali Ahmad

papers.title: Linking Outer Solar System Objects in Archival DECam Imaging: A Multi-year Linker Tested on Held-out Known Objects, and 189 Multi-opposition Candidates Including Five L4 Neptune Trojans, Two Retrograde Objects and Eight with a > 150 au
papers.summary: I link single-night detections in public DECam imaging: 74% of the NOIRLab Source Catalog DR2 (2012-2019) sky with four or more nights, and my extraction from 149,421 exposures (2020-2026). Of 931 secure known objects, single-season linking recovers 22.1-25.0%, a multi-year linker 26.5%, together 36.2%. The multi-year rule, fixed before its held-out tests, recovers 68% of DES objects brighter than r = 23.5 in a strip of its footprint and 14 of 47 known objects outside it. Its shifted-sky controls, complete for 162 of 165 blocks, return no candidate. For its 34 candidates not already known this limits pure chance alignments to under 4% (11% at seven nights), but not links that mix real and chance detections. At six nights real and control counts are indistinguishable. Identification by orbit finds 14 designated objects that a position check missed. The catalogue has 189 undesignated candidates with orbits from two or more oppositions, whose linked detections were re-measured on the images; 41 were then detected on two or more nights that their fits did not use. Listed apart are 63 weaker entries and 19 designated objects, 12 of them Rubin discoveries with 4.9-13.2 yr of earlier arc. Five are candidate L4 Neptune Trojans whose orbits and clones librate for 10 Myr (one reported independently by Jongma 2026, mostly from other data), two are retrograde candidates and eight have a > 150 au. There is no follow-up and no selection function. The Minor Planet Center has astrometry of 37 objects; unreleased positions are available on request, in confidence.

authors.name: Gioele Cerati

papers.title: $uvby-\beta$ photoelectric photometry of FGK-type pulsating star candidates in the Kepler field: observations, stellar parameters and asteroseismic analysis
papers.summary: We present $uvby-\beta$ photoelectric photometry of 218 FGK-type stars brighter than $Kp = 12$ mag in the Kepler field. Interstellar reddening was estimated using the observed photometric indices, distances from Gaia DR3, and the Bayestar19 three-dimensional dust maps. The sample was classified into dwarf and giant stars, and their metallicities and effective temperatures were determined using empirical photometric calibrations. The resulting parameters were compared with those reported in previous photometric and spectroscopic studies. We also analyzed the Kepler long-cadence light curves of the sample and determined the global asteroseismic parameters, including the frequency of maximum oscillation power ($\nu_{\max}$) and the large frequency separation ($\Delta\nu$), for red giants exhibiting solar-like oscillations. Finally, we performed a Bayesian isochrone-fitting analysis using PARSEC stellar evolutionary models, incorporating the photometric metallicities and effective temperatures, the asteroseismic parameters, and absolute visual magnitudes derived from Gaia DR3 data as observational constraints. This analysis provides estimates of the fundamental stellar parameters, including effective temperatures, metallicities, surface gravities, masses, and radii, together with their associated uncertainties.

authors.name: L. Fox-Machado

papers.title: Unsupervised learning reveals a small number of galaxy formation pathways in IllustrisTNG
papers.summary: Understanding the main drivers of galaxy formation and the connection between observable properties and evolutionary pathways is a central goal of extragalactic astronomy. Observations provide single-epoch snapshots of galaxies at different stages of their development, whereas cosmological simulations allow us to trace the full formation histories of individual systems within a theoretical framework. Extracting information from these datasets remains challenging. Our aim is to use machine-learning techniques to unveil physical properties from the simulation datasets. We apply two unsupervised ML techniques, dimensionality reduction and clustering, to identify galaxy evolution key parameters. We use UMAP as our dimensionality reduction tool and k-means as our clustering method. We perform dimensionality reduction on the star formation histories (SFHs) of a sample of aproximately 10000 galaxies drawn from the TNG50 and TNG100 simulations. The resulting representation of the SFHs in a two-dimensional UMAP space reveals a clear ordering of galaxy mass assembly histories, separating quenched and star-forming systems, as well as galaxies with significant ex situ stellar mass contributions. Galaxy properties from simulation catalogs that are not used in the dimensionality reduction show correlations across the UMAP plane. Furthermore, using a k-means clustering analysis, we identify six groups of galaxies with distinct evolutionary histories. These groups show systematic differences in stellar mass, morphology, angular momentum, star formation activity, and merger history, and occupy different regions of the SFR-mass and mass-size planes. Our results indicate that the diversity of galaxy formation histories in IllustrisTNG can be organized into a small number of characteristic evolutionary pathways linking galaxy accretion histories and present-day structural and star-forming properties.

authors.name: C. Alvarez-Fernandez, H. Dominguez Sanchez, J. Vega-Ferrero, E. Angeloudi, A. Ferre-Mateu, D. Sotillo-Ramos

papers.title: Searching for Anisotropic Cosmic Birefringence with SPT-3G
papers.summary: We search for anisotropic cosmic birefringence using two years of data from the SPT-3G instrument on the South Pole Telescope. Anisotropic cosmic birefringence refers to a theorized dependence of the refractive index of the vacuum on the polarization of light that varies across the Universe in a statistically isotropic manner. Such an effect would manifest as a direction-dependent mixing of the $E$ and $B$ polarization modes of the cosmic microwave background (CMB), caused by rotation of the polarization angle as photons travel from the CMB last scattering surface to us. We present a measurement of the power spectrum of the rotation angle $\alpha$ in six bins across the angular multipole range $20 < L < 2048$, finding no evidence for cosmic birefringence with the spectrum consistent with zero. At 95% confidence, we set a new best upper limit on the amplitude of a scale-invariant birefringence power spectrum of $A_{\rm CB}<0.027$. Additionally, we place upper limits on a scale-dependent white noise model. We translate the scale-invariant upper limit to constraints on the axion coupling constant and primordial magnetic field strength, finding 95% confidence limits of $g_{\alpha\gamma} < 1.7\times 10^{-2}/H_I$ and $B_{\rm 1\,Mpc} < 9.6\,{\rm nG}$ respectively. We expect these limits to improve several-fold with the complete SPT-3G survey.

papers.title: Rule-based curation and validation in batch fermentation of a genome-scale metabolic model of the mycoprotein fungus Fusarium venenatum A3/5
papers.summary: Sustainable protein supply is a central food-system challenge, and mycoprotein from Fusarium venenatum is an established, low-impact option. Its production relies on refined glucose, and yields on lower-cost feedstocks are normally found by fermentation. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) can estimate these yields before any experiment, but to our knowledge none has been published for this fungus, and models transferred from related species inherit template errors. Here we built iJL1143, a GEM of strain A3/5, from an Aspergillus niger model and curated it with rules based on homology, thermodynamics and the literature. We compared it with the uncurated Draft model in four oxygen-enriched batch fermentations on glucose and fructose. Thermodynamic directionality rules and the direction of the mitochondrial GTP/GDP carrier brought the maximum ATP yield of the Draft model within the theoretical range. As a result, with sequential sugar uptake and no fitted parameters, the mean final-biomass discrepancy fell from 20% for the Draft model to 6% for iJL1143. Sequential uptake and a fitted lag time also reduced its biomass time-course error from 4.88 to 0.42 g/L. In oxygen-enriched batch fermentation, iJL1143 can therefore estimate obtainable biomass before fermentation, which could reduce the experiments needed to develop lower-cost mycoprotein.

authors.name: Jaewook Lee, Thomas Vinestock, Miao Guo

papers.title: ST-FateFlow: Continuous Gene-Spatial Reconstruction with Differentiation-Potential Learning from Time-Resolved Spatial Transcriptomics
papers.summary: Time-resolved spatial transcriptomics provides a powerful view of dynamic biological processes by measuring cellular states together with their spatial organization across time. However, destructive profiling and experimental cost restrict observations to a few discrete time points collected from independent samples, with no known cell pairing across time. This makes it difficult to reconstruct gene expression and tissue organization at unobserved stages and to characterize differentiation-associated dynamics. Here, we introduce ST-FateFlow, a flow-matching framework for continuous gene-spatial dynamics and differentiation-potential learning. ST-FateFlow jointly learns gene-expression and spatial-coordinate velocity fields, enabling interpolation of missing time points and continuous modeling of transcriptional evolution and tissue remodeling. In parallel, it independently learns a time-conditioned differentiation potential, whose values organize cell states along inferred differentiation progressions and support the analysis of differentiation-associated transcriptional changes. Across multiple time-resolved spatial transcriptomics datasets, ST-FateFlow effectively captures coordinated gene-expression and spatial dynamics. Case studies further show that the learned potential landscapes are consistent with known developmental and regenerative trajectories and help identify candidate genes associated with differentiation progression.

authors.name: Zhe Yu, Xiaobo Sun, Hao Wu

papers.title: Earth-strength magnetic-field axis modulates non-spatial probabilistic decision-making in humans
papers.summary: Magnetoreception has been primarily studied in orientation and navigation, but whether Earth-strength magnetic fields influence non-spatial decisions remains unclear. Evidence for human magnetic responses is limited, and the transduction mechanism is unknown. Using a Go stone selection paradigm in which near-zero geomagnetic field and Larmor-frequency conditions previously showed lower black stone rates, we tested whether non-spatial choice depends on magnetic-field geometry. Fasted men played in pairs under ten static two-seat configurations varied component-wise at near-constant north-seat intensity. The north-seat black stone rate was lower under the two configurations with horizontal fields transverse to the geomagnetic field than under the other eight, which did not differ detectably. The difference emerged promptly, without evidence of outcome-driven learning or configuration-dependent associations with the partner's preceding actions, and process analyses linked it to the joint parity-choice outcome without isolating either step. A Larmor-frequency difference observed over the ambient field was not detected over horizontal-only or vertical-only backgrounds, suggesting a potential magnetoresponsive axis, although the background difference was statistically unresolved. Frequency, light-spectrum, and posture analyses support a radical-pair mechanism as a leading working hypothesis. These findings associate the geomagnetic field axis with human non-spatial choice, providing a paradigm linking magnetic sensing to decision processes.

authors.name: In-Taek Oh, Yong-Hwan Kim, Soo-Chan Kim, Yongkuk Kim, Kwon-Seok Chae

papers.title: Molecular memory reduces timing noise in stochastic gene expression
papers.summary: Fluctuations in gene expression affect the timing precision of downstream events triggered when a gene product reaches a critical threshold. The first-passage time (FPT) to this threshold characterizes the timing of such events. In conventional single-step birth--death models, reaction waiting times are exponentially distributed and hence memoryless. In this setting, FPT noise exhibits a U-shaped dependence on the threshold, attaining its minimum near one-half of the steady-state mean. However, mRNA production and degradation often involve multiple sequential steps, leading to hypoexponential distributions of mRNA production times and mRNA lifetimes. Here, we investigate how molecular memory arising from multistep mRNA production and degradation affects FPT statistics in bursty gene expression. We calculate FPT statistics in the small-noise limit. Both multistep mechanisms reduce FPT noise, but through distinct mechanisms. Multistep burst arrival reduces mRNA copy-number fluctuations, thereby suppressing timing noise. Multistep degradation instead reshapes transient accumulation dynamics, reducing relative timing noise even when steady-state mRNA noise increases. The threshold that minimizes FPT noise remains close to one-half of the steady-state mean, except for multistep burst arrival with constant burst sizes, for which it shifts to lower values. Stochastic simulations support the analytical predictions within their regimes of validity and show that these qualitative conclusions persist beyond the small-noise approximation.

authors.name: Kuheli Biswas, Supravat Dey, Abhyudai Singh

papers.title: Feedback and Resource Competition in Incoherent Feedforward Loops: When Is Cumulative Dose Ordering Preserved?
papers.summary: Biochemical coupling can change the expression levels and timing predicted by an incoherent feedforward loop (IFFL) model without changing cumulative dose ordering. We derive ordering conditions using shared-production identities and Metzler comparison bounds, with tail guarantees beyond finite computation. A nonlinear example exhibits delayed slope reversal at a fixed dose, on an $O(1/\eta)$ timescale as pathway mismatch $\eta$ vanishes. At one fixed joint fit, validated bounds establish decreasing cumulative output across 20-100 ng nominal burden, from zero to full target loading, at every positive finite observation time for a translation-blocking model and an RNA-decay model. Full loading at 20 ng reduces 48-hour cumulative output by 13.35% and 10.18%, respectively, while endpoint concentration in the first model changes by only +0.15%. Preserved ordering therefore does not ensure quantitative agreement.

authors.name: Iva Jankovi\'c, Fabiana Calandra, Giansimone Perrino, Velia Siciliano, Filippo Menolascina

papers.title: Optimising Recruitment and Sample Allocation in Multi-Site Rare Disease Studies
papers.summary: Clinical research in rare diseases is challenged by the limited availability and broad geographical distribution of eligible patients. This necessitates multi-centre collaboration and strategic selection of analytical laboratories based on capacity, cost, and capability. We present a mathematical framework based on cardinality optimisation to support key operational decisions in study design, balancing clinical relevance, feasibility, budgetary constraints, and logistical factors. The framework was implemented in the Reconstruction and Computational Modelling for Inherited Metabolic Diseases (Recon4IMD) project, aiming to recruit 1,900 diagnosed patients across 24 healthcare centres and eight metabolomic laboratories. Compared to both proportional heuristic and greedy marginal allocation baselines, the proposed optimisation model consistently achieved higher recruitment yields in simulated multi-centre scenarios and reduced metabolomic analysis costs by approximately 30% under unconstrained conditions. Notably, both the heuristic and greedy allocation baselines became infeasible under progressively tighter laboratory capacity constraints, whereas the optimised model maintained feasibility and cost control. These findings highlight the value of integrated optimisation strategies for improving recruitment, platform selection, and sample allocation in complex, resource-limited research settings.

authors.name: Farid Zare, Catherine Clancy, Tal Dattner, Martina Messina, Julian Teinert, Jack McGoldrick, Pavel Je\v{s}ina, Sabine Weller Gr{\o}nborg, Ute Spiekerkoetter, James J O'Byrne, Trine Tangeraas, Maria Luz Couce, Jos\'e A. Cocho, Javier de las Heras, Niklas Darin, Dorothea M\"oslinger, Peter Witters, Ina Knerr, Giancarlo La Marca, Ans T. van der Ploeg, Hidde H. Huidekoper, Terry G. J. Derks, Francjan J. van Spronsen, Sandra D. K Kingma, Anibh M. Das, Carlo Dionisi-Vici, Clara D. van Karnebeek, Julia B. Hennermann, Siobh\'an O'Sullivan, Sabine A. Fuchs, Luciana Hannibal, M. Rebecca Heiner-Fokkema, Marek J. Noga, Irene M. L. W. K\"orver-Keularts, Katja Benedikte Prest{\o} Elgst{\o}en, George J. G. Ruijter, J J M Jans, Amy Harms, Thomas Hankemeier, Maurizio Scarpa, Ines Thiele, Shamima Rahman, Stefan K\"olker, Ronan M. T. Fleming

papers.title: Fully Spiking Neural Implementation of Lambda-Calculus Beta-Reduction via Biologically Documented Mechanisms
papers.summary: We present the first complete implementation of $\beta$-reduction in the untyped $\lambda$-calculus using exclusively spiking neural dynamics. Every step of the reduction---redex detection, subterm segmentation, variable-binding detection, De~Bruijn index arithmetic, token copying, and inter-step role maintenance---is performed by leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neurons with explicit membrane dynamics, exponential synaptic currents, axonal delays, and pair-based spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP). Each neural component maps onto a specific, experimentally documented mechanism: Jeffress-type delay-line coincidence for redex detection; a line-attractor balance counter for subterm segmentation; $\theta$--$\gamma$ cross-frequency coupling for De~Bruijn variable binding; a phase-ring traveling wave for depth-index arithmetic; theta-cycle STDP for token copying; and recurrent persistent firing for role maintenance between reduction steps. All synaptic weights are derived analytically from measured EPSP amplitudes; no hand tuning is performed. The closed-loop system achieves 100\,\% agreement with a symbolic oracle across ten validation classes, including Church numeral arithmetic (\textsc{plus}, \textsc{mult}, \textsc{pred}), Boolean logic with divergent branches, Y-combinator steps, terms with up to six bound-variable occurrences, De~Bruijn indices up to~12, noise robustness, and determinism. To our knowledge this is the first Turing-complete symbolic computation performed entirely within spike dynamics using biologically grounded circuit primitives. We discuss implications for neuromorphic proof assistants and the neural basis of symbolic reasoning.

authors.name: Vladimir A. Lazovskiy, Victor B. Kazantsev, Sergey V. Stasenko

papers.title: HoloGene: Learning to Lift Sliced Spatial Transcriptomics to Holistic 3D Gene Fields
papers.summary: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) provides spatially resolved gene expression measurements, but most 3D ST datasets are acquired as independently processed 2D sections. Computational approaches span slice registration and integration, explicit or generative interpolation, and coordinate-field modeling. Within the last family, implicit neural representations (INRs) offer a continuous, coordinate-queryable parameterization, but standard isotropic coordinate encodings do not explicitly reflect that serial-section measurements are dense in-plane and sparse along the axial direction. We present HoloGene, an anisotropic conditional INR framework for estimating continuous 3D gene-expression fields from pre-registered ST sections. Its central contribution is an acquisition-aware factorization that couples dense in-plane synthesis with sparse axial evolution using established GAE, FiLM, pseudo-label supervision, and CORAL components. HoloGene compresses high-dimensional expression profiles into a graph-autoencoder latent manifold, uses pseudo-label-derived signature conditioning to provide coarse intra-section context, and applies depth-dependent FiLM modulation to model axial variation. A signature-stratified correlation-alignment regularizer encourages cross-slice covariance alignment in latent features. Using held-out measured sections as cross-sectional references, HoloGene improves reconstruction accuracy and biological preservation metrics compared with general-purpose INRs and adapted spatial-transcriptomics baselines. These results support anisotropic conditional modeling as a practical strategy for estimating 3D expression fields from discontinuous ST sections. Code is available at https://github.com/Szym29/HoloGene.

authors.name: Yumin Zheng, Qingtian Zhu, Ziyan Zhu, Kailu Song, Yinqiang Zheng, Jun Ding

papers.title: Diversity Preservation Recovers Transcription Factor Motifs Across Challenging Confounder Landscapes
papers.summary: Motif discovery is a process where DNA sequences are searched for the short patterns, called motifs, that transcription factor (TF) proteins bind. However, the motif lengths are often unknown and motif attribution often competes with a near-identical motif of a related protein. In this work, we pair a motif genotype whose length emerges from an evolvable gate with MAP-Elites archives organized by three descriptor pairs, and validate every motif against the full HOCOMOCO database. On five liver ChIP-seq datasets spanning distinct confounder landscapes, a $({\mu} + {\lambda})$ baseline differing only in survivor selection collapses onto a single motif and never ranks the target first across three datasets, while every MAP-Elites archive does so in at least 13 of 30 seeds on every dataset. Against the motif discovery tool MEME, run on the same sequences and validated identically, the archives recover the target signal as reliably on four datasets and more robustly when motif width is constrained. Neither method ranks the target above its closest relatives on HNF4A and JUND over the full width range, but narrow archive motifs rank HNF4A first in up to 43% of seeds, where MEME misses the motif in all settings. Diversity preservation improves our ability to recover consistent motif signal, although motif annotation remains a challenging problem for all methods we tested.

authors.name: Alejandro Medina, Mary Lauren Benton

papers.title: Overlooked weak structural connections support human cognition under nonlinear connectome scaling
papers.summary: Human cognition depends on large scale communication constrained by white matter architecture. Although weak connections are abundant in mammalian connectomes, they have long been treated as noise and downweighted because of tractography uncertainty in the human brain, and their relevance to human cognition and large scale functional organization remains unresolved. Across multiple datasets and tractography pipelines, we show that, when tractography derived connection weights are interpreted through a nonlinear weighting framework, weak connections make measurable contributions to cognitive predictions, functional connectivity simulation, and structure function coupling. These effects are selective, nonlinear weighting improves the prediction of general cognitive ability and memory more than that of crystallized intelligence or processing speed, consistent with the notion that weak connections preferentially expand the modal repertoire of brain structural networks to enhance both large scale integration and fine grained segregation, thereby supporting the functional balance essential for diverse cognitive abilities. Importantly, these effects are replicated in a reliability aware connectome generated by integrating two post tractography filtering methods, in which preserving weak links consistently outperforms conventional thresholding strategy in structure function coupling and model based simulation. Finally, we show that weak connections contain functional information organized along system level and gene expression gradients. In particular, weak connections with negative gene coexpression predominantly link visual, motor with limbic regions and exert a disproportionately large influence on brain function than those with positive gene coexpression.

authors.name: Rong Wang, Zhao Chang, Xuechun Liu, Daniel Kristanto, \'Etienne G\'erard Guy Gartner, Xinyang Liu, Mianxin Liu, Ying Wu, Ming Lui, Changsong Zhou

papers.title: Emergent frequency-dependent selection predicts mutation outcomes in complex ecological communities
papers.summary: Ecological interactions can dramatically alter evolutionary outcomes in complex communities. Yet, most population genetics models neglect how interactions within complex communities shape evolutionary dynamics. Here, we bridge this gap by using dynamical mean-field theory to integrate community ecology into classical population genetics models. We show that near an ecological steady state, interactions generate emergent negative frequency-dependent selection between parents and phenotypically similar mutants. Strikingly, even in species-rich communities, this frequency-dependent selection can be characterized by a single parameter measuring the strength of ecological feedback. We find that these interactions strongly suppress the fixation of moderately beneficial mutations. This suppression arises because frequency-dependent selection promotes prolonged coexistence between parent and mutant lineages, creating a barrier to fixation. These effects strengthen with larger effective population sizes and more open niches in the community. Applying our theory to human gut microbiome data, we estimate the average strength of ecological feedback and find it consistent with the negative frequency dependence our theory predicts. Our study establishes a framework for integrating ecological feedback from complex communities into population genetics.

authors.name: Shing Yan Li, Zhijie Feng, Akshit Goyal, Pankaj Mehta

papers.title: Quantum-Like Models of Cognition and Decision Making: Open-Systems and Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad Dynamics
papers.summary: This paper starts with surveying the evolution of quantum-like models of cognition and decision making, transitioning from static kinematic representations to a robust dynamical framework based on open quantum systems. We provide a comprehensive analysis of the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation's application in cognitive psychology and decision making, illustrating how it models mental state evolution as a dissipative process influenced by an informational environment. We categorize dynamical regimes into Passive and Active Hamiltonians, demonstrating how non-commutation with projections on decision basis serves as a mathematical signature of cognitive agency and Quantum Escape from classical equilibria. The utility of this framework is further explored through its ability to stabilize non-Nash outcomes in strategic games, such as the Prisoner's Dilemma. Building upon this dynamical foundation, we identify ``cognitive beats'' as a signature of the internal struggle between competing ``flows of mind'' deliberated at approximately equal frequencies. Distinct from the damped oscillations of simple interference, these beats emerge from a structural tension between Liouvillian channels that generates a secondary, slow-scale modulation of conviction. This beat envelope dictates the timing of peak readiness and hesitation, providing a mathematical map of the transition between conflicting cognitive states. By resolving these nested time scales, we provide a new spectral diagnostic for the depth of cognitive agency and the complexity of the underlying deliberation process. This paper develops a theoretical framework linking GKSL dynamics with quantum-like cognition and decision-making (QCDM), highlighting how dissipative quantum models can capture features of human thought and decision processes.

authors.name: Masanari Asano, Irina Basieva, Andrei Khrennikov

papers.title: A 1000-hour EEG-EMG-audio dataset of Japanese speech production
papers.summary: We present a multimodal dataset of 1020 hours of simultaneously recorded scalp electroencephalography (EEG), facial electromyography (EMG), and speech audio from three healthy native Japanese speakers during open-vocabulary overt speech, covert repetition and speech listening. Recordings were acquired in many sessions over several months with three EEG systems of 61-128 channels, an ultra-high-density system (g.Pangolin) and two cap-type systems (g.SCARABEO and eego sports). Each session provides time-synchronized EEG, facial EMG, and audio, together with speech-event annotations and transcriptions. Although collected with speech decoding as a primary motivation, the dataset also supports work on multimodal signal processing, artifact modeling, longitudinal and cross-device adaptation, and EEG representation learning. Technical validation used power spectral density and event-related potential analyses to characterise spectral profiles and time-locked responses across participants, devices, and tasks. The dataset is available in Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) format from Harvard Dataverse under controlled access for research use. Its speech audio is voice-masked.

authors.name: Motoshige Sato, Ilya Horiguchi, Masakazu Inoue, Kenichi Tomeoka, Eri Hatakeyama, Yuya Kita, Atsushi Yamamoto, Ippei Fujisawa, Shuntaro Sasai

papers.title: Fly Whiskers Meet LiDAR: Robust Navigation under Sensor Failure
papers.summary: We extend FLYNN, a leaky integrator recurrent network wired on the Drosophila melanogaster connectome, with a 32-ray 2D LiDAR interface that requires no learned fusion layer beyond a scalar input gain. A 270 degree frontal scan at 8 m range is injected as inverted proximity into the 37 BM Vib head-bristle neurons. Across 24 paired comparisons in a four-state vision matrix with LiDAR on or off, FLYNN-LiDAR has 17 significant wins, 5 nonsignificant comparisons, and 2 significant losses against three LiDAR-capable baselines. Both losses are to MobileNet with the left eye off. With full vision, FLYNN-LiDAR reaches 96.6% success. Under total vision loss, the scan raises success from 45.2% to 64.6%; the baselines reach 44.6% to 56.6% with the scan on. Under out of distribution textures, it is the only LiDAR-capable model whose success improves with the scan (44.2% to 58.4%); both CNNs score 0%, and SmallWorld declines from 26.8% to 7.4%. Under periodic vision dropout, FLYNN-LiDAR achieves 93.6% and 89.6% success at 25% and 50% duty with fewer collisions. Profiling the evaluated forward paths gives 3.93M multiply accumulate operations per step; EfficientNet and MobileNet require 4.60x and 2.94x as many. Final-state analysis shows near-linear sensory superposition (cosine 0.9955).

authors.name: Ali Mahzarnia, Homayoun Jamshidi

papers.title: Analysis choices can produce apparent rich-club differences: an Alzheimer's disease EEG case study
papers.summary: Background: The weighted rich-club coefficient tests whether a network's most strongly connected nodes are preferentially interconnected. Its interpretation depends on two often-implicit choices: how the randomised comparison networks are constructed, and whether the hubs are re-identified in each comparison network or held fixed at those of the observed network. When hubs are defined by connection strength, these choices change what the coefficient tests. New method: We examined how these choices affect inference using resting-state EEG from 20 people with Alzheimer's disease and 20 controls. Holding the data fixed, we compared four analysis pipelines, crossing two ways of building the comparison networks (global weight reshuffle or strength-conditioned null) with the two hub choices, and ran a calibration study using data constructed to contain no preferential hub coupling beyond nodal strength. Results: An apparent eyes-open group difference in rich-club organisation appeared only under the pipeline combining a global weight reshuffle with re-identified hubs. Under the empirical resampling ensemble, that pipeline reported a group difference in 43% of pseudo-studies, always higher in the Alzheimer's disease group, while the other three stayed near the expected 5%. Comparison with existing methods: Unlike global weight reshuffling, strength-conditioned nulls approximately preserve nodal strengths; fixing observed hubs also retains the identity of the core being tested. Conclusions: The same data can support or dissolve an apparent rich-club difference depending on these choices. No single choice is universally correct, but reporting which were made, and why they fit the question being asked, is essential to interpreting the result.

authors.name: Kai-Wayne Liu, Ryan Tian En Pang, Pholpat Durongbhan

papers.title: Remark on internal relaxation in large number qubit systems
papers.summary: For a time $t_{c}$ of calculation in an $N$ qubit quantum computer that is much shorter than the intrinsic Heisenberg time $t_H$, $t_c\ll t_H$, the dynamics of the system is effectively irreversible and the couplings between the qubits give rise to a relaxation time scale $\tau_r$. If $t_H\gg t_c >\sim \tau_r$ one looses quantum coherence exponentially fast. Since $t_H$ scales exponentially with $N$ there is a threshold $N_c$ such that for $N\gg N_c$ one must be aware of possible intrinsic relaxation during calculation. As an order of magnitude estimation we find $N_c\approx \ln(\tau_r/T)$ where $T$ is a typical system specific oscillation time of a single qubit. $\tau_r$ can be estimated as the typical inverse transition rate between two parts of the system, one of which is treated as an environment of the other.

authors.name: Martin Jan{\ss}en

papers.title: CSS circuits are ICM circuits without magic states
papers.summary: Gidney and Jones recently introduced ``CSS circuits'', generated by $X$, $Z$, $\MX$, $\MZ$ and CNOT, and showed that they can be sampled with $O(1)$ work per gate. They suspected that the class had been seen before. We point out that it is, up to a normal form, the initialisation--CNOT--measurement (ICM) form introduced in 2015 for compiling fault-tolerant circuits, restricted to $\ket{0}$ and $\ket{+}$ initialisations. The ICM construction answers constructively their question about ``non-CSS-ness as a resource'': every Clifford$+T$ circuit compiles to a CSS circuit acting on $\ket{Y}$ and $\ket{A}$ input states.

authors.name: Alexandru Paler

papers.title: QEDist: Practical Exact Distance Certification for Stabilizer Codes
papers.summary: We present QEDist, a method and software package that certifies the distance of qubit stabilizer codes. Building on tree-search methods, QEDist constructs candidate logical operators one qubit at a time, using sparse parity checks, stabilizer equivalence, and verified symmetries to reduce the work. For a cutoff $W$, a completed search either finds a nontrivial logical operator of weight at most $W$ or proves that none exists. Because satisfying one check can violate another, we use both satisfied and unsatisfied checks to lower-bound the weight needed to complete a logical operator, and prune branches whose bound exceeds the remaining budget, which substantially reduces net search time. We benchmark QEDist mainly on Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes; the same formulation extends to non-CSS codes and to the fault distance of syndrome-extraction circuits. For lifted-product (LP) codes, we further exploit the product structure to replace part of the full-code search with a smaller search on a classical constituent. We establish exact distances for codes with up to several thousand qubits, including Abelian and non-Abelian LP codes whose distances were previously reported only as upper bounds. In several seconds of search on one laptop core, QEDist certifies exact distances up to 20 for many of these codes and fault distance 10 for the syndrome-extraction circuit of the $[[144,12,12]]$ code. With orders-of-magnitude speedups over the tested exact solvers, QEDist makes exact distance certification a practical tool for selecting and optimizing finite-length quantum codes.

authors.name: Jong Yeon Lee

papers.title: Restoring quantum neural network trainability through reusable calibration
papers.summary: Quantum neural networks (QNNs) rely on measured quantum observables to guide optimization, but hardware noise can suppress the parameter-dependent signals essential for learning. Here, we develop a structure-preserving error-mitigation framework that improves QNN trainability through reusable calibration of the quantum circuit's effective noise response. By calibrating a reference circuit with the same gate architecture as the trainable circuit, we construct regularized estimators of local quantum features that remain fixed throughout training. We quantify how calibration errors and response mismatches affect the recovery of both observables and their derivatives. Numerical simulations demonstrate enhanced loss-landscape contrast, faster convergence, and improved classification performance, and an IBM Quantum experiment confirms improved closed-loop variational optimization under hardware noise. We further demonstrate calibration reuse in a modular QNN comprising 25 independent four-qubit channels, corresponding to 100 qubits in aggregate. Our results establish reusable feature calibration as a practical approach to improving noise-limited quantum machine learning without repeated calibration at every training step.

authors.name: Ruizhe Shen, Xianquan Yan, Kenji Kawaguchi, Ching Hua Lee

papers.title: Robust Passive Quantum Memory in Three Dimensions, Part I: Thermal and Zero-Temperature Perturbative Stability
papers.summary: Whether a three-dimensional quantum many-body system with geometrically local, bounded-degree interactions can passively protect encoded quantum information has remained a central open question since Kitaev introduced topological quantum computation. Passive protection requires stability against both thermal noise at nonzero temperature and generic static Hamiltonian perturbations Balasubramanian, Davydova, and Lin (BDL) recently established unperturbed three-dimensional thermal self-correction using a recursively defined family of stabilizer Hamiltonians. However, they left open whether their construction remains stable against quantum perturbations, even at zero temperature. In this paper, we show that a slight variant of the BDL code family achieves stability along both boundary axes of the perturbation-temperature phase diagram as the system size grows. Following BDL, in the absence of perturbation it is thermally stable below a critical temperature, achieving a stretched-exponentially long memory lifetime when coupled to any local Markovian thermal bath generated by single-site system-bath interactions satisfying detailed balance with bounded coupling rates. At zero temperature under arbitrary weak, superpolynomially decaying quantum perturbations, the family maintains a uniform bulk spectral gap, superpolynomially small ground-space splitting, and a superpolynomially long closed-system unitary memory lifetime for quasi-locally dressed logical observables. To prove this zero-temperature stability, we establish local topological quantum order across the multiscale hierarchy using a linearly dilated relaxation of the usual Bravyi-Hastings-Michalakis criteria. In the companion paper, we combine the tools developed here with finite-temperature worldline cluster expansions to establish passive self-correction throughout the phase diagram's positive-temperature perturbed interior.

authors.name: Patrick Hayden

papers.title: Loss-Tolerant Quantum Correlations Between Atomic and Photonic Qubits
papers.summary: Quantum physics forbids cloning of a qubit. Therefore, a qubit is irreversibly lost upon loss of the information carrier. To mitigate this physical loss, it has been proposed to distribute the logical information across an entangled set of physical qubits, some of which can be lost. Previous experiments illustrated this concept, but failed to demonstrate a gain in the information-retrieval efficiency. Here we address this challenge with photons for which the total loss, from generation to detection, is below the loss-tolerance threshold of $50\%$. Using two single-atom emitters in an optical cavity, we encode information into the photons of a graph state and observe an efficiency gain for retrieving quantum correlations between the atoms and the photons for single-qubit measurements in the Pauli $X$ and $Z$ bases. Although technical errors reduce the probability to obtain the \textit{correct} result, we achieve average fidelities as high as $\gtrsim\!70\%$ without and $\gtrsim\!75\%$ with error detection, demonstrating entanglement between the atomic and encoded photonic qubits. Lowering the encoding errors is a next natural step toward loss-tolerant photonic quantum-information processing.

authors.name: Leonardo Ruscio, Love A. Pettersson, Philip Thomas, Stefano Paesani, Olivier Morin, Anders S. S{\o}rensen, Gerhard Rempe

papers.title: Distrustful entanglement-based Quantum Key Distribution
papers.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is the one of the most explored application of quantum information theory. While practical QKD systems are being deployed around the world, a major issue of these setups are that one has to trust the measurement devices of both parties. On the other hand, the most secure among such schemes are called device-independent (DI) QKD protocols, where no component of the setup is assumed to be trusted. However, due to their high technological demand, their loophole-free version currently remain out of practical reach. Inspired by the real world, we consider the traditional QKD in a distrustful measurement setting, that is, the measurement devices can only be trusted upto some level of confidence, which might still be large but not completely trusted. We then derive a general lower bound on the asymptotic key rate in this scenario. Then considering perfect detectors and source, and the entanglement-based BB84 (BBM) protocol, we show that to obtain secure keys one needs to trust their devices more than 82 %. However, we observe that such a protocol can not be realised with any level of distrust using the realistic detectors and sources at the current technology. Finally, we also consider the BBM protocol with arbitrary dimensional systems and observe that they are more robust to distrust than qubit systems. Consequently, with the same level of distrust, along with same detector and source efficiences, one can get better key rates with high-dimensional systems.

authors.name: Shubhayan Sarkar

papers.title: AI Scientist Discovered Robust Quantum Control
papers.summary: Protecting quantum coherence is a central theme of modern quantum technologies. Carefully designed control pulses can extend coherence by suppressing disorder and unwanted interactions. However, designing robust pulse sequences remains challenging in interacting multi-level systems, where multiple independent error channels must be controlled in the presence of experimental imperfections. Here we introduce QORA, a multi-agent artificial intelligence framework that integrates theoretical reasoning, automated experimental calibration and control for closed-loop discovery of quantum control sequences. Applied to a dense ensemble of spin-1 nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond, QORA discovers AID-ROD, a series of AI-discovered sequences that nearly double the measured spin coherence time relative to the state-of-the-art human-designed sequence DROID-C3PO. Subsequence analysis by human researchers reveals a hierarchy of error suppression: 18-pulse blocks suppress linear and quadratic onsite disorder and common-mode drive-amplitude errors, while their arrangement over a longer cycle reduces dipolar interactions, providing a physical explanation for the observed improvement and robustness in AID-ROD. These results demonstrate AI-guided experimental discovery of robust quantum control and identify a design strategy for protecting coherence in interacting multi-level systems beyond qubits.

authors.name: Jiahao Yan, Xuanying Lai, Xiaoshui Lin, Yizhou Wang, Changyu Yao, Guanghui He, Thomas Lewer, Chong Zu, Chuanwei Zhang

papers.title: Transient State Preservation of a Dissipative Qubit via Lyapunov Control
papers.summary: Preserving quantum states in the presence of environmental decoherence remains a fundamental challenge for quantum information processing. This work investigates whether Hamiltonian Lyapunov feedback can transiently preserve the state of an open qubit by reshaping its trajectory under Markovian dissipation. A state-error Lyapunov function is adopted to derive an analytical feedback law for Lindblad dynamics, ensuring a nonincreasing Lyapunov function whenever the control sensitivities are nonzero. The analysis identifies the geometric conditions under which the feedback becomes ineffective, showing that control authority vanishes when the current and target Bloch vectors are collinear. Numerical simulations are performed for amplitude damping and pure dephasing using selected target states. Performance is evaluated through fidelity, accumulated infidelity, dwell time above a fidelity threshold, coherence, and control effort. The results demonstrate that the proposed feedback cannot eliminate irreversible dissipation or achieve universal asymptotic stabilization, but it can provide transient benefits for selected target-channel combinations. In particular, under amplitude damping, the controller significantly reduces accumulated infidelity and substantially extends the interval during which the system remains above a prescribed fidelity threshold. In the pure dephasing cases examined, improvements in fidelity are generally limited, although transient coherence preservation is observed for the oblique target considered, revealing a trade-off between coherence and state fidelity. These findings indicate that Lyapunov-based Hamiltonian feedback is best suited as a transient preservation mechanism and motivate its application to gate operations and preservation of prepared states during finite time intervals before their use or readout.

authors.name: Ilan Sabaj, Pablo Monz\'on

papers.title: Microwave-optical quantum transduction with quantum-well exciton polaritons
papers.summary: Linking superconducting quantum processors over optical fiber requires microwave-optical quantum transducers that are efficient, high-bandwidth, and low-noise. This combination has been out of reach because of the weak nonlinearities of conventional electro-optic (EO) materials. We propose a transducer with an engineered, strong EO nonlinearity using the quantum-confined Stark effect (QCSE) of quantum-well excitons. The QCSE transducer leverages the strong light-matter interactions and extreme polarizability of quantum well excitons. Strong coupling to an optical cavity forms exciton-polaritons whose vacuum EO coupling is up to five orders of magnitude larger than in a typical thin-film lithium niobate device. We describe a GaAs/AlGaAs stepped-quantum-well transducer design with predicted transduction efficiencies above 60% and fewer than 0.01 added noise quanta over a $\sim$60 MHz bandwidth, using pump powers below 10 $\mu$W and loaded optical and microwave quality factors of only $3\times10^4$ and $10^3$. We further show that the cavity protection of the polariton provides robustness against inhomogeneous broadening of the quantum well excitons.

authors.name: Nicholas S. Yama, Mohammad Khalifa, Yuxuan Wei, Adbhut Gupta, Loren N. Pfeiffer, Feng Wang, Alp Sipahigil

papers.title: Charge self-consistent DFT+QDMFT framework with a Krylov-based quantum impurity solver
papers.summary: We integrate a quantum impurity solver into a charge self-consistent density functional theory (DFT) plus quantum dynamical mean-field theory framework. The solver optimizes adaptive circuits to approximate the ground state of the impurity model and its particle and hole excitations, and reconstructs the impurity Green's function from their Hamiltonian moments. Higher-order moments are predicted from low-order ones using a machine-learning model, while regularized optimization mitigates violations of causality in the resulting self-energy. The latter is used to update the charge density until self-consistency is achieved. We demonstrate the framework through body-centered cubic lithium calculations and compare the results with a reference one using a continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo solver. These calculations converge with root-mean-square charge-density residuals below $\boldsymbol{2\times10^{-3}}$ and yield a nearly vanishing impurity self-energy, consistent with the noninteracting limit used for weakly correlated lithium.

authors.name: M. Karabin, T. Sohail, E. A. Coello P\'erez, S. Ghosh, M. Sajjan, H. Terletska, M. Eisenbach

papers.title: Quantum Fisher information matrices for time-evolved bosonic Gaussian thermal states
papers.summary: Quantum Fisher information (QFI) is a fundamental quantum metrological quantity arising from the second order term in a Taylor expansion of a smooth divergence evaluated at nearby quantum states. The $\alpha$-$z$ information matrix is a QFI measure arising from the $\alpha$-$z$ R\'enyi relative entropy, and QFI measures corresponding to various underlying smooth divergences may be recovered from the $\alpha$-$z$ information matrix, including the standard symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) QFI. Bosonic Gaussian states are common probe states for quantum metrological tasks and admit a complete characterization in terms of their first and second moments. In this work, we consider the quantum metrological task of estimating parameters that characterize a Gaussian unitary time evolution of a faithful bosonic Gaussian thermal state. We establish a formula for the $\alpha$-$z$ information matrix of faithful bosonic Gaussian thermal states that have undergone a Gaussian unitary time evolution. As an example, we calculate entries of the $\alpha$-$z$ information matrix for a two-mode Gaussian thermal state that has undergone a beam splitting operation. For a parametrized family of time-evolved bosonic Gaussian states, we also derive a formula for the SLD operator, which is known to provide a measurement scheme that saturates the quantum Cr\'amer-Rao bound and thus achieves the ultimate precision for single parameter estimation.

authors.name: Hailey S. Murray, Diego Estrada, Mark M. Wilde

papers.title: A Geometric Framework for Local-to-Global Symmetry: Global Constraints on Local Dynamics
papers.summary: Aggregate molecular systems are routinely understood by decomposing them into local structural units, such as monomers in J/H-aggregates, chemical moieties, motifs, and functional groups. Implicit in such decompositions is the assumption that these local structures remain meaningful within the aggregate. Here, we ask how the symmetries of constituent structures relate to aggregate symmetry, and how this relation determines the constraints that global symmetry imposes on transitions between local symmetry sectors. We construct a covariant local-to-global representation from framed local symmetry data and show that its reconstruction map intertwines with a global quantum representation. By identifying which global symmetry sectors overlap each local symmetry sector, we resolve symmetry-enforced dynamical exclusions into site-resolved pathways. Through Frobenius reciprocity, these exclusions can be determined from standard character tables of the local and global symmetry groups, with the character values in the inner product paired according to the relative positions and orientations of local structures within the aggregate. Although motivated by molecular aggregates, the construction is formulated for arbitrary geometries modeled by a homogeneous space of an ambient transformation group.

authors.name: Connor Terry Weatherly, Roel Tempelaar

papers.title: Probing the real-time decoding accuracy bounds in trapped ion architectures
papers.summary: Fault tolerant quantum computers will rely on real-time decoders that process syndromes faster than the QEC cycle duration. The millisecond cycle times offered by trapped ion platforms relax low-latency decoding demands, but simulations and experiments have not yet exploited this time budget to reach maximum logical error suppression. We show how a hybrid sliding window decoding scheme composed of a lower-accuracy and a higher-accuracy decoder can yield substantially improved logical error rates, while preserving low latency. All windows are handled by the lower-accuracy decoder, with some windows being infrequently switched to the higher-accuracy decoder. We extract soft-output information from the lower-accuracy decoder efficiently for any QLDPC code, which allows us to identify decoding windows of low confidence. We simulate memory experiments of bivariate bicycle (BB) codes, using trapped-ion informed noise models. Depending on the physical error rate and BB code, we find up to 3-4 orders of magnitude logical error rate reduction compared to the $\texttt{BP-LSD}$ decoder, and up to 2-3 orders of magnitude lower logical error rate compared to the $\texttt{Beamsearch}$ decoder. By leveraging available classical processing time, our decoding protocol significantly boosts decoding accuracy, ultimately reducing the demands on increasing code size.

authors.name: Arianna Meinking, Evangelia Takou, Kenneth R. Brown

papers.title: Simplifying models of noisy stabilizer QEC on leakage qubits by Pauli twirling
papers.summary: The growing capabilities of quantum error-correction (QEC) experiments make it increasingly important to develop methods that predict or assess logical performance over many QEC cycles. Prior work has shown that a stabilizer QEC cycle subject to Pauli-stochastic noise can be modeled by a classical Markov process over syndrome states, with a logical Pauli channel attached to each syndrome transition. Here, we extend this framework to systems in which physical qubits are subject to leakage. We first develop the theory of leakage-dephased Pauli twirling and show that twirled processes can be expressed in terms of Pauli maps on the computational subspace, conditioned on transitions between leakage patterns. We apply this theory to noisy stabilizer QEC with leakage, demonstrating that a QEC cycle with leakage can be modeled by a classical Markov process over the joint syndrome and leakage patterns, with a logical Pauli channel attached to each joint transition.
