As a key result enabling this analysis, we derive decompositions of the entanglement entropy and logarithmic negativity that separate the ground-state value, including topological terms, from a contribution given by the driven quasiparticles. For a drive inducing non-interacting $f$ dynamics, these decompositions allow us to leverage numerical methods for free fermions and to link the emergence of the proposed long-time ordered state to the equilibration of $f$ anyons to a periodic Gibbs ensemble. For drives inducing Floquet eigenstate thermalization of $f$, our results suggest a scenario where Floquet heating of the $f$ sector stabilizes a genuine non-equilibrium topological phase, in contrast with the usual view of heating as an obstacle to order in periodically driven systems.

authors.name: Francesco Petiziol

papers.title: Teleportation of Logical Qubits using Lattice Surgery with Superconducting Circuits
papers.summary: Demonstrating a quantum advantage when solving large-scale computational problems on a quantum computer requires the correction of errors that occur due to limitations in control accuracy and coherence. Using the concept of quantum error correction, fault-tolerant logical qubits can be realized and manipulated with logical single- and two-qubit gates. In this paper, we experimentally analyze fault-tolerant lattice-surgery, which is a key primitive that enables operations between logical qubits realized in the surface-code. Using this primitive, we demonstrate the teleportation of logical states between two distance-three logical qubits realized in a superconducting circuit composed of 41 physical qubits. Throughout this process, we study the step-by-step transfer of logical information from a source to a target logical qubit by characterizing the time evolution of logical observables. We find that repeated execution of stabilizer measurements, after merging two surface-code patches, restores fault tolerance and yields increased fidelity of the teleported state. When optimizing the protocol in terms of gate count and sequence duration, we observe further improvements in fidelity. Our work offers new insights into the optimization of fault-tolerant lattice-surgery operations, while also providing a comprehensive description of the physical device and gate sequences used. We expect the efficient implementation of increasingly complex logical circuits to enhance the performance of future fault-tolerant quantum computers.

authors.name: Luca Hofele, Yongxin Song, \'Aron M\'arton, Ian Hesner, Ilya Besedin, Jakob Ekert, Jonathan Trebst, Fran\c{c}ois Swiadek, Felix Henrich, Dante Colao Zan\'uz, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Lukas B\"odeker, Nicholas Gialouris, Chrysander D. Hagen, Marek Pechal, Jean Claude Besse, Markus M\"uller, Christoph Hellings, Andreas Wallraff

papers.title: Integral Tensor Isomorphism via Cubic Rings and Lattice Methods
papers.summary: We prove that isomorphism of integral $2\times3\times3$ tensors under $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ is decidable in bounded-error quantum polynomial time. For a tensor $T=(A,B)$ with nonzero determinant form $\det(xA-yB)$, we use the parametrization of Wood by balanced modules to reduce the isomorphism problem to principality tests for compatible lattices, and use the algorithms of Bley, Hofmann, and Johnston to solve this in BQP. When the determinant form vanishes identically, we get either an integral $2\times2\times2$ core, or a polynomial kernel vector of degree one or two. The linear-kernel case yields another compatible lattice problem, while the quadratic-kernel case reduces to a fixed system of polynomial congruences and unimodular lifting. A quantifier-elimination argument decides these congruences in deterministic polynomial time given the prime factorization of the modulus, which quantum integer factorization supplies. Finally, we show that zero padding preserves integral $2\times2\times2$ tensor isomorphism, yielding a polynomial-time reduction from real-quadratic principality to the identically singular $2\times3\times3$ problem.

authors.name: Thomas Huffstutler

papers.title: Nonlinearity-preserving quantum simulation of flows in the early fault-tolerant regime
papers.summary: Ensemble prediction of nonlinear dynamics propagates a probability density whose linear transport equation retains the nonlinear drift, but grid-dependent circuit costs leave end-to-end feasibility in early fault-tolerant quantum computing unresolved. We couple polynomial reduced-order models fitted by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics to Walsh-synthesized Koopman-von Neumann (KvN) transport and surface-code resource estimation. At fixed model dimension and drift degree, per-step transport rotation counts scale polylogarithmically with cells per reduced coordinate. Balancing model accuracy against circuit costs makes reduced-model polynomial degree a design variable for early fault-tolerant quantum simulation. For a cylinder wake approaching saturation, preparation, propagation and sampling to 1% relative root-mean-square field error against the radial model are estimated to take 1.62 h on about 560,000 physical qubits. Estimated three-coordinate wake runtimes span hours to weeks below one million qubits. IBM hardware experiments demonstrate nonlinear radial KvN transport for this wake, using reference circuits to mitigate noise.

authors.name: Hansol Noh (David), Unam Oh (David), Sangkyu Baek (David), Doyeol (David), Ahn

papers.title: Local interference algorithms for observables in large random circuits
papers.summary: In quantum dynamics, it is generally believed that interference effects lead to a sign problem for classical Monte Carlo sampling methods, rendering sampling ineffective. In this paper we show that this is generically not the case for the task of simulating the evolution of observables in random instances of circuit dynamics. Specifically, we consider two examples of observables which give large signals despite the randomness of the dynamics: first order out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) in unstructured random circuits without conservation laws and time-ordered charge-charge correlators (TOCs) in particle number-preserving random circuits. We show that these observables can be approximated by classical stochastic processes and that these approximations can be systematically improved with a series expansion that incorporates coherent corrections associated with clusters of gates. We design and implement algorithms that combine Monte Carlo sampling and tensor network methods to approximate the series. We observe numerically that the computational complexity of approximating TOCs and OTOCs scales polynomially in the circuit size and in the target precision. We study the accuracy of these algorithms by directly mapping their ensemble-averaged errors to partition functions of replica statistical models, allowing for perturbative analysis and numerics in $1$d brickwork geometries. Our theoretical analysis explains the empirical observation of polynomial complexity of these algorithms and is consistent with polynomial complexity extending to arbitrarily small precision and to the thermodynamic limit.

authors.name: Philippe Suchsland, Brayden Ware, Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Vadim Smelyanskiy, Kostyantyn Kechedzhi

papers.title: Modeling quantum information scrambling in realistic protein NMR experiments
papers.summary: Out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) are important probes of operator spreading and information scrambling, and have recently been proposed as a means of extracting molecular structural information through nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). Realizing this potential requires accurate modeling of OTOCs in complex molecular environments within experimentally relevant settings. Here, we develop an end-to-end computational pipeline connecting molecular structures to OTOC dynamics in protein systems. Our framework incorporates molecular motion through molecular dynamics simulations, orientational averaging appropriate for powder samples, and spin-network truncation, using an experimentally realizable double-quantum effective Hamiltonian. We apply this framework to a dataset of over 350 carbon-carbon spin pairs across 10 protein systems, spanning interspin distances of 5-17 A. We find that OTOC arrival times scale approximately linearly with interspin distance, revealing system-dependent operator-spreading velocities that enable correlations to propagate over extended distances within milliseconds. Our sensitivity analysis further shows that individual OTOCs predominantly constrain a single structural parameter, primarily associated with interspin distance. Together, these findings highlight the potential of OTOCs to probe spatially extended spin correlations on timescales compatible with solid-state NMR experiments.

authors.name: Alec F. White, Joseph Haslehurst, Daniel R. Moberg, Justin Provazza, Nicholas C. Rubin, Thomas E. O'Brien, Christian Bengs

papers.title: Expressivity of two-dimensional Gaussian fermion tensor network states
papers.summary: Tensor network states (TNS) provide a family of efficiently compressed approximations to physically relevant many-body quantum states. An important quantity that characterizes the computational resources required by a TNS is its bond dimension. While in one dimension an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy guarantees an exact matrix product state representation with a bond dimension independent of the system size, an analogous statement does not hold for general states in two dimensions (2D). This leaves open the question of how the expressivity of 2D TNS is related to the entanglement properties of the states they represent. In this work, we focus on two families of 2D translation-invariant Gaussian fermionic states: single-band BCS superconductors and half-filled two-band insulators (including semimetals). For each family, we prove that an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy is equivalent to having an exact Gaussian fermionic TNS representation with a finite bond dimension determined by the Renyi-0 entropy. We also establish equivalent characterizations in terms of compactly supported Wannier-type orbitals and the momentum-space wavefunction, relating the spatial extent of these orbitals and the structure of the wavefunction to the required bond dimension.

authors.name: Pok Man Tam, William Musk, Zhehao Dai

papers.title: On pseudospectra of the relativistic rotated harmonic oscillator
papers.summary: We establish an upper bound to the norm of the resolvent of a relativistic version of the non-self-adjoint operator obtained by a dilation analytic transformation of the quantum harmonic oscillator. The estimate implies a decay for large complex energies along rays with angles larger than that of the dilation. In this way we positively answer a question left open in [Proceedings of the Royal Society A 2025].

authors.name: David Krejcirik, Petr Siegl

papers.title: Statistical Properties of the $q$-Deformed Monolayer and Bilayer Graphene
papers.summary: We investigate the statistical properties of the $q$-deformed Dirac oscillator for monolayer and bilayer graphene in the presence of a constant external magnetic field. Using $q$-deformed creation and annihilation operators, we obtain the corresponding energy spectra and eigenfunctions, as well as their probability current densities, recovering the conventional Landau-level structures in the undeformed limit. For bilayer graphene, the lowest Landau levels are explicitly constructed within the $q$-deformed framework. The partition functions for both systems are derived using zeta-function techniques and the Euler-Maclaurin formula, allowing us to determine their main thermodynamic quantities for small values of the deformation parameter. Our results show that the $q$-deformation modifies the energy spectra, the behavior of the probability current density components, and the thermodynamic response of the systems. A comparison between monolayer and bilayer graphene reveals distinct thermal behaviors, reflecting their different Landau-level structures and highlighting the influence of the $q$-deformation on their statistical properties.

authors.name: Omar Pedraza, Erik D\'iaz-Bautista, L. A. L\'opez, Daniel O-Campa

papers.title: The Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic PBC clusters
papers.summary: We construct and solve the three-colored Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic lattices with periodic boundary conditions. We describe a self-contained procedure which uses finite quotients of orientation- preserving triangle groups to generate regular maps on compact genus-g surfaces. From these, one can extract their lattice connectivity, plaquette structure, homology cycles and Wilson sectors while implementing consistent boundary conditions. On the example of {8, 3} and {12, 3} lattices, we enumerate a selection of quotients with up to 72 vertices, which constitute the discrete steps in a finite-size scaling analysis. For the isotropic point, corresponding to the spin-liquid phase in the thermodynamic limit, we identify the ground state superselection sectors, quantify their deviation from the homogeneous {\pi} flux sector and show how the selected flux background depends on the quotient geometry. We then discuss how the resulting ground state sector degeneracies are entirely generated by physical lattice symmetries acting on both the plaquette fluxes and non-contractible Wilson loops. Finally, we study the behaviour of the finite-size two-vison gap and matter fermion correlations. We find that the gap does not decrease monotonically with increasing system size, while one still recovers the expected algebraic decay of the correlations at the isotropic point, even for the considered modest system sizes.

authors.name: Alberto Zorzato, Jiri Min\'a\v{r}

papers.title: Parametric and Universal Thouless Invariants in Matrix Product States
papers.summary: We investigate the classification of continuous families of translation-invariant injective matrix product states on an infinite chain, parametrized by a paracompact Hausdorff space $X$ and subject to a compact Hausdorff symmetry $G$. We construct an invariant for phases of such families, valued in $\check{H}^1(X;\widehat{G})$, that generalizes the known $\widehat{G}$ phase invariant for $G$-symmetric Thouless pumps. The phase invariant is constructed as the pullback to $X$ of a single universal \v{C}ech cohomology class on a classifying space of $G$-symmetric translation-invariant injective matrix product states. Several examples are given over various parameter spaces where this invariant is nontrivial.

authors.name: Leonardo Goller, Amartya H. Singh, Daniel D. Spiegel, Marco Venuti

papers.title: Tunable Topological Charge Order in Magnetic Moir\'e Systems
papers.summary: Two-dimensional electrons in a strong magnetic field exhibit two seemingly incompatible ground states: incompressible quantum Hall liquids with a quantized Hall conductance, and electron crystals in which interactions drive the charge into ordered patterns. Moir\'e superlattices in transition-metal-dichalcogenide bilayers offer a tunable arena for this competition. Using neural quantum states (NQS) together with several methodological advances, we show how this competition unfolds. In particular, we demonstrate that the two end points are separated by an extended regime in which molecular charge order coexists with a quantized Hall response. We map the ground-state phase diagram of electrons at Landau-level filling $\nu_B=1$ in the presence of a moir\'e superlattice potential, with three electrons per moir\'e cell. In the deep triangular potential limit, the electrons form the topologically trivial "Wigner molecular crystal'' of three-electron artificial atoms, a state recently imaged at zero magnetic field in moir\'e bilayers. As the potential depth is lowered, molecular charge order remains while quantized Hall response emerges. At the honeycomb point, where each cell contains three electrons and two degenerate moir\'e minima, wells are either singly or doubly occupied and the doublons provide an emergent Ising degree of freedom. Starting from modest interaction strength, we find short-range doublon correlations within the Chern insulator which grow with interaction strength and eventually break sublattice symmetry, forming a N\'eel CDW with long-range order between doublons. The topological molecular regime lies at twist angles and magnetic fields directly accessible to current experiments. The methodological advances presented provide a scalable framework for exploring a broad range of questions in correlated quantum matter in the presence of magnetic fields.

authors.name: Conor Smith, Yubo Yang, Shiwei Zhang, Miguel A. Morales

papers.title: Exact Dynamic Scaling of Quantum Jump Statistics in Monitored Many-Body Systems
papers.summary: Quantum measurement has opened a new frontier in nonequilibrium many-body physics, revealing striking phenomena such as measurement-induced entanglement transitions, whose experimental observation typically requires costly postselection. Quantum jump statistics offer another route to studying such measurement-induced many-body phenomena without postselection, motivating the search for universality in measurement outcomes themselves. In this Letter, we discover that fluctuation of the number of quantum jumps within a subsystem exhibits novel dynamic scaling, characterized by diffusive time scale and anomalous super-Poissonian system-size scaling that depend on the subsystem size in monitored many-body systems. For free fermions under continuous monitoring, we exactly determine the scaling exponent and the scaling function by deriving an exact finite-size solution of the Liouvillian autocorrelation function. We also analytically show that the dynamic scaling with the same scaling exponent and the scaling function even holds for interacting fermions in the limit of large measurement strength. Our work provides a novel framework to classify measurement-induced nonequilibrium many-body universality through experimentally friendly, postselection-free quantities.

authors.name: Kazuki Yamamoto, Taiki Ishiyama, Toranosuke Matsubara, Kazuya Fujimoto, Tomohiro Sasamoto, Ryusuke Hamazaki

papers.title: Coexisting orders and dipolar Luttinger liquids in $\mathbb{Z}_N$ quantum torus chain
papers.summary: We establish a unified ground-state phase diagram for the one-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ quantum torus chain, which is connected to dipolar cluster and dipolar Ising chains via noninvertible dualities. Combining tensor-network calculations with bosonization and perturbation theory, we establish a rich phase diagram governed by the local Hilbert-space dimension $N$ and its parity. We identify phases with coexisting $X$ and $Z$ long-range orders ($C$ phase), and dipolar Luttinger liquids (dLL$_{\rm I}$ and dLL$_{\rm II}$) separating coexisting phases from single-order phases. Gapless dipolar excitations coexist with long-range order in dLLs. Both the $C$ and dLL phases appear at $N \geq 5$, but only the $C$ phases persist as $N\to \infty$. The stability of the dLL phase is understood by an emergent Luttinger liquid theory, with Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions out of it driven by competing umklapp and clock anisotropy perturbations. For odd $N \geq 5$, a third dLL phase (dLL$_{\rm III}$) emerges near $\theta = \pi$ due to the low-energy dynamics inside the exponentially degenerate ground-state manifold that maps onto an effective XXZ chain. Duality considerations suggest a possible gapless dipolar symmetry-protected topological phase and spontaneous dipole-symmetry breaking in dipolar cluster chains.

authors.name: Seunghun Lee, Seungho Lee, Hyun-Yong Lee, Jung Hoon Han

papers.title: Electrostatic screening and nitrogen-vacancy charge states in boron-doped/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions
papers.summary: Boron-doped diamond (BDD) enables the integration of electrical functionality with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, but the influence of junction electrostatics on NV charge-state stability remains unclear. In this study, we investigate the equilibrium electrostatics of BDD/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions using self-consistent Poisson-Fermi calculations. The results reveal two distinct electrostatic length scales in the nitrogen-doped substrate: a near-interface region of ionized donors that produces dominant band bending and determines the NV$^{0/-}$ charge-state boundary, and a much longer screening tail associated with weak donor ionization in the neutral bulk. The resulting NV$^-$ depletion depth depends strongly on the nitrogen concentration but exhibits a more moderate dependence on boron doping. At $N_B = 10^{21}$ cm$^{-3}$, varying the interface grading scale $w$ from 0.5 to 8 nm changes the depletion depth by approximately 22 nm, whereas variations in the modeled bulk BDD charge response produce a shift of only 1.27 nm. These results indicate that, under the conditions studied, the nitrogen donor concentration and local interface structure primarily govern the equilibrium NV charge-state profile, rather than the bulk electronic response of BDD alone.

authors.name: Masato Koga, Haizen Cho, El Mustapha Mansouri, Eikichi Kimura, Ryo Matsumoto, Yoshihiko Takano, Keigo Arai

papers.title: MASQ: Measurement-Adaptive Sampling for Near-Clifford Quantum Error Correction Circuits
papers.summary: Classical sampling of quantum error correction (QEC) circuits supports fault-tolerant protocol evaluation, but estimating rare logical failures requires many independent shots. Frame-active-state simulators isolate non-stabilizer information in a dense active-state vector, yet dense-state processing remains exponential in the active width. This paper presents MASQ, an exact measurement-adaptive sampler for near-Clifford QEC circuits based on selective materialization of non-Clifford rotations. At each measurement boundary, MASQ materializes only rotations in a measurement-relevant closure capturing direct and indirect non-commuting dependencies, deferring the rest to limit active-state expansion. Stabilizer-assisted elimination further removes rotations certified to be invisible to all future measurements. A circuit-dependent schedule is computed once and shared across shots, while adaptive caching of conditional Born probabilities and batched execution reduce repeated sampling work while preserving the measurement-record distribution. Across 19 QEC benchmarks, MASQ reduces peak active width by up to 40 active virtual qubits and achieves up to 8,098-fold CPU throughput speedup over Clifft on multi-round circuits.

authors.name: Chaebin Jung, Sangmin Jeon, Kyeongwon Lee, Sechan Park, Woojoo Lee

papers.title: Quantum Interband-Coherence-Driven Inverse Faraday Effect in Intrinsic Graphene
papers.summary: The inverse Faraday effect converts the angular momentum of circularly polarized light into a quasistatic magnetization, providing a fundamental route to ultrafast optical control of magnetic fields. We develop an analytical quantum theory of this effect in intrinsic graphene, where massless Dirac fermions, electron-hole symmetry, and weak spin-orbit coupling suppress conventional population-based interpretations. We show that in intrinsic graphene, the helicity-dependent orbital magnetization arises from the off-diagonal zero-harmonic component of the second-order density matrix, rather than from intraband carrier circulation or diagonal population imbalance. We obtain closed expressions for the induced temporal surface magnetization, its finite-pulse dynamics, and the nonlocal stray magnetic field generated by the two-dimensional (2D) source. Optical helicity, frequency, pulse envelope, and beam profile independently control the response. Our results identify intrinsic graphene as an ideal platform for coherent orbital optomagnetism in 2D Dirac matter.

authors.name: Xingdi Wang, Haiming Dong, Kai Chang

papers.title: Complex mobility edges from competing localization channels in non-Hermitian quasicrystals
papers.summary: Non-Hermitian localization transitions often accompany multiple mobility edges, but their physical origin can be ambiguous. To address the issue, we introduce an extension of the Ganeshan-Pixley-Das Sarma model with both asymmetric hopping and complex onsite potential, thereby incorporating a broad range of non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chains. Its solution reveals two energy-dependent localization contributions manifested as distinct Lyapunov growth scales, whose competition determines the structure of mobility edges. We derive exact Lyapunov exponents via Avila's global theory, obtain thresholds of the two channels on complex-energy plane, and formulate a selection rule that distinguishes physical mobility edges from suppressed analytical candidates. The channel that uniquely controls localization can switch with energy, producing complex mobility edges of non-Hermitian origins. Nonreciprocal hopping further shifts the thresholds and alters the bulk energy patterns. Numerical spectra and finite-size localization diagnostics confirm the theory. Our work thus provides a unified framework for characterizing phase transitions and mobility edges under competing localization mechanisms in non-Hermitian quasicrystals.

authors.name: Bing Shao, Weiwei Zhu, Longwen Zhou

papers.title: Unique continuation for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
papers.summary: We prove a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, viewed as functions of the electron configuration with values in the spin-photon space. The vector potential may lie in $L^6_\mathrm{loc}$, with its divergence, curl, and the scalar potential in $L^p_\mathrm{loc}$ for some $p>2$. As an application, we prove a Hohenberg-Kohn theorem at positive coupling strength: the spin-summed ground-state density and combined current density determine the external potentials up to a gauge transformation and an additive constant.

authors.name: Mih\'aly A. Csirik

papers.title: Optimal Min-Entropy Estimation with High Probability
papers.summary: Min-entropy plays a fundamental role in assessing the unpredictability of randomness sources. In particular, NIST SP 800-90B specifies min-entropy estimation as a key procedure for entropy sources used in cryptographic random bit generators, illustrating the practical importance of reliable min-entropy estimation. In this paper, we settle the sample complexity of min-entropy estimation with high probability in both the classical and quantum cases. Specifically, for min-entropy estimation with additive error $\varepsilon$ and probability at least $1-\delta$, the sample complexity is $\Theta(d\log(d/\delta)/\varepsilon^2)$ for classical distributions on $d$ symbols and $\Theta((d^2+d\log(1/\delta))/\varepsilon^2)$ for quantum states on a $d$-dimensional Hilbert space. Our results admit short and simple proofs.

authors.name: Qisheng Wang

papers.title: From nonlocal correlations to local symmetry breaking: Asymmetry dynamics of crosscap states
papers.summary: Under unitary dynamics preserving a global symmetry, bipartite entanglement typically grows while an initially broken symmetry is locally restored. Here, we show that this conventional scenario can be reversed when symmetry-breaking coherence is initially encoded in long-range entanglement. We investigate this phenomenon in a family of charge deformed crosscap states, characterized by antipodal entangled pairs with tunable entanglement and symmetry breaking. We first characterize their static properties, finding a Page-like entanglement profile and an entanglement asymmetry that vanishes for subsystems smaller than half the system size, but grows logarithmically for larger subsystems. For symmetric subsystems, we also analyze the symmetry-resolved entanglement and investigate how it evolves as the subsystem is continuously deformed away from a symmetric partition. Following a quench to a free-fermion tight-binding chain, we uncover an unconventional dynamics in which the entanglement entropy decreases whereas the entanglement asymmetry increases, so that initially symmetric subsystems dynamically develop local symmetry breaking. This behavior is quantitatively captured by a quasiparticle picture describing the propagation of antipodal correlations. Our results reveal how symmetry-preserving dynamics can redistribute globally encoded symmetry-breaking coherence, making it locally accessible, and establish the initial entanglement structure as a key ingredient in determining the fate of local symmetries out of equilibrium.

authors.name: Konstantinos Chalas, Pasquale Calabrese, Colin Rylands

papers.title: Spin-Polarized Transport Tomography of a Quantum-Dot Spin Qubit via Ferromagnetic Leads
papers.summary: We propose a theoretical protocol for reconstructing the density matrix of a single-electron spin qubit using spin-polarized transport. The system consists of a quantum dot coupled to ferromagnetic reservoirs and subject to a magnetic field lying in the $xy$ plane of the Bloch sphere. Spin-dependent tunneling events measured along the $x\pm$, $y\pm$, and $z\pm$ quantization axes give rise to probability distributions that encode the quantum state of the qubit. The open-system dynamics are described using a Lindblad master equation, which captures the time evolution of the spin under continuous coupling to the reservoirs. By counting tunneling events for four different magnetic alignments, we formulate a scheme for reconstructing the full density matrix of the qubit. The resulting simulation data are analyzed using Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) as a supervised machine-learning post-processing tool to reconstruct smooth time-dependent density-matrix elements from the measured probability distributions. The proposed model enables complete access to the open-system density matrix, including both population probabilities and relative phase information. Successful state reconstruction demonstrates the validity and robustness of the approach, highlighting its applicability to experimentally accessible spin-transport platforms.

authors.name: M. B. Samb\'u, L. Sanz, F. M. Souza

papers.title: A Diamond Quantum Oscilloscope
papers.summary: Quantum-enhanced metrology has achieved remarkable precision in parameter estimation, but extending these advantages to continuous time-dependent fields (waveform sensing) remains a formidable challenge due to the infinite-dimensional nature of the signal. Here, we report the first experimental realization of a room-temperature solid-state quantum oscilloscope based on a sequential quantum difference amplification strategy. Within a zero-order-hold reconstruction framework, our method completely bypasses the need for massive entanglement. Crucially, we demonstrate that the overall waveform reconstruction error unequivocally follows the theoretically predicted Heisenberg scaling of \(O(N^{-1/2})\), decisively surpassing the classical \(O(N^{-1/3})\) limit. This transformative precision requires approximately 30-fold fewer quantum resources than conventional methods to achieve the same waveform error. Furthermore, we demonstrate the reconstruction of a multicomponent waveform and distinctly resolve weak high-frequency components that are entirely drowned in the shot noise of classical sampling. These results transition quantum metrology from parameter estimation into a practical instrument, establishing a genuine quantum advantage in continuous waveform reconstruction and paving the way for critical applications such as nanoscale nuclear magnetic resonance imaging, where detecting extremely weak signals is crucial for resolving molecular structures.

authors.name: Yang Dong, Yu Zheng, Wang Jiang, Zhi-Wei Liu, Shao-Chun Zhang, Xiang-Dong Chena, Guang-Can Guo, Fang-Wen Sun

papers.title: Quantum Advantage in Storage and Retrieval of Isometry Channels
papers.summary: Storage and retrieval refer to the task of encoding an unknown quantum channel $\Lambda$ into a quantum state, known as the program state, such that the channel can later be retrieved. There are two strategies for this task: classical and quantum strategies. The classical strategy uses multiple queries to $\Lambda$ to estimate $\Lambda$ and retrieves the channel based on the estimate represented in classical bits. The classical strategy turns out to offer the optimal performance for the storage and retrieval of unitary channels. In this work, we analyze the asymptotic performance of the classical and quantum strategies for the storage and retrieval of isometry channels. We show that the optimal fidelity for isometry estimation is given by $F = 1-{d(D-d)\over n} + O(n^{-4/3})$, where $d$ and $D$ denote the input and output dimensions of the isometry, and $n$ is the number of queries. This result indicates that, unlike in the case of unitary channels, the classical strategy is suboptimal for the storage and retrieval of isometry channels, which requires $n = \Theta(\epsilon^{-1})$ to achieve the diamond-norm error $\epsilon$. We propose a more efficient quantum strategy based on port-based teleportation, which stores the isometry channel in a program state using only $n = \Theta(1/\sqrt{\epsilon})$ queries, achieving a quadratic improvement over the classical strategy. As an application, we extend our approach to general quantum channels, achieving improved program cost compared to prior results by Gschwendtner, Bluhm, and Winter [Quantum \textbf{5}, 488 (2021)].

authors.name: Satoshi Yoshida, Jisho Miyazaki, Mio Murao

papers.title: Entanglement preservation and Clauser-Horne nonlocality in electromagnetically induced transparency quantum memories
papers.summary: Understanding how decoherence-induced loss affects entanglement and nonlocal correlations in quantum memories is important for quantum information science. Here we develop a quantitative description of photonic quantum states retrieved from electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) memories in a ground-state-decoherence-limited regime. Using the dark-state-polariton formalism, we derive the attenuation factor of the retrieved probe mode from the EIT dynamics. This attenuation depends on the coupling field and ground-state coherence decay and is not introduced as an independent phenomenological loss parameter. Within a specified quantum-limited pure-loss model, we use this attenuation to obtain the reduced photonic density operator. We show that, in the symmetric case, the complete retrieved state of an initially path-entangled single photon remains entangled for any nonzero storage efficiency, despite acquiring a vacuum component. In contrast, violation of the unconditional Clauser-Horne inequality under displaced on/off detection without post-selection requires an intrinsic efficiency above 89.7%. We further derive the retrieved N-qubit photonic density operator for multiple independently operating EIT memories. These results establish a quantitative connection between EIT memory dynamics, retrieved quantum states, and operational nonlocality benchmarks under explicit channel assumptions.

authors.name: Po-Han Tseng, Yong-Fan Chen

papers.title: From Rotations to Unitaries: Reversible Quantum Processes and the Emergence of the $SU(2)-SO(3)$ Homomorphism
papers.summary: We present an operational reconstruction of the well-known two-to-one homomorphism between the groups $SU(2)$ and $SO(3)$, grounded in the physical description of quantum state preparation and evolution. Starting from the connection between vectors in three-dimensional physical space and quantum states of two-level systems, we investigate how reversible transformations-modeled as completely positive and trace-preserving maps-give rise to a correspondence between spatial rotations and unitary operations. Our approach reveals how this group-theoretic structure naturally emerges from physical constraints, particularly the preservation of purity and reversibility in quantum processes. Beyond its theoretical relevance, the construction offers a pedagogically accessible framework for introducing core ideas in quantum mechanics and symmetry groups, making the abstract correspondence between $SU(2)$ and $SO(3)$ tangible through experimentally meaningful procedures.

authors.name: V. G. Valle, B. F. Rizzuti

papers.title: Classification of Transuranium Elements in Terms of `Winding' Numbers in the Bohr-Sommerfeld Model
papers.summary: We revisit the Bohr-Sommerfeld atomic model to explore hydrogen-like ions of Uranium ($Z=92$), Oganesson ($Z=118$), and hypothetical superheavy elements beyond. Although superseded by the Dirac equation and modern quantum electrodynamics, the semiclassical approach offers a historically and pedagogically valuable perspective. Using the Sommerfeld fine structure formula and computer algebra methods, we demonstrate the appearance of self-intersecting orbits in super strong Coulomb fields, beginning with Oganesson and hypothetical elements up to $Z\le137$. These orbits can be classified by their `winding' numbers, providing a simple topological description of Coulomb field strength in this framework. Our results highlight a conceptual bridge between early quantum theory and modern superheavy element physics.

authors.name: Sergei K. Suslov

papers.title: All-Gaussian State Discrimination Beyond the Coherent Helstrom Bound
papers.summary: A core problem in communications is the optimal discrimination of binary-phase-shift-keyed (BPSK) signals. A longstanding goal has been to reach the fundamental quantum limit, known as the Helstrom bound, for BPSK signals encoded in coherent states. However, due to technical constraints, proposals for reaching the bound remain impractical. In this letter we take an alternative approach: using only Gaussian optics - displaced squeezed states and homodyne detection - we achieve discrimination of BPSK signals with error rates below what can be achieved using coherent states and any quantum measurement.

authors.name: Angus Walsh, Lorcan Conlon, Biveen Shajilal, Ozlem Erkilic, Jiri Janousek, Syed Assad, Jie Zhao, Ping Koy Lam

papers.title: Harnessing Intrinsic Noise for Quantum Simulation of Open Quantum Systems
papers.summary: Simulating open quantum systems on quantum computers is challenging because dissipative dynamics are nonunitary, whereas gate-based quantum algorithms are typically built from unitary operations. Conventional approaches can overcome this mismatch by embedding nonunitary processes into enlarged unitary circuits, often with ancillary-qubit and gate overhead. In this work, we propose an alternative perspective in which we selectively preserve the physical noise to emulate nonunitary channels. More specifically, we present a partial encoding algorithm that iteratively leverages intrinsic noise to mimic the dynamics of a target open-system. We benchmark the convergence of this algorithm against the dissipative exciton transport Hamiltonian and retrieve their dynamics. By utilizing intrinsic hardware noise to emulate the target nonunitary dynamics, this approach avoids the dual overhead of error-correcting that noise and using ancillary qubits to re-introduce nonunitarity. This significantly reduces both qubit requirements and physical fidelity thresholds, paving the way for more efficient techniques to simulate open quantum systems on quantum computers.

authors.name: Sameer Dambal, Akira Sone, Yu Zhang

papers.title: Improved parameter initialization for the (local) unitary cluster Jastrow ansatz
papers.summary: The unitary cluster Jastrow (UCJ) ansatz and its variant known as local UCJ (LUCJ) are promising choices for variational quantum algorithms for chemistry due to their combination of physical motivation and hardware efficiency. The parameters of these ansatzes can be initialized from the output of a coupled cluster, singles and doubles (CCSD) calculation performed on a classical computer. However, truncating the number of repetitions of the ansatz, as well as discarding interactions to accommodate the connectivity constraints of near-term quantum processors, degrade the approximation to CCSD and the resulting energy accuracy. In this work, we propose two methods to improve the parameter initialization. The first method, which is applicable to both expectation value- and sample-based algorithms, uses compressed double factorization of the CCSD amplitudes to improve or recover the CCSD approximation. The second method, which is applicable to sample-based algorithms, uses approximate tensor network simulation to improve the quality of samples produced by the ansatz circuit. Both methods perform classical preprocessing to construct the initial circuit parameters and can be followed by parameter optimization using quantum measurements, although we do not perform such optimization in this work. We validate our methods using exact state vector simulation on systems of up to 52 qubits, as well as experiments on superconducting quantum processors using up to 65 qubits. Our results indicate that our methods can significantly improve the output of both expectation value- and sample-based quantum algorithms.

authors.name: Wan-Hsuan Lin, Fangchun Liang, Mario Motta, Haimeng Zhang, Kenneth M. Merz Jr., Kevin J. Sung

papers.title: Integrated Generation and Purification of Entangled Coherent States for Non-Gaussian Teleportation
papers.summary: Entangled coherent states (ECS) provide a powerful non-Gaussian resource for continuous-variable (CV) quantum communication, but their generation in scalable architectures remains challenging. We propose an integrated photonic scheme that creates high-fidelity quasi-entangled coherent states (quasi-ECS) from a two-mode squeezed vacuum state (TMSVS) via photon subtraction in a symmetric waveguide trimer. The resulting non-Gaussian entanglement is further enhanced by single-photon catalysis, which purifies the distributed state after transmission through lossy channels. The improvement in conditional teleportation fidelity is accompanied by a reduced heralding probability. Using these purified quasi-ECS resources, we analyze a photon-number-based teleportation protocol and demonstrate high-fidelity transfer of both coherent states and Schrodinger cat states. For the logical cat qubit, we use an orthogonal even/odd-cat basis, measurement-dependent phase corrections, and the success-probability-weighted fidelity over six logical input states. For completeness and benchmarking, we also study the Braunstein-Kimble (BK) teleportation protocol using Gaussian TMSVSs. In particular, the teleportation fidelity for cat states exceeds the benchmark value of 2/3 over a broad range of realistic channel and squeezing parameters. By contrast, the underlying TMSVS performs poorly within the photon-number-based protocol, whereas in the BK protocol it exceeds this benchmark only in a restricted regime of high squeezing and high transmissivity. Our results show that integrated photon subtraction and catalysis enable practical, chip-compatible generation of non-Gaussian entanglement suitable for advanced quantum teleportation and CV quantum networks.

authors.name: Ananga Mohan Datta, William J. Munro, Nicolo Lo Piparo, Kae Nemoto

papers.title: Group Fourier filtering of quantum resources in quantum phase space
papers.summary: Recently, it has been shown that group Fourier analysis of quantum states, i.e., decomposing them into the irreducible representations (irreps) of a symmetry group, enables new ways to characterize their resourcefulness. Given that quantum phase spaces (QPSs) provide an alternative description of quantum systems, and thus of the group's representation, one may wonder how such harmonic analysis changes. In this work we show that for general compact Lie-group quantum resource theories (QRTs), the entire family of Stratonovich-Weyl quantum phase-space representations, characterized by the Cahill--Glauber parameter $s$, has a clear resource-theoretic and signal-processing meaning. Specifically, changing $s$ implements a continuously tunable group Fourier filter. In the examples of spin coherence, multipartite entanglement, and fermionic Gaussianity, this gives a low-pass representation at $s=-1$, an unfiltered spectrum at $s=0$, and a high-pass representation at $s=1$. Moreover, we show that the norms of the QRT's free-state Fourier components completely determine this family of phase-space representations. Finally, we uncover an $s$-duality relating the nontrivial phase-space spectra of free states to the ensemble-averaged spectra of typical (Haar-random) states through a shift in $s$. Overall, our results provide a new interpretation of QPSs and establish them as a signal-processing framework for characterizing, filtering, and visualizing quantum resources.

authors.name: Luke Coffman, N. L. Diaz, Martin Larocca, Maria Schuld, M. Cerezo

papers.title: Realisation of a Protected Cat-Qutrit Manifold via Engineered Quantum Tunnelling
papers.summary: Engineering quantum tunnelling in phase space has emerged as a viable method for creating a protected logical qubit manifold with biased-noise properties. A promising approach is to combine a Kerr nonlinearity with a multi-photon drive, resulting in a system known as a Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO). In this work, we implement a three-photon KPO and explore its potential as a protected bosonic qutrit. We confirm quantum coherence by demonstrating three-photon Rabi oscillations and performing direct Wigner function measurements that reveal the formation of three-component cat-like states. Crucially, we observe a breathing-like dynamic in phase space, a characteristic feature of driven quantum systems. This dynamic arises from macroscopic temporal interference between the cat-qutrit manifold and the excited states. The frequency of resulting oscillations in the mean photon number provides a direct, time-domain measurement of the energy gap separating the qutrit from the excited states, thereby establishing an experimental hallmark of qutrit manifold protection. Furthermore, we identify a parasitic higher-order pump term as the primary mechanism constraining the mean photon number, highlighting its mitigation as a requisite for maximising protection. Our findings elucidate the basic quantum properties of the three-photon KPO and establish the first step towards its use as an alternative qutrit platform.

authors.name: Sangil Kwon, Daisuke Hoshi, Toshiaki Nagase, Daichi Sugiyama, Hiroto Mukai, Kengo Takemura, Rintaro Kojima, Yu Zhou, Shohei Watabe, Fumiki Yoshihara, Jaw-Shen Tsai

papers.title: A Quantum Photonic Approach to Graph Coloring
papers.summary: Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS) is a quantum computational model that leverages linear optics to solve sampling problems believed to be classically intractable. Recent experimental breakthroughs have demonstrated quantum advantage using GBS, motivating its application to real-world combinatorial optimization problems. In this work, we reformulate the graph coloring problem as an integer programming problem using the independent set formulation. This enables the use of GBS to identify cliques in the complement graph, which correspond to independent sets in the original graph. Our method is benchmarked against classical heuristics and exact algorithms on two sets of instances: Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graphs and graphs derived from a smart-charging use case. The results demonstrate that GBS can provide competitive solutions, highlighting its potential as a quantum-enhanced heuristic for graph-based optimization.

authors.name: Jesua Epequin, Pascale Bendotti, Joseph Mikael

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced Markov Chain Monte Carlo for Combinatorial Optimization
papers.summary: Quantum computing offers an alternative paradigm for addressing combinatorial optimization problems compared to classical methods. However, despite recent hardware improvements, the execution of empirical quantum optimization experiments at scales known to be hard for state-of-the-art classical solvers is not yet in reach. In this work, we offer a different way to approach combinatorial optimization with near-term quantum computing. Motivated by the promising results observed in using quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QeMCMC) for approximating complicated probability distributions, we combine ideas of sampling from the device with QeMCMC together with warm-starting and parallel tempering, in the context of combinatorial optimization. We demonstrate empirically that our algorithm recovers the global optima for instances of the Maximum Independent Set problem (MIS) up to 117 decision variables using 117 qubits on IBM quantum hardware. We observe an indication of more favorable scaling relative to the tested classical MCMC methods on the chosen MIS instances. MIS is practically relevant across domains such as financial services and molecular biology. Although some MIS instances with a few hundred variables can be difficult for classical solvers, the instances studied here are solved efficiently by CPLEX.

authors.name: Kate V. Marshall, Daniel J. Egger, Michael Garn, Francesca Schiavello, Sebastian Brandhofer, Christa Zoufal, Stefan Woerner

papers.title: Classical shadows for non-iid quantum sources
papers.summary: Classical shadows allow many properties of a quantum system to be estimated from relatively few measurements. Their standard guarantees, however, assume independent and identically distributed experimental rounds and a fixed analysis procedure. These assumptions can fail when the source drifts or the analysis adapts to previous measurement outcomes. We show that average expectation values along the run can be estimated with the usual classical-shadow sample-complexity scaling, even when the prepared states depend arbitrarily on the past and the analysis learns from earlier outcomes. For bounded shadow estimators, we further derive error bars that adapt to the observed data and remain valid throughout the experiment, allowing measurements to stop once the desired precision is reached. We illustrate these results numerically by certifying entanglement hidden by time averaging and reducing the measurements needed to estimate energy densities in many-body systems with small fluctuations.

authors.name: Leonardo Zambrano

papers.title: Zero-Uncertainty States Relative to Observable Algebras
papers.summary: We study zero-uncertainty states (ZUSs) for projective readout with quantum memory. In such tasks, Alice and Bob first share a quantum state. Alice then chooses one measurement from a prescribed family of projection-valued measures (PVMs), performs the measurement, and announces her choice. Bob must infer Alice's outcome from his memory system with zero error. We prove that the admissible shared states are governed by the operator algebra generated by the entire PVM family, and in the physically important case where both systems have equal dimension and the measurements generate the full matrix algebra, every ZUS must be pure and maximally entangled. As a further application to quantum state verification, we use this purity result to give a direct proof that the target maximally entangled state is uniquely verified, extending Zhu's uniqueness criterion to degenerate projective measurements. Moreover, for protocols built from rank-one binary settings, we find an optimal spectral gap of $(3-\sqrt3)/6$ using three settings on two qutrits in $d=3$, and we also characterize all strategies attaining this gap. Finally, we show that different relaxations of exact readout yield inequivalent notions of approximate ZUSs depending on the task.

authors.name: Jiayu Ran

papers.title: Coherent and dissipative energy transfer in driven open quantum systems: a driven quantum master equation approach
papers.summary: Understanding how coherent driving and quantum dissipation cooperatively control nonequilibrium energy transfer is challenging in driven open quantum systems. Here, we develop a driven quantum master equation (dQME) that uses the eigenstates of the full driven Hamiltonian in the rotating frame and retains the driving phase in the system-reservoir interactions. This approach includes driving effects in both coherent evolution and dissipative exchange processes. We apply this approach to a coupled-qubit charger-battery system and dissipative energy transfer through one and two driven qubits. For a driven coupled-qubit battery, weak driving produces three peaks in stored energy near the central and two side resonances, whereas strong driving merges these peaks into a broad central peak. Ergotropy and charging efficiency are suppressed at the weak-driving resonances as battery coherence decreases. The central suppression of charging efficiency persists under strong driving. For dissipative energy transfer, the driven single-qubit model reveals three energy exchange channels set by the driving frequency and the dressed-state energy gap. Interqubit coupling produces additional current resonances, while strong driving broadens the frequency range of enhanced energy currents. We hope that the dQME may provide a common framework for understanding coherent energy charging and dissipative energy transfer.

authors.name: Junran Kong, Yitian Chen, Huan Liu, Liwei Duan, Chen Wang

papers.title: Thermal Entanglement and Out-of-Equilibrium Thermodynamics in 1D Bose Gases
papers.summary: We investigate entanglement in and out of equilibrium in a one-dimensional Bose gas in its low-energy Bogoliubov regime. In this Gaussian setting, the state is fully characterized by its covariance matrix, which allows us to detect and quantify entanglement directly from the density and phase fluctuations of the gas. For thermal states, we determine the optimal entanglement witness arising from the covariance matrix criterion and show that it has a remarkably simple form: it depends only on the density fluctuations of the lowest normal mode and on the phase fluctuations of the highest one. For Dirichlet boundary conditions, this gives the exact temperature below which the gas is entangled, which, for many pixels, is given by $k_BT_{\rm sep}\simeq0.83\,\hbar c_0/\Delta$, where $c_0$ is the speed of sound and $\Delta$ the size of the pixels used to resolve the gas. We then study out-of-equilibrium dynamics induced by unitary compression and show that entanglement can be generated even from initially separable thermal states. This requires a non-adiabatic compression, since an adiabatic compression acts separately, and in the same way, on every pixel and therefore conserves entanglement. Moreover, the amount of entanglement created is limited by the compression ratio. We finally discuss how a subsequent contact with a thermal bath, modeled by global or local master equations, affects entanglement. Our methods and results provide a unified and physically intuitive picture of how entanglement emerges and evolves in 1D quantum Bose gases, and identify a simple optimal witness that is relevant more broadly to the analysis of entanglement in quadratic bosonic models and of its role in thermodynamic transformations.

authors.name: Julia Math\'e, Nicky Kai Hong Li, Pharnam Bakhshinezhad, Giuseppe Vitagliano

papers.title: Quantum Gibbs sampling through the detectability lemma
papers.summary: Gibbs state preparation is an important subroutine in quantum computing. In this work we use the detectability lemma to improve Gibbs state preparation. Specifically, we design new Gibbs state preparation methods that do not rely on simulating Lindbladian evolution, thus avoiding the overhead from it. For local Lindbladians consisting of $M$ terms, this approach reduces the cost by a factor of $O(M)$. We also combine the detectability lemma operator and quantum singular value transformation to implement ground state projection operators of frustration-free Hamiltonians, resulting in a quadratic speedup in the spectral gap dependence. Applying this method to Lindbladians for the Gibbs state of local commuting Hamiltonians, we achieve quadratically better dependence on the Lindbladian spectral gap.

authors.name: Di Fang, Jianfeng Lu, Yu Tong, Chu Zhao

papers.title: Finite-size Entanglement Certification via Third-Order Local Randomized Measurements
papers.summary: Certifying entanglement in high-dimensional systems usually requires full state tomography, whose cost grows rapidly with the system dimension. Local randomized measurements offer a scalable alternative, but existing tests based on second-order correlations access only limited information about the state. Here, we derive a finite-size entanglement certificate that extends local randomized measurements to third order. The additional third-order information reveals entanglement that remains undetected at second order, while a dimension-independent concentration bound provides rigorous control of finite-sample errors. Our result opens a practical route to extracting stronger entanglement information from experimental platforms without the dimension-dependent overhead of state tomography.

authors.name: Giovanni Scala, Corrado C. Mattiacci, Dorota Pietryka, Gniewomir Sarbicki

papers.title: Scalable spin-nematic squeezing in multi-level dipole-interacting Rydberg atom arrays
papers.summary: We study the dynamical generation of metrologically useful entanglement in arrays of three-level (spin-1) systems coupled by spin-exchange interactions, as realized by dipole-interacting Rydberg atoms in optical tweezers. We quantify the metrological gain by a generalized squeezing parameter optimized over all linear $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ phase generators and readout observables. For equal exchange couplings on the two transitions, the dynamics reduces to one-axis twisting (OAT) of an effective two-level system. Away from this point, the full three-level structure provides a genuine advantage. For all-to-all couplings, the optimal squeezing at $N=4000$ exceeds the OAT value by a factor of 3.6, with a fitted scaling exponent of $0.93$ compared with $0.69$ for OAT over $100\le N\le4000$. For two-dimensional dipolar arrays, exact and tensor-network simulations up to $N=49$ show that the optimal three-level protocol outperforms the effective spin-1/2 dynamics, with a gain that increases with system size, and semiclassical simulations show that squeezing continues to grow up to $N=10^4$. Crucially, our results demonstrate a real advantage of utilizing the full three-level $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ structure of the spin-1 system over $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ type one-axis twisting dynamics. Our results extend interaction-driven scalable squeezing beyond the well-studied qubit setting to spin-exchange-coupled qudits with dipolar interactions, and can be realized in current Rydberg tweezer experiments.

authors.name: Sakshi Bahamnia, Thomas Bilitewski

papers.title: Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization with Amplitude Amplification
papers.summary: Recently, sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) has emerged as a promising approach to compute ground and excited states of problem Hamiltonians. This method classically diagonalizes a Hamiltonian in a subspace that is spanned by samples obtained from a quantum computer. However, by its nature, SQD suffers from a fundamental sampling problem, as some basis states that are required for a targeted accuracy may only be sampled extremely rarely. To alleviate this limitation, we introduce the SQD-AA algorithm that combines SQD with amplitude amplification (AA). SQD-AA uses AA to sequentially reduce probabilities of already measured bitstrings, thus making the observation of new ones more likely. We observe a reduction in the total query complexity of more than a factor 100 for algebraically and exponentially decaying model distributions, and analytically show a quadratic advantage for the latter. Moreover, we evaluate real molecules in an early fault-tolerant scenario and compare SQD-AA to SQD and iterative quantum phase estimation (iQPE). For almost all considered examples, we observe the lowest total number of T-gates for SQD-AA while only requiring circuits that are 2-4 orders of magnitude shallower than those needed for iQPE. Given this substantial reduction in circuit depth compared to iQPE while saving 2 orders of magnitude in total runtime compared to SQD, we expect a significant regime in early fault-tolerance where SQD-AA runs feasibly, but iQPE circuits are too deep to execute confidently.

authors.name: Nina Stockinger, Ludwig N\"utzel, Michael J. Hartmann

papers.title: Mechanism of wavefunction collapse in measurements of separated quantum subsystems
papers.summary: The specific advance of this work is to propose a mechanism by which superpositions collapse during measurement of the separated subsystems of entangled quantum states. It is shown how the phase that locks together entangled states could play a special role in the measurement of isolated subsystems. This `contextual' phase is installed into separated subsystems of an entangled state, and decides the measurement outcomes for the subsystems by directing the collapse of each superposition to a particular classical outcome when a subsystem is measured. The measuring apparatus thus obtains a classical read-out of the quantum correlations embedded in an entangled state. More broadly, these results suggest insights into the theory of measurement of quantum superpositions.

authors.name: Gregory D. Scholes

papers.title: On the cryptographic potential of single-qubit rotations
papers.summary: In the domain of quantum communication, cryptographic protocols often require users to have access to trusted qubit sources or detectors. Recently, it was shown that on an architecture called the Qline, several protocols can equivalently be performed by parties capable only of single-qubit rotations. In this work, we introduce two composably secure constructions that together show how in most quantum cryptographic protocols, parties traditionally required to perform trusted qubit preparation or measurement can delegate these tasks to an untrusted provider and instead rely on a trusted single-qubit rotation device. Our first construction implements single-qubit measurement and is universally applicable across any context. In contrast, our second construction, which addresses qubit preparation, relies on specific assumptions regarding the underlying protocol. We show, however, that these assumptions are inherently satisfied by the vast majority of common quantum cryptographic protocols. A notable consequence of our results is the formal validation of the Qline as a versatile architecture capable of supporting a wide range of single-qubit protocols.

authors.name: Alex B. Grilo, Lucas Hanouz, Anne Marin

papers.title: Component-selective engineering of two-photon sources in a cavity-coupled two-atom system
papers.summary: In multiphoton blockade, drive-induced excitations are not necessarily fully converted into cavity photons, leaving unwanted lower-photon-number contributions that degrade source purity. This motivates a source-oriented component-selection strategy, in which the internal composition of the resonant two-excitation state is tailored to favor the component associated with the desired quantum-light output. In a cavity-coupled two-atom system, by engineering the resonant-state composition and controlling the interference between excitation pathways, we suppress both single- and three-photon backgrounds at matched two-photon populations, although a residual single-photon contribution remains. This residual background originates from a structural tradeoff between the photonic character of the target state and the spectral anharmonicity required for photon-number selectivity. Furthermore, selecting the double-atomic-excitation component at another operating point enables the generation of strongly correlated fluorescence photon pairs, demonstrating two distinct two-photon sources within the same physical platform.

authors.name: Zhicai Chen, Jun Xu, Deyi Kong, Xiangming Hu, Fei Wang

papers.title: Optimal Dynamic Cooling of Multiple Qubits
papers.summary: We solve the closed-system problem of cooling $M$ qubits, selected from $N$ identical thermal qubits, to the lowest common local temperature allowed by unitarity. The optimal protocol consists of two conceptually distinct steps. First, a passive rearrangement assigns the largest eigenvalues of the initial state to target sectors of lowest Hamming weight, thereby minimizing the total target energy. Second, a target-only complex-Hadamard transformation within each fixed-Hamming-weight subspace equalizes the one-qubit target marginals without changing any target-sector probability or the total energy. Consequently, imposing a common local temperature costs neither cooling depth nor additional work: the constrained optimum coincides with the unconstrained passive minimum for every $N>M$ and every initial temperature. The complex-Hadamard correction may nevertheless be costly at the circuit level. We therefore derive an exact arithmetic criterion for when the same optimum can be attained by a temperature-independent computational-basis permutation alone, and exhaustively classify the resulting finite-size islands of feasibility for $M+2\leq N\leq 128$. At isolated temperatures, further optimal permutations can arise through numerical cancellations between different thermal eigenvalue shells. These alternative realizations may reduce implementation complexity, but they cannot improve the cooling curve already attained by the universal protocol. We also derive the exact cooling curve, prove that at least two ancillary qubits are necessary and sufficient for nontrivial cooling, and show that joint many-target cooling can strictly outperform parallel single-target strategies.

authors.name: Mattia Reda, Massimiliano F. Sacchi, Chiara Macchiavello, Giacomo Guarnieri

papers.title: Exact Matching-Polynomial Solution of the Periodic Baxter-Fendley $Z_N$ Clock Chain
papers.summary: The periodic-boundary non-Hermitian Baxter-Fendley $Z_N$ chain does not have the same free-parafermionic structure as the open-boundary chain. We construct a matching polynomial for the corresponding cycle of its cyclic Weyl algebra. Its coefficients form conserved quantities containing the periodic Hamiltonian, while the matching polynomial itself realizes a Yang-Baxter transfer matrix. Root-of-unity fusion gives a second matching-polynomial closure and a system of spectral equations in each charge sector. The normalized energy resultant of these equations coincides with the charge-sector characteristic polynomial, yielding the complete finite-size energy spectrum with algebraic multiplicity. For positive reflection-symmetric chains, we prove that the periodic-boundary ground state is the unique analytic continuation of the open-boundary ground state. This yields an efficient large-size ground-state algorithm without enumerating the full spectrum. For the homogeneous three-state chain, seam-response asymptotics and finite-size ground-state calculations support two reciprocal candidate critical couplings distinct from the self-dual point, while the full periodic phase diagram is left for future work.

authors.name: Yuguan Li, D. C. Liu, Murray T. Batchelor

papers.title: Current statistics for quantum transport along a bosonic tight-binding chain connected to Markovian reservoirs
papers.summary: We study quantum transport of non-interacting particles in a bosonic tight-binding chain coupled to Markovian reservoirs at its boundaries. Using the analytic solution in the form of an anti-normally ordered quantum characteristic function, we obtain exact probability distribution functions for the current on each bond in the chain, as well as the inter-bond current correlation functions. We extend the analysis to tight-binding chains subject to uniform on-site phase damping. In the phasedamped case, we find that a Gaussian approximation for the quantum characteristic functions predicts current fluctuations with good accuracy.

authors.name: P. S. Muraev, A. R. Kolovsky, D. N. Maksimov

papers.title: Exact Replica-Sector Hierarchy of Multi-Resolvent Spectral-Weight Fluctuations in Random Free Fermions
papers.summary: The one-point ETH envelope fixes the smooth part of a spectral density but not how the spectral weight of an eigenstate is distributed across channels; its higher-order correlations are joint fluctuations of those weights and are carried by connected products of channel resolvents. In random free fermions every channel overlap is a squared Slater minor of a Haar-orthogonal one-body eigenvector matrix, and the multi-resolvent hierarchy has an exact microscopic realization there. The $r$-resolvent moment admits a decomposition into finitely many overlap sectors whose values are fixed by the channel and eigenstate overlap patterns and whose weights are exact finite-$N$ orthogonal Weingarten functions: the sector theorem holds at arbitrary finite multiplicity, it is realized in full at $r=3$ ($k=2,3,4$) and through exact sector slices at $r=4,5$, and the sector moments lift to connected resolvent cumulants and to the irreducible Feshbach self-energy vertices, whose deep plane begins at the order $z^{-(3r-2)}$. At $r=2$ this structure reproduces and completes an exact benchmark in which a flat envelope coexists with a non-Porter--Thomas intensity hierarchy and closes the two-resolvent covariance, and under interaction it separates into a deep plane fixed by Hamiltonian channel moments and a bulk that requires eigenstate-resolved information.

authors.name: Zhiqiang Huang

papers.title: Nonequilibrium energy transport and fluctuations in two-photon-driven nonlinear quantum optical systems
papers.summary: Understanding nonequilibrium transport and fluctuations under a parametric drive in nonlinear quantum optical systems is challenging. Here, we formulate a driven quantum master equation in the rotating frame combined with full counting statistics, retaining the drive-induced frequency shifts in the system-reservoir interactions and providing a unified description of drive-assisted incoherent transitions based on the rotated system dressed-basis. Applied to a Kerr resonator and a nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings model, the approach reveals pronounced multiphoton-resonant enhancement of the drive input energy current, with significant high peaks under two-photon driving compared to the single-photon case. The two-photon resonance relations are analytically obtained. Resonance structure in the nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings model nonlinearly relies on qubit-photon couplings, with additional dressed-state branches. A low-energy-state approximation attributes the resonant current enhancement to dressed-state hybridization and efficient activation of incoherent energy exchange processes. Beyond the average current, two-photon-driving induced energy exchange picture near resonance also substantially modifies the second-order current fluctuation and higher-order current cumulant, while increasing the time-normalized signal-to-noise ratio. Adding two-photon loss introduces extra incoherent photon-pair exchange pathways and further reshapes the current and its fluctuations. We hope these results may deepen interpretation of photon driving and quantum dissipation cooperatively governing nonequilibrium energy transport and fluctuations.

authors.name: Y. T. Chen, Y. W. Lu, J. C. Lu, C. Wang

papers.title: A depolarizing choir sings in Gaussian harmony
papers.summary: We study the noise threshold for positive quantum capacity for the qubit depolarizing channel. We explore analytically the action of the qubit depolarizing channel on the symmetric subspaces of the input qubits, in the limit of asymptotically many uses of the channel. We observe the emergence of a bosonic Gaussian channel. Furthermore, the codes previously developed for the depolarizing channel can be translated to codes for the emergent Gaussian channel, and it is easier to further optimize these codes for the simpler emergent Gaussian channel. Translating these codes back to the depolarizing channel leads to extremely good input states for the coherent information of the depolarizing channel producing new lower bounds on the noise threshold for positive capacity. In addition to improved lower bounds on the threshold, this newly found link between depolarizing noise and Gaussian channels offers a novel perspective contributing to our understanding of these symmetric codes.

authors.name: Rabsan Galib Ahmed, Sujeet Bhalerao, Sungjai Lee, Felix Leditzky, Debbie Leung, Luke Schaeffer, Graeme Smith

papers.title: Efficient Quantum Monte Carlo through Cluster Expansions
papers.summary: The sign problem remains a major obstacle to extending the success of Monte Carlo methods to generic quantum many-body systems. A powerful alternative relies on cluster expansions, which provide convergent representations of free energies and related quantities, with applications ranging from tensor network contractions to quantum dynamics and circuits. Within their convergence regime, these expansions often yield deterministic polynomial-time algorithms. However, such methods require exhaustive enumeration of connected clusters, leading to a computational overhead of $(N\varepsilon^{-1})^{\mathcal{O}(\log\Delta)}$, where $N$ is the system size, $\varepsilon$ the desired precision, and $\Delta$ the interaction-graph degree. This becomes particularly severe in long-range systems, where $\Delta\equiv N$, resulting in quasi-polynomial runtimes. Here, we introduce a Markov chain algorithm that samples cluster expansions directly in the space of connected clusters, replacing deterministic enumeration by Monte Carlo sampling. Because sampling occurs in an abstract cluster space rather than a physical configuration space, the conventional exponential sign problem is absent within the convergence regime. For general polymer models, we establish an FPRAS with runtime $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(N^4\varepsilon^{-3})$. For quantum partition functions at temperatures $\beta\leq\beta_{\mathrm{sampling}}\equiv\mathcal{O}(1)$, this improves to $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(N^{3+1/D}\varepsilon^{-3})$, where $D$ is the lattice dimension. The framework applies to long-range quantum systems with interactions $\propto1/r^\alpha$, including $2$-local models with $\alpha>2D$.

authors.name: Jorge S\'anchez-Segovia, \'Alvaro M. Alhambra

papers.title: Randomness Certification from Statistically Hiding Commitments
papers.summary: Randomness certification aims to guarantee that the output of an untrusted quantum device contains genuine randomness that remains unpredictable even given quantum side information held by an adversary. For a classical verifier interacting with a single quantum device, such a guarantee cannot rely on the physical separation underlying standard Bell tests and must instead follow from computational restrictions on the prover. Building on the framework of computational Bell inequalities, we distinguish classical and quantum virtual-input hiding, showing that the former suffices for proofs of quantumness, whereas the latter enables randomness certification against quantum side information. Our main technical contribution is to establish quantum virtual-input hiding for a commitment-based protocol derived from an earlier proof of quantumness (Morimae and Yamakawa, CRYPTO, 2024). We show that statistical hiding together with ordinary computational binding against quantum polynomial-time senders suffices, without requiring stronger quantum binding notions such as sum-binding or collapse-binding. This yields a randomness-certification protocol from post-quantum statistically hiding bit commitments. We give three instantiations. The NOVY commitment from any post-quantum one-way permutation yields randomness certification in the standard model with an inefficient classical verifier. Post-quantum trapdoor claw-free functions additionally provide trapdoor inversion, enabling an efficient classical verifier. In the quantum random-oracle model, a hash-based commitment yields randomness certification without additional computational assumptions, again with an inefficient verifier. These instantiations separate the cryptographic properties sufficient for randomness certification from the additional structure required for efficient verification within our commitment-based framework.

authors.name: Ilya Merkulov, Rotem Arnon

papers.title: Noise redistribution by stabilizer codes: an organizing view of concatenated three-qubit codes
papers.summary: We formulate stabilizer-code error correction as a code- and recovery-dependent transformation of the noise channel. For a fixed recovery map, syndrome projection produces a logical channel that is block diagonal with respect to the syndrome partition, whose diagonal Pauli weights are fixed by the code-induced error classes, with no physical Pauli twirl required. Concatenation is then iterated redistribution, with the dominant logical error guiding the next code. The bit-flip and phase-flip three-qubit codes with standard recoveries supply a closed-form benchmark, and logically inequivalent recoveries appear as a design degree of freedom for shaping the channel presented to the next decoder. For amplitude damping, the rules select $C_2(\hat\sigma_y)C_1(\hat\sigma_x)$ within this family: one level converts the damping into a nearly pure logical-$X$ channel at the price $f_1=1-3\gamma/4$, the second level suppresses that channel to $f_2=1-\frac94\gamma^2$, and the concatenated protocol overtakes the unencoded channel below $\gamma_c=0.2905$ ($f_c=0.8485$) under ideal encoding and recovery; with a per-gate error rate $\varepsilon$ the crossover survives only for $\varepsilon$ below about $5\times10^{-4}$, and then only inside a window of $\gamma$ that contracts as $\varepsilon$ grows. Across the $n$-qubit repetition family with odd $n$, the suppression order rises as $\gamma^{w+1}$ with $w=(n-1)/2$, while the gate budget grows as $n^L$. Correlated noise requires joint class statistics, whereas coherent noise retains intra-class coherences that make the same transformation usable in reverse as a tomographic fingerprint, whose local identifiability is established in a companion paper. The construction remains an analytic benchmark, not a universal prescription for an inner code beneath a surface code.

authors.name: Long Huang

papers.title: Helium States Inspired by Quantum Photonics Circuit
papers.summary: We present a four-mode Fock-state photonics implementation of the variational quantum deflation (VQD) algorithm to calculate the ground-state and excited-state energies for the neutral helium atom in a CAS(2,2) Subspace. Its CAS(2,2) electronic Hilbert space is encoded into a bosonic Fock-space representation and subsequently optimized using a continuous-variable quantum circuit. The circuit architecture under study is constructed of single-mode phase shifts, beam splitters, and cross-Kerr interactions. The variational circuit is initialized in the Fock state $\ket{1100}$ and its performance is benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the active-space configuration-interaction (CASCI) Hamiltonian. We also extend the method to optimize from the first to three excited states of the helium atom with the aid of the variational quantum deflation $(VQD)$ method in a CAS(2,2). We then investigate the performance of this circuit architecture as a basis for implementing the VQD method.
