The competition between the skyrmion--skyrmion repulsion and an emergent quasiperiodic pinning landscape gives rise to a sequence of distinct skyrmion lattice configurations as a function of field. The resulting hierarchy of quasiperiodic pinning potentials, characterized by closely spaced quasi-degenerate minima, enables a quasi-continuous suppression of the skyrmion density as the saturation field is approached, in sharp contrast to the strongly first-order collapse of skyrmion crystals on periodic lattices. This provides a direct mechanism for controlling the topological charge and, consequently, the emergent gauge field for itinerant electrons. As a consequence, the Hall conductivity can be strongly modified with small changes in the magnetic field and driven smoothly to zero near saturation. This field-controlled tunability, rooted in the underlying multistability, identifies quasicrystalline magnets as a platform for tunable topological textures, with potential applications in magnetic memory and magnetoelectronic response.

authors.name: Leandro M. Chinellato, Flavia A. G\'omez Albarrac\'in, Cristian D. Batista, Pablo S. Cornaglia

papers.title: Field-induced first order transitions and phase coexistence in the Kitaev quantum spin liquid candidate BaCo2(AsO4)2
papers.summary: BaCo2(AsO4)2 (BCAO) is an insulating Kitaev quantum spin liquid candidate with a rich low-temperature phase diagram. Below 5 K, it exhibits double-zigzag magnetic order. Upon application of an in-plane magnetic field, the magnetic structure first transforms into an up-up-down (UUD) state near 0.12 T and then enters a fully spin-polarized ferromagnetic (FM) state near 0.5 T. In the narrow field regime close to the polarized phase, a finite residual thermal conductivity has been reported, suggesting a possible field-induced quantum spin liquid phase. Using neutron scattering, we show that the field-induced double-zigzag-to-UUD transition near 0.15 T is accompanied by the emergence of a cluster of localized UUD spin excitations that coexist with conventional spin waves. Upon further increasing field, BCAO undergoes a first-order UUD-to-FM transition with coexistence of UUD and FM phases, accompanied by a sharp response in the spin Seebeck coefficient. These results do not support a quantum spin liquid scenario near the UUD-to-FM critical field. Instead, modeling indicates that the broad excitations arise from bound spin-flip pairs, while a low-lying dispersive branch near the FM phase boundary carries the same sign of magnetization as the FM order. These excitations naturally account for the observed sign of the spin Seebeck response and are likely relevant to the thermal conductivity near the critical field.

authors.name: Tanner J. Legvold, Bin Gao, Rong-Zhu Lin, Violet Williams, Tong Chen, Dehong Yu, Chien-Lung Huang, Gage Eichman, Renjie Lui, Benedetta Flebus, Pengcheng Dai, Douglas Natelson

papers.title: Convergence to the solution of the one-dimensional Riviera model
papers.summary: The Riviera model is a random sequential deposition model for house building on a lattice, in which a house cannot be built when both nearest-neighbor sites are already occupied. In one dimension, an attempted deposition is therefore rejected whenever the target site is an isolated vacancy. Despite the apparent simplicity of this rule, no exact analytical solution of the original model is currently known. We derive an infinite hierarchy of kinetic equations governing its dynamics and introduce a systematic closure scheme that can be implemented at arbitrary finite order. Solving the resulting systems order by order, we show that the corresponding kinetics converges rapidly toward the exact behavior. At high order, the method yields an exceptionally accurate estimate of the jamming density while retaining explicit analytical expressions for the full time-dependent evolution.

authors.name: Pascal Viot

papers.title: Mechanism-Dependent Descriptors for Oxygen Capacity in Perovskite Oxides
papers.summary: Perovskite oxides can reversibly accommodate substantial changes in oxygen stoichiometry, making them attractive for clean-energy technologies including chemical looping and oxygen storage. However, predicting oxygen capacity across diverse compositions remains challenging. Here, we combine experiments and first-principles calculations to establish composition-capacity relationships using the model perovskite series LnxSr1-xCoO3. Increasing redox-inactive Sr2+ content promotes high-valence Co4+ formation, expanding the cationic redox reservoir and enhancing oxygen capacity. While oxygen-vacancy formation energy tracks this trend for light rare earths, net oxygen release counterintuitively decreases from La to Lu despite lower vacancy formation energies. We reveal that this behavior originates from an alternative charge-compensation pathway where lattice oxygen is partially oxidized to O1-like species. Heavy rare earths (Tb-Lu) preferentially stabilize these oxygen holes through distinct local bonding, with charge compensation involving both oxidized lattice oxygen and reduced cations, ultimately suppressing oxygen release. We identify the average metal-oxygen bond strength, quantified by the integrated crystal orbital Hamilton population (ICOHP), as a physically meaningful descriptor when anionic redox dominates. These findings reveal how distinct charge-compensation mechanisms determine the applicability of oxygen-capacity descriptors, establishing a mechanism-dependent framework for predicting and optimizing oxygen exchange in perovskite oxides.

authors.name: Shuiping Gong, Yi Li, Eric Isbrandt, Xiaoman Guo, Jie Su, Zhenhao Zhou, Xiaobo Liao, Jian Deng, Jiangang He, Tao Deng, Chris Wolverton, Runxia Cai, Chaochao Dun, Zhenpeng Yao

papers.title: Three-body contact for fermions. II. Non-degenerate limit
papers.summary: A fundamental quantity characterizing Fermi gases with zero-range interactions is the three-body contact $C_3$, which determines several observables including the number of nearby triplets of fermions and the three-body loss rate in cold atom experiments, as shown in a companion article. Here, we compute $C_3$ to leading order in the non-degenerate limit for the homogeneous gas with negative or infinite scattering length $a$. At $a=\infty$, using a wavefunction approach, we obtain the analytical expression of $C_3$, which has a remarkably slow $1/T^{0.22728}\ $ dependence on the temperature $T$. In the Feynman diagram technique, which we use for $a<0$, the correct three-body short-distance correlations emerge only after a non-trivial cancellation between leading order two-body and three-body correlations, and the resulting power-law scaling comes from the large-wavevector tail of the 3-body T-matrix, which we derive inspired by the analytical solution of the three-body problem at the unitary limit.

authors.name: Xavier Leyronas, F\'elix Werner

papers.title: Spin preservation in screw-symmetric molecules
papers.summary: In electronic transport through long molecules, spin is expected to be preserved only when the dwell time is much shorter than the characteristic spin-mixing timescale $\hbar/\Delta$, where $\Delta$ is the magnitude of a spin-dependent potential, such as spin-orbit coupling. We show that, in molecules featuring discrete screw symmetry, spin preservation can be enhanced far beyond this timescale owing to strong spin separation in quasi-momentum. This spin fidelity in long molecules is consistent with chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS), suggesting spin-dependent transport in long, chiral molecules with amplified spin-splitting mechanisms. We provide analytical derivation of the enhanced spin preservation and test it on tight-binding models, which confirm that the effect gradually weakens when the screw symmetry is broken or changes from discrete to continuous. Furthermore, we perform transport simulations to show that a strong magnetoresistance trace of symmetry-protected spin fidelity emerges in a spin-valve setup with two magnetic leads, which we propose as an experimentally accessible signature.

authors.name: Jonas Bloch, Fedor Baranov, Maxim Breitkreiz

papers.title: Enhanced Multifractality Induced by Non-Hermitian Disorder in Quantum Percolation
papers.summary: We study the two-dimensional quantum site-percolation model with reciprocal hopping and random imaginary on-site potentials, which describe spatially uncorrelated gain and loss. The localization properties of the eigenstates are characterized through the complex spacing ratio, the participation entropy, and the generalized fractal dimensions $D_q$. Finite-size scaling yields an effective quantum percolation threshold $p_q$ that increases monotonically with $\gamma$, with a shift larger than that produced by a real on-site potential of equal strength. We show that the onset of extended behavior drifts toward larger occupation probabilities as the system size increases. The localization--delocalization change is therefore a crossover, consistent with the absence of a sharp transition for reciprocal non-Hermitian disorder in two dimensions. Accordingly, the interval between the classical threshold $p_c$ and $p_q$ constitutes an extended multifractal crossover regime and its width at accessible sizes grows with $\gamma$. Although all states are expected to localize in the thermodynamic limit, above $p_q$ the localization length exceeds the largest system size simulated, which is already larger than current photonic samples. The size-dependent threshold and the multifractal regime, which widens with the loss strength and can therefore be reached without fine-tuning, are thus directly accessible in photonic waveguide lattices.

authors.name: W. S. Oliveira, Julian Faundez, Rodrigo Arouca, Welles Morgado

papers.title: Hidden Rotational Dynamics from Crystal Geometry
papers.summary: From hidden spin order to electronic loop currents and frustrated fluctuations, unconventional quantum matter reveals the rich patterns that electronic and magnetic degrees of freedom form across space and time. Recent advances in chiral phononics have extended this perspective to lattice vibrations, raising the question of whether the lattice itself can generate spatially organized rotational correlations. Here we show that crystal geometry provides an autonomous mechanism for generating equilibrium angular-momentum circulation and staggered antisymmetric displacement interactions, independently of coupling to electronic or magnetic order. Our framework applies broadly to crystalline systems hosting locally symmetry-lowered environments embedded within a higher-symmetry global structure. We identify how directional elastic forces organize displacement correlations and how eliminating internal coordinates generates staggered antisymmetric interactions-a phononic analogue of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya exchange-even in globally centrosymmetric crystals. By separating intersite angular-momentum transfer from crystalline restoring torques, we show that both elastic anisotropy and the induced antisymmetric interactions together drive oppositely circulating angular-momentum currents on neighboring plaquettes, despite vanishing mean angular momentum at every site. Sustained by quantum and thermal fluctuations, this circulation preserves time-reversal and inversion symmetry and requires neither external driving nor spontaneous symmetry breaking. Our results establish lattice geometry as a microscopic source of spatially organized angular-momentum dynamics.

authors.name: Rule Yi, Vincent P. Flynn, Benedetta Flebus

papers.title: Interplay of Activity and Attraction in the Coil-to-Globule Transition of Tangentially Driven Polymers
papers.summary: The coil-to-globule transition is a paradigmatic phenomenon in polymer physics and biophysics, driven by intrachain attractions. However, in biopolymers, attractive interactions coexist with nonequilibrium active processes, leaving open the question of how activity modifies the transition. Using Brownian dynamics simulations of tangentially driven polymers, we show that activity broadens the coil-to-globule crossover without shifting the $\Theta$ point by generating transient pearl-necklace conformations, which delay globule formation. Activity-induced chain backfolding defines an emergent active blob of $g_a$ monomers that together with a thermal blob of $g_T$ monomers govern the transition. From scaling arguments, we identify a new scaling variable based on the ratio $g_a/g_T$ that collapses the gyration-radius expansion factors near the $\Theta$ point onto the master curve of passive polymers across a broad activity range. Our results establish a blob-scaling framework for active polymer collapse.

authors.name: Baptiste Parage, Sara Jabbari-Farouji

papers.title: Artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice: a tricritical bridge from square to kagome
papers.summary: Artificial spin ices (ASIs) are arrays of interacting nanomagnets in which phase transitions can be imaged and controlled. Studies of the thermodynamic have focused mainly on the square and kagome lattices, and on their variants. Here we study artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice, formed of squares and octagons. At fixed lattice constant, the ratio $r$ of the square and octagon link lengths tunes the interactions strongly while changing the geometry only slightly. Magnetic force microscopy and Monte Carlo simulations show a continuous bridge from square-ice-like to kagome-like behavior. At small $r$ the system has a single ordering transition, whereas at large $r$ it passes from a correlated paramagnet to charge order and then long-range order. The two regimes meet in a multicritical region, accurately modeled by a Blume-Capel model of the octagon toroidal moments. From this picture, we design a comparative magnetometry protocol that unambiguously separates interaction effects from single-nanomagnet effects in thermally active samples. Finally, the charge-ordered region maps onto a tunable dimer model, with a Coulomb phase and pinch points along the line between two ordered dimer phases. The CaVO ASI thus provides access to a rich phase diagram only through geometric tuning, without requiring extreme experimental conditions.

authors.name: F. Museur, G. M. Macauley, S. Nilsson, V. Scagnoli, P. M. Derlet, L. J. Heyderman

papers.title: Ni ordering in the van der Waals gap of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$: from disorder through $2\times2$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order to stripe order
papers.summary: We report a synchrotron x-ray diffraction study of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$ over the range $0.18 \le x \le 0.57$, with Ni contents measured by energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy. Powder diffraction on the whole series shows that the NbS$_2$ host is preserved, while the Ni ions in the van der Waals gap evolve from a disordered arrangement to $2\times2$ order at $x=1/4$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order at $x=1/3$, through a range where both motifs coexist, to an orthorhombic stripe-type order at $x=0.57$. The in-plane lattice parameter increases with Ni content, whereas the interlayer spacing remains nearly constant except for a pronounced minimum at $x=1/4$, which density-functional calculations reproduce for the ordered structure. Single-crystal diffraction on the two commensurate phases shows that the $x=1/4$ structure, with Ni on a single site and a trimerized Nb lattice, is free of stacking faults, whereas the chiral $x=1/3$ structure contains Ni on the nominally empty site, inversion twins and stacking faults of the Ni layers. The comparison between powders and crystals shows that grinding mainly degrades the stacking of the Ni layers. These results establish the structural phase diagram of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ and the intercalant disorder to be taken into account in the interpretation of its magnetic properties.

authors.name: Naveen Singh Dhami, Ricardo Guillermo Torres Ramirez, Gaurav Pransu, Ivo Batisti\'c, Pierre Fertey, Erik Elkaim, El-Eulmi Bendeif, Bruno Gudac, Nikolina Peni\'c, Naveen Kumar Chogondahalli Muniraju, Neven Bari\v{s}i\'c, Petar Pop\v{c}evi\'c, Victor Bal\'edent

papers.title: Frustrated Interlayer Coupling Creates a Higher-Order Helical Superstructure in a Twist-Bend Smectic Phase
papers.summary: Bent liquid-crystalline dimers provide a model system for studying the spontaneous emergence of chirality from achiral molecules. Depending on terminal-chain length, these materials exhibit a competition between heliconical, synclinic, and anticlinic packing tendencies in tilted smectic phases. In short homologues, the tendency to form twist-bend phases dominates, leading to two distinct helical phases: the SmCTB-SH phase, with a helical periodicity of four molecular lengths, and at lower temperatures, a double helical structure - the SmCTB-DH phase, with progressive rotation of the four-layer unit. With increasing terminal chain length, this twist-bend tendency is gradually suppressed, favoring phases with simple synclinic and anticlinic tilt arrangement in successive layers. Remarkably, in the regime where these tendencies become comparable, a new modulated smectic phase, SmCTB-mod develops; a double helical structure in which the internal four-layer unit undergoes a periodic modulation. This additional level of structural organization provides a means of accommodating competing heliconical and synclinic/anticlinic tendencies and produces a characteristic splitting of the resonant x-ray diffraction peaks into four signals symmetrically located around a signal of four-layer periodicity. These results reveal how bent dimers resolve local-packing-mode frustration through complex spontaneous hierarchical structural organization.

authors.name: Abigail Pearson, Damian Pociecha, Magdalena M. Majewska, Nata\v{s}a Vaupoti\v{c}, Rebecca Walker, Ewa Gorecka

papers.title: Giant Raman Optical Activity in Chiral and Polar Ni$_3$TeO$_6$
papers.summary: Raman optical activity (ROA) measures the difference in Raman scattering intensity for right- and left-circularly polarized light and reflects the chirality of excitations. In solids, ROA is commonly very weak. For the phonons of chiral and polar Ni$_3$TeO$_6$, we find a giant ROA with magnitude 100 times higher than commonly reported for molecules. The systematic analysis based on phonon selection rules allows the chiral and achiral scattering channels to be separated. First-principles calculations of the Raman tensor at finite phonon momentum relate the effect to the phonon modulation of the band-geometric and band-dispersion contributions to optical gyrotropy. This establishes Raman optical activity as a probe of electron--phonon modulation of the band geometry in an insulator.

authors.name: Philipp Stein, Ravi Kaushik, Evgenia V. Komleva, Thomas C. Koethe, Vladimir Tsurkan, Istv\'an K\'ezsm\'arki, Markus Gr\"uninger, Sergey V. Streltsov, Sergey Artyukhin, Paul H. M. van Loosdrecht

papers.title: Interface-Selective Extreme Ultraviolet Second Harmonic Generation Away from Linear Absorption Edges
papers.summary: Extreme ultraviolet (XUV) second harmonic generation (SHG) combines interface selectivity with core-level element specificity but has so far been limited to linear absorption edges. Here, we measure XUVSHG from an indium tin oxide capped MoO$_3$/SiO$_2$/Si photovoltaic heterojunction for fundamental energies of 60--76\,eV, below the Si L$_{2,3}$-edge. Where linear absorption is a featureless valence background, we observe a strong, structured XUVSHG response with maxima near 70 and 76\,eV. Layer-resolved first-principles calculations reproduce both maxima and assign them to the Si/SiO$_2$ interface, the 76\,eV peak to the bridging Si monolayer and the 70\,eV peak to the near-interface substrate. Bethe--Salpeter calculations for bulk Si connect the signal to Si 2$p$ excitons at 140--160\,eV. At the Si L$_{2,3}$-edge, the calculated response is instead governed by MoO$_3$-induced asymmetry at the oxide interface. These findings establish off-edge XUV SHG as a powerful approach for selectively probing distinct buried interfaces within complex material heterostructures.

authors.name: Bailey R. Nebgen, Shane W. Devlin, Franky Bernal, Aga Ridhova, James Bullock, Daniel R. Schacher, Jake D. Koralek, Yuya Kubota, Gota Yamaguchi, Shigeki Owada, Toshihide Sumi, XingYu Su, Iwao Matsuda, Keith V. Lawler, Walter S. Drisdell, Michael W. Zuerch, Craig P. Schwartz

papers.title: Dynamical theory of the East model. I. A review on the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism
papers.summary: The East model is a paradigmatic kinetically constrained spin model in one dimension that exhibits glassy dynamics. This review surveys the progress on the theoretical description of the dynamics of the East model, focusing on the spin time correlation function and the relaxation time. We summarize rigorous results on the super-Arrhenius scaling of the relaxation time in the low-temperature limit. We then present a unified derivation of the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism for both the fluctuation and domain bases. Within this formalism, an infinite hierarchy of coupled equations for the time correlation function and memory kernels emerges---a structure reminiscent of generalized mode-coupling theory developed for supercooled liquids. We review the analytical approximations obtained by truncating or closing the hierarchy at first or second orders and compare them against Monte Carlo simulations. Although these approaches perform reasonably at moderate temperatures, they universally fail in the low-temperature regime: mode-coupling closure schemes in the fluctuation basis introduce spurious ergodicity-breaking transitions, while truncations in the domain basis discard slower modes and fail to capture the asymptotic divergence of the relaxation time. The loss of analytical tractability beyond second order remains the central obstacle, underscoring the fundamental difficulty of describing hierarchical relaxation even in this ``simplest'' model of glassy dynamics.

authors.name: Chong Zha, Yuliang Jin

papers.title: Antiferromagnetic Long-Range Order in a Lattice Fermion Model
papers.summary: We study a lattice fermion model with antiferromagnetic interactions on the three-dimensional cubic lattice. The hopping term of the Hamiltonian has a Weyl-type dispersion. We prove that the model has reflection positivity. Moreover, by relying on the property, we prove the existence of the antiferromagnetic long-range order at low temperatures in a strong coupling regime.

authors.name: Yukimi Goto, Tohru Koma

papers.title: Cluster Expansion and Decay of Correlations for Multidimensional Long-Range Ising Models
papers.summary: We develop the cluster expansion for the multidimensional multiscaled contours defined by three of us. These contours are suitable for long-range Ising models with interaction $J_{xy}=J(|x-y|)= J/|x-y|^\alpha$, $J>0$, and $\alpha>d$. As an application of the convergence of the cluster expansion at low temperatures, we study the decay of the truncated two-point correlation functions, showing that the decay is algebraic with coefficient $\alpha$.

authors.name: Lucas Affonso, Rodrigo Bissacot, Jo\~ao Maia, Jo\~ao F. Rodrigues, Kelvyn Welsch

papers.title: Critical phenomena in 2D Coulomb gas: Birth of a gap
papers.summary: We investigate a family of radially symmetric Coulomb gas systems at inverse temperature $\beta = 2$. The family is characterised by the property that the density of the equilibrium measure vanishes on a ring at radius $r_*$, which lies strictly inside the droplet. The large-$n$ expansion of the logarithm of the partition function is obtained up to the constant term and features a novel term of order $n^{1/4}$. We perform a double scaling limit of the correlation kernel at the $n^{1/4}$ scale and obtain a new limiting kernel in the bulk, which differs from the well-known Ginibre kernel.

authors.name: Matthias Allard, Sampad Lahiry

papers.title: Generalized Boltzmann-Gibbs Distributions and the Electronic Partition Function Paradox
papers.summary: The maximization of the nonadditive entropic functional $S_{q}(p)=k\sum_{i}p_{i}\ln_{q}(1/p_{i})$, $q\in(0,1)$, under a linear mean-energy constraint, i.e., the best-behaved case from Dognini and Tsallis (2026), is used to derive generalizations of the Boltzmann-Gibbs distribution for physical systems whose description requires a limiting process over the energy spectrum: the hydrogen atom in free space; an energy spectrum that uniformly approaches a continuous, unbounded limit with a common degeneracy; the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution of velocities; the harmonic oscillator; and the one-dimensional box. For the hydrogen atom with mean energy $U\in[0,e_{ion}]$, the limiting optimal distribution is a two-tier one, concentrated on the ground level and on the ionization threshold, with weights $1-U/e_{ion}$ and $U/e_{ion}$ for every $q\in(0,1)$, and the temperature rescaled by $\ln_{q}W$ is finite and given by $T_{q,s}=T_{ion}(U/e_{ion})^{1-q}$, with $T_{ion}=e_{ion}/kq$. This circumvents the Electronic Partition Function Paradox and yields a family of well-defined thermodynamic behaviors.

authors.name: Leandro Lyra Braga Dognini

papers.title: Super-Arrhenius relaxation of the triangular plaquette model in any dimension
papers.summary: Consider the following plaquette model from statistical physics: a lamp lies at every vertex of the triangular lattice and a switch lies at every even vertex of the (bipartite) dual hexagonal lattice. Each switch toggles the three lamps on its face. The energy of a configuration is the number of ON lamps. For the Glauber dynamics associated with the Gibbs measure defined by this Hamiltonian at any inverse temperature $\beta>0$, we show that, in any dimension $d\ge 2$, the infinite volume relaxation time satisfies \[e^{\beta^2/C}/C \le T_{\mathrm{rel}}\le Ce^{e^{C\beta}}\] for some $C>0$. Our result entails that the Gibbs measure is unique. The $e^{\beta^2}$ scaling was conjectured by Garrahan and Newman in 2000 and matches the behaviour of supercritical rooted kinetically constrained models such as the East model, thus recovering fragile glass phenomenology in the absence of kinetic constraints. More precisely, we show that, on a torus of side length $2^k$, when $\beta\to\infty$ and $k/\beta\to0$, we have $T_{\mathrm{rel}}=e^{2\beta k(1+o(1))}$, confirming a prediction of Newman and Moore. Quite surprisingly, however, we also prove that, on non-periodic finite domains of size $n\le e^{\beta/C}$ for large $C>0$, we have the much larger asymptotics $\ln T_{\mathrm{rel}}=\beta n^{\Theta(1)}$. The main ingredients of the proofs are new results in extremal and enumerative combinatorics and rely on renormalisation ideas for the dynamics and its groundstates also known as the Ledrappier subshift. Our combinatorial results also have consequences in geometric group theory (more precisely to the complexity of the word problem for the Baumslag finitely presented group), ergodic theory and linear coding theory.

authors.name: Laurent Bartholdi, Ivailo Hartarsky, Ivan Mitrofanov

papers.title: The Impact of Scenario Representation in Scenario-based Optimization Certification
papers.summary: Scenario-based optimization provides finite-sample guarantees for decisions constructed from sampled uncertainty, but its certification procedures can be sensitive to how those samples are represented. We investigate this sensitivity under lossless scenario regrouping, which preserves the sampled information, feasible region, optimizer, and primitive violation probability. For an equal-allocation support-subsample certificate, we derive the distortion factor \(k^2(1-\epsilon)^{k-1}\), establish certification reversals between equivalent representations, and provide sufficient conditions for acceptance dominance under nested coarsening. We further apply nondegeneracy-free Wait-and-Judge theory to coordinatewise scenario envelopes, enabling stronger certification directly from the primitive observations. In paired scenario-MPC experiments, exact regrouping increases certification availability from 318 to 471 of 480 attempts without changing the samples, numerical proposals, or requiring any reduction in witness cardinality. Primitive Wait-and-Judge certification accepts the same 471 attempts without regrouping. These results demonstrate that apparent scenario sample-efficiency gains can arise from certificate accounting rather than additional information or reduced decision risk.

authors.name: Stephen Crawford, Nora Ayanian

papers.title: Mechanism Design and Active Systems Theory: 60 Years of Parallel Development
papers.summary: The survey compares two research traditions within the mathematical theory of designing the rules of interaction (mechanisms) for purposeful participants: mechanism design, together with contract theory and implementation theory, and the theory of active systems created by V.N. Burkov and developed into the theory of control in organizations (TCO) by D.A. Novikov's school; the main results of Yu.B. Germeier's school and of the domestic schools adjacent to active systems theory (AST) are covered as well. The problem statements and principal results of 2006-2026 are presented: for mechanism design (MD) - robust and dynamic mechanism design, multidimensional screening, information design, simplicity of mechanisms and credibility of the designer, market design, algorithmic and learning-based design, mechanisms for AI agents, and robust, relational, dynamic and algorithmic contracts; for AST and TCO - a general typology of control, strategy-proof and incentive-compatible planning mechanisms, decomposition of the agents' game, systems with distributed control and coalitional interaction, reflexive games and informational control, control of staff and structure, dynamic active systems, and project management. A correspondence between the classical results is established (the fair play principle and the revelation principle, the serial resource allocation mechanism and the uniform rule, active expertise mechanisms and generalized median schemes, quasi-compensatory incentive schemes and contracts under observable actions), and priorities are delineated by uniform rules; the areas where the two traditions diverge are identified, as are the dimensions of the problem (staff, structure, institutions, awareness, agents' beliefs) covered only by TCO.

authors.name: Dmitry A. Novikov

papers.title: Tie-Line Scheduling Using Real-Time Contraction Metrics: Hierarchical Reachable Sets for Multi-Area Inverter-Dominated Grids
papers.summary: Managing transmission congestion in multi-area power grids dominated by inverter-based resources (IBRs) requires bridging a severe timescale and modeling divide. Supervisory congestion optimizers -- such as Online Feedback Optimization (OFO) and two-tiered differentiable Model Predictive Control (MPC) -- rely on linearized, convex algebraic grid approximations that cannot guarantee dynamic stability during sub-second converter transients. Conversely, fast distributed consensus schemes like Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) depend on convex plant assumptions and iterative message exchanges that lag behind rapid tie-line surges. This paper replaces convex ADMM emergency consensus with a Distributed Nonlinear Separable Control Contraction Metric (SCCM) architecture spanning three nested tiers: the Device layer, the Area layer, and the Grid tie-line layer. By pairing online Prediction Error Method and Moving Horizon Estimation (PEM-MHE) parameter tracking with offline convex Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) synthesis, the controller executes a closed-form nonlinear feedback law online without solving real-time optimization problems. We derive the Pontryagin attainable (reachable) ellipsoids for each layer, prove hierarchical tube containment via Schur-complement matrix inequalities, and project the certified Grid reachable tube through Power Transfer Distribution Factors (PTDFs) to supply guaranteed safe thermal limits to the supervisory coordinator. Validation on modified IEEE 39-bus (100% IBR, zero synchronous generators) and 3-area IEEE 118-bus systems demonstrates an 82.8% reduction in cumulative tie-line thermal overload while maintaining strict exponential contraction ($\lambda_{\max} \le -2.43$) even under a 3 s communication blackout.

authors.name: Richard Sherman

papers.title: Who Gets the Grid Capacity? Allocating Dynamic Access Among Multiple Virtual Power Plants
papers.summary: Virtual power plants (VPPs) trade in the same wholesale market and share distribution lines and transformers, and uncoordinated, profit-maximizing VPPs can push a shared transformer past its thermal limit or drive a feeder voltage out of band. The utility, which only observes the front-of-the-meter net injection at each bus, must keep the network safe from that net injection alone. We allocate a 24-hour active and reactive operating envelope to each VPP by a Benders decomposition: the utility sets a trial envelope, each VPP solves its private convex portfolio problem, and the returned value and dual gradient become supporting cuts that rebuild its value function while its schedule, state, and cost stay private. The envelope carries the transformer's thermal state across hours, bounds a joint conditional value-at-risk over forecast uncertainty, and is re-optimized each hour with the current hour committed. On a reduced IEEE-13 feeder with real load and prices, an active-power-only implementation lowers the transformer's peak-temperature CVaR from 254 to 97\,$^\circ$C at a 28\% value give-up and holds the transformer below its limit where nameplate access breaches it.

authors.name: Nakul Sreekanth, Jun He, Andrew L. Liu, S. Sivaranjani

papers.title: Emerging Vertical Power Delivery in AI Data Centers: Challenges and Solutions
papers.summary: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads is increasing power demand in AI data centers, and processor current is projected to reach 2000 A and beyond. This trend is exposing the limitations of lateral power delivery (LPD) to processors and has motivated growing interest in vertical power delivery (VPD). This paper reviews the power delivery network (PDN) of AI data centers and the upcoming transition from LPD to VPD. First, the 800 VDC power delivery architecture, the impedance behavior of the PDN, and the limitations of LPD are discussed. Then, VPD implementation approaches, reported converter designs, and packaging technologies are examined, together with integrated voltage regulators (IVRs) and embedded passive components. In addition, power integrity simulations are presented to compare regulator and plane positions, from which a set of PDN design guidelines is derived. The results show that moving a voltage regulator module (VRM) from 50 mm away to directly below the die reduces the loop inductance by nearly half. In a complete PDN, this relocation lowers the low-frequency anti-resonant peak, whereas the mid- and high-frequency impedance depends on the decoupling stages and the position of the power and ground planes. This paper also shows that achieving practical VPD remains closely tied to challenges such as regulator height, passive-component embedding, and thermal management.

authors.name: Charles Isaac Zahner, Amirhossein Habibi, Mehdi Ferdowsi

papers.title: First-Order Model-Free Policy Gradient for Undiscounted LQR with Global Optimality and Convergence Guarantees
papers.summary: We provide a first-order model-free policy gradient (PG) framework for learning undiscounted infinite-horizon linear quadratic regulator (LQR) policies with global optimality and convergence guarantees. We first construct a stochastic wrapper policy class parameterized by the LQR gain to enable exploration around a deterministic linear control law. We analyze the additional cost induced by exploration over infinite-horizon, and establish a weak gradient dominance condition that characterizes global optimality under exploration. We then construct a model-free first-order PG algorithm using sampled trajectory information, without identifying the dynamics or approximating a value function. Finally, we establish finite-time convergence guarantees, providing the sufficient number of samples required for near-global optimality with our proposed PG algorithms.

authors.name: Vipul K Sharma, S Sivaranjani

papers.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Hard Constraints: Policy Gradient Methods with Intersample Guarantees
papers.summary: We develop a policy-gradient (PG) reinforcement learning (RL) framework with hard inter-sample control barrier function (CBF)-based safety constraints for nonlinear sampled-data systems. We first design a class of stochastic policies with support truncated to sampling-period-dependent safe control sets, that guarantee safety-by-construction at sampling instants. We then propose a model-free PG algorithm that searches over the class of safe-by-design policies and establish sufficient conditions on sampling-period such that any action sampled from safe control sets remains safe throughout the sampling interval, providing inter-sample guarantees. We further establish finite-time convergence and sample complexity guarantees for the proposed PG algorithm and characterize its global optimality under gradient dominance. Finally, we illustrate inter-sample safety guarantees on a safe quadrotor navigation environment.

authors.name: Vipul K. Sharma, S. Sivaranjani

papers.title: PS-HalluBench: Taxonomy-Driven Benchmarking of LLM Hallucinations in Power Systems
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for power-system applications, yet their reliability in engineering analysis remains uncertain. We introduce PS-HalluBench, a manually constructed benchmark of 200 questions that evaluates hallucination-related failures across five power-system task categories: numerical reasoning, network topology, constraint verification, false-premise acceptance, and abstention. We evaluate ten LLMs over the benchmark, yielding 39.35\% overall correctness, with constraint verification achieving only 21.75\%, and highlighting persistent difficulties in engineering reasoning. We further investigate engineering-grounded reasoning through numerical solver support and verified network information both of which show significant performance improvement. The findings reveal important limitations of standalone LLM reasoning and motivate integrating LLMs with verified engineering tools for reliable power-system analysis.

authors.name: S. M. Monzurul Hoque Chowdhury, Nabila Tasfiha Rahman, Qinghua Li

papers.title: An Explainable Agentic AI Framework for Distribution System Load Restoration
papers.summary: Distribution system load restoration is a sequential decision-making problem in which restoration actions must maximize served load, prioritize critical loads, and preserve power-flow feasibility. This paper proposes an explainable agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework for distribution system load restoration. The proposed framework uses multiple large language model (LLM) agents for planner guidance, strategic plan generation, decision arbitration, memory-based feedback, and explanation generation. Unlike unconstrained LLM-based control, the proposed method restricts agent decisions to feasible restoration actions and evaluates all candidate plans using deterministic AC power-flow feasibility checks. The framework is evaluated on IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus distribution feeders, as well as a larger IEEE 118-bus test case, and compared against reinforcement learning and planning baselines. The results show that the proposed agentic framework achieves better restoration performance while producing structured explanations for operator-facing decision support. A direct comparison with a Single-LLM-Agent baseline further shows that the proposed multi-agent decomposition improves weighted restored load and critical-load recovery compared with a monolithic LLM decision structure.

authors.name: S. M. Monzurul Hoque Chowdhury, Qinghua Li

papers.title: Grid-Aware Assessment of Forced Oscillations from Spatially Distributed Large Loads
papers.summary: This paper develops a unified analytical framework for assessing forced oscillations induced by spatially distributed large-load fluctuations to determine their grid-aware fluctuation magnitudes. Emerging computational loads, such as hyperscale datacenters, present cyclic power variations with dynamic impacts depending on the waveform characteristics, forcing frequency, and source location. Our grid-aware framework represents these fluctuations using deterministic harmonic and probabilistic spectral models, and analyzes the resulting bus-wise frequency deviations based on a generic grid frequency-response model. Deterministic, risk-aware, and band-based probabilistic severity measures are further developed to obtain admissible fluctuation limits under different assumptions on frequency and phase uncertainty. We also formulate a security-constrained (SC) optimization of locational fluctuation magnitudes among existing large loads, accounting for their aggregated frequency deviation level. Case studies on the IEEE 39-bus and 14-generator Australian systems validate the proposed severity measures and admissible limit analysis. The SC optimization results further show that distributing a given amount of aggregate fluctuation toward dynamically less sensitive locations can substantially reduce system-wide oscillation severity.

authors.name: Min-Seung Ko, Hao Zhu

papers.title: Facet-offset Polytope Expansion for Dynamic Operating Envelopes of Aggregated Distribution Grid Resources
papers.summary: This paper presented a facet-offset polytope expansion framework with sensitivity-informed directions (FOPE-sen) for constructing DOEs in three-phase unbalanced distribution systems. The facet directions are selected from DGR coordinate directions and sensitivity-informed network-critical directions, while the facet locations are determined through a two-step bisection procedure guided by a power-flow feasibility oracle. Numerical results demonstrate that FOPE-sen captures at least 106% more flexibility per dimension than box-shaped and random-direction expansion methods. Moreover, FOPE-sen constructs DOEs comparable to or larger than those of VBPE while using fewer than 1/40 as many facets in dimensions greater than four. Future work will focus on stronger safety verification for nonconvex AC feasible regions, scalability in high-dimensional spaces, and extensions to multi-aggregator allocation and market-participation applications.

authors.name: Feng Chen, Kumarsinh Jhala, Kiran Kumar Challa, Zongjie Wang

papers.title: Stability-Constrained Imitation Learning for Performance-Guaranteed Neural Feedback Frequency Control in Microgrids
papers.summary: Guaranteeing performance for frequency control is challenging within traditional control paradigms, as it demands precise disturbance estimation and real-time control signal computation within a timeframe of seconds. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing a stability-certified imitation learning framework for frequency regulation in low-inertia microgrids. Based on the frequency response model of the microgrid, an offline numerical optimal control is employed to generate near-optimal pairs of state and control dataset, which are subsequently used to train a deep neural network (DNN) feedback controller. To ensure the closed-loop stability, the DNN controller is trained with a set of Lyapunov-based stability constraints derived using absolute stability theory. Such an imitation learning paradigm can significantly improve the training efficiency, while the resulting DNN controller acts as an end-to-end function that simultaneously handles disturbance estimation and control optimization. The proposed framework is validated on a modified IEEE 33-node diesel-wind microgrid. The DNN controllers are deployed in wind turbine generators (WTGs) to provide decentralized, intelligent supplementary active power support to always maintain frequency deviations within predefined safety bounds under different disturbances while preserving closed-loop stability.

authors.name: Sajid Kamal, Yichen Zhang, Feng Qiu, Tianqiao Zhao

papers.title: AI Agents Executing an RMS and EMT Ride-Through Workflow on a 2,000-Bus Synthetic Texas Grid: A Case Study with Open-Source Tools
papers.summary: This paper reports a case study of engineer-supervised AI agents executing a predefined RMS and EMT ride-through workflow on the 2,000-bus ACTIVSg2000 synthetic Texas grid with open-source tools. The test case is a 133 MW battery with a co-located 130 MW data-center load, assessed against ride-through criteria fixed before simulation and for loss of synchronism elsewhere in the grid. One agent ran 44 RMS cases and 15 without-project comparisons in ANDES; the other ran a 220-row EMT intake bench and an 84-row system study in DPsim and ParaEMT on a Kron-reduced area. Across the 44 RMS cases, 127 criterion cells fail, including loss of synchronism in all 44. Two findings concern the project plant. The battery keeps absorbing reactive power during sags on the light-load schedule (B3, as low as -19.8 Mvar on S4 T1), and the data-center load returns only at 5.00-5.56 s after long bolted faults (L3), which misses the ERCOT load-return requirement. In 13 of the 15 comparisons, which the authors selected after slips or speed-gate stops, the same machines slip without the project; the other 29 runs have no without-project comparison. RMS and EMT values differ in network, plant model, controls, operating point, and base, and so they are reported as separate, unaligned observations. The paper reports the errors the authors identified in the agent logs, 63 author messages, and 3.8 days from agent start to the integrated study report. The agents executed and documented the predefined ride-through and stability workflow, which covers one part of an interconnection study.

authors.name: Tam Kemabonta, Brighton Ombuki, Vladimir Abdelnour

papers.title: Benchmarking a Grid Foundation Model for AC Optimal Power Flow: Feasibility and Warm-Start Results on Synthetic Texas and South Carolina Grids
papers.summary: Learning-based surrogates for alternating-current optimal power flow (AC-OPF) are often judged by the gap between their objective value and that of a nonlinear solver, which does not show that a prediction satisfies power balance and network limits. This paper tests whether predictions from the pretrained foundation model GridSFM-Open 1.1.0, recently released by Microsoft, are feasible AC-OPF operating points and whether they are useful initial values for a nonlinear solver. The model was evaluated zero-shot and after fine-tuning on 10, 100, and 1,000 labeled scenarios (FT10, FT100, and FT1000) on 500 scenarios for each of two synthetic grids, ACTIVSg2000 (Texas) and ACTIVSg500 (South Carolina), with Ipopt, MATPOWER MIPS, and pandapower PIPS as solver references. The lowest Texas median cost gap, 0.44\% for FT100, coincided with thermal violations in 24.1\% of cases and a median maximum bus power mismatch of 89 MW and 197 Mvar. Texas zero-shot predictions had a median maximum mismatch of 648 MW and 1,641 Mvar, and every South Carolina case violated a thermal limit for every model variant. Seeding Ipopt with FT1000 predictions gave geometric-mean solve-time speedups of 1.55x on South Carolina and 1.12x on Texas (p = 0.06, not significant at the 5\% level), while zero-shot seeds slowed South Carolina solves (0.26x). A small objective gap therefore did not indicate feasibility: although median zero-shot inference took only 1.32 s on Texas and 0.157 s on South Carolina on a shared host, every prediction still required a nonlinear solver, and fine-tuned predictions gave modest, grid-dependent warm-start speedups while zero-shot predictions slowed convergence on one grid. GridSFM may therefore be useful for initializing a nonlinear solver, but obtaining feasible AC-OPF solutions still required the solver.

authors.name: Tam Kemabonta, Brighton Ombuki, Vladimir Abdelnour

papers.title: Device-Centric Cooperative Floor-Level Estimation under Sparse Anchor Deployment for Construction-Site Applications
papers.summary: For construction-site applications in multi-story buildings, accurate floor-level estimation is important for tracking workers, equipment, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices. In buildings under construction, communication infrastructure and power-supply facilities are often limited and the indoor environment changes as construction progresses, making localization systems that rely on dense wireless infrastructure or fingerprint databases difficult to deploy and maintain. Low-power wide-area (LPWA) communication can provide wide-area coverage with a small number of temporarily deployed access points (APs), but under sparse AP deployment, AP-to-terminal observations alone may provide insufficient floor-related information for reliable floor-level estimation. To address this problem, this paper develops a device-centric cooperative floor-level estimation method that exploits inter-terminal observations as relative floor-difference information to complement AP-side information. For practical application with limited measurement data, AP-to-terminal observations are represented by an upper/lower-AP RSS contrast, while inter-terminal observations are statistically modeled according to floor-difference classes. The resulting AP-side and pairwise scores are combined in a weighted floor-label objective and approximately optimized using dual-order sequential iterated conditional modes (ICM). Ray-tracing simulations and LoRa measurement experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method under different AP deployments and terminal-selection limits.

authors.name: Jiaxu Liang, Zhuoran Li, Osamu Muta, Haruto Morokuma, Naohiro Ikeda, Takamasa Kitanouma

papers.title: Grid-Responsive Pricing of Dynamic Wireless Charging with Coupled Residential Demand
papers.summary: Dynamic wireless charging (DWC) is an emerging technology that enables electric vehicles (EVs) to recharge while traveling. Its unique operational model creates two revenue streams for DWC operators through lane access tolls and electricity sales. However, these prices influence not only traffic flow and roadway energy delivery but also how much EV charging moves to homes instead, potentially within the same distribution network. Neglecting this coupling can underestimate grid loading and compromise pricing decisions. We develop a coupled traffic, EV energy, driver-response, and AC distribution network model with a model predictive control (MPC) framework that jointly optimizes DWC tolls and charging prices while explicitly accounting for displaced residential charging and network losses. Using 78 days of I-210 West traffic data, we show that conventional MPC exceeds feeder loading limits on 52 days, whereas the proposed residential load aware controller eliminates these violations with only 0.6% lower operator revenue. Under a more constrained feeder configuration, it eliminates 50 overloaded days with a 0.9% revenue reduction. Sensitivity analyses highlight the importance of accurate residential demand estimation and feeder loss modeling, while peak-aware pricing further reduces daily peak loading by 3.7% relative to the base load. These results demonstrate the value of coordinated pricing that captures the interaction between roadway and residential charging.

authors.name: Zhiheng Wang, Dipanjan Ghose, S. Sivaranjani, Junjie Qin, Qin Lv

papers.title: Safely Mitigating Grid Imbalance: A Hybrid Distributional Wide-Margin Recourse Approach
papers.summary: This paper proposes the Multi-Agent Distributional Wide-Margin Policy Gradient (MADWMPG) framework: a dual-policy hybrid imitation and safe reinforcement learning (IL-SRL) method designed for safely mitigating grid imbalance in multiphase active distribution networks with distributed soft open points (SOPs). The framework comprises a wide-margin constraint barrier recourse (WCBR) module that seeks the maximal separation of constraint-compliant and unsafe actions and learns to proactively suppress exploratory violations. The framework addresses operational volatility using a novel adaptation of noncrossing quantile regression (NQR) distributional critics that track the complete distribution of policy returns. The set of behavior and recourse policies integrates an instantaneous physics-based and differentiable action projection mechanism that generates SOP constraint-compliant actions without relying on active learning. Policy safety is made responsive using an enhancement of conventional experience replay, and the safety performance of the framework is supported by probabilistic bounds derived in the paper. The proposed framework was trained and tested on a modified multiphase IEEE 123-bus test feeder. Results demonstrate its superiority to conventional reinforcement learning and SRL methods and show that it is highly competitive against the nonlinear AC optimal power flow.

authors.name: Shoaib Hussain, Mostafa Farrokhabadi, Hamidreza Zareipour

papers.title: Optimal Energy and LLM Task Scheduling for Multiple Cloud Data Centers
papers.summary: This paper studies coordinated Large Language Model (LLM) training-task scheduling and facility operation for geographically distributed cloud data centers (CDCs). The central question is how two scheduling flexibilities - cross-CDC task transfer and task reordering - affect service and economic outcomes when remote execution remains subject to compute, bandwidth, energy, and zone-temperature constraints. We formulate a mixed-integer optimization model that jointly determines task outcomes, heterogeneous-node assignment, execution timing, pre-execution data transfer, node activation, and facility operation. A deterministic 24-hour case study contains 3 CDCs, 15 heterogeneous graphics processing unit (GPU) nodes, 4 thermal zones per CDC, and 103 tasks. In this instance, enabling transfer increases net profit by 57.9% relative to the otherwise matched no-transfer variant and increases completed tasks from 76 to 103. The more restrictive no-transfer FIFO-prefix variant completes 14 tasks and yields negative profit. The proposed schedule transfers 39 tasks, achieves 70.3% node utilization, and maintains zone temperatures within 24{\deg}C-27{\deg}C. These fixed-instance results indicate that cross-CDC transfer and task-reordering flexibility can improve the modeled profit and task-completion outcomes under the studied conditions.

authors.name: Zhongqi Zhao, Lei Fan, Zhu Han

papers.title: Virtual EMI Receiver Generation (VERGE) for Improved EMI Removal in MRI
papers.summary: MRI is not designed to operate in the presence of EMI emitting electronic devices. To accomodate this, we propose VERGE which improves on previous EMI removal methods and can operate without external EMI sensors. VERGE estimates a reference coil non-linearly from all imaging and non-imaging coils by training a small per-scan convolutional neural net to generate a virtual coil. The virtual coil is then used with STRIDE, a reference-based EMI removal method. For single-source EMI contamination, VERGE performed similarly to the reference method. For multi-source dynamic EMI contamination, VERGE outperformed the comparison methods. Notably, VERGE with zero physical EMI sensors outperformed the comparison methods even with two physical EMI sensors. A non-linearly estimated virtual EMI coil improves reference-coil-based EMI removal under dynamic multi-source EMI, and enables effective EMI removal without physical EMI sensors or training data.

authors.name: Alexander Mertens, Diego Martinez, Amgad Louka, Ying Yang, Chad Harris, Ian Connell

papers.title: Hardware Impairment Parameter Estimation in Fluid Antenna Systems by Inverse Optimization
papers.summary: In this paper, the problem of estimating the hardware impairment parameters of fluid antennas (FAs) in a multi-base station (BS) multi-user communication system is studied. The actual hardware coefficients are unknown, whereas the FA positions and transmit beamforming vectors adopted by the BSs are known. We first formulate a forward spectral efficiency (SE) maximization problem and introduce aggregate interference variables whose consistency with the physical inter-cell interference can be maintained through a pricing mechanism. For inverse estimation, the aggregate interference is obtained from receiver-side interference measurements associated with the observed network decisions. We then construct a trust-region linear model of the position-update problem around the observed FA positions. To extend the applicability of the proposed framework to antenna positions obtained from inexact or heuristic algorithms, we develop an inverse optimization model with an explicit duality-gap tolerance, which is solved using sequential quadratic programming (SQP). Simulation results show that the proposed scheme attains a lower estimation error than KKT residual minimization (KKT-RM) at both considered transmit-power levels and improves the SE by up to 22.86% over the Ideal-hardware-assumption scheme.

authors.name: Songling Zhang, Zhaohui Yang, Ruopeng Xu, Hao Xu, Xusheng Zhu, Zhaoyang Zhang, Kai-Kit Wong

papers.title: Connections Between Instrumental Variable, Pseudo-Linear Regression, and Prediction Error Methods in Terms of Their Minimized Criteria
papers.summary: This paper explores the connections between the criteria directly or indirectly minimized by Prediction Error (PE), Instrumental Variable (IV), and Pseudo-Linear Regression (PLR) algorithms for the identification of output-error models. By definition, PE methods aim to minimize the variance of the prediction error. In contrast, the correlation functions appearing in the stationarity conditions of IV and PLR algorithms are not the gradients of any underlying loss function involving a signal variance. Nevertheless, if the true system lies in the model set, we show that one IV algorithm minimizes asymptotically the variance of an unmeasurable signal called the equivalent prediction error. This signal was introduced previously to analyze the bias distribution of PLR schemes. It turns out that, regardless of whether the true system lies in the model set, some iterative IV and PLR algorithms aim to minimize the prediction error variance and can therefore be interpreted as indirect PE algorithms.

authors.name: Bernard Vau, Henri Bourl\`es

papers.title: Data-driven model reduction: An identification perspective using Generalized Bases of Orthonormal Functions
papers.summary: This paper proposes a data-driven model order reduction approach based on system identification concepts. A revised equation error formulation is introduced, in which the model is parameterized using Generalized Bases of Orthonormal Transfer Functions (GBOFs). The generalized reduction problem is formulated in the Hambo frequency domain associated with the GBOF transform. The frequency-domain fit of the reduced-order model is adjusted through the selection of the basis poles. A fit indicator depending on these poles is introduced, providing valuable heuristic guidance for their selection.

authors.name: Bernard Vau, Henri Bourl\`es

papers.title: Explicit Dual Model Predictive Path Integral Control
papers.summary: In this work, we present a fully sampling-based explicit dual control algorithm that combines a particle filter and model predictive path integral control for partially observed nonlinear systems. The key idea is to roll out multiple sampled input sequences from all particles of the particle filter to obtain a belief-averaged control cost that induces caution. The same rollouts are used to sample imagined future measurements, which are drawn from the predictive distribution of the particle belief. This results in a Monte Carlo information term that gives a sample estimate of the expected information gain of each sampled input sequence and thereby induces probing. In contrast to existing explicit dual control schemes, the proposed scheme neither relies on gradients of the dynamics or measurement models nor requires a Gaussian belief. Furthermore, all computations can be parallelized across input sequences, particles, and imagined measurements, which makes the scheme amenable to real-time implementation on suitable hardware. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in a simulation example of a planar terrain-aided navigation task.

authors.name: Christopher Narr, Martin Buss

papers.title: Model Augmentation for thermo-mechanical hysteretic dynamics
papers.summary: Accurate prediction of thermo-mechanical wafer deformation is essential for sub-nanometer overlay in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography. Localized heating expands the wafer, while friction between the wafer and its supporting elastic pillars causes hysteresis. Modeling this is challenging because of the system's large scale, the computational cost of friction-induced hysteresis and the sparse deformation measurements. This work augments a linear thermo-mechanical baseline model with a learning-based structure in a linear fractional representation (LFR) framework, identified from sparse measurements. Simulation results show that the augmented model captures the unmodeled dynamics with hysteretic effects and predicts the deformation significantly more accurately than the baseline.

authors.name: Samarth Toolhally, Ozan Celik, Daniel Deenen, Maarten Schoukens, Siep Weiland

papers.title: MARS: Feature-guided physics-informed deep learning for real-time battery health and lifetime prediction
papers.summary: Accurate and robust estimation of battery state-of-health (SOH) and remaining useful life (RUL) is essential for safe and cost-effective operation of electrified transportation systems, yet it remains challenging under operating variability, non-stationary aging, and non-Gaussian measurement disturbances. This paper proposes Multi-scale Adaptive Robust State Estimation (MARS), a multi-scale adaptive robust state-estimation framework that couples a dual-branch temporal encoder with an equivalent-circuit-model-constrained differentiable generalized-correntropy adaptive Kalman filter. The encoder disentangles fast intra-cycle voltage-current-temperature dynamics from slow inter-cycle degradation, and the fused degradation context adaptively parameterizes the cycle-level process covariance, measurement covariance, and correntropy bandwidth. Through the unrolled robust filtering recursion, MARS performs physics-consistent state propagation and generalized-correntropy-based innovation correction, while uncertainty decomposition and Monte Carlo dropout provide calibrated prediction intervals for SOH estimation and conditional RUL prediction. Experiments on the NASA and CALCE benchmarks demonstrate improved SOH accuracy, achieving mean absolute error/root mean square error values of 0.72%/0.92% and 0.63%/0.80%, respectively, together with competitive conditional RUL performance against representative data-driven and hybrid baselines. The resulting conditional-RUL prediction intervals achieve coverage probabilities of 100.00% and 99.24% on NASA and CALCE, respectively. Ablation, disturbance-sensitivity, near-end-of-life, and runtime analyses further verify the contribution of each module and the practical inference cost for online battery management.

authors.name: Innocent Izabayo, Haiquan Zhao

papers.title: A Discrete Digital Isolator with Shielded Planar Transformer for Gate Driver Applications
papers.summary: Galvanically isolated gate drivers are required in many power electronics applications. This paper describes an implementation of a digital isolator using discrete components with a planar coreless PCB signal transformer providing the isolation. The use of an electrostatic shield between the transformer windings is shown to provide sufficient common-mode transient immunity to support IGBT half-bridge drivers, an application subject to a severe dV/dt transient during switching. The design is verified through the experimental implementation of a prototype half bridge using two of the proposed discrete digital isolators with SiC power transistors and demonstrates common-mode transient immunity greater than 15 kV/us with very low implementation complexity.

authors.name: Thomas A. Conway

papers.title: Edge-Combining Subharmonic Mixer-First Receiver
papers.summary: A 1-10 GHz subharmonic mixer-first receiver using edge combining to drive N-path switches from 50% duty-cycle clocks at half the local oscillator (LO) frequency avoids the gain penalty of harmonic mixing. Inverter-based differential baseband amplifiers with back-gate feedback linearization set their gain by process-defined capacitance ratios, using no additional components and consuming no additional power. A 22 nm fully depleted silicon on insulator (FD-SOI) prototype receiver achieves a conversion gain of 12.8-18.1 dB and a noise figure of 5.7-11 dB across the band. It achieves up to 15.4 dBm out-of-band IIP3 while consuming 16.7-22.3 mW.

authors.name: Eric Danson, Jeffrey S. Walling

papers.title: Least ln-cosh-based adaptive filtering algorithm for graph signal processing
papers.summary: Currently, an increasing number of irregular signals are being defined within graph structures. This paper proposes a Least ln-cosh-based Adaptive Filtering for Graph Signal Processing (GSP LLAF) algorithm for offline/online graph signal estimation under various non-Gaussian noise conditions. Compared to the recently proposed Graph Adaptive Least Mean p-th Power (GSP LMP) algorithm, GSP LLAF eliminates the need for prior knowledge of the noise characteristics. Simultaneously, GSP LLAF addresses the limitation in estimation accuracy encountered by the Sign Algorithm for Graph Signal Processing (GSP Sign) and the Graph Signal Processing algorithm based on the Generalized Maximum Correntropy Criterion (GSP GMCC). Furthermore, the algorithm features low computational complexity and fast execution speed. To achieve a balance between convergence speed and estimation accuracy, a variable step-size variant, the Modified Variable Step-Size Least ln-cosh-based Adaptive Filtering Algorithm for Graph Signal Processing (GSP MVSS-LLAF), is proposed. In estimation experiments involving both static and time-varying graph signals, the proposed GSP LLAF and GSP MVSS-LLAF algorithms demonstrate fast, stable, and robust graph signal estimation performance under various non-Gaussian noise conditions, including Bernoulli-Gaussian (BG) modeled impulse noise, as well as alpha-stable, Cauchy, and Laplace distributions.

authors.name: Chong Zhang, Haiquan Zhao

papers.title: Robust DOA Estimation for GNSS-like Signals Under Jamming: A Rotation-Enhanced SWN-MUSIC Approach
papers.summary: In jamming environments, accurate direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-like signals using antenna arrays is crucial for spoofing detection and subsequent countermeasures. However, estimation accuracy strongly depends on the incident direction of the signal of interest (SOI) under a given jamming and array configuration, with severe errors occurring in certain directions---a phenomenon whose physical mechanisms remain unclear. To address this gap, we identify two types of geometric ill-conditions between the array manifold and the jamming subspace, clarifying that certain directions suffer from inherently unfavorable observation geometry, which cannot be overcome by algorithmic refinement alone. Motivated by this insight, we introduce a paradigm namely rotational diversity, which treats the array attitude as a controllable sensing resource to actively reconfigure the observation geometry, thereby providing complementary perspectives in which the problematic directions can be accurately estimated. To implement this paradigm, we develop a Rotation-Enhanced Spatial Whitening and Normalized Multiple Signal Classification (SWN-MUSIC) framework, which performs independent DOA estimations across multiple rotation angles and selectively integrates reliable estimates. Simulation results demonstrate substantial improvement in accuracy in the directions that were poorly estimated under the fixed-array SWN-MUSIC, while maintaining performance in well-conditioned directions, thereby producing more robust DOA estimates.

authors.name: Jiyao Jiang, Xiaowei Cui, Gang Liu, Sihao Zhao, Mingquan Lu

papers.title: Personalized Causal Low-Bitrate Coded Speech Restoration with Speaker Embeddings
papers.summary: Legacy low-bitrate speech codecs such as AMR-NB remain widely used in telephony, where they restrict speech bandwidth and degrade listening quality. Coded speech restoration (CSR) aims to restore the speech bandwidth while improving the overall quality of coded speech, but typically without adapting to different speakers. In this paper, we systematically investigate personalization for restoration of speech coded at low bitrates, using a causal, low-complexity Universal Bandwidth Extension Generative Adversarial Network (UBGAN) model as the basis. We propose two personalization methods based on speaker embeddings, which incur little additional computational cost at inference: (i) conditioning a single CSR model on speaker embeddings, and (ii) cluster-based model selection, where multiple personalized models are trained on clusters of acoustically similar speakers. Experiments are performed on AMR-NB coded speech at 4.75 kbps. Experimental results with disjoint seen- and unseen-speaker test sets show that cluster-based model selection does not consistently outperform the non-personalized UBGAN baseline, whereas embedding conditioning significantly improves ViSQOL and WB-PESQ scores for both seen and unseen speakers.

authors.name: Eray \"Ozg\"unay, Christian Rollwage, Kishan Gupta, Andreas Brendel, Xavier Domont, Mattes Ohlenbusch, Jan Rennies, Simon Doclo

papers.title: Reference Coordinates, Output Perturbations, and Information Loss in EEG Decoding
papers.summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) decoders can respond to reference changes that preserve all relative-potential information. We use established measurement-operator theory to distinguish coordinate sensitivity, additional output-channel perturbations, and electrode loss. Exact pseudoinverse alignment supplies a consistency control; measurement-operator canonicalization (MOC) denotes a graph-Tikhonov estimator. The broader evaluation covers three public motor-imagery datasets and four decoders. The primary EEGNet comparison on Cho2017 and PhysioNet uses three paired training seeds, three shared noise realizations, and six front ends, with identical CAR training inputs sharing checkpoints. At 10 dB output perturbation, MOC-minus-raw disagreement was -0.144 and -0.107, while balanced-accuracy differences were 0.044 and 0.050, respectively; these four contrasts passed the retained Holm correction. MOC also reduced disagreement relative to pseudoinversion across all three seeds in both cohorts. However, comparison with fixed graph smoothing after pseudoinversion did not establish an additional MOC benefit. Preserving zero reference rows changed raw disagreement by less than 0.001 in magnitude; inverse-method predictions were unchanged. For canonical front ends, cross-reference disagreement was close to the reference obtained from independent noise within the same operator. Controlled weak-mode reconstruction and equal-rank electrode masks exposed separate stability and information-loss effects. The results locate the complete-reference gains within spatial processing under the specified stress model, while requiring decoding accuracy alongside consistency to assess practical utility.

authors.name: Runni Zhou, Rongrong Fu, Xinghao Yan, Xiaoyang Li

papers.title: Structured Design of Layered Sparse Unitary Space-Time Modulation for Integrated Noncoherent and Coherent MIMO Communications
papers.summary: This work presents a novel structured constellation design based on unitary space-time modulation (USTM) for integrated noncoherent and coherent multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Information is encoded into the sparse space-time matrices through two layers: a noncoherent layer that distinguishes points on the Grassmann manifold (subspaces) and a coherent layer that distinguishes among the Stiefel representatives associated with each of those points (bases for the subspaces). We consider sequential decoding of the two layers to reduce computational complexity, while explicitly identifying the matrix structures that favor this decoding strategy. The proposed constellation builds on a previous structured Grassmannian signaling design, which has the remarkable property of producing space-time matrices with a single nonzero entry per row, while introducing a novel systematic design for the second layer corresponding to the Stiefel representatives. The design of the second layer preserves the sparsity of the first layer and significantly reduces the decoding computational complexity, while ensuring reliable performance under sequential decoding and enabling a simple yet effective bit labeling, as validated by numerical results in terms of bit error rate (BER) and symbol error rate (SER). Numerical results also show graceful performance degradation under channel correlation and, for limited coherence intervals where channel state information at the receiver (CSIR) can be estimated only imperfectly, improved performance compared with classical space-time block coding (STBC) schemes based on QAM and PSK.

authors.name: \'{A}lvaro Pend\'{a}s-Recondo, Enrique Pend\'{a}s-Recondo, Rafael Gonz\'{a}lez Ayestar\'{a}n, Jes\'{u}s Alberto L\'{o}pez-Fern\'{a}ndez, Ignacio Santamaria

papers.title: Classical heat exchanger fouling-resistance laws as first-moment identities of additive stochastic deposition
papers.summary: Heat-exchanger fouling is monitored through the fouling resistance, whose record is routinely fitted with the classical linear (Ebert--Panchal) or asymptotic (Kern--Seaton) law, and the shape of the fit is often taken as evidence of the underlying deposition or removal mechanism. We show that it cannot be. If the deposit grows by non-negative, statistically stationary increments, the mean fouling resistance is exactly linear without removal and exactly the Kern--Seaton asymptote under first-order removal, whatever the microscopic deposition law. Shear-driven erosion, per-element detachment, intermittent sloughing and saturation of the surface all give the same mean curve, so a fit identifies a net deposition rate and a relaxation time, and nothing else. Modelling the deposit as a Levy subordinator, we show where the missing information lies and what it costs to retrieve it from monitoring data. Removal mechanisms separate in the variance: sloughing leaves a plateau scatter that persists even for smooth deposition and can be read from a record that saturates. Deposition laws separate only in higher cumulants, which the measurement noise of a thermally reconstructed resistance attenuates; the record needed to distinguish them grows as the fourth power of the conductance error, which places it beyond reach at realistic measurement accuracy. For the time to reach a cleaning limit, the deposition law matters only near the threshold; farther away, the mean rate and its uncertainty dominate the prediction.

authors.name: Simone Casolo

papers.title: Capacity Credit of Data-Centre Flexibility: The Role of Workload Scheduling and Usable Battery Energy
papers.summary: Data centres that offer the same reduction in grid demand can make different contributions to supply adequacy. We estimate the effective load-carrying capability of workload scheduling and on-site batteries by matching expected unserved energy across paired simulations. Longer task deadlines increase capacity credit by giving operators more choice over when to defer and recover work. A fixed evening commitment shifts more work than deadline-based scheduling but delivers a smaller reduction in expected unserved energy. Protected backup reserves leave uninterruptible power supplies with limited capacity credit, while longer discharge durations raise the credit of dedicated batteries at the same response rating. These findings suggest assessing recovery deadlines and dispatchable energy alongside offered demand reductions.

authors.name: Pengyu Ren, Wei Sun, Jiakai Wu, Yifan Wang

papers.title: Generation of Sample Complex Wishart Distributed Matrices and Change Detection in Polarimetric SAR Data
papers.summary: The complex Wishart distribution is used to describe synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data in the so-called covariance matrix representation. We give a test statistic for detection of differences between two instances in this distribution and an associated probability measure. Generated complex Wishart distributed covariance matrices are used to show that this test statistic and the probability measure in situations with no differences follow the expected distributions.

authors.name: Allan A. Nielsen, Henning Skriver, Knut Conradsen

papers.title: On the recursive feasibility and stability of MPC without terminal constraints
papers.summary: In this paper, we analyze stability and recursive feasibility of a model predictive control (MPC) scheme that does not rely on terminal ingredients -- such as terminal constraints or a terminal cost based on a terminal controller. In the proposed formulation, we augment the cost function by a weighted finite tail which is optimized online, and we show it plays the role of a stabilizing terminal cost. Under a relaxed, local dynamic programming condition on the tail, we certify a family of regions -- parameterized by the tail's weight coefficient -- on which the problem is recursively feasible and the origin is asymptotically stable. These regions are larger as the weight increases: in particular, we show that any state that can be steered within the control horizon to a predefined neighborhood of the origin is contained in a certified region for a sufficiently large weight. Finally, we characterize the closed-loop performance over the certified region, bounding the suboptimality of the closed loop with respect to the infinite-horizon optimal cost. We conclude the discussion by illustrating these results on a simple numerical example.

authors.name: Mara Perez, Ignacio Sanchez, Filiberto Fele, Daniel Limon

papers.title: Satisfiability Modulo Theories for Robust Synthesis of Signal Temporal Logic Specifications
papers.summary: Signal Temporal Logic is a popular framework for describing a robotic system's goals. Once described using a temporal logic framework, synthesis turns the goals into actual steps for the robots to follow. Currently, the state of the art for sound and complete synthesis is using Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), which struggles on long time horizons and large environments, preventing the construction of guaranteed safe plans for long deployments. This paper introduces a new synthesis method using Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) which scales better for long deployments and adapts to environmental changes more quickly.
